questions.e: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Morocco's Abdelatif Loudyi inaugurated TASL's plant at Berrechid — the first overseas defence factory by an Indian private company in Africa.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The TASL plant in Morocco will produce which armoured platform for the Royal Moroccan Army?
questions.e: The 20,000 sq.m plant will produce the DRDO–TASL co-developed WhAP 8×8 armoured platform for the Royal Moroccan Army.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Agni-Prime, test-fired on 24 September 2025, has a range of up to how many km?
questions.e: The canisterised Agni-Prime, with a range up to 2,000 km, was test-fired from a rail-based mobile launcher in a full operational scenario.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: What was special about the 24 September 2025 Agni-Prime test?
o: It was launched from a rail-based mobile launcher
It was launched from a submarine
It carried multiple warheads in combat mode
questions.e: DRDO and the Strategic Forces Command test-fired Agni-Prime from a rail-based mobile launcher, putting India among select nations with rail-mobile launch capability.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed which session of the UN General Assembly on 27 September 2025?
questions.e: Jaishankar addressed the 80th session of the UNGA in New York, calling for reformed multilateralism and condemning terrorism.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar's final electoral roll after the Special Intensive Revision listed about how many electors?
questions.e: The Election Commission published Bihar's final roll after SIR on 30 September 2025, listing about 7.42 crore electors.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: After Bihar's draft SIR roll, how many names were added and how many deleted?
questions.e: Around 21.53 lakh names were added after the draft roll and 3.66 lakh deleted after scrutiny.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The southwest monsoon 2025 ended with all-India rainfall at what percentage of the Long Period Average?
questions.e: The southwest monsoon ended on 30 September 2025 with all-India rainfall at 108% of the LPA — an above-normal season.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which region received only 80% of the LPA during the 2025 monsoon, while Bihar too remained rainfall-deficient?
questions.e: Northwest India got 127%, central India 115% and the southern peninsula 110%, while east and northeast India got only 80%; Bihar remained rainfall-deficient.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which countries form the EFTA bloc with which India's TEPA entered into force on 1 October 2025?
questions.e: The India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, signed with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, entered into force on 1 October 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the India–EFTA TEPA, the bloc committed to how much investment and how many direct jobs in India over 15 years?
o: $200 billion investment and two million jobs
$100 billion investment and one million direct jobs
questions.e: The TEPA commits the bloc to $100 billion in investment and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years — India's first FTA with a European bloc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A 6.9-magnitude earthquake struck off which Philippine island on 30 September 2025?
questions.e: A 6.9-magnitude earthquake struck off Cebu in the Philippines, killing at least 72 people, in the seismically active Pacific Ring of Fire.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Around how many houses were torched in the communal clashes along the Assam–Nagaland border on 2 October 2025?
questions.e: Around 100 houses were torched in communal clashes along the Assam–Nagaland border amid long-standing inter-state boundary disputes.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar raised dearness allowance for state employees from 55% to what percentage, effective 1 July 2025?
questions.e: The Bihar cabinet raised DA/DR from 55% to 58% effective 1 July 2025, costing the exchequer ₹917.78 crore in FY26.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar doubled annual scholarships for government-school students of Classes 1–4 from ₹600 to what?
questions.e: The Bihar cabinet doubled scholarships: Classes 1–4 from ₹600 to ₹1,200, Classes 5–6 from ₹1,200 to ₹2,400, and Classes 7–10 from ₹1,800 to ₹3,600.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: After doubling, what is the annual scholarship for Classes 7–10 students in Bihar's government schools?
questions.e: Scholarships for Classes 7–10 rose from ₹1,800 to ₹3,600, covering government and aided schools including minority institutions, madrasas and Sanskrit schools.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar's 3 October cabinet approved a ₹5,000 monthly stipend for which group?
questions.e: Bihar approved a ₹5,000 monthly stipend for newly enrolled advocates for three years, and a ₹1,000 monthly unemployment allowance for graduate youth aged 20–25 for five years.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: How much did CM Nitish Kumar disburse to women beneficiaries under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana on 3 October 2025?
questions.e: Nitish Kumar disbursed ₹2,500 crore to 25 lakh women beneficiaries under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana in Patna.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana, how much seed support does one woman per family receive for self-employment?
questions.e: Under the scheme, one woman per family receives ₹10,000 as seed support, with up to ₹2 lakh additional assistance linked to enterprise progress.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which ministry conferred the National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2025?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.e: The Ministry of AYUSH conferred the National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2025 on Prof. Banwari Lal Gaur, Vaidya Neelakandhan Mooss E.T. and Vaidya Bhavana Prasher.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Who heads the six-member Payments Regulatory Board constituted by the RBI?
questions.e: The RBI constituted a six-member Payments Regulatory Board headed by the RBI Governor — a body proposed by the Watal Committee in 2017.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The National Pulses Mission, approved by the Union Cabinet on 3 October 2025, runs for which period?
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved the National Pulses Mission (2025–31) to achieve self-sufficiency in pulses and cut import dependence.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The National Pulses Mission focuses on incentives for the cultivation of which pulses?
questions.e: The mission focuses on quality seed distribution, expanded procurement at MSP, and incentives for tur, urad and masoor cultivation.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: India won how many medals at the World Para Athletics Championships 2025 in New Delhi?
questions.e: India recorded its best-ever haul at the World Para Athletics Championships in New Delhi — 22 medals (6 gold, 9 silver, 7 bronze) to finish tenth.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: What was India's gold-silver-bronze tally at the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships?
questions.e: India won 22 medals — 6 gold, 9 silver and 7 bronze — at the championships that concluded in New Delhi on 5 October 2025.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Where was the Israel–Hamas Gaza ceasefire and hostage-release agreement signed on 9 October 2025?
questions.e: Israel and Hamas signed the Gaza ceasefire and hostage-release agreement at Sharm el-Sheikh on 9 October 2025, based on a 20-point peace plan.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Under the October 2025 Gaza deal, how many surviving hostages did Hamas release on 13 October?
questions.e: The ceasefire took effect on 10 October; Hamas released 20 surviving hostages on 13 October while Israel freed 1,968 Palestinian prisoners.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Who became the first Indian to win the Kenton R. Miller Award in October 2025?
questions.e: Dr. Sonali Ghosh, Field Director of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, became the first Indian to win the Kenton R. Miller Award.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Kenton R. Miller Award won by Dr. Sonali Ghosh is presented by which body?
o: IUCN's World Commission on Protected Areas
questions.e: Presented by IUCN's World Commission on Protected Areas at the World Conservation Congress in Abu Dhabi, it honours innovation in sustainable protected-area management.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Under the NDA's seat-sharing for the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, how many seats each did the BJP and JD(U) contest?
questions.e: The NDA announced: BJP and JD(U) 101 seats each, LJP (Ram Vilas) 29, and RLM and HAM (Secular) 6 each, for the 243-member House.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Chirag Paswan's LJP (Ram Vilas) was allotted how many seats in the NDA's Bihar seat-sharing?
questions.e: Under the 12 October 2025 NDA seat-sharing, Chirag Paswan's LJP (Ram Vilas) got 29 seats.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: LEAPS 2025, launched by DPIIT at Bharat Mandapam, marks how many years of PM GatiShakti?
questions.e: DPIIT launched LEAPS 2025 — the Logistics Excellence, Advancement, and Performance Shield awards across 13 categories — marking four years of PM GatiShakti.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: India was elected to the UN Human Rights Council for which term in October 2025?
questions.e: India was elected to the 47-member UN Human Rights Council for the 2026–28 term on 14 October 2025, securing 177 votes.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: India's election to the UNHRC in October 2025 marks its which term on the body?
questions.e: It will be India's seventh term on the Geneva-based body, which reviews human-rights records through the Universal Periodic Review.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who became the first transgender person appointed to a Supreme Court-constituted committee?
questions.e: Transgender rights activist Akkai Padmashali became the first transgender person appointed to a Supreme Court-constituted committee on 17 October 2025.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The SC-constituted committee on transgender welfare is headed by whom?
questions.e: Headed by former Delhi High Court judge Justice Asha Menon, the panel will draft a National Equal Opportunity Policy for transgender persons.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Who was sworn in as Madagascar's transitional president on 17 October 2025?
questions.e: Colonel Michael Randrianirina was sworn in as Madagascar's transitional president after Gen-Z-led protests forced President Andry Rajoelina to flee.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: DRDO began the second phase of trials of its Stratospheric Airship Platform at which location in October 2025?
questions.e: DRDO began the second phase of trials of its helium-filled unmanned Stratospheric Airship Platform at Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: In Chhath 2025, Sandhya Arghya fell on which date?
questions.e: Chhath 2025 began with Nahay Khay on 25 October, followed by Kharna (26th), Sandhya Arghya (27th) and Usha Arghya (28th).

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: During Chhath, devotees offer arghya to the setting and rising sun at ghats along which river in Bihar?
questions.e: Devotees offered arghya to the setting and rising sun at ghats along the Ganga and other rivers.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Dr. Patrick Herminie was sworn in as President of Seychelles after winning what vote share?
questions.e: Dr. Patrick Herminie was sworn in as the sixth President of Seychelles after winning the election with 52.7% of the vote, succeeding Wavel Ramkalawan.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Election Commission's Phase II of the Special Intensive Revision, announced in October 2025, covers about how many electors?
questions.e: Phase II of SIR, announced on 27 October 2025, covers nine states and three UTs with about 51 crore electors.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: For SIR Phase II, enumeration runs during which period and final rolls are due when?
o: 1 November–1 December 2025; final rolls due 31 January 2026
15 November–15 December 2025; final rolls due 15 March 2026
4 October–4 November 2025; final rolls due 7 January 2026
4 November–4 December 2025; final rolls due 7 February 2026
questions.e: Enumeration runs 4 November–4 December 2025, with final rolls due 7 February 2026, extending the Bihar SIR model nationwide.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved how much under the Nutrient-Based Subsidy scheme for Rabi 2025–26?
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved ₹37,952.29 crore under the NBS scheme for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for Rabi 2025–26.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The NBS subsidy for Rabi 2025–26 covers fertilisers for which period?
questions.e: The subsidy for DAP and NPKS grades covers Rabi 2025–26 (1 October 2025–31 March 2026), keeping farm-gate prices affordable.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: In the ICC Women's ODI World Cup semifinal on 30 October 2025, what target did India chase down against Australia?
questions.e: India chased down 339 against Australia, reaching 341/5 in 48.3 overs — the highest successful chase in Women's World Cup history.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Who struck the unbeaten 127 in India's record Women's World Cup semifinal chase?
questions.e: Jemimah Rodrigues struck an unbeaten 127 and captain Harmanpreet Kaur 89 in the famous win over Australia.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's 150th birth anniversary was observed on 31 October 2025 as which day?
questions.e: India marked the 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on 31 October 2025, observed as National Unity Day.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: Sardar Patel, the 'Iron Man of India', is credited with integrating how many princely states?
questions.e: The 'Iron Man of India', who integrated 562 princely states, was honoured with unity runs and tributes at the Statue of Unity in Kevadia, Gujarat.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: ISRO's LVM3-M5 launched CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) weighing how much on 2 November 2025?
questions.e: LVM3-M5 launched the 4,410 kg CMS-03 into geosynchronous transfer orbit from Sriharikota — the heaviest satellite ever launched from Indian soil.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: The CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) satellite will serve which arm of India's defence forces?
questions.e: Costing ₹1,589 crore, the secure communications satellite will serve the Indian Navy, succeeding the decade-old GSAT-7.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: India won their maiden ICC Women's ODI World Cup by beating which team in the final?
questions.e: India won their maiden ICC Women's ODI World Cup on 2 November 2025, beating South Africa by 52 runs in the final (298/7 vs 246).

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Who starred with 58 and 5/39 in the 2025 Women's ODI World Cup final?
questions.e: Shafali Verma scored 87, while Deepti Sharma starred with 58 and 5/39; captain Harmanpreet Kaur lifted the trophy.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Zohran Mamdani, elected New York City mayor in November 2025, takes office on which date?
questions.e: Mamdani became NYC's first Muslim and first South Asian mayor-elect — and its youngest since 1917 — taking office on 1 January 2026.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The first phase of the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, held on 6 November, covered how many constituencies?
questions.e: The first phase on 6 November 2025 covered 121 of the 243 constituencies, with the NDA and Mahagathbandhan facing off.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Which two main alliances contested the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections?
questions.e: The NDA and the Mahagathbandhan faced off in the high-stakes contest for the 243-member House.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: Who composed 'Vande Mataram', whose 150th anniversary was commemorated from 7 November 2025?
questions.e: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterji in 1875 and later adopted as India's national song.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: The 150-years-of-'Vande Mataram' commemoration was marked with which two honours?
o: A commemorative coin and postage stamp
A coin and a national holiday
questions.e: The year-long commemoration launched on 7 November 2025 was marked with a commemorative coin and postage stamp.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Harihar Kshetra Sonepur Mela is held at the confluence of the Ganga and which other river?
questions.e: The month-long Sonepur Mela began on 9 November 2025 in Saran district, at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: SWAYAM, launched by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in November 2025, stands for what?
questions.e: SWAYAM (Sustainable and Green Defence Manufacturing), anchored in the Comprehensive Energy Efficiency Action Plan (2023), pushes energy efficiency and renewables across defence PSUs.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Sergio Gor, sworn in as US Ambassador to India, will concurrently serve as Special Envoy for which region?
questions.e: Sergio Gor was sworn in on 10 November 2025 and will concurrently serve as Special Envoy for South and Central Asia.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: What was Bihar's highest-ever voter turnout, recorded in Phase II of the 2025 Assembly polls?
questions.e: The second phase on 11 November 2025 saw Bihar record its highest-ever turnout of 66.91% — the best since 1951.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: In Bihar's Phase II polling, women outvoted men at what turnout figures?
questions.e: Women outvoted men at 71.6% versus 62.8%, across 45,399 polling stations in Phase II.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified on which date?
questions.e: The government notified the final DPDP Rules, 2025, on 13 November.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under the notified DPDP Rules, principal compliance obligations take effect after how many months?
questions.e: Data Protection Board provisions take effect immediately, consent-manager rules after 12 months, and principal compliance obligations after 18 months.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Jharkhand, which marked 25 years of statehood on 15 November 2025, was carved out of Bihar on which date?
questions.e: Jharkhand observed its 25th Foundation Day on 15 November 2025, marking a quarter-century since its carving out of Bihar on 15 November 2000.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which gallery of Science City Kolkata won the CIMUSET Award in November 2025?
questions.e: Science City Kolkata's climate-change gallery 'On the Edge?' won the CIMUSET Award at the 27th ICOM General Conference in Dubai.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission, which submitted its report in November 2025, is chaired by whom?
questions.e: The 16th Finance Commission, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, submitted its report for 2026–31 to President Droupadi Murmu on 17 November 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission's report covers which award period and was submitted under which constitutional articles?
questions.e: The report for 2026–31, submitted under Articles 280 and 281, recommends the vertical and horizontal devolution of taxes between the Centre and states.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which state was adjudged Best State in the 6th National Water Awards (2025)?
questions.e: In the National Water Awards, Maharashtra was adjudged Best State, followed by Gujarat and Haryana.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: After the 2025 Bihar polls, CM Nitish Kumar gave up which portfolio to the BJP for the first time since 2005?
questions.e: Nitish Kumar allocated portfolios on 21 November 2025, giving up the Home department to ally BJP for the first time since he came to power in 2005.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who became Bihar's Home Minister after the 2025 portfolio allocation?
questions.e: Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary (BJP) became Home Minister, while Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Sinha got Land and Revenue.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: How many central labour laws did the four new labour codes consolidate?
questions.e: The four labour codes — on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations (2020), Social Security (2020), and OSHWC (2020) — came into force on 21 November 2025, consolidating 29 central labour laws.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The four labour codes came into force on which date?
questions.e: The four labour codes came into force on 21 November 2025, modernising wages, working hours and social-security coverage including gig workers.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: The G20 Leaders' Summit of November 2025 was held in which city — the first on African soil?
questions.e: The first G20 Leaders' Summit on African soil was held in Johannesburg on 22–23 November 2025.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: What was South Africa's theme for the November 2025 G20 Summit?
questions.e: Held under South Africa's theme of 'Solidarity, Equality and Sustainability', the declaration addressed disaster resilience, debt relief, just energy transitions and critical minerals.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025?
questions.e: Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as the 53rd CJI on 24 November 2025, succeeding Justice B.R. Gavai.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Justice Surya Kant's tenure as CJI runs till which date?
questions.e: His tenure runs till 9 February 2027; he was elevated to the Supreme Court in 2019.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who was nominated as Executive Chairman of NALSA effective 24 November 2025?
questions.e: President Droupadi Murmu nominated Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath as Executive Chairman of NALSA, succeeding Justice Surya Kant.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: CJI Surya Kant nominated whom as Chairman of the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee?
questions.e: CJI Kant separately nominated Justice J.K. Maheshwari as Chairman of the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: In its first meeting, the new Bihar cabinet approved a target of how many jobs and employment opportunities over five years?
questions.e: The new Bihar cabinet approved the Bihar State AI Mission and a target of one crore jobs and employment opportunities over five years.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The new Bihar cabinet cleared how many new sugar mills and greenfield townships?
o: 25 new sugar mills and 11 greenfield townships
questions.e: It cleared 11 greenfield townships, 25 new sugar mills (and revival of nine closed ones), plus plans for a defence corridor and semiconductor park.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: South Africa's 2–0 Test series win in India in November 2025 was their first series victory in India since which year?
questions.e: South Africa completed a 2–0 Test series win in India — their first since 2000 — winning the second Test at Guwahati by 408 runs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's real GDP grew by what percentage in Q2 FY26 (July–September 2025)?
questions.e: India's real GDP grew 8.2% in Q2 FY26, sharply up from 5.6% a year earlier, cementing India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In Q2 FY26, manufacturing grew 9.1% and construction 7.2% — what was the tertiary sector's growth?
questions.e: Manufacturing grew 9.1%, construction 7.2% and the tertiary sector 9.2%, per NSO estimates released 28 November 2025.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: How many women were elected as MLAs in the 2025 Bihar Assembly?
questions.e: Twenty-nine women were elected as MLAs in 2025 — up from 26 in 2020, though below the record 34 of 2010; 26 belong to the NDA and three to the RJD.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: The 26th Hornbill Festival was held from 1–10 December 2025 at which venue near Kohima?
questions.e: The 26th Hornbill Festival began on 1 December 2025 at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, Nagaland, running till 10 December.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Who was appointed Managing Director of LIC on 1 December 2025?
questions.e: The Ministry of Finance appointed Ramakrishnan Chander as MD of the Life Insurance Corporation of India.

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: The 15th International Sand Art Festival and 36th Konark Festival were inaugurated at which heritage site?
questions.e: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi inaugurated the twin festivals on 1 December 2025 at the Konark Sun Temple heritage site.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Usha Janakiraman was appointed RBI Executive Director and assigned which department?
o: Department of Supervision (Risk, Analytics and Vulnerability Assessment)
Department of Payment and Settlement Systems
questions.e: Usha Janakiraman was appointed RBI Executive Director from 1 December 2025, assigned the Department of Supervision (Risk, Analytics and Vulnerability Assessment).

questions.subject: Miscellaneous
questions.q: Oxford University Press named which term its Word of the Year 2025?
questions.e: OUP named 'rage bait' — content designed to provoke anger for online engagement — as its Word of the Year 2025.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who was unanimously elected the 18th Speaker of the Bihar Legislative Assembly on 2 December 2025?
questions.e: Senior BJP leader Prem Kumar, a nine-term Gaya Town MLA, was unanimously elected the 18th Speaker.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Prem Kumar's unopposed election as Bihar Assembly Speaker was the first since which year?
questions.e: His unopposed election — the first since 2015 — reflected the NDA's comfortable majority in the new House.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The 14th EKUVERIN exercise, between the Indian Army and the Maldives National Defence Force, was held at which venue?
questions.e: The 14th EKUVERIN commenced at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, on 2 December 2025, running till 15 December, focusing on counter-insurgency and humanitarian assistance drills.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025, passed by Parliament in December, raises excise duties on which products?
questions.e: Parliament passed the Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025, on 3 December, raising excise duties on tobacco products to discourage consumption.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Russian President Vladimir Putin's December 2025 India visit was for which edition of the India-Russia Annual Summit?
questions.e: Putin arrived in New Delhi on 4 December 2025 for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit — his first visit since 2021.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Putin's December 2025 visit to India was his first since which year?
questions.e: The two-day state visit was his first since 2021; talks covered defence, trade, energy, civil nuclear cooperation and labour mobility.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who was elected Deputy Speaker of the Bihar Assembly in the December 2025 session?
questions.e: Bihar's five-day Assembly session concluded on 5 December 2025 with Narendra Narayan Yadav elected Deputy Speaker, and a second supplementary budget exceeding ₹37,498 crore passed.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: On 5 December 2025, the RBI's MPC cut the repo rate to what level?
questions.e: The MPC cut the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.25%, retaining a neutral stance; the SDF stands at 5.00% and the MSF/Bank Rate at 5.50%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: After the December 2025 rate cut, the RBI raised the FY26 growth forecast to what and projected inflation at what?
questions.e: The central bank raised the FY26 growth forecast to 7.3% and projected inflation at 2.0%.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: On the MHA's directive, Raj Bhavans were redesignated as what?
questions.e: Raj Bhavans were redesignated as Lok Bhavan and Raj Niwas as Lok Niwas, with the PMO complex renamed Seva Teerth.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: How many states renamed their Raj Bhavans following the directive?
questions.e: Twenty states — including Bihar — renamed their Raj Bhavans, while J&K and Ladakh adopted Lok Niwas.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Who received the inaugural 'FIFA Peace Prize — Football Unites the World' in December 2025?
questions.e: US President Donald Trump received the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize from FIFA President Gianni Infantino at the Kennedy Center on 5 December 2025.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: NASA lost communication with the MAVEN spacecraft in December 2025; when was it launched?
questions.e: NASA lost communication with MAVEN on 6 December 2025; launched in 2013, the mission studied how Mars lost its atmosphere.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: The India International Science Festival 2025 was held at which city?
questions.e: IISF 2025 was held at Panchkula, Haryana, from 6–9 December, co-organised by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Simranpreet Kaur Brar won gold in which event at the ISSF World Cup Final 2025 in Doha?
questions.e: Simranpreet Kaur Brar, 21, won gold in the women's 25m pistol, scoring 41/50 to equal the junior world record.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Which three new departments did the Bihar cabinet create on 9 December 2025?
o: Youth, Employment & Skill Development; Higher Education; Civil Aviation
questions.e: The Bihar cabinet created three new departments — Youth, Employment & Skill Development; Higher Education; and Civil Aviation.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated how many BRO infrastructure projects worth ₹5,000 crore in December 2025?
questions.e: Rajnath Singh inaugurated 125 BRO projects — 28 roads, 93 bridges and four others, worth ₹5,000 crore — from Ladakh, the highest single-day BRO rollout.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The archaeological site of Lothal, famous for the world's earliest known dockyard, is located in which present-day state?
questions.e: Lothal in Gujarat's Ahmedabad district was a major port city of the Harappan civilization, with a brick-built dockyard used for berthing ships and trade with Mesopotamia.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The 'Great Bath' of the Indus Valley Civilization was excavated at which site?
questions.e: The Great Bath, a large watertight rectangular tank, was found at Mohenjo-daro in Sindh (now Pakistan) and was likely used for ritual bathing.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Evidence of a ploughed agricultural field, the earliest of its kind in the world, was found at which Harappan site?
questions.e: Kalibangan in Rajasthan revealed a ploughed field with criss-cross furrow marks, showing that Harappans practised double cropping of wheat and barley.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: How many mandalas (books) does the Rig Veda contain?
questions.e: The Rig Veda, the oldest of the four Vedas, is divided into 10 mandalas containing 1,028 hymns dedicated mainly to deities like Indra, Agni and Varuna.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Gayatri Mantra, found in the Rig Veda, is dedicated to which deity?
questions.e: The Gayatri Mantra appears in the third mandala of the Rig Veda and is addressed to Savitri, the solar deity, seeking illumination of the intellect.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, attained nirvana (death) at which place in Bihar?
questions.e: Mahavira died at Pavapuri (Pawapuri) in present-day Nalanda district of Bihar in 468 BCE, a site now marked by the Jal Mandir Jain temple.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Mahavira was born at Kundagrama, which was located near which ancient city?
questions.e: Mahavira was born in 540 BCE at Kundagrama near Vaishali, the capital of the Lichchhavi republic, into a Kshatriya family.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon, the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta, at which place?
questions.e: After enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, the Buddha gave his first sermon to five disciples at the Deer Park in Sarnath, an event called the turning of the wheel of Dhamma.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at which place in Bihar?
questions.e: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya on the banks of the Niranjana river at age 35, after which he became known as the Buddha.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Gautama Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (death) at which place?
questions.e: The Buddha died at Kushinagar (in present-day Uttar Pradesh) in 483 BCE at the age of 80, between two sal trees, an event called Mahaparinirvana.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgir during the reign of which Magadhan king?
questions.e: The First Buddhist Council met at the Saptaparni cave in Rajgir around 483 BCE under King Ajatashatru, where the Sutta and Vinaya Pitakas were compiled.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Second Buddhist Council was convened at Vaishali during the reign of which king?
questions.e: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali about a century after the Buddha's death, during the reign of Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty, to settle disputes over monastic discipline.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under the patronage of which emperor?
questions.e: Ashoka convened the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra around 250 BCE under the presidency of Moggaliputta Tissa, after which missionaries were sent abroad.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir during the reign of which Kushan king?
questions.e: Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana in Kashmir, where the Sarvastivada doctrines were compiled and Buddhism split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: How many Mahajanapadas are traditionally listed in ancient Buddhist and Jain texts?
questions.e: Ancient texts list sixteen Mahajanapadas, the great states of 6th century BCE India, of which Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti were the most powerful.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Bimbisara, the first great king of Magadha, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.e: Bimbisara (c. 544-492 BCE) founded the Haryanka dynasty and made Rajgir (Girivraja) the capital of Magadha, beginning its rise to imperial power.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The fortification of Pataligrama (later Pataliputra) was undertaken by which Magadhan king to repel Licchavi attacks?
questions.e: Ajatashatru fortified the village of Pataligrama at the confluence of the Ganga and Son; his successor Udayin later made it the capital as Pataliputra.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Mahapadma Nanda, called the 'first empire builder' of Magadha, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.e: Mahapadma Nanda overthrew the Shishunagas around 345 BCE and founded the Nanda dynasty; the Puranas call him the destroyer of all Kshatriyas for his vast conquests.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the last Nanda king Dhanananda with the guidance of which minister?
questions.e: Chanakya, also called Kautilya or Vishnugupta, mentored Chandragupta Maurya and authored the Arthashastra, the classic treatise on statecraft and administration.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The treaty between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus Nicator is dated to approximately which year?
questions.e: Around 305 BCE Seleucus ceded the Indus region to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 war elephants, and sent Megasthenes as ambassador to the Mauryan court at Pataliputra.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Ashoka fought the Kalinga war in which year?
questions.e: The Kalinga war of 261 BCE caused massive bloodshed that transformed Ashoka, leading him to embrace Buddhism and propagate Dhamma through rock and pillar edicts.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka describes the horrors of the Kalinga war and his remorse?
questions.e: Major Rock Edict XIII gives a graphic account of the suffering in Kalinga and Ashoka's moral transformation, and also mentions his missions to Hellenistic kingdoms.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Lion Capital that became India's National Emblem was originally atop an Ashokan pillar at which site?
questions.e: The four-lion capital from the Ashokan pillar at Sarnath was adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950, with the motto Satyameva Jayate below it.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Megasthenes, the author of 'Indica', was the ambassador of which foreign ruler at Chandragupta Maurya's court?
questions.e: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus Nicator to the Mauryan court at Pataliputra; his 'Indica' is a key (though fragmentary) Greek account of Mauryan India.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, was assassinated by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga in which century BCE?
questions.e: Pushyamitra Shunga killed Brihadratha around 185 BCE during a military parade and founded the Shunga dynasty, ending nearly 140 years of Mauryan rule.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Kanishka, the greatest Kushan king, is credited with starting which era in 78 CE?
questions.e: Kanishka's accession in 78 CE marks the beginning of the Saka era, still used in India's national calendar alongside the Gregorian system.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Charaka, the author of the Charaka Samhita on medicine, lived in the court of which king?
questions.e: Charaka, the 'father of Indian medicine', was the court physician of Kanishka; his Charaka Samhita remains a foundational text of Ayurveda.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Nagarjuna, the philosopher who founded the Madhyamika school of Mahayana Buddhism, lived during the rule of which dynasty?
questions.e: Nagarjuna (c. 150-250 CE) expounded the doctrine of emptiness (Shunyavada) during the Satavahana period in the Deccan and is regarded as the second Buddha in Mahayana tradition.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Samudragupta is often called the 'Napoleon of India'. Who gave him this title?
questions.e: Historian V. A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' for his extensive military campaigns across north and south India, recorded in the Allahabad pillar inscription.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Allahabad pillar inscription (Prayaga Prashasti) eulogising Samudragupta was composed by which court poet?
questions.e: Harisena, the court poet and minister of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad, detailing the king's conquests.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of which Gupta emperor?
questions.e: Fa-Hien travelled in India from 399 to 412 CE during Chandragupta II Vikramaditya's reign and left an account describing a prosperous, well-administered empire.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Nalanda Mahavihara, the ancient university of Bihar, was founded by which Gupta emperor?
questions.e: Kumaragupta I (c. 415-455 CE) founded Nalanda, which grew into the world's greatest centre of Buddhist learning with thousands of students including Hiuen Tsang.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Vikramshila University in Bihar was founded by which Pala king?
questions.e: Dharmapala (c. 775-810 CE) founded Vikramshila near Bhagalpur as a great centre of Tantric Buddhist learning, second only to Nalanda in fame.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Odantapuri Mahavihara, another great Pala-era university of Bihar, was established by which king?
questions.e: Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty (c. 750 CE), established Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif region), which flourished as a major Buddhist learning centre.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Harshavardhana made which city his capital after uniting Thanesar and Kannauj?
questions.e: Harsha (606-647 CE) shifted his capital to Kannauj on the Ganga, from where he ruled a vast empire covering much of north India.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Hiuen Tsang, the Chinese pilgrim who studied at Nalanda, visited India during the reign of which king?
questions.e: Hiuen Tsang travelled in India from 630 to 645 CE during Harsha's reign, studied at Nalanda for years, and recorded his observations in the Si-yu-ki.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Which Chalukya king of Badami defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada, an event recorded in the Aihole inscription?
questions.e: Pulakesin II halted Harsha's southward advance at the Narmada around 618 CE; his court poet Ravikirti celebrated the victory in the Aihole inscription.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur was built by which Chola king?
questions.e: Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) built the Brihadeeswara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site and masterpiece of Dravidian architecture with its 66-metre vimana.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The earliest Tamil grammar, Tolkappiyam, belongs to which body of ancient Tamil literature?
questions.e: Tolkappiyam is the oldest surviving Tamil grammatical work and belongs to the Sangam corpus, composed in the early centuries CE in the Tamil country.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Gautamiputra Satakarni, the greatest Satavahana king, had his capital at which place?
questions.e: The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan from Pratishthana (modern Paithan in Maharashtra); Gautamiputra Satakarni's exploits are recorded in the Nasik inscription of his mother Gautami Balashri.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Indo-Greek king Menander is famous in Buddhist tradition for his dialogues with which monk, recorded in the Milinda Panha?
questions.e: The Milinda Panha records the philosophical dialogue between King Menander (Milinda) and the monk Nagasena, ending with Menander's conversion to Buddhism.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Kushan capital Purushapura corresponds to which modern city?
questions.e: Purushapura, modern Peshawar in Pakistan, served as the Kushan capital under Kanishka, alongside Mathura as the southern capital.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Gandhara art, blending Greco-Roman and Indian styles, flourished under which dynasty?
questions.e: Gandhara art developed in the northwest under Kushan patronage (1st-5th century CE), producing the earliest Buddha images in human form with Hellenistic drapery.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Vikram era, beginning in 57 BCE, is traditionally associated with which legendary king of Ujjain?
questions.e: The Vikram Samvat beginning in 57 BCE commemorates King Vikramaditya of Ujjain's victory over the Sakas and remains widely used in Hindu calendars.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Aryabhata, who explained the decimal system and the earth's rotation, composed the Aryabhatiya in which year?
questions.e: Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE at Kusumapura (Patna), presenting the place-value system, zero, and the theory that the earth rotates on its axis.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Varahamihira, the author of Brihat Samhita and Panchasiddhantika, adorned the court of which Gupta emperor?
questions.e: Varahamihira was one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) in Chandragupta II Vikramaditya's court; his Brihat Samhita is an encyclopaedia of astronomy, astrology and natural science.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Ajanta cave paintings, depicting the Jataka tales, were mainly executed during the rule of which dynasty?
questions.e: Most Ajanta paintings date to the 5th century CE under Vakataka patronage during the Gupta age, depicting the life of the Buddha and Jataka stories in brilliant murals.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli, famous for its rust-resistant composition, bears an inscription of which Gupta king?
questions.e: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription praises 'Chandra', identified with Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, and the pillar's corrosion resistance testifies to advanced Gupta metallurgy.

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: Which of the following texts is attributed to Harshavardhana himself?
questions.e: Harsha wrote the Sanskrit dramas Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda; the Harshacharita and Kadambari were written by his court poet Banabhatta.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion of Sindh in 712 CE defeated which ruler?
questions.e: Muhammad bin Qasim, sent by the Umayyad governor Hajjaj, defeated Raja Dahir of Sindh in 712 CE, marking the first Arab foothold in India.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated which invader?
questions.e: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori at Tarain in 1191, but Ghori returned the next year and won the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), opening Delhi to Turkish rule.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Slave dynasty, died in 1210 due to which accident?
o: Fall from a horse while playing chaugan (polo)
questions.e: Aibak died from injuries sustained in a fall from his horse while playing chaugan (polo) at Lahore in 1210, just four years after founding the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Aibak and completed by whom?
questions.e: Aibak began the Qutub Minar around 1199 to celebrate Turkish victory; his successor Iltutmish completed the five-storeyed tower.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Razia Sultan, the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate, was the daughter of which Sultan?
questions.e: Razia (r. 1236-1240) was Iltutmish's daughter, chosen by him over his sons as the most capable heir; the Turkish nobles deposed and killed her within four years.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Balban propounded the theory of kingship based on which concept, calling himself the 'shadow of God' on earth?
questions.e: Balban (r. 1266-1287) styled himself Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God) and enforced rigid court etiquette like sijda and paibos to exalt the monarchy above the Turkish nobles.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Alauddin Khalji's famous market reforms and price control system were primarily designed to achieve what?
o: Maintain a large standing army on low salaries
questions.e: Alauddin fixed prices of grain, cloth and other essentials so that his huge standing army could be maintained on modest cash salaries, curbing both inflation and Mongol threats.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Which Sultan introduced token currency of brass and copper in place of silver tankas, leading to economic chaos?
questions.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency (1329-30) failed because the state could not prevent forgery; citizens minted fake coins at home and the scheme was withdrawn.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Muhammad bin Tughlaq transferred his capital from Delhi to which city in the Deccan?
questions.e: In 1327 the Sultan ordered the transfer of the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) for central location and safety from Mongols, but the forced migration caused great suffering and the plan was abandoned.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Firoz Shah Tughlaq is credited with building an extensive canal network and founding which city in the east?
questions.e: Firoz Shah Tughlaq (r. 1351-1388) dug major canals from the Yamuna and Sutlej, founded Jaunpur, Firozabad and Hissar, and levied jizya even on Brahmins.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Timur's invasion of India in 1398 took place during the reign of which Tughlaq ruler?
questions.e: Timur sacked Delhi in December 1398 during the weak reign of Nasir-ud-din Mahmud, dealing a death blow to the Tughlaq dynasty and the Sultanate's power.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Lodhi dynasty was founded by Bahlol Lodhi, and its last ruler Ibrahim Lodhi was defeated by Babur in which battle?
questions.e: Babur's superior artillery and tulughma tactics crushed Ibrahim Lodhi's larger army at Panipat on 21 April 1526, founding the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Babur's autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), was originally written in which language?
questions.e: Babur wrote his frank and detailed memoirs in his native Chagatai Turkish; it was later translated into Persian during Akbar's reign.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: In the Battle of Khanwa (1527), Babur defeated which Rajput confederacy leader?
questions.e: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at Khanwa near Agra in 1527, breaking Rajput resistance and securing Mughal dominance in north India.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at the Battle of Chausa in 1539. In which present-day Bihar district is Chausa located?
questions.e: Chausa lies in Buxar district of Bihar; Sher Shah's victory there in June 1539 forced Humayun to flee, and a second defeat at Kannauj (1540) drove him into exile.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Sher Shah Suri, who built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam) and introduced the rupiya, was born at which Bihar town?
questions.e: Sher Shah was born Farid Khan at Sasaram (Rohtas district); his magnificent tomb stands there, and his five-year rule (1540-45) reformed administration, currency and roads.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, the first garden-tomb in India, was commissioned by whom?
questions.e: Humayun's widow Haji Begum built the tomb (1565-72); its charbagh design and red sandstone-white marble blend became the prototype for the Taj Mahal.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in 1556 at the age of thirteen. Who acted as his regent (Vakil) initially?
questions.e: Bairam Khan served as Akbar's regent from 1556 to 1560, defeating Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat before falling from favour.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: In the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), Akbar's forces defeated which claimant to the Delhi throne?
questions.e: Bairam Khan's army defeated Hemu, the Hindu general of Adil Shah Suri, at Panipat in November 1556; Hemu was captured and executed, securing Akbar's throne.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap and the Mughal army led by whom?
questions.e: Akbar sent Raja Man Singh of Amber against Maharana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576; though Pratap was defeated, he continued guerrilla resistance from the Aravallis.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Akbar proclaimed the Din-i-Ilahi in 1582. Which of his Navaratnas was the only Hindu to join it?
questions.e: Din-i-Ilahi was Akbar's syncretic order blending elements of various faiths; Birbal was the only Hindu among its handful of adherents.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Ain-i-Akbari, a detailed account of Akbar's administration, was written by whom?
questions.e: Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari, the third volume of the Akbarnama, is the richest source on Mughal administration, revenue, army and court life.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: During Jahangir's reign, the English East India Company obtained trading rights after the visit of which ambassador in 1615?
questions.e: Sir Thomas Roe, envoy of James I, secured a farman from Jahangir in 1615 allowing the Company to establish factories, beginning formal Anglo-Mughal trade relations.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653. Who is credited as its chief architect?
questions.e: Ustad Ahmad Lahori, also associated with the Red Fort's design, is credited as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal, built in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya tax on non-Muslims in which year?
questions.e: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 after Akbar had abolished it in 1564; the move deepened Rajput, Maratha and Sikh alienation from Mughal rule.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Shivaji was crowned as Chhatrapati at Raigad in which year?
questions.e: Shivaji's coronation at Raigad in 1674 formalised the Maratha kingdom; he created the Ashtapradhan council of eight ministers for administration.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and which Afghan invader?
questions.e: Ahmad Shah Abdali shattered the Maratha army at Panipat on 14 January 1761 in one of the bloodiest battles of the 18th century, checking Maratha expansion northward.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Bhakti saint Kabir is traditionally regarded as a disciple of which teacher?
questions.e: Kabir (c. 1440-1518), the weaver-saint of Varanasi, is counted among Ramananda's disciples; his dohas rejected both Hindu and Muslim ritualism in favour of formless devotion.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469 at Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib, located in which present-day country?
questions.e: Nankana Sahib, Guru Nanak's birthplace, lies in Pakistan's Punjab province; his teachings of one God, honest labour and equality founded the Sikh faith.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Chishti Sufi order in India is most closely associated with which saint, whose dargah is at Ajmer?
questions.e: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (d. 1236) established the Chishti order in India; his Ajmer dargah remains one of the subcontinent's most visited shrines.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka on the banks of which river?
questions.e: The Sangama brothers founded Vijayanagara at Hampi on the Tungabhadra; under Krishnadevaraya (r. 1509-29) it became the subcontinent's greatest Hindu empire of the age.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Krishnadevaraya, the greatest Vijayanagara king, authored which Telugu epic poem?
questions.e: Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada, a Telugu mahakavya on the Alvar saint Andal, reflects his scholarship; his court hosted the Ashtadiggajas, eight great Telugu poets.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565), which destroyed Vijayanagara's imperial power, was fought against an alliance of which sultanates?
questions.e: The combined armies of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar crushed Vijayanagara at Talikota (Rakshasa-Tangadi) in 1565 and sacked Hampi.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Bahman Shah with its first capital at which city?
questions.e: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah founded the Bahmani Sultanate with Gulbarga as capital; it later shifted to Bidar and eventually split into five Deccan sultanates.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Charminar of Hyderabad was built in 1591 by which Qutb Shahi ruler?
questions.e: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad and built the Charminar in 1591, traditionally to mark the end of a plague epidemic.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Battle of Plassey (1757), in which Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, was won largely because of the betrayal of which commander?
questions.e: Mir Jafar, Siraj's commander-in-chief, held back his troops under a secret pact with Clive; Plassey gave the British political control of Bengal.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought in present-day Bihar between the British and a combined army of which three powers?
o: Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II
questions.e: At Buxar on 22 October 1764, Hector Munro defeated the alliance of Bengal's Mir Qasim, Awadh's Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II, leading to the Diwani of Bengal in 1765.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', died defending his capital in which Anglo-Mysore War?
questions.e: Tipu died fighting at Seringapatam on 4 May 1799 in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War against the British under Arthur Wellesley, ending Mysore's resistance.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with which treaty in 1782?
questions.e: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War, restoring the status quo and giving the British two decades of peace with the Marathas.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over which region?
questions.e: The 54-metre Buland Darwaza (1575) celebrates Akbar's conquest of Gujarat in 1573; Fatehpur Sikri served as his capital from 1571 to 1585.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Rani Durgavati of Gondwana died fighting the Mughal forces of Akbar in 1564. Her capital was at which place?
questions.e: Rani Durgavati ruled Gondwana from Chauragarh; rather than surrender to Asaf Khan's Mughal army in 1564, she chose death on the battlefield.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699 at which place?
questions.e: On Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur Sahib, Guru Gobind Singh baptised the first five Panj Pyare, creating the Khalsa order of saint-soldiers.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604 and was executed on the orders of which Mughal emperor?
questions.e: Jahangir had Guru Arjan Dev executed at Lahore in 1606 for supporting Prince Khusrau's rebellion, the first Sikh martyrdom, which militarised the Sikh community.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Maharaja Ranjit Singh signed the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809 with the British, represented by which envoy?
questions.e: The Treaty of Amritsar (1809) between Ranjit Singh and Charles Metcalfe fixed the Sutlej as the boundary between the Sikh Empire and British India.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Nadir Shah's invasion of 1739 culminated in the Battle of Karnal and the plunder of Delhi, including which famous throne?
questions.e: Nadir Shah defeated Muhammad Shah at Karnal in February 1739, then looted Delhi for 57 days, carrying away the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor diamond.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Sayyid brothers, Abdullah Khan and Hussain Ali Khan, are known in Mughal history by which title?
questions.e: The Sayyid brothers made and unmade four Mughal emperors between 1713 and 1720, earning the title 'king makers' before their fall.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Chand Bibi is remembered for her heroic defence of which Deccan fort-city against Akbar's forces in 1595?
questions.e: Chand Bibi, regent of Ahmednagar, defended the fort against Akbar's son Murad in 1595 and negotiated an honourable settlement before her murder in 1599.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: Malik Ambar, the Abyssinian-born military genius who defied the Mughals, served as regent of which Deccan sultanate?
questions.e: Malik Ambar (1548-1626), prime minister and regent of Ahmednagar, pioneered Maratha-style guerrilla warfare and repeatedly checked Jahangir's Deccan campaigns.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Red Fort of Delhi was commissioned by Shah Jahan in 1639. Its chief architect is credited to be the same as that of the Taj Mahal. Who was he?
questions.e: Ustad Ahmad Lahori designed both the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort (Shahjahanabad), blending Persian, Timurid and Indian architectural traditions.

questions.subject: Medieval Indian History
questions.q: The Sufi saint Salim Chishti, in whose honour Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, lived at which place?
questions.e: Sheikh Salim Chishti lived at Sikri; after his blessing was followed by the birth of Prince Salim (Jahangir), Akbar built his new capital Fatehpur Sikri there.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498 with the help of a Gujarati pilot. Whose patronage did he seek on landing?
questions.e: Da Gama landed at Kappad near Calicut in May 1498 and was received by the Zamorin, opening the direct sea route between Europe and India.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Dutch East India Company established its first factory in India at Masulipatnam in which year?
questions.e: The Dutch set up their first Indian factory at Masulipatnam in 1605; they were later confined to the spice trade and ousted by the British after the Battle of Bedara (1759).

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The English East India Company established its first factory at Surat in 1613 during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
questions.e: After Sir Thomas Roe's mission, Jahangir permitted the Company to set up its first factory at Surat in 1613, the beachhead of British trade in India.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760), which ended French ambitions in India, was won by the British under which general?
questions.e: Eyre Coote defeated the French under Count de Lally at Wandiwash in 1760; the Treaty of Paris (1763) then confined France to minor trading posts.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The system of Dual Government in Bengal was introduced by Robert Clive in which year?
questions.e: After Buxar, the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal; Clive's Dual Government left administration to the Nawab while revenue went to the Company.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784 along with whom?
questions.e: Hastings and Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society at Calcutta in 1784 to study Indian history, languages and culture; Jones translated the Manusmriti and Shakuntala.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in which year?
questions.e: Cornwallis's Permanent Settlement (1793) fixed land revenue permanently and made zamindars landowners, creating absentee landlordism and peasant misery in Bihar and Bengal.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Subsidiary Alliance system, which made Indian rulers accept British troops and residents, was devised by which Governor-General?
questions.e: Wellesley (1798-1805) used the Subsidiary Alliance to bring Hyderabad, Mysore, Awadh and the Marathas under British control without direct annexation.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Which of the following was NOT introduced during Lord Dalhousie's tenure?
questions.e: Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, the first railway (1853) and the telegraph; the Widow Remarriage Act (1856) was passed under his successor Lord Canning.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Mangal Pandey, whose revolt at Barrackpore sparked the 1857 uprising, belonged to which district of present-day Uttar Pradesh?
questions.e: Sepoy Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, a native of Ballia, attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was hanged on 8 April.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Veer Kunwar Singh, the octogenarian hero of the 1857 revolt in Bihar, belonged to which place?
questions.e: Kunwar Singh of Jagdispur in Bhojpur district led the Bihar uprising at nearly 80 years of age, defeating British forces at Arrah before dying of wounds in April 1858.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting the British at which place in June 1858?
questions.e: After the fall of Jhansi, the Rani joined Tantia Tope and died in battle at Gwalior on 18 June 1858; Hugh Rose called her the most dangerous of all Indian leaders.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Tantia Tope, the great guerrilla leader of 1857, was captured and executed in 1859 at which place?
questions.e: Tantia Tope was betrayed, captured and hanged at Shivpuri (Madhya Pradesh) on 18 April 1859, ending the last organised resistance of the revolt.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: After the Revolt of 1857, Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled by the British to which place?
questions.e: The last Mughal emperor was tried and exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862; his grave there remains a pilgrimage site.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858, announcing direct Crown rule, was read out at Allahabad on 1 November 1858 by which Viceroy?
questions.e: Lord Canning, the last Governor-General and first Viceroy, read the Queen's Proclamation at Allahabad, ending Company rule and promising non-interference in religious matters.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 at Bombay. Who was its first president?
questions.e: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first Congress session at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay; A. O. Hume was the founder-organiser, not president.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was ordered by which Viceroy?
questions.e: Curzon partitioned Bengal on 16 October 1905 on administrative grounds, but Indians saw it as divide-and-rule; it triggered the Swadeshi and boycott movements.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Surat Split of 1907 divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists over the issue of the presidentship. Who were the rival candidates?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji and Bipin Chandra Pal
Rash Behari Ghosh and Lala Lajpat Rai
questions.e: At the Surat session (1907), Moderates backed Rash Behari Ghosh while Extremists wanted Lala Lajpat Rai; the session ended in chaos and the Congress split until Lucknow 1916.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant because it marked an agreement between which two organisations?
o: Congress and the Home Rule League
questions.e: The Lucknow Pact brought the Congress and the Muslim League together on joint constitutional demands, with the Congress accepting separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded the Home Rule League in April 1916 at which place?
questions.e: Tilak launched his Home Rule League at Poona in April 1916 with the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright'; Annie Besant started her own league at Madras in September.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, was launched at the invitation of which peasant leader?
questions.e: Rajkumar Shukla, an indigo cultivator from Champaran, persuaded Gandhi to visit Bihar; the 1917 satyagraha against the tinkathia system was Gandhi's first Indian campaign.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The tinkathia system, against which the Champaran Satyagraha was directed, forced peasants to grow indigo on what proportion of their land?
questions.e: Under tinkathia, Champaran peasants had to plant indigo on 3/20 of their holdings for European planters; the 1918 Champaran Agrarian Act abolished the system.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919. Who ordered the firing on the unarmed gathering?
questions.e: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire without warning at Amritsar, killing hundreds; the Hunter Committee condemned the act but the British establishment largely shielded him.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura incident. On which date did that violence occur?
questions.e: At Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur), a mob set fire to a police station killing 22 policemen on 5 February 1922; Gandhi suspended the movement, shocking many Congress leaders.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Lala Lajpat Rai died in 1928 from injuries sustained during a protest against which commission?
questions.e: Lajpat Rai led the boycott of the all-white Simon Commission and was lathi-charged at Lahore; his death enraged revolutionaries, leading to Saunders' assassination.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Nehru Report of 1928, the first Indian-authored constitutional blueprint, was chaired by whom?
questions.e: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee that produced the Nehru Report demanding dominion status; its rejection by the British pushed the Congress towards Purna Swaraj.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: At the Lahore session of December 1929, the Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution. Who presided over this historic session?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore session that declared complete independence as the goal and fixed 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Gandhi began the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram. How long was the march to Dandi?
questions.e: Gandhi walked 240 miles over 24 days to Dandi, where he broke the salt law on 6 April 1930, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931. Which of the following was a key outcome?
o: Release of political prisoners and Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference
questions.e: The pact secured the release of civil disobedience prisoners and Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference, though Gandhi failed to get Bhagat Singh's sentence commuted.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Poona Pact of September 1932 was an agreement between Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar on which issue?
o: Reservation of seats for the Depressed Classes within joint electorates
questions.e: After Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award's separate electorates for Depressed Classes, the Poona Pact provided reserved seats for them within Hindu joint electorates.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: During the Quit India Movement, seven young students were shot dead by the British at Patna Secretariat on 11 August 1942 while hoisting the tricolour. The martyrs' memorial at Patna is known as what?
questions.e: The Shaheed Smarak at Patna Secretariat commemorates the seven students martyred on 11 August 1942, Bihar's most iconic Quit India sacrifice.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Indian National Army was revived by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943 at which place?
questions.e: Bose took command of the INA at Singapore in July 1943, gave the 'Delhi Chalo' call, and formed the Azad Hind Government; the INA's trials at the Red Fort later ignited nationalist fury.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in 1946. Which of the following was NOT a member of the mission?
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission comprised Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Alexander; Mountbatten arrived later as Viceroy in March 1947 to oversee the transfer of power.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, India's first President, was born in 1884 at Zeradei in which present-day Bihar district?
questions.e: Rajendra Prasad was born at Zeradei village in Siwan district; he led the Champaran movement's legal work, presided over the Constituent Assembly and served as President from 1950 to 1962.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Jayaprakash Narayan, who led the Total Revolution movement of 1974, was born at Sitabdiara in which Bihar district?
questions.e: JP was born at Sitabdiara (Saran district) in 1902; his 1974 call for Sampoorna Kranti against corruption led to the Emergency and earned him the title Loknayak.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936 at Lucknow with which Bihar leader as its first president?
questions.e: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, the militant peasant leader of Bihar, became the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Bihar was separated from Bengal Presidency and created as the province of Bihar and Orissa on which date, celebrated as Bihar Day?
questions.e: Bihar and Orissa became a separate province on 22 March 1912; Orissa was carved out in 1936 and Jharkhand in 2000, leaving the present 38-district Bihar.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Patna University, one of India's oldest modern universities, was established in which year?
questions.e: Patna University was founded in 1917, the same year as the Champaran Satyagraha, and became the intellectual hub of Bihar's freedom movement.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Sadaqat Ashram in Patna, Gandhi's headquarters during the Bihar movements, was established on land donated by which leader?
questions.e: Barrister Mazharul Haque donated his land at Digha, Patna, for Sadaqat Ashram in 1921; it became the nerve centre of the Congress in Bihar.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Sachchidananda Sinha is notable in constitutional history for which role?
o: Temporary (pro tem) Chairman of the Constituent Assembly
questions.e: Sachchidananda Sinha, the veteran Bihar leader, was elected temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946 before Rajendra Prasad took over permanently.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Shri Krishna Sinha, the first Chief Minister of Bihar, is popularly remembered by which honorific?
questions.e: Shri Krishna Sinha (1887-1961), called Bihar Kesari, led the state from 1946 to 1961 with deputy Anugrah Narayan Sinha, pioneering land reforms and industrialisation.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Anugrah Narayan Sinha served as the first Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar alongside Shri Krishna Sinha. He is honoured with which title?
questions.e: Anugrah Narayan Sinha, called Bihar Vibhuti, was the architect of Bihar's early development as finance and deputy chief minister until his death in 1957.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Amar Singh, who carried forward the 1857 revolt in Bihar after Kunwar Singh's death, was related to Kunwar Singh as his what?
questions.e: Amar Singh, Kunwar Singh's younger brother, continued guerrilla warfare in Shahabad after April 1858 and kept British forces engaged for months.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Santhal rebellion of 1855-56, which preceded the 1857 revolt, was led by which brothers?
questions.e: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal hul (rebellion) of 1855-56 against zamindars and moneylenders in the Santhal Parganas (then part of Bihar).

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: Birsa Munda, who led the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) against British rule, died in 1900 in the jail at which city?
questions.e: Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900 under mysterious circumstances; his movement forced the British to pass the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Tana Bhagat movement among the Oraon tribe of Chotanagpur was inspired by the ideals of which leader?
questions.e: Started by Jatra Bhagat in 1914, the Tana Bhagat movement adopted Gandhian ideals of non-violence, abstinence and khadi, merging tribal protest with the national movement.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Wahabi movement in Bihar, an early anti-British resistance, was centred at which place under the leadership of Syed Ahmad Barelvi's followers?
questions.e: Patna was the chief centre of the Wahabi movement in eastern India; leaders like Wilayat Ali and Inayat Ali organised resistance until the British crushed it after 1857.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The first session of the Bihar Provincial Congress Committee was held in 1908 at which city?
questions.e: The Bihar Provincial Congress held its first session at Patna in 1908, formalising the Congress organisation in the newly created province.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, the famous salt satyagraha in Bihar was led at which coastal-adjacent centre?
o: Bihar had no coastline, so satyagrahis marched to Gujarat
Bihar's satyagraha focused on chowkidari tax boycott instead of salt
questions.e: Being landlocked, Bihar's civil disobedience centred on boycotting the chowkidari (village watchman) tax rather than salt-making, with leaders like Rajendra Prasad guiding it.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bihar lies approximately between which latitudinal and longitudinal extents?
questions.e: Bihar extends from about 24°20'N to 27°31'N latitude and 83°19'E to 88°17'E longitude, entirely in the subtropical zone of the Gangetic plain.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which of the following states does NOT share a border with Bihar?
