questions.e: Bihar borders Uttar Pradesh (west), Nepal (north), West Bengal (east) and Jharkhand (south); Madhya Pradesh does not touch Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: How many districts are there in present-day Bihar?
questions.e: Bihar has 38 districts organised into 9 divisions, with Patna as the capital and most populous district.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Ganga enters Bihar at Chausa and exits the state near which area, covering about how many kilometres within Bihar?
o: About 445 km, exiting near the Bengal border
questions.e: The Ganga flows roughly 445 km through Bihar from Chausa (Buxar) in the west to the West Bengal border in the east, dividing the state into north and south Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Son river joins the Ganga near Maner, west of Patna. The Son originates from which hill range?
questions.e: The Son rises near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh, flows north through the Kaimur range, and meets the Ganga at Maner in Patna district.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Gandak river, which joins the Ganga at Hajipur (Sonepur), originates in which country?
questions.e: The Gandak (Narayani in Nepal) rises in the Himalayas of Nepal, enters Bihar at Valmikinagar, and joins the Ganga opposite Patna at Hajipur.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent and devastating floods?
questions.e: The Kosi shifts its course westward unpredictably, causing severe floods in north Bihar; the 2008 breach at Kusaha inundated millions, earning its grim title.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Ghaghara (Sarayu) river joins the Ganga at which place in Bihar?
questions.e: The Ghaghara meets the Ganga at Revelganj near Chhapra in Saran district after flowing through Uttar Pradesh and along Bihar's western border.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Punpun river joins the Ganga at Fatuha. Near which pilgrimage city does the Punpun flow?
questions.e: The Punpun flows past Gaya and joins the Ganga at Fatuha; pilgrims performing pind-daan at Gaya also bathe in its waters.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Falgu river, sacred to pilgrims at Gaya, is formed by the confluence of which streams and is known by what other name upstream?
questions.e: The Falgu is called the Niranjana upstream where the Lilajan and Mohana unite; at Gaya it flows underground, so pilgrims offer pindas on its sandy bed.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest district of Bihar by area?
questions.e: West Champaran (headquarters Bettiah) is Bihar's largest district by area, bordering Nepal and housing the Valmiki Tiger Reserve.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which is the smallest district of Bihar by area?
questions.e: Sheohar, carved out of Sitamarhi in 1994, is the smallest district of Bihar by area in the Tirhut division.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: According to the 2011 Census, which district of Bihar has the highest population?
questions.e: Patna district is the most populous in Bihar with over 5.8 million people in 2011, while Sheikhpura is the least populous.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among Indian states in the 2011 Census. What was it approximately?
questions.e: Bihar's literacy rate was 61.8% in 2011 (male 71.2%, female 51.5%), the lowest among states, though it rose sharply from 47% in 2001.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: What was Bihar's sex ratio (females per 1000 males) according to the 2011 Census?
questions.e: Bihar's sex ratio improved to 918 in 2011 from 919 in 2001 (a marginal dip), remaining below the national average of 943.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bihar has the highest population density among Indian states. What was it in the 2011 Census?
questions.e: Bihar's density of 1,106 persons per sq km (2011) is the highest among major states, reflecting intense pressure on agricultural land.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The dominant soil type of the Gangetic plain in Bihar is which of the following?
questions.e: Bihar is covered by fertile Gangetic alluvium deposited by the Ganga and its Himalayan tributaries; older alluvium (bhangar) lies south and newer (khadar) near riverbeds.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Terai region of north Bihar is characterised by which type of soil and vegetation?
o: Marshy, fertile soil with dense sal forests
questions.e: The Terai belt along the Nepal border has high water tables, marshy fertile soils and dense moist deciduous forests, now largely protected in the Valmiki Tiger Reserve.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is the main kharif (monsoon) crop of Bihar?
questions.e: Rice is Bihar's principal kharif crop, grown across the Gangetic plain; wheat dominates the rabi season, followed by maize, pulses and sugarcane.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Muzaffarpur is world-famous for which fruit, which has received a GI tag as 'Shahi'?
questions.e: Muzaffarpur's Shahi litchi received a GI tag; Bihar is India's largest litchi producer, with the fruit ripening in May-June.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Mithila Makhana, which received a GI tag in 2022, is primarily cultivated in which region of Bihar?
questions.e: Fox nut (makhana) is cultivated in the ponds and wetlands of the Mithila region; Bihar produces about 90% of India's makhana.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Jardalu mango, which has a GI tag, is associated with which Bihar district?
questions.e: The Jardalu mango of Bhagalpur, known for its aroma and sweetness, received a GI tag; Bhagalpur's Katarni rice is also GI-tagged.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Sugar mills in Bihar are concentrated in which region?
o: North Bihar plain (Champaran, Siwan, Gopalganj belt)
questions.e: Sugarcane grows best in the fertile, well-watered north Bihar plain, so mills cluster in West and East Champaran, Gopalganj, Siwan and Samastipur.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Barauni oil refinery in Begusarai district belongs to which public sector company?
questions.e: The Barauni refinery of Indian Oil, commissioned in 1964, is Bihar's only oil refinery and the anchor of the Barauni industrial complex with its thermal plant and fertiliser unit.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Valmiki National Park, Bihar's only national park, is located in which district?
questions.e: Valmiki National Park and Tiger Reserve in West Champaran, on the Nepal border, is Bihar's only national park and its largest protected area.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is located in which Bihar district?
questions.e: The 50-km sanctuary stretch of the Ganga at Bhagalpur protects the endangered Gangetic dolphin, India's national aquatic animal.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary in Bihar by area?
questions.e: Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary in the Kaimur hills is Bihar's largest sanctuary, known for its waterfalls, tigers and leopards.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Kanwar Lake, one of Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lakes and a bird sanctuary, is located in which district?
questions.e: Kanwar Lake (Kabar Taal) in Begusarai, formed by a meander of the Gandak, is a Ramsar-listed wetland hosting thousands of migratory birds.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries are located in which Bihar district?
questions.e: The Nagi and Nakti dam reservoirs in Jamui district are notified bird sanctuaries, important wintering grounds for migratory waterfowl.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Rajgir in Nalanda district is famous for hot springs and for having which of the following?
questions.e: Rajgir's ropeway to the Vishwa Shanti Stupa on Ratnagiri hill was among India's oldest; the town's hot springs (Brahmakund) attract pilgrims year-round.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Kakolat waterfall, a popular picnic spot, is located in which Bihar district?
questions.e: Kakolat Falls on the Mahabar hill in Nawada district cascades in multiple tiers and hosts an annual fair.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: What is the state animal of Bihar?
questions.e: The gaur, the largest wild bovine, is Bihar's state animal; the state bird is the house sparrow, the state tree the peepal, and the state flower the kachnar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: What is the state bird of Bihar?
questions.e: The house sparrow (ghar ki chidiya) is Bihar's state bird, chosen to draw attention to its declining urban population.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Chhath, the most important festival of Bihar, is dedicated to which deity?
questions.e: Chhath, celebrated six days after Diwali, honours Surya and Chhathi Maiya with offerings at riverbanks at sunrise and sunset, observed with strict fasting.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Sonepur Mela, held at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak, is famous as which kind of fair?
questions.e: The month-long Sonepur Mela (Harihar Kshetra Mela) in Saran district is among Asia's largest cattle fairs, trading elephants, horses and cattle.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which language was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution in 2003 and is the mother tongue of the Mithila region?
questions.e: Maithili was included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment in 2003; Bhojpuri, Magahi and Angika remain major regional dialects of Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Urdu enjoys which official status in Bihar?
questions.e: Urdu is Bihar's second official language after Hindi, used in government notifications and education alongside Hindi.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?
questions.e: UNESCO inscribed the Mahabodhi Temple Complex, marking the Buddha's enlightenment site, in 2002; the present temple largely dates to the Gupta period.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Vaishali is celebrated in history as which of the following?
o: Site of the Fourth Buddhist Council
One of the world's earliest republics (Licchavi)
questions.e: Vaishali's Licchavi republic, with its assembly of 7,707 representatives, is regarded among the world's earliest republics; it hosted the Second Buddhist Council.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Patna Museum, housing the famous Didarganj Yakshi statue, was established in which year?
questions.e: Founded in 1917 during the nationalist era, the Patna Museum holds Mauryan and Gupta sculptures, including the polished sandstone Didarganj Yakshi.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Golghar, the beehive-shaped granary of Patna, was built in 1786 by the British under which Governor-General's orders?
questions.e: Captain John Garstin built Golghar in 1786 on Warren Hastings' orders to store grain against famine; its 145-step spiral stairway offers a panoramic city view.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib at Patna Sahib is sacred to Sikhs as the birthplace of which Guru?
questions.e: Guru Gobind Singh was born at Patna Sahib in 1666; the takht built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh is one of Sikhism's five temporal seats.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The ruins of Vikramshila University are located at Antichak in which Bihar district?
questions.e: Excavations at Antichak in Bhagalpur district revealed Vikramshila's cruciform stupa and monastic complex founded by the Pala king Dharmapala.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bhagalpur is traditionally known as the 'Silk City' of Bihar because of which industry?
questions.e: Bhagalpur's handloom weavers produce famous tussar (bhagalpuri) silk sarees and fabrics, a craft with centuries of history along the Ganga.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Indrapuri Barrage on the Son river, one of the longest barrages in India, is located in which district?
questions.e: The 1,407-metre Indrapuri Barrage in Rohtas district feeds the Son canal system, irrigating large parts of south Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of Bihar's GI-tagged products is correct?
o: Shahi Litchi - Muzaffarpur and Jardalu Mango - Bhagalpur
Alphonso Mango - Ratnagiri and Shahi Litchi - Patna
Katarni Rice - Purnia and Makhana - Gaya
Jardalu Mango - Darbhanga and Litchi - Hajipur
questions.e: Muzaffarpur's Shahi litchi and Bhagalpur's Jardalu mango both hold GI tags, along with Bhagalpur's Katarni rice and Mithila makhana.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The annual Pitrapaksha Mela, when Hindus offer pind-daan for ancestors, is held at which Bihar city?
questions.e: Gaya's Vishnupad Temple and the Falgu river host the fortnight-long Pitrapaksha Mela, drawing lakhs of pilgrims each year.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Malmas Mela, held once every three years, takes place at which Bihar town?
questions.e: Rajgir hosts the month-long Malmas Mela during the intercalary month (adhik maas), when pilgrims bathe in its hot springs.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which national highway connects Patna to Delhi via the Grand Trunk Road corridor?
questions.e: NH-19 (the renumbered NH-2) follows the historic Grand Trunk Road from Delhi through Bihar towards Kolkata, passing Sasaram, Aurangabad and Barhi.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) crosses 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: India's Standard Meridian (82°30'E) passes through which city of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.e: The 82°30'E meridian passes near Mirzapur and defines Indian Standard Time, which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The southernmost point of India, Indira Point, is located on which island?
questions.e: Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island is India's southernmost tip; much of it was submerged by the 2004 tsunami.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The McMahon Line forms the boundary between India and which country?
questions.e: The McMahon Line, drawn at the 1914 Shimla Convention, is India's claimed boundary with China in Arunachal Pradesh, though China disputes it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Radcliffe Line demarcates the border between India and which country?
questions.e: Sir Cyril Radcliffe drew the India-Pakistan boundary in 1947; the same line, inherited by Bangladesh in 1971, forms the India-Bangladesh border.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Durand Line is the disputed border between which two countries?
questions.e: Drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan, the Durand Line is now the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, never recognised by Afghan governments.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the highest mountain peak in India?
questions.e: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is India's highest peak, though it lies in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir; the highest peak fully within undisputed India is Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.e: Rajasthan (342,239 sq km) is India's largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh; Goa is the smallest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the longest river of India?
questions.e: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is India's longest river, rising at Gaumukh in Uttarakhand and emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Brahmaputra enters India in Arunachal Pradesh under which name?
questions.e: The Yarlung Tsangpo of Tibet enters Arunachal as the Dihang/Siang, becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam, and flows to Bangladesh as the Jamuna.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which river is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South)?
questions.e: The Godavari, India's second-longest river (1,465 km), is called Dakshin Ganga; it rises at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and drains into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Narmada river originates at Amarkantak and flows westward into which water body?
questions.e: The Narmada flows west through the rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India?
questions.e: Chilika in Odisha is India's largest brackish lagoon and a Ramsar site, famous for Irrawaddy dolphins and migratory birds from Siberia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.e: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir, fed by the Jhelum, is India's largest freshwater lake, though it has shrunk due to encroachment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Loktak Lake in Manipur is famous for which unique feature?
questions.e: Loktak's floating phumdis are masses of vegetation and soil; Keibul Lamjao National Park on the lake is the world's only floating national park, home to the sangai deer.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Anamudi (2,695 m), the highest peak of peninsular India, is located in which hill range?
questions.e: Anamudi in Kerala's Anaimalai Hills is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India, within Eravikulam National Park.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which Indian state?
questions.e: The Thar (Great Indian Desert) covers western Rajasthan, extending into Pakistan; the Indira Gandhi Canal has greened parts of it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, is shared by India and which country?
questions.e: The Sundarbans delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra spans West Bengal and Bangladesh; it is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the last stronghold of the Royal Bengal tiger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The southwest monsoon normally reaches the Kerala coast around which date?
questions.e: The southwest monsoon typically hits Kerala around 1 June, then advances northward, reaching Bihar by mid-June and covering all India by mid-July.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Mawsynram in Meghalaya is famous as which of the following?
questions.e: Mawsynram receives over 11,000 mm of annual rainfall, making it the wettest place on Earth, slightly ahead of nearby Cherrapunji.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Black regur soil, ideal for cotton cultivation, is derived from which rock formation?
questions.e: Regur (black cotton soil) formed from weathered Deccan basalt retains moisture well, suiting cotton; it covers much of Maharashtra, MP and Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Laterite soils are typically found in regions with which climatic condition?
o: High rainfall with alternate wet and dry seasons
questions.e: Intense leaching by heavy seasonal rainfall leaves iron and aluminium oxides behind, forming laterite soils common in the Western Ghats, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian state is the largest producer of tea?
questions.e: Assam produces over half of India's tea from the Brahmaputra valley gardens; India is the world's second-largest tea producer after China.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian state is the largest producer of coffee?
questions.e: Karnataka's Coorg, Chikmagalur and Hassan districts grow most of India's coffee, mainly robusta and arabica, on Western Ghats slopes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Bailadila iron ore mines, among India's richest, are located in which state?
questions.e: Bailadila in Dantewada district, Chhattisgarh, holds high-grade hematite ore feeding the Bhilai and Vizag steel plants.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which state has the largest coal reserves in India?
questions.e: Jharkhand holds India's largest coal reserves, concentrated in the Jharia, Bokaro and North Karanpura Gondwana coalfields.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which state is the largest producer of bauxite (aluminium ore) in India?
questions.e: Odisha's Panchpatmali and Gandhamardan deposits make it India's top bauxite producer, feeding NALCO's alumina refinery at Damanjodi.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: India's first oil refinery was established in 1901 at which place in Assam?
questions.e: Digboi, where oil was struck in 1889, hosts Asia's oldest operating refinery, commissioned in 1901 and now a heritage site.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Green Revolution in India began in 1966-67 with high-yielding varieties of which crop first?
questions.e: Mexican dwarf wheat varieties introduced by Norman Borlaug, championed by M. S. Swaminathan, transformed Punjab and Haryana into India's granary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Operation Flood, which made India the world's largest milk producer, is associated with which person?
questions.e: Verghese Kurien's Operation Flood (1970) built the Amul cooperative model nationwide, an achievement called the White Revolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 2011 Census was the 15th census of India. What was its official slogan?
questions.e: The 2011 Census used the slogan 'Our Census, Our Future'; it recorded India's population at 121.08 crore with a growth rate of 17.7%.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian state has the highest literacy rate as per the 2011 Census?
questions.e: Kerala's literacy rate was 94% in 2011, the highest among states, while Bihar's 61.8% was the lowest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which state had the highest sex ratio in the 2011 Census?
questions.e: Kerala's sex ratio of 1,084 females per 1,000 males (2011) was India's highest, while Haryana's 879 was the lowest among states.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.e: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is traditionally regarded as the world's longest river, flowing through eleven African countries to the Mediterranean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert. In which continent is it located?
questions.e: The Sahara spans about 9.2 million sq km across North Africa, roughly the size of the United States.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Equator passes through all of the following countries EXCEPT which one?
questions.e: The Equator crosses Ecuador, Brazil, Indonesia, Kenya and others, but Mexico lies entirely north of it in the Tropic of Cancer zone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The International Date Line approximately follows which meridian?
questions.e: The 180° meridian in the Pacific is the basis of the International Date Line, where the calendar day changes; it zigzags to keep island nations on one side.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects which two water bodies?
questions.e: The Strait of Gibraltar links the Atlantic to the Mediterranean between Spain and Morocco, a vital shipping chokepoint.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connects which two seas?
o: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
questions.e: The Suez Canal cuts through Egypt joining the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, shortening Europe-Asia voyages by thousands of kilometres.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
questions.e: The Panama Canal (opened 1914) links the Atlantic and Pacific across Central America, a key route for world trade.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
questions.e: Greenland (about 2.16 million sq km), an autonomous Danish territory, is the world's largest island, mostly covered by an ice sheet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth's surface, lies in which ocean?
questions.e: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep plunges about 10,900 metres in the western Pacific, east of the Mariana Islands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall, is located in which country?
questions.e: Angel Falls drops 979 metres from a tabletop mountain in Venezuela's Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a west-flowing river of peninsular India?
questions.e: The Tapi (Tapti) flows west from the Satpuras into the Gulf of Khambhat; most peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow east.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Coromandel Coast lies along which Indian state?
questions.e: The Coromandel Coast is the southeastern Tamil Nadu coast along the Bay of Bengal, receiving most rain from the retreating northeast monsoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which canal links the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic trade via Egypt and is administered by an Egyptian authority?
questions.e: The Suez Canal is operated by the Suez Canal Authority of Egypt; its 2021 blockage by the Ever Given showed its critical role in global trade.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Gulf Stream is a warm ocean current in which ocean?
questions.e: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic towards Europe, moderating Western Europe's climate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following Indian rivers is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
questions.e: The Damodar's devastating floods earned it the title 'Sorrow of Bengal' until the Damodar Valley Corporation tamed it with dams in the 1950s.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Zojila Pass connects Kashmir Valley with which region?
questions.e: Zojila on the Srinagar-Leh highway links the Kashmir Valley to Ladakh; a tunnel under it is under construction for all-weather connectivity.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date?
questions.e: The Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day); it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up in August 1947 and is regarded as the chief architect of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946. Who was elected its temporary (pro tem) chairman?
questions.e: Sachchidananda Sinha, the senior-most member, presided temporarily on 9 December 1946; Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent chairman two days later.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were inserted into the Preamble by which constitutional amendment?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976), passed during the Emergency, added Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble and is called the Mini Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.e: Part III (Articles 12-35) guarantees the six Fundamental Rights, enforceable by courts; they were inspired partly by the US Bill of Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Equality is guaranteed under which Articles of the Constitution?
questions.e: Articles 14-18 cover equality before law, prohibition of discrimination, equality of opportunity in public employment, abolition of untouchability and abolition of titles.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21 has been expansively interpreted by the Supreme Court to include which of the following?
o: Right to a clean environment and dignified life
questions.e: Through cases like Maneka Gandhi (1978) and later PILs, Article 21 now covers the right to live with dignity, clean environment, privacy and speedy trial.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) were borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.e: The DPSP (Articles 36-51) drew inspiration from the Irish Constitution; they are non-justiciable but fundamental to governance.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.e: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties, inserted as Part IVA (Article 51A) with ten duties; an eleventh was added in 2002.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 86th Amendment (2002) made free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children of which age group?
questions.e: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment, guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14, implemented through the RTE Act 2009.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of which members?
o: Elected MPs and elected MLAs of states and UTs with legislatures
questions.e: Article 54 provides that the President is elected by elected MPs and elected MLAs of states and Delhi, Puducherry and J&K, through proportional representation by single transferable vote.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The procedure for impeachment of the President is laid down in which Article?
questions.e: Article 61 allows impeachment for violation of the Constitution by a two-thirds majority in both Houses; no President has ever been impeached.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of which body?
questions.e: Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; unlike the President, the VP is elected only by MPs.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under Article 75, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, but by convention the President appoints whom?
o: The leader of the majority party or coalition in Lok Sabha
questions.e: Parliamentary convention requires the President to invite the leader commanding majority support in the Lok Sabha, ensuring the government enjoys the House's confidence.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as prescribed by the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 81 caps Lok Sabha at 550 (530 from states, 20 from UTs); the 104th Amendment (2020) ended the two Anglo-Indian nominated seats, reducing the earlier 552 cap.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: Article 80 caps Rajya Sabha at 250 members: 238 elected from states and UTs plus 12 nominated by the President for expertise in various fields.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and requires the prior certification of whom?
questions.e: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; the Speaker's certificate that a bill is a Money Bill is final, and the Rajya Sabha can only suggest amendments within 14 days.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The maximum gap permitted between two sessions of Parliament is how long?
questions.e: Article 85 requires the President to summon Parliament such that no more than six months elapse between sessions; normally three sessions are held yearly.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Zero Hour in Parliament is an Indian innovation. Which statement about it is correct?
o: It is the same as Question Hour
It is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure
It is an informal convention starting at noon for raising urgent matters without notice
questions.e: Zero Hour (around noon, after Question Hour) is not in the rule book but an Indian convention since the 1960s for raising matters of public importance without prior notice.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Governor of a state is appointed by the President under which Article, and holds office during whose pleasure?
o: Article 155, pleasure of the Chief Minister
questions.e: Article 153 provides for Governors and Article 155 for their appointment by the President; Article 156 says they hold office during the President's pleasure, normally five years.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was appointed to examine which subject?
questions.e: The Sarkaria Commission reviewed Centre-State relations and recommended restraint in using Article 356 and strengthening the Inter-State Council.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The National Emergency under Article 352 has been proclaimed in India how many times?
questions.e: National Emergency was declared thrice: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Pakistan war) and 1975-77 (internal disturbance); the 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: President's Rule under Article 356 was first imposed in 1951 in which state?
questions.e: Article 356 was first used in Punjab (then PEPSU) in 1951; its frequent later misuse led the Supreme Court to lay down safeguards in the Bommai case (1994).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Financial Emergency under Article 360 has been declared in India how many times?
questions.e: Article 360 has never been invoked, even during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, when the government instead pledged gold and launched economic reforms.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Supreme Court of India came into existence on 26 January 1950 and was inaugurated on which date?
questions.e: The Supreme Court came into being with the Constitution on 26 January 1950 and held its inaugural sitting on 28 January 1950, succeeding the Federal Court.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of India?
questions.e: Justice Harilal J. Kania became the first Chief Justice of India in 1950, serving until his death in 1951.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.e: Judicial review, the power of courts to strike down unconstitutional laws, is borrowed from the USA, though India's Parliament also retains significant powers unlike the American model.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Public Interest Litigation in India was pioneered by which judge, with the first major case being Hussainara Khatoon (1979) concerning undertrial prisoners in Bihar?
questions.e: Justice P. N. Bhagwati pioneered PIL, relaxing locus standi so that public-spirited citizens could seek justice for the disadvantaged, beginning with Bihar's undertrial prisoners.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) is famous for establishing which doctrine?
questions.e: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, a 13-judge bench held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Minerva Mills case (1980) is significant for which ruling?
o: Right to property is a Fundamental Right
Balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles; limited amending power
questions.e: Minerva Mills struck down clauses of the 42nd Amendment and held that harmony between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is part of the basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article, and who was its first Chief Election Commissioner?
questions.e: Article 324 vests superintendence of elections in the Election Commission; Sukumar Sen conducted India's first two general elections (1951-52, 1957).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Union Public Service Commission is provided for in which Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 315 establishes the UPSC and State PSCs; the UPSC chairman and members are appointed by the President and can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed under which Article, and who was the first CAG?
questions.e: Article 148 provides for the CAG as the guardian of public finances; V. Narahari Rao was the first CAG (1948-54).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Attorney General of India is provided for in which Article, and what is the key qualification?
o: Article 76; qualified to be a Supreme Court judge
Article 76; qualified to be a High Court judge
questions.e: Article 76 creates the office of Attorney General, the government's chief legal adviser, who must be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992), which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, was based on the recommendations of which committee?
questions.e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended three-tier Panchayati Raj; Rajasthan's Nagaur became the first to implement it on 2 October 1959.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Urban local bodies received constitutional status through which amendment?
questions.e: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IXA with municipalities, Nagar Panchayats and Municipal Corporations, paralleling the 73rd Amendment for rural areas.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on which date?
questions.e: NITI Aayog was constituted on 1 January 2015 as a policy think tank with cooperative federalism, replacing the top-down Planning Commission.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced by the 101st Amendment and launched on 1 July 2017. Which Article deals with the GST Council?
questions.e: Article 279A creates the GST Council chaired by the Union Finance Minister, deciding tax rates and exemptions by weighted voting.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Information Act came into force in which year?
questions.e: The RTI Act (2005) empowers citizens to seek information from public authorities within 30 days, a landmark transparency law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Citizenship provisions are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.e: Part II (Articles 5-11) deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution; Parliament regulates later acquisition under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently lists how many official languages?
questions.e: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages; the last additions were Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali through the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Anti-Defection Law was inserted as the Tenth Schedule by which constitutional amendment?
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule disqualifying MPs/MLAs who defect, though splits and mergers have tested its effectiveness.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by which constitutional amendment?
questions.e: The 61st Amendment (1989) lowered the voting age to 18, enfranchising crores of young Indians.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under the 73rd Amendment, seats are reserved for women in Panchayats in what proportion?
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment mandates not less than one-third reservation for women in Panchayat seats and chairperson offices; many states like Bihar raised it to 50%.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Governor's power to promulgate ordinances when the legislature is not in session is given by which Article?
questions.e: Article 213 empowers the Governor to issue ordinances (Article 123 is the President's parallel power); they lapse six weeks after the legislature reassembles.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted under which Article, and who chairs the 16th Finance Commission?
questions.e: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission every five years; the 16th Commission under Arvind Panagariya recommends tax devolution for 2026-31.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Inter-State Council, meant to promote coordination between the Centre and states, is established under which Article?
questions.e: Article 263 allows the President to establish an Inter-State Council; it was actually set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which writ is issued by a court to a public authority to perform its legal duty?
questions.e: Mandamus ('we command') directs an authority to perform a mandatory duty; habeas corpus secures release from illegal detention, and certiorari quashes lower court orders.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's New Economic Policy of 1991, marking liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation, was launched under which Prime Minister and Finance Minister?
o: P. V. Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh
Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Yashwant Sinha
questions.e: Facing a balance-of-payments crisis, the Rao government with Finance Minister Manmohan Singh devalued the rupee, opened the economy and dismantled the licence raj in 1991.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on which economic model and gave priority to which sector?
questions.e: The First Plan used the Harrod-Domar model and prioritised agriculture, irrigation and power projects like Bhakra-Nangal, achieving growth above target.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Second Five Year Plan is associated with which economist's model emphasising heavy industry?
questions.e: P. C. Mahalanobis's model drove the Second Plan's focus on heavy industry and steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur with Soviet and German help.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under which legislation?
questions.e: The RBI was set up under the RBI Act, 1934, as a private shareholders' bank and nationalised in 1949; it began operations on 1 April 1935.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.e: C. D. Deshmukh became the first Indian RBI Governor in 1943; Osborne Smith was the first Governor overall (1935).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks took place in which year?
questions.e: Indira Gandhi's government nationalised 14 banks on 19 July 1969 to direct credit to agriculture and small industry; six more followed in 1980.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The State Bank of India was formed in 1955 from which earlier institution?
questions.e: The Imperial Bank (1921), itself a merger of the three presidency banks, was nationalised and renamed State Bank of India in 1955.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: NABARD, the apex bank for agriculture and rural development, was established in which year?
questions.e: NABARD was set up in 1982 on the Sivaraman Committee's recommendation, taking over RBI's agricultural credit functions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: SEBI was given statutory powers in which year?
questions.e: SEBI, set up in 1988, became a statutory regulator through the SEBI Act, 1992, after the Harshad Mehta scam exposed market manipulation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In India, inflation at the retail level is measured by the Consumer Price Index with which base year?
questions.e: The CPI (combined) uses 2012 as base year and is the RBI's anchor for inflation targeting; WPI uses 2011-12 as base.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: When the RBI increases the repo rate, which of the following is the likely intended effect?
o: Costlier loans, reduced money supply and lower inflation
questions.e: A higher repo rate makes RBI lending to banks costlier, transmitting into costlier loans, dampening demand and cooling inflation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) differs from the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in which key respect?
o: CRR is kept with RBI and earns no interest; SLR is kept with banks themselves in liquid assets
CRR earns interest, SLR does not
CRR applies only to foreign banks
questions.e: Banks park CRR funds with the RBI without interest, while SLR is maintained by banks themselves in cash, gold or approved securities.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Fiscal deficit is defined as which of the following?
o: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.e: Fiscal deficit measures the government's total borrowing need: total expenditure less total receipts other than borrowings.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The FRBM Act, which mandates fiscal discipline, was enacted in which year?
questions.e: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (2003) set deficit targets; the N. K. Singh committee later recommended a 3% fiscal deficit norm.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following taxes was subsumed under GST?
questions.e: GST absorbed central excise, service tax, state VAT, octroi and entry tax into one destination-based tax; income tax, customs and STT remain outside.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Demonetisation of Rs 500 and Rs 1000 notes was announced on which date?
questions.e: On 8 November 2016 the government demonetised high-value notes to curb black money and counterfeiting, pushing digital payments.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: UPI (Unified Payments Interface), which revolutionised digital payments, was launched by which organisation in 2016?
questions.e: The National Payments Corporation of India launched UPI in 2016, enabling instant bank-to-bank transfers that now handle billions of monthly transactions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, the national financial inclusion mission, was launched in which year?
questions.e: PMJDY (2014) opened crores of zero-balance bank accounts with RuPay cards and overdraft facilities, forming the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the MUDRA scheme, loans up to Rs 50,000 to micro entrepreneurs fall in which category?
questions.e: MUDRA's Shishu covers loans up to Rs 50,000, Kishore up to Rs 5 lakh, and Tarun up to Rs 10 lakh (later extended with Tarun Plus).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Make in India' initiative to boost manufacturing was launched in which year?
questions.e: Make in India (September 2014) aimed to raise manufacturing's GDP share and attract investment through 25 focus sectors.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's GDP is currently estimated using which base year series?
questions.e: The CSO's 2011-12 base series is the current GDP benchmark; a new base revision has been under discussion.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which sector employs the largest share of India's workforce?
questions.e: Agriculture still employs over 40% of workers though its GDP share is under 20%, reflecting disguised unemployment and the need for diversification.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Unemployment and employment data in India is now primarily released through which survey?
questions.e: The PLFS, launched in 2017 by the NSO, provides annual and quarterly employment-unemployment estimates, replacing the old five-year NSSO rounds.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Tendulkar Committee (2009) is associated with the estimation of which of the following?
questions.e: The Suresh Tendulkar Committee revised poverty estimation methodology, broadening it beyond calorie norms; the Rangarajan Committee later suggested higher poverty lines.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Bihar consistently records one of the lowest per-capita incomes among Indian states. Which structural feature best explains this?
o: High population density with overwhelming dependence on low-productivity agriculture
questions.e: Bihar's 1,106 persons per sq km density and 70%+ workforce in agriculture fragment landholdings and depress productivity, keeping per-capita income low despite fast GSDP growth.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Approximately what share of Bihar's workforce is engaged in agriculture and allied activities?
questions.e: More than 70% of Bihar's workers depend on agriculture, far above the national average, making monsoon and farm prices decisive for the state's economy.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is the principal rabi crop of Bihar?
questions.e: Wheat is Bihar's main rabi (winter) crop, sown after kharif paddy; the state's rice-wheat rotation dominates the Gangetic plain.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Bihar is India's largest producer of which of the following?
questions.e: Bihar leads India in litchi (Muzaffarpur belt) and makhana (Mithila wetlands), both GI-tagged specialities with export potential.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced the establishment of a Makhana Board in which state?
questions.e: The 2025-26 Budget announced a Makhana Board in Bihar to boost production, processing and marketing of fox nut, grown mostly in the Mithila region.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Bhagalpur's Katarni rice, known for its aroma, holds which distinction?
o: It is exported only to Europe
questions.e: Katarni rice of Bhagalpur district received a GI tag for its unique aroma and grain quality, alongside Jardalu mango and Shahi litchi.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Barauni fertiliser plant, revived under the HURL joint venture, produces mainly which fertiliser?
questions.e: Hindustan Urvarak and Rasayan's Barauni unit produces neem-coated urea, critical for Bihar's agriculture, alongside the IOCL refinery complex.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: JEEViKA, often cited as a model livelihoods programme, operates in which state?
questions.e: The Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (JEEViKA) organises rural women into self-help groups for credit and enterprises, covering lakhs of households.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Student Credit Card Yojana, launched in 2016, provides education loans up to what amount?
questions.e: Under the Mukhyamantri Nishchay Swayam Sahayata Bhatta Yojana's credit card component, students get loans up to Rs 4 lakh for higher education at low interest.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Blue Revolution' in India?
questions.e: The Blue Revolution refers to rapid growth in fish production through aquaculture; India is now among the world's top fish producers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (2016) provides crop insurance with a uniform premium of what rate for kharif crops?
questions.e: PMFBY charges farmers only 2% premium for kharif crops, 1.5% for rabi and 5% for horticultural crops, with the government subsidising the rest.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which institution publishes the Multidimensional Poverty Index for India at the national level?
questions.e: NITI Aayog releases India's national MPI based on the Alkire-Foster method, tracking deprivations in health, education and living standards across states.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax is described as a destination-based tax. What does this mean?
o: Tax is collected only at ports
Tax is shared equally by Centre and states
Tax is levied where goods are produced
Tax accrues to the state where goods/services are consumed
questions.e: Under destination-based GST, tax revenue goes to the consuming state through IGST settlement, unlike the earlier origin-based excise system.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which body decides GST rates and exemptions in India?
questions.e: The GST Council under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Finance Minister with state finance ministers as members, decides rates by weighted voting.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The term 'stagflation' refers to which economic condition?
o: Stagnant growth combined with high inflation
questions.e: Stagflation, the painful mix of stagnant output and rising prices seen in the 1970s oil shocks, defeats conventional monetary remedies.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Laffer Curve' in economics illustrates the relationship between which two variables?
questions.e: Arthur Laffer's curve suggests tax revenue rises with rates up to a point, beyond which higher rates discourage activity and reduce revenue.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax?
questions.e: Corporate tax and income tax are direct taxes levied on income; GST, customs and the old excise were indirect taxes on goods and services.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank are both located in which city?
questions.e: Both Bretton Woods institutions created in 1944 are headquartered in Washington D.C.; India is a founding member of each.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's foreign exchange reserves are managed by which institution?
questions.e: The RBI manages forex reserves under the RBI Act, deploying them to stabilise the rupee and meet external obligations.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The term 'devaluation' of currency means which of the following?
o: Official reduction in the currency's external value by the government/central bank
questions.e: Devaluation is a deliberate official lowering of a fixed or managed exchange rate, as India did in 1966 and 1991; market-driven falls are called depreciation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following schemes provides collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh to small street vendors?
questions.e: PM SVANidhi (2020) gives street vendors working-capital loans starting at Rs 10,000 with interest subsidy and digital cashback incentives.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: PM Vishwakarma scheme, launched in 2023, primarily benefits which group?
questions.e: PM Vishwakarma supports 18 traditional trades (carpenters, blacksmiths, potters and others) with training, toolkits, credit and marketing support.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'One Nation One Ration Card' scheme enables migrant workers to access subsidised foodgrains through which mechanism?
o: Aadhaar-seeded portability across fair price shops nationally
questions.e: ONORC lets NFSA beneficiaries lift their quota from any fair price shop in India using Aadhaar authentication, vital for Bihar's migrant workers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a Bihar industrial centre with its industry?
questions.e: Dalmianagar (Rohtas) was Bihar's cement hub under the Rohtas Industries group; Barauni refines oil, Bhagalpur weaves silk, and Muzaffarpur is known for litchi.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The SI unit of force is the newton. Which of the following is the SI unit of work and energy?
questions.e: Work and energy are measured in joules (force times distance); the watt measures power, the pascal measures pressure, and the volt measures electric potential.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately which of the following?
questions.e: Light travels at about 3 x 10^8 metres per second in vacuum, the universal speed limit confirmed by Einstein's relativity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, the gravitational force between two bodies varies with distance in which way?
o: Inversely proportional to the square of distance
questions.e: Gravitational force follows the inverse-square law: doubling the distance reduces the force to one-fourth, a principle underpinning planetary motion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Ohm's law states the relationship between voltage, current and resistance as which formula?
questions.e: Ohm's law (V = IR) says current through a conductor is directly proportional to voltage across it, provided temperature remains constant.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The filament of an electric bulb is made of tungsten because of which property?
o: Very high melting point and high resistance
questions.e: Tungsten melts at about 3,422°C, so the filament glows white-hot without melting; the bulb is filled with inert argon-nitrogen gas to slow evaporation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: An electric fuse wire is made of an alloy of lead and tin because it has which characteristic?
o: Low melting point and high resistance
questions.e: Fuse wire melts quickly when excess current flows, breaking the circuit and protecting appliances from damage due to overloading or short circuits.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A transformer works on the principle of which phenomenon?
questions.e: A transformer transfers electrical energy between coils through mutual induction in a changing magnetic field, stepping voltage up or down.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Ultrasonic waves used in SONAR and medical imaging have frequencies of what range?
questions.e: Ultrasound exceeds the 20 kHz upper limit of human hearing; SONAR uses it to detect submarines and map the ocean floor by echo timing.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The blue colour of the sky is explained by which phenomenon?
questions.e: Air molecules scatter shorter (blue) wavelengths far more than longer ones, so the sky appears blue; at sunrise and sunset, blue light is scattered away, leaving red.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A rainbow is formed due to which combination of optical phenomena in raindrops?
questions.e: Sunlight refracts into droplets, reflects internally and disperses into colours, forming the familiar arc when the sun is behind the observer.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles, and why?
o: Convex, gives wider field of view with erect diminished image
questions.e: Convex mirrors diverge light to show a wider area behind the vehicle, though with smaller images, warning 'objects are closer than they appear'.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A person with myopia (near-sightedness) needs spectacles with which type of lens?
questions.e: Myopia focuses distant images in front of the retina; a concave (diverging) lens pushes the focus back onto the retina.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Sound travels fastest in which medium?
questions.e: Sound needs a material medium and moves fastest in solids (about 5,000 m/s in steel), slower in liquids and slowest in gases; it cannot travel in vacuum.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Nuclear fission was first demonstrated by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann in 1938 with the theoretical explanation by which scientists?
questions.e: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium nuclei; Meitner and Frisch explained it as fission, opening the path to reactors and atomic energy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: India's first nuclear research reactor, Apsara, was commissioned in 1956 at which place?
questions.e: Apsara at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay, was Asia's first research reactor, built under Homi Bhabha's leadership.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The atomic number of an element is equal to which of the following?
questions.e: Atomic number counts protons, defining the element; mass number adds neutrons, and isotopes differ in neutron count.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which element is the most abundant in the Earth's crust?
questions.e: Oxygen makes up about 46.6% of the crust's weight, followed by silicon (27.7%) and aluminium (8.1%); in the universe, hydrogen dominates.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The pH of pure water at 25°C is 7. What is the approximate pH of human blood?
questions.e: Blood is slightly alkaline at pH 7.35-7.45, tightly regulated by buffers; deviations cause acidosis or alkalosis with serious health effects.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches the common name with its chemical formula?
questions.e: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na2CO3.10H2O), and bleaching powder is CaOCl2.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Diamond and graphite are both forms of carbon. What accounts for their vastly different properties?
o: Different crystal structures (arrangement of carbon atoms)
questions.e: Diamond's tetrahedral lattice makes it the hardest natural material, while graphite's layered hexagonal sheets slide easily, making it a lubricant and pencil lead.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) used as domestic cooking fuel consists mainly of which gases?
questions.e: LPG is mostly propane and butane, odourised with ethyl mercaptan for leak detection; CNG is mainly methane and biogas is methane plus carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Rusting of iron is prevented by galvanisation, which coats iron with which metal?
questions.e: Zinc coating protects iron sacrificially: zinc corrodes preferentially, and its oxide layer seals the surface, preventing rust (hydrated iron oxide).

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Acid rain is primarily caused by the emission of which gases?
questions.e: SO2 and NOx from fossil-fuel burning form sulphuric and nitric acids in rain, damaging buildings, forests and aquatic life.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, is located in which atmospheric layer?
questions.e: The ozone layer sits 15-35 km up in the stratosphere; CFCs depleted it, prompting the 1987 Montreal Protocol that is healing the ozone hole.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Mendeleev's periodic table, published in 1869, arranged elements primarily in order of which property?
questions.e: Mendeleev ordered elements by atomic mass and grouped chemically similar ones, leaving gaps to predict undiscovered elements like gallium and germanium.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.e: Nitrogen (78%) dominates air, followed by oxygen (21%) and argon (0.93%); carbon dioxide is only about 0.04% but drives the greenhouse effect.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Hard water contains dissolved salts of which elements?
questions.e: Calcium and magnesium bicarbonates, chlorides and sulphates make water hard, preventing soap lather and scaling kettles; boiling removes temporary hardness.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: In the electrolysis of water, hydrogen and oxygen are liberated at the electrodes in which volume ratio?
questions.e: Water (H2O) yields twice the volume of hydrogen as oxygen, confirming its molecular formula through simple electrolysis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Dry ice, used for refrigeration and stage effects, is the solid form of which compound?
questions.e: Solid CO2 sublimates directly to gas at -78.5°C without melting, making dry ice ideal for cold transport without liquid residue.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.e: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration; plant cells additionally use chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The double-helix structure of DNA was proposed in 1953 by which scientists?
questions.e: James Watson and Francis Crick, building on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, described DNA's double helix with complementary base pairing.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system. Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.e: O negative red cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be transfused to anyone in emergencies; AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the average lifespan of human red blood cells?
questions.e: RBCs circulate about 120 days before being recycled by the spleen; they are produced continuously in the red bone marrow.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is the largest and strongest bone in the human body, and which is the smallest?
questions.e: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone, while the stapes of the middle ear is the smallest at about 3 mm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Insulin, the hormone regulating blood sugar, is secreted by which organ's beta cells?
questions.e: Pancreatic beta cells in the islets of Langerhans secrete insulin; its deficiency or resistance causes diabetes mellitus.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Goitre, the enlargement of the thyroid gland, is caused by the deficiency of which element?
questions.e: Iodine is essential for thyroid hormones; its deficiency enlarges the thyroid, which is why iodised salt is promoted nationally.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches the vitamin with its deficiency disease?
questions.e: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, and B1 deficiency causes beriberi.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The overall equation for photosynthesis is 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. The oxygen released comes from which raw material?
questions.e: Isotope experiments showed the released oxygen comes from water, not carbon dioxide; chlorophyll merely captures light energy in chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: In plants, water and minerals are transported upward through which tissue, and food through which?
questions.e: Xylem vessels carry water and minerals from roots to leaves, while phloem translocates sugars from leaves to growing parts.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The human heart has four chambers. Which blood vessel is the largest artery in the body?
questions.e: The aorta, arising from the left ventricle, is the body's largest artery, distributing oxygenated blood through systemic circulation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is called what?
questions.e: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter blood, reabsorb essentials and form urine; the glomerulus is just the filtering tuft within a nephron.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for balance and coordination?
questions.e: The cerebellum fine-tunes movement and balance; the cerebrum handles thought, the medulla controls involuntary functions, and the hypothalamus regulates homeostasis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Edward Jenner is famous for developing the world's first vaccine against which disease in 1796?
questions.e: Jenner used cowpox material to immunise against smallpox; global vaccination eradicated the disease, declared in 1980.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in which year?
questions.e: Fleming noticed Penicillium mould killing bacteria in 1928; Florey and Chain later purified it, saving millions in World War II.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by which mosquito?
questions.e: Only female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria when taking blood meals; Aedes spreads dengue and chikungunya, Culex spreads filariasis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which of the following is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.e: Skin, weighing several kilograms, is the largest organ, protecting against pathogens, regulating temperature and sensing touch; the liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Quinine, the traditional anti-malarial drug, is obtained from the bark of which tree?
questions.e: Cinchona bark from the Andes yields quinine; its synthetic derivatives like chloroquine dominated malaria treatment for decades.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: BCG vaccine, given at birth under India's immunisation programme, protects against which disease?
questions.e: The Bacillus Calmette-Guerin vaccine guards infants against severe forms of tuberculosis like TB meningitis.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The first UN Conference on the Human Environment was held at Stockholm in 1972. Which day is observed as World Environment Day in its commemoration?
questions.e: World Environment Day is observed on 5 June, the opening day of the 1972 Stockholm Conference that created the UN Environment Programme.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 1992 Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro produced which of the following outcomes?
o: Agenda 21, UNFCCC and Convention on Biological Diversity
questions.e: The Rio Earth Summit adopted Agenda 21, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Biodiversity Convention, shaping modern environmental governance.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) differed from the Paris Agreement (2015) in which key respect?
o: Kyoto set legally binding emission targets only for developed countries; Paris requires pledges from all
Kyoto dealt with ozone, Paris with climate
Kyoto was voluntary, Paris is binding
questions.e: Kyoto imposed binding cuts on developed nations alone, while Paris has all countries submit Nationally Determined Contributions to keep warming well below 2°C.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: At COP26 in Glasgow (2021), India announced its net-zero target for which year?
questions.e: India pledged net-zero emissions by 2070 along with 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, balancing development needs with climate action.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Tiger was launched in 1973. Which was the first tiger reserve brought under it?
questions.e: Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand became India's first tiger reserve in 1973; the programme now covers over 50 reserves.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Elephant, launched in 1992, aims to protect elephants and their corridors. Which state has the highest elephant population?
questions.e: Karnataka holds India's largest elephant population, concentrated in the Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats landscape spanning three states.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches India's national symbols?
o: Animal: elephant, Flower: rose, River: Yamuna
Animal: tiger, Bird: sparrow, Tree: neem
Animal: lion, Bird: peacock, Tree: banyan
Animal: Bengal tiger, Bird: Indian peacock, Aquatic animal: Ganges river dolphin
questions.e: India's national animal is the Bengal tiger, national bird the Indian peacock, national aquatic animal the Ganges river dolphin, national tree the banyan and national flower the lotus.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is most famous for which animal?
questions.e: Kaziranga holds two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses and is a UNESCO World Heritage site on the Brahmaputra floodplain.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which was the first biosphere reserve established in India in 1986?
questions.e: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was India's first under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's first two Ramsar sites, designated in 1981, were which of the following?
o: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.e: Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo (Rajasthan) became India's first Ramsar wetlands in 1981; India now has more than 80 Ramsar sites, the most in Asia.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in which year?
questions.e: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, created schedules of protected species, national parks and sanctuaries, and was amended in 2022 to align with CITES.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, was enacted in the wake of which disaster?
questions.e: The Bhopal gas leak of December 1984, which killed thousands, prompted the umbrella Environment (Protection) Act empowering the Centre to regulate pollution.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The National Green Tribunal was established in which year under the NGT Act?
questions.e: The NGT (2010) is a specialised judicial body for speedy disposal of environmental cases, applying the polluter-pays and precautionary principles.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Chipko movement of 1973, in which villagers hugged trees to prevent felling, began in which present-day state?
questions.e: Chipko began at Mandal village in Chamoli (then UP, now Uttarakhand) under leaders like Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Silent Valley National Park, saved from a hydroelectric project by a famous campaign, is located in which state?
questions.e: Silent Valley in Kerala's Palakkad district preserves pristine tropical rainforest with the endangered lion-tailed macaque.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following regions is recognised as a biodiversity hotspot in India?
questions.e: The Western Ghats and the Himalaya are India's two globally recognised biodiversity hotspots, rich in endemic species.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird, is the state bird of which state?
questions.e: The Great Indian Bustard survives mainly in Rajasthan's Desert National Park; habitat loss and power lines have pushed it to the brink.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Olive Ridley turtles are famous for mass nesting (arribada) at which Odisha beach?
questions.e: Gahirmatha hosts the world's largest arribada of Olive Ridleys; Odisha's seven-month fishing ban (November-May) protects them.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India banned identified single-use plastic items with effect from which date?
questions.e: From 1 July 2022 India banned items like plastic cutlery, straws, stirrers and thin carry bags under the Plastic Waste Management Rules.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Green India Mission is one of the eight missions under which national plan?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)
questions.e: The NAPCC (2008) has eight missions including Solar, Green India, Water and Sustainable Habitat missions to combat climate change.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed on which date?
questions.e: Ozone Day on 16 September marks the 1987 Montreal Protocol signing; the protocol is the most successful environmental treaty, healing the ozone hole.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Biological Diversity Act, which set up the National Biodiversity Authority, was passed in which year?
questions.e: The Biological Diversity Act (2002) implements the Convention on Biological Diversity, regulating access to genetic resources and benefit-sharing.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Red Data Book, which lists threatened species, is published by which organisation?
questions.e: The IUCN Red List categorises species from Least Concern to Extinct, guiding global conservation priorities.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, holds which distinction?
questions.e: Hailey National Park (1936), renamed after hunter-conservationist Jim Corbett, was India's first national park and later its first tiger reserve.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Asiatic lion's only wild population survives in which protected area?
questions.e: Gir in Gujarat holds the world's only wild Asiatic lions (around 700), recovered from barely a dozen a century ago.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Hemis National Park, India's largest national park, is famous for which animal and located in which UT?
questions.e: Hemis in Ladakh is India's largest national park and the best place to spot the elusive snow leopard in winter.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park, protects which endangered deer?
questions.e: Keibul Lamjao on Loktak Lake's phumdis is the last refuge of the sangai, Manipur's state animal.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: E-waste in India is regulated under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, which introduced which responsibility on producers?
questions.e: EPR makes electronics producers responsible for collecting and recycling end-of-life products, curbing hazardous informal dismantling.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Nagarhole and Bandipur reserves, famous for tigers and elephants, are located in which state?
questions.e: Bandipur and Nagarhole in Karnataka form part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, among India's richest tiger-elephant landscapes.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following greenhouse gases has the highest global warming potential per molecule?
questions.e: Sulphur hexafluoride, used in electrical switchgear, has a warming potential tens of thousands of times that of CO2, though emitted in tiny quantities.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.e: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10 (increasing by 2), so the next difference is 12, giving 30 + 12 = 42. Equivalently, each term is n(n+1).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Find the next number in the Fibonacci-like series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
questions.e: Each term is the sum of the previous two (5 + 8 = 13), the classic Fibonacci pattern.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 190
questions.e: 121 (11²), 144 (12²) and 169 (13²) are perfect squares, while 190 is not.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and so on, what is the sum of the letter values in the word CAT?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A person facing north turns 90 degrees to his right, then 90 degrees to his right again. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.e: First right turn faces east, second right turn faces south.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to Ravi?
questions.e: The grandfather's only son is Ravi's father, so the father's daughter is Ravi's sister.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
