questions.q: A father's age is three times his son's age. The sum of their ages is 48. How old is the son?
questions.e: If the son is x, then 3x + x = 48, so x = 12; the father is 36.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What is 20% of 350?
questions.e: 20% is one-fifth, and 350 / 5 = 70.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.e: The sum 1 to 10 is 55, and 55 / 10 = 5.5; for consecutive numbers the average is (first + last) / 2.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, what is A:B:C?
questions.e: Make B common: A:B = 8:12 and B:C = 12:15, so A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A train covers 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.e: Speed = distance / time = 120 / 2 = 60 km/h.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What is the simple interest on Rs 10,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: At 3:00, what is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock?
questions.e: At 3:00 the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 3, exactly one-quarter of the dial, or 90 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Complete the analogy: Book : Pages :: Wall : ?
questions.e: A book is made of pages as a wall is made of bricks; the relationship is whole to its constituent units.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A can complete a work in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 of the work per day, so together they take 6 days.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What is the probability of getting an even number when a fair die is rolled once?
questions.e: Three of the six faces (2, 4, 6) are even, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Find the next number: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ?
questions.e: Differences are 3, 5, 7, 9 (odd numbers), so the next difference is 11, giving 27 + 11 = 38.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: In a row of students, Anil is 7th from the left and 9th from the right. How many students are in the row?
questions.e: Total = position from left + position from right - 1 = 7 + 9 - 1 = 15.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If 5 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take at the same rate?
questions.e: Total work = 5 × 12 = 60 worker-days; 60 / 6 = 10 days.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Which year is a leap year?
questions.e: A year is a leap year if divisible by 4, except century years which must be divisible by 400; 2000 qualifies, 1900 and 2100 do not.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India held the presidency of the G20 in which year, with the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'?
questions.e: India's G20 presidency in 2023 culminated in the New Delhi Leaders' Summit, where the African Union was admitted as a permanent G20 member.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which country held the G20 presidency in 2025, hosting the summit at Johannesburg?
questions.e: South Africa presided over the G20 in 2025, the first African presidency, hosting the leaders' summit at Johannesburg.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: COP29, the UN climate conference of 2024, was held in which city?
questions.e: COP29 met at Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024, agreeing a new climate finance goal; COP28 was at Dubai and COP30 at Belem, Brazil.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: At the Paris Olympics 2024, how many medals did India win in total?
questions.e: India won six medals at Paris 2024: one silver (Neeraj Chopra, javelin) and five bronze, including Manu Bhaker's two shooting bronzes.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India won the ICC T20 World Cup in 2024 by defeating which team in the final at Barbados?
questions.e: India beat South Africa by 7 runs in a thrilling final on 29 June 2024, ending an 11-year ICC title drought.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 by defeating New Zealand in the final held at which city?
questions.e: India defeated New Zealand by 4 wickets in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025, with Rohit Sharma's team remaining unbeaten through the tournament.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to soft-land near the Moon's south pole on which date?
questions.e: Vikram lander touched down on 23 August 2023 at the site named Shiv Shakti Point, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory mission, was placed in its halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1 in which month?
questions.e: Launched in September 2023, Aditya-L1 reached the Sun-Earth L1 point in January 2024 to study the solar corona and space weather.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The new Parliament building of India was inaugurated on which date?
questions.e: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the new triangular Parliament building on 28 May 2023 as part of the Central Vista redevelopment.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Act), 2023, provides what share of reservation for women in legislatures?
questions.e: The 106th Constitutional Amendment reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, effective after delimitation.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The three new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA) replacing the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act came into force on which date?
questions.e: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam took effect on 1 July 2024, modernising colonial-era codes.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The consecration (pran pratishtha) ceremony of the Ram Mandir at Ayodhya was held on which date?
questions.e: The Ram Lalla idol was consecrated at the Ayodhya temple on 22 January 2024, following the Supreme Court's 2019 verdict and the 2020 bhoomi pujan.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The international airport at Ayodhya is named after which sage?
questions.e: Ayodhya's airport is the Maharishi Valmiki International Airport, honouring the sage traditionally regarded as the author of the Ramayana.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue at 182 metres, depicts which leader and stands in which state?
questions.e: The 182-metre Statue of Unity honouring Sardar Patel stands on the Narmada at Kevadia, Gujarat, inaugurated in October 2018.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, connecting the temple to the Ganga ghats, was inaugurated in which year?
questions.e: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor in December 2021, easing pilgrim access in Varanasi.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Mahakumbh Mela of 2025 was held at which city?
questions.e: The Purna Mahakumbh of 2025 at Prayagraj's Triveni Sangam drew crores of pilgrims over January-February 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 18th Lok Sabha general elections were held in 2024. Which alliance formed the government with Narendra Modi as Prime Minister for a third term?
questions.e: The BJP-led NDA won the 2024 elections and Modi was sworn in for a third consecutive term in June 2024, though the BJP fell short of a solo majority.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India became the world's most populous country in 2023 according to which organisation's estimates?
questions.e: UN population data showed India overtaking China as the most populous country in April 2023, with over 1.42 billion people.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, governing personal data in India, was passed in which year?
questions.e: The DPDP Act (2023) establishes consent-based data processing, data principal rights and a Data Protection Board, following the Puttaswamy privacy verdict.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Education Policy 2020 replaced the 10+2 school structure with which new design?
questions.e: NEP 2020 introduced the 5+3+3+4 structure (foundational, preparatory, middle, secondary stages) with emphasis on mother-tongue instruction and multidisciplinary learning.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Operation Sindoor, launched by India in May 2025, was a military response to which event?
questions.e: After the 22 April 2025 terror attack at Baisaran Valley, Pahalgam, India launched precision strikes on terror infrastructure across the border in May 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2024 was awarded to which organisation?
questions.e: Nihon Hidankyo, the Japanese organisation of atomic bomb survivors, won the 2024 Peace Prize for its efforts towards a world free of nuclear weapons.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for work related to which field?
o: Machine learning with artificial neural networks
questions.e: Hopfield and Hinton were honoured for foundational discoveries enabling modern machine learning through artificial neural networks.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Han Kang won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature. From which country is she?
questions.e: South Korean author Han Kang, known for 'The Vegetarian', became the first Asian woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In January 2024, the Bharat Ratna was announced for Karpoori Thakur. He is remembered as a champion of which cause and belonged to which state?
o: Social justice and backward-class empowerment; Bihar
questions.e: Karpoori Thakur, twice Bihar's Chief Minister, pioneered reservations for backward classes; he received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 along with Advani, Narasimha Rao, Charan Singh and M. S. Swaminathan.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The BRICS summit of 2024 was hosted by Russia in which city, and which countries had joined BRICS in January 2024?
o: Kazan; Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE
questions.e: The 2024 BRICS summit at Kazan followed the January 2024 expansion admitting Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE; Indonesia joined as a full member in 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit of 2025 was hosted by which country in Tianjin?
questions.e: China hosted the 2025 SCO summit at Tianjin; India and Pakistan have been full SCO members since 2017.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The QUAD grouping consists of which four countries?
questions.e: The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue brings together India, the United States, Japan and Australia for Indo-Pacific cooperation.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's first bullet train project connects which two cities using Japanese Shinkansen technology?
questions.e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail, funded largely by a Japanese loan, is under construction with trial runs progressing on completed sections.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chenab Bridge, the world's highest railway bridge, was inaugurated in June 2025 in which region?
questions.e: The 359-metre-high Chenab arch bridge in Reasi district, J&K, completed the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla rail link.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Atal Tunnel at Rohtang, inaugurated in 2020, has what length and connects which two valleys?
questions.e: The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel under the Rohtang Pass gives all-weather connectivity between Kullu and the Lahaul-Spiti valley.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who took over as Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in December 2024, succeeding Shaktikanta Das?
questions.e: Sanjay Malhotra, former Revenue Secretary, became the 26th RBI Governor in December 2024 for a three-year term.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who took charge as Chairman of ISRO in January 2025, succeeding S. Somanath?
questions.e: V. Narayanan, a cryogenics expert who led the LVM3 programme, became ISRO Chairman in January 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission, whose recommendations cover 2026-31, is chaired by whom?
questions.e: Arvind Panagariya, former NITI Aayog vice-chairman, chairs the 16th Finance Commission on Centre-state tax devolution.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The PM Vishwakarma scheme, launched in September 2023, supports which group?
o: Traditional artisans and craftspeople in 18 trades
questions.e: PM Vishwakarma gives Vishwakarmas (carpenters, masons, potters, tailors and others) training, toolkits, collateral-free loans and marketing support.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was expanded in 2024 to cover which additional category regardless of income?
o: All senior citizens aged 70 and above
questions.e: In 2024 PM-JAY was extended to all Indians aged 70+, giving them Rs 5 lakh annual health cover irrespective of income.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 'One Nation One Election' proposal was examined by a committee chaired by whom, which submitted its report in 2024?
questions.e: The high-level committee under former President Ram Nath Kovind recommended simultaneous Lok Sabha and assembly elections; related bills were introduced in December 2024.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, passed in April 2025, primarily seeks to do what?
o: Reform waqf property management with transparency and representation
questions.e: The 2025 amendments renamed the law and reformed waqf boards' composition and property management, generating major political debate.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, replaced which colonial-era laws?
o: The Foreigners Act 1946, Passport Act 1920 and two other pre-independence laws
questions.e: The 2025 Act consolidated the Passport (Entry into India) Act 1920, Registration of Foreigners Act 1939, Foreigners Act 1946 and Immigration (Carriers' Liability) Act 2000.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which alliance won the Bihar Assembly elections held in November 2025?
questions.e: The BJP-JD(U)-led NDA won a decisive majority in the November 2025 Bihar elections, returning Nitish Kumar as Chief Minister.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Bihar hosted the Khelo India Youth Games in 2025. In which month were they held, with Patna as the main venue?
questions.e: Bihar hosted the seventh Khelo India Youth Games in May 2025 across Patna, Nalanda, Gaya and other cities, its biggest multi-sport event.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Z-Morh tunnel, inaugurated in January 2025, provides all-weather connectivity to which tourist destination?
questions.e: The 6.5-km Z-Morh tunnel on the Srinagar-Leh highway keeps Sonamarg accessible through winter, ahead of the larger Zojila tunnel project.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's National Quantum Mission, approved in 2023, aims to develop quantum computers of what capacity within eight years?
questions.e: The Rs 6,000-crore National Quantum Mission targets 50-1000 physical-qubit quantum computers alongside quantum communication and sensing.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023, targets annual green hydrogen production of how much by 2030?
questions.e: India aims to produce 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen yearly by 2030, cutting fossil imports and building electrolyser capacity.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which Indian city hosted the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention in January 2025?
questions.e: The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas was held at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in January 2025, celebrating the diaspora's contributions.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative, aiming to make three crore women lakhpatis, is implemented through which programme?
o: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
questions.e: Lakhpati Didi works through DAY-NRLM self-help groups, skilling rural women for enterprises earning at least Rs 1 lakh annually.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's first Constitution Museum was inaugurated in 2024 at which university?
questions.e: O.P. Jindal Global University at Sonipat opened India's first Constitution Museum in November 2024, tracing the making of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for work on which of the following? (2025 prizes announced October 2025)
questions.e: The 2025 Chemistry Nobel went to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for developing metal-organic frameworks with wide applications.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which Indian state became the first to implement the Uniform Civil Code in 2024, with rules notified in January 2025?
questions.e: Uttarakhand's UCC Act (2024) took effect with rules in January 2025, standardising marriage, divorce, inheritance and live-in relationship registration.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 38th National Games of India were hosted in 2025 by which state?
questions.e: Uttarakhand hosted the 38th National Games in January-February 2025, with the mascot Mauli (monal bird).

questions.subject: Ancient Indian History
questions.q: The Dhamekh Stupa at Sarnath, marking the Buddha's first sermon site, was substantially rebuilt during the reign of which dynasty?
questions.e: The massive Dhamekh Stupa at Sarnath dates in its present form to the Gupta period (5th-6th century CE), though the site has Mauryan origins.

questions.subject: Modern Indian History
questions.q: The Rowlatt Act of 1919, which sparked nationwide protest, allowed the British government to do what?
o: Detain suspects without trial for up to two years
questions.e: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act (Rowlatt Act) permitted detention without trial, triggering Gandhi's first all-India satyagraha and the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which Bihar city is known as the 'Manchester of Bihar' for its historic textile and handloom industry?
questions.e: Bhagalpur's centuries-old silk handloom industry earned it the nickname 'Manchester of Bihar', with its tussar fabrics prized across India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Palghat Gap in the Western Ghats connects Kerala with which neighbouring state?
questions.e: The 30-km-wide Palghat Gap is the major break in the Western Ghats, linking Kerala's Malabar coast with Tamil Nadu's Coimbatore region.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to amend the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 368 lays down the amendment procedure; the 24th Amendment affirmed Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights, later limited by the basic structure doctrine.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The doctrine of 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 is borrowed from which country's constitution?
questions.e: Unlike America's 'due process', India's Constitution adopted Japan's 'procedure established by law', though the Supreme Court in Maneka Gandhi (1978) read fairness into it.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The headquarters of NABARD is located in which city?
questions.e: NABARD, the apex refinancing institution for agriculture and rural development, is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Kharif crop?
questions.e: Wheat is the principal rabi (winter) crop; rice, cotton, maize, jowar and groundnut are kharif (monsoon) crops.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin with the help of sunlight?
questions.e: Ultraviolet B rays convert cholesterol in skin to vitamin D3, essential for calcium absorption and bone health.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The unit of electrical resistance is the ohm. Which of the following is the unit of electrical capacitance?
questions.e: Capacitance is measured in farads; the henry measures inductance, the tesla magnetic flux density, and the weber magnetic flux.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Pataliputra, the celebrated capital of Magadha, was founded by which ruler?
questions.e: Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, founded the city of Pataliputra (near modern Patna) as the new Magadhan capital; it later became the imperial seat of the Mauryas and Guptas.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Which was the first capital of the Magadha mahajanapada?
questions.e: Rajagriha (modern Rajgir), ringed by five hills, was the earliest capital of Magadha under the Haryanka dynasty before the seat shifted to Pataliputra.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Bimbisara, the Magadhan king, is referred to by which epithet in Jain texts?
questions.e: Jain tradition calls Bimbisara 'Seniya'; he was the first historical Magadhan king and a patron of both Mahavira and the Buddha.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, was born at which place in present-day Bihar?
questions.e: Mahavira was born around 540 BCE at Kundagrama near Vaishali in the Vrijji confederacy; he attained nirvana at Pavapuri in present-day Nalanda district.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali in 383 BCE during the reign of which ruler?
questions.e: The Second Buddhist Council met at Vaishali about a century after the Buddha's death, in the reign of the Shishunaga king Kalashoka, to settle monastic disputes.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Third Buddhist Council was convened at Pataliputra under Ashoka and presided over by whom?
questions.e: Ashoka's Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra (c. 250 BCE) was presided over by the monk Moggaliputta Tissa, after which missions were sent to nine regions including Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Megasthenes, author of 'Indica', visited India as the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator to the court of which emperor at Pataliputra?
questions.e: Megasthenes stayed at Pataliputra as Seleucus Nicator's envoy to Chandragupta Maurya after the treaty of 305 BCE; his 'Indica' is a key source on Mauryan administration.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Nalanda Mahavihara was founded during the reign of which Gupta emperor?
questions.e: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE under Kumaragupta I (Mahendraditya); it grew into the world's greatest Buddhist university under Harsha and the Palas.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Vikramashila Mahavihara, the great Pala-era university, was established by which ruler?
questions.e: Dharmapala, the greatest Pala emperor, founded Vikramashila in the late 8th century CE; its scholar Atisha carried Buddhism to Tibet.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Pala dynasty of Bengal and Bihar was founded by Gopala, who was chosen king in about 750 CE by what unusual method?
questions.e: After a century of anarchy (matsya-nyaya), the leading men of the region elected Gopala as king around 750 CE — a rare elective kingship in Indian history.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Sher Shah Suri's land-revenue system, under which fields were measured with a rope and the state's share was fixed at one-third of the produce, was known as what?
questions.e: Sher Shah's zabt system measured cultivated land with the jarib (rope) and fixed the state's share at one-third of average produce, recorded through the patta and qabuliyat; it later became the model for Akbar's revenue administration.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Which revenue arrangement did Sher Shah Suri introduce, requiring the peasant to sign a deed of agreement for land revenue?
questions.e: Sher Shah measured land and fixed revenue through the zabt system; the state issued a patta (title deed) and the peasant signed a qabuliyat (agreement), curbing middlemen.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Lichchhavi republic, praised by the Buddha as a model confederacy, had its capital at which city?
questions.e: Vaishali was the capital of the Lichchhavi-led Vrijji confederacy, one of the world's earliest republican states; the Buddha admired its seven principles of non-decline.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda during the reign of which emperor?
questions.e: The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang spent years at Nalanda in the 630s–640s CE during Harshavardhana's reign, leaving a detailed account of the university's 10,000 students.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Karnata dynasty ruled Mithila (Tirhut) from Simraon; its last great king Harisimhadeva was defeated in 1324 by which Delhi Sultan's general?
questions.e: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's forces ended Karnata rule in Mithila in 1324; Harisimhadeva fled to Nepal, carrying the Mithila scholarly tradition to the Kathmandu valley.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Bakhtiyar Khilji destroyed the great monasteries of Nalanda, Odantapuri and Vikramashila around which year?
questions.e: Bakhtiyar Khilji's raids around 1193 CE destroyed Nalanda, Odantapuri and Vikramashila, ending Bihar's era as the heartland of Buddhist learning.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Odantapuri Mahavihara, one of the five great Pala monasteries, was founded by which Pala king?
questions.e: Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, established Odantapuri near modern Bihar Sharif in the 8th century CE.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Kautilya's Arthashastra, the classic treatise on statecraft, is traditionally associated with the minister of which Magadhan emperor?
questions.e: Tradition identifies Kautilya (Chanakya/Vishnugupta), author of the Arthashastra, as the chief minister who guided Chandragupta Maurya's rise at Pataliputra.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Ajatashatru fortified the village of Pataligrama (later Pataliputra) chiefly against which republican confederacy?
questions.e: Ajatashatru built the fort at Pataligrama to guard against the Vrijji-Lichchhavi confederacy of Vaishali, whom he eventually subdued through diplomacy and war.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Mahapadma Nanda, called 'the first historical emperor of India' and 'destroyer of Kshatriyas', belonged to which dynasty that ruled Magadha before the Mauryas?
questions.e: Mahapadma Nanda founded Nanda power in Magadha in the 4th century BCE; the Nanda empire's vast army deterred Alexander's troops from advancing beyond the Beas.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Battle of Buxar (1764), fought on Bihar's soil, gave the East India Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa through which treaty?
questions.e: After Hector Munro's victory at Buxar in October 1764, the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) granted the Company the Diwani — the real beginning of British territorial rule in India.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: During the 1857 revolt, the sepoys who mutinied at Danapur on 25 July 1857 marched to join Kunwar Singh at which place?
questions.e: The Danapur mutineers joined Kunwar Singh's forces and together they besieged Arrah, inflicting a famous defeat on Captain Dunbar's relief force.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Gandhi's protest against which exploitative practice?
questions.e: In Champaran, European planters forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th (tinkathia) of their land; Raj Kumar Shukla persuaded Gandhi to take up the cause in 1917.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Bihar was separated from Bengal Presidency and made a province in which year?
questions.e: On 22 March 1912 Bihar and Orissa were carved out of Bengal as a separate province; Bihar Diwas is celebrated on 22 March every year.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: During the Quit India Movement, the Patna Secretariat firing of 11 August 1942 killed seven young protesters; their memorial stands at which place in Patna?
questions.e: Seven students, including 14-year-old Umakant Prasad Sinha, were shot while hoisting the flag at the Patna Secretariat; the Shaheed Smarak (martyrs' memorial) honours them.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the Constituent Assembly in which year?
questions.e: Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946 and later became India's first President in 1950.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Jayaprakash Narayan, who led the 'Total Revolution' and the Bihar Movement of 1974, was born at which village?
questions.e: JP was born in 1902 at Sitabdiara (Saran district, on the UP–Bihar border); his 1974 call for Sampoorna Kranti galvanised the movement that led to the Emergency.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Karpoori Thakur, honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 2024, is remembered as the champion of which cause in Bihar?
questions.e: Karpoori Thakur, twice Chief Minister and called 'Jannayak', implemented pioneering reservations for backward classes in Bihar government jobs in the 1970s.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Sri Krishna Sinha, the first Chief Minister of Bihar, is popularly known by which title?
questions.e: Dr Sri Krishna Sinha, Bihar's first Chief Minister (1946–1961), earned the title 'Bihar Kesari' (Lion of Bihar) for his leadership in the freedom movement and early statehood.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Patna was renamed 'Azimabad' in the early 18th century by which Mughal prince?
questions.e: Prince Azim-ush-Shan, grandson of Aurangzeb and governor of Bengal, renamed Patna as Azimabad in 1704; the name persisted into the early British period.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The ancient port-town of Champa, capital of the Anga mahajanapada, is located near which modern Bihar city?
questions.e: Champa, near modern Bhagalpur, was the capital of Anga — one of the sixteen mahajanapadas — before Bimbisara annexed Anga into Magadha.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Santhal Rebellion of 1855–56, led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, broke out in the region that today lies mostly in which state?
questions.e: The Santhal hul erupted in the Daman-i-koh (Rajmahal hills) region, then part of Bihar's Bhagalpur division and now in Jharkhand; it prompted the creation of Santhal Pargana.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Which Bihar-born socialist leader broke out of Hazaribagh Central Jail in 1942 to join the Quit India underground?
questions.e: JP escaped from Hazaribagh jail on 9 November 1942 with five comrades and directed underground resistance, becoming a legend of the Quit India movement.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936; the peasant movement he led was centred in which region?
questions.e: Sahajanand built the kisan movement in Bihar's Shahabad region against zamindari oppression and founded the All India Kisan Sabha at Lucknow in 1936.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The new Nalanda University campus at Rajgir was inaugurated in June 2024 by the Prime Minister; the ancient university it revives was destroyed in which century?
questions.e: Nalanda was destroyed around 1193 CE (12th century) by Bakhtiyar Khilji's raids; the modern international university at Rajgir began full academic operations from the new campus in 2024.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Which of these Bihar crafts holds a Geographical Indication tag: Madhubani (Mithila) painting, Sikki grass work, Bhagalpuri silk, or all of them?
o: Madhubani painting and Sikki grass work only
questions.e: Madhubani/Mithila painting, Sikki grass craft and Bhagalpuri silk all carry GI tags, along with Sujini embroidery, Mithila makhana and Shahi litchi of Muzaffarpur.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: Bihar's second official language, alongside Hindi in Devanagari script, is which language?
questions.e: Urdu is Bihar's second official language; Maithili, written in Devanagari (and traditionally Tirhuta/Mithilakshar), is in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Vikramshila Setu connects Bhagalpur across the Ganga; the ancient Vikramashila university whose name it bears was located near which modern town?
questions.e: Vikramashila's ruins lie at Antichak near Kahalgaon in Bhagalpur district, on the Ganga's bank; the Vikramshila Setu bridge spans the river nearby.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: In which year did Orissa separate from Bihar to become its own province?
questions.e: Bihar and Orissa were split in 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935, giving Bihar its present territorial core; Bihar Day marks the 1912 separation from Bengal.

questions.subject: Bihar History
questions.q: The Mundeshwari Devi Temple in Kaimur district, among the oldest functional temples in India, is dedicated to which deities?
questions.e: Mundeshwari temple atop the Kaimur hills, dated to around the 4th–5th century CE, enshrines Shiva and Shakti and is regarded as one of India's oldest living temples.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: What is the strength of the Bihar Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council respectively?
questions.e: Bihar's Vidhan Sabha has 243 elected members and the Vidhan Parishad has 75 members, making Bihar one of the six states with a bicameral legislature.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The Patna High Court, one of India's oldest high courts, was established in which year?
questions.e: The Patna High Court was established in 1916 and began functioning in 1916, exercising jurisdiction over Bihar (and earlier over Orissa too).

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Bihar became the first Indian state to provide 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions through which legislation?
questions.e: The Bihar Panchayat Raj Act, 2006 reserved 50% of seats for women in all three tiers of panchayats — a first in India, later emulated by many states.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly, constituted after the November 2025 elections, began its term on which date?
questions.e: The 18th Assembly was constituted on 20 November 2025 following elections held on 6 and 11 November 2025, in which the NDA won about 202 of 243 seats.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Who is the Speaker of the 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly (elected 2025)?
questions.e: Senior BJP leader Prem Kumar became Speaker of the 18th Assembly, with Narendra Narayan Yadav as Deputy Speaker.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister of Bihar in April 2026; what is historically significant about his appointment?
o: He is the first Deputy CM to become CM
He is the youngest CM of Bihar
He is the first BJP leader to become CM of Bihar
questions.e: Samrat Choudhary, who took office on 15 April 2026 after Nitish Kumar stepped down, is the first BJP leader to head a government in Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: After the April 2026 transition in Bihar, who became the Deputy Chief Ministers?
o: Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav
questions.e: Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav took office as Deputy Chief Ministers on 15 April 2026 in the Samrat Choudhary government.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: How many Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha seats does Bihar have?
questions.e: Bihar elects 40 members to the Lok Sabha and 16 to the Rajya Sabha, reflecting its large population among Indian states.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Who was the first woman Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.e: Renu Devi became Bihar's first woman Deputy Chief Minister in November 2020 in the NDA government headed by Nitish Kumar.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Bihar's liquor prohibition, one of the strictest in India, came into force in which month and year?
questions.e: Bihar enforced complete prohibition in April 2016 under the Bihar Excise (Amendment) Act, banning the manufacture, sale and consumption of liquor.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The 'Saat Nishchay' (Seven Resolves) governance programme in Bihar is currently in which phase covering 2025–2030?
questions.e: Saat Nishchay-3 is the 2025–2030 roadmap announced in the Bihar Budget 2026–27, succeeding the 2015–20 and 2020–25 phases of the seven-resolves programme.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Under the Bihar Right to Public Services Act, 2011, citizens can demand time-bound delivery of notified services; which body hears appeals against denial?
o: Appellate authority designated under the Act
questions.e: The 2011 Act designates appellate authorities to hear appeals when services are denied or delayed, with penalties on defaulting officials.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Mukhyamantri Nishchay Swayam Sahayata Bhatta Yojana gives unemployed youth in Bihar an allowance of what amount per month?
questions.e: Under this Saat Nishchay scheme, unemployed youth aged 20–25 receive Rs 1,000 per month for two years while they search for work or train in skills.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The Bihar Student Credit Card scheme provides education loans up to what amount for higher studies?
questions.e: The scheme offers collateral-free education loans up to Rs 4 lakh to students pursuing higher education, with the state as guarantor.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Kushal Yuva Karyakram, Bihar's flagship skill programme for youth, targets which age group?
questions.e: Kushal Yuva Karyakram trains youth aged 15–28 in language, communication and basic computer skills.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana, the flagship pre-election scheme of 2025, transferred what amount to each woman beneficiary?
questions.e: About 1.25–1.56 crore women received Rs 10,000 each in their bank accounts under the scheme; the 2026–27 budget promised up to Rs 2 lakh more for those starting enterprises.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Which two universities did the Bihar cabinet approve on 23 September 2026 under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026?
o: Mata Sita Women's University, Patna and Dinkar University, Begusarai
Aryabhatta University and Maulana Mazharul Haque University
questions.e: The cabinet created Mata Sita Women's University (Patna — Bihar's first women's university) and Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar' University (Begusarai), with Rs 15 crore each for establishment.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: At the 23 September 2026 cabinet meeting, the monthly salary of chairpersons of Bihar's boards and commissions was raised from Rs 25,000 to what?
questions.e: The cabinet raised chairpersons' monthly salary from Rs 25,000 to Rs 65,000 and daily allowance from Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,500.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: JEEVIKA, the backbone of women's self-help groups in rural Bihar, is formally known as what?
questions.e: The Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (JEEVIKA) organises millions of rural women into self-help groups and is among India's largest SHG movements.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Legislative Council in states like Bihar?
questions.e: Article 169 empowers Parliament to create or abolish Legislative Councils in states; Article 171 lays down their composition (Bihar's Council has 75 members).

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The Governor of Bihar (as of the 18th Assembly, 2025–26) is whom?
questions.e: Lt Gen (Retd.) Syed Ata Hasnain is the Governor of Bihar during the 18th Assembly period.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Bihar Diwas is celebrated every year on 22 March to mark which event?
o: Formation of Bihar as a separate province in 1912
questions.e: 22 March 1912 is the date Bihar and Orissa were carved out of Bengal as a separate province; the state celebrates Bihar Diwas on this day.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The Bihar cabinet meeting of 23 September 2026, chaired by the Chief Minister, took how many decisions?
questions.e: The 23 September 2026 cabinet meeting took 24 decisions, including the two new universities, revised board allowances and a sugar mill for Nawada.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Under the Seventh Schedule, 'police' and 'public order' fall under which list, giving Bihar primary jurisdiction over its police force?
questions.e: Police and public order are State List subjects (Entries 1 and 2), so law and order is constitutionally the Bihar government's domain.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: In the November 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, the NDA's total vote share was approximately what?
questions.e: The NDA secured about 46.7% of the vote against the INDIA bloc's 37.5%, converting it into roughly 202 of 243 seats.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Budget 2026–27, presented on 3 February 2026, has a total outlay of what amount — the largest in the state's history?
questions.e: Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav presented a Rs 3,47,589.76 crore budget for 2026–27, up from Rs 3.17 lakh crore in 2025–26.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 targets a fiscal deficit of what percentage of GSDP, staying within the FRBM ceiling?
questions.e: The fiscal deficit is targeted at Rs 39,111.80 crore — 2.99% of GSDP — just inside the 3% ceiling under the FRBM Act, with a small revenue surplus of Rs 1,143.19 crore.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 earmarked what amount for social welfare schemes under the 'nyay ke saath vikas' principle?
questions.e: Presenting the budget, the Finance Minister said Rs 7,724 crore was earmarked for social welfare schemes supporting vulnerable sections.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2025–26, the state's GSDP grew by what rate in 2024–25 at current prices?
questions.e: Bihar's GSDP grew 13.1% at current prices (8.6% at constant prices) in 2024–25, outpacing the national growth of 9.8% (6.5% real).

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Economic Survey 2025–26 puts the state's per capita GSDP at Rs 76,490 — yet Bihar remains at what position among states on per capita income?
questions.e: Despite high growth, Bihar's per capita income of roughly Rs 70,000–76,000 remains the lowest among Indian states, a paradox repeatedly flagged by the Survey.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Bihar accounts for roughly what share of India's makhana (foxnut) production?
questions.e: Bihar — chiefly Darbhanga, Madhubani, Purnia and Saharsa — produces around 90% of India's makhana; the Union Budget 2025–26 announced a Makhana Board for Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Shahi litchi, which holds a GI tag, is chiefly associated with which Bihar district?
questions.e: Muzaffarpur's Shahi litchi received the GI tag for its distinctive flavour; the district is called the 'litchi capital' of India.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a GI-tagged product of Bihar?
questions.e: Mithila makhana, Sikki grass work and Sujini embroidery are all GI-tagged Bihar crafts; Banarasi silk belongs to Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Phase-2 of the Industrial Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) announced in the Bihar Budget 2026–27 will come up at which place?
questions.e: The budget announced phase-2 of the Industrial Manufacturing Cluster at Gaya to anchor manufacturing investment in south Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Begusarai is often called the industrial capital of Bihar because of which major installation?
o: Barauni oil refinery and fertilizer plant
questions.e: Begusarai hosts Indian Oil's Barauni refinery and the HURL fertilizer plant, making it Bihar's foremost industrial district; it also ranks high in per-capita income.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 projects the state's nominal GSDP for 2026–27 at approximately what level?
questions.e: Nominal GSDP is projected at about Rs 13.1 lakh crore for 2026–27, implying 15% growth over the previous year.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Between 2020–21 and 2024–25, the share of capital expenditure in Bihar's total spending rose from 15.8% to what?
questions.e: The Economic Survey 2025–26 records capital expenditure's share rising from 15.8% to 22.3%, signalling a shift toward asset-creating investment.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Bihar's revenue receipts grew from Rs 1.28 lakh crore in 2020–21 to how much in 2024–25?
questions.e: Revenue receipts rose from Rs 1.28 lakh crore to Rs 2.18 lakh crore, with tax revenue as the dominant source, per the Economic Survey 2025–26.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Which sector contributes the largest share (about 55%) to Bihar's Gross State Value Added?
questions.e: The tertiary sector contributes about 54.8% of GSVA, while the secondary sector has risen to 26.8% and the primary sector fallen to 18.3%.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The literacy rate of Bihar reported in the Economic Survey 2025–26 is approximately what?
questions.e: The Survey reports historic improvement in literacy to 61.8%, alongside life expectancy of 68.9 years for males and 69.7 for females (2019–23).

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: A new sugar mill approved by the Bihar cabinet in September 2026 will come up in which district?
questions.e: The 23 September 2026 cabinet approved a sugar mill for Nawada, reviving agro-processing in a district with strong sugarcane potential.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The guiding principle of the Bihar Budget 2026–27, 'nyay ke saath vikas', means what?
questions.e: 'Nyay ke saath vikas' (development with justice) has been the state government's stated guiding principle; the budget themes were imaan, gyaan, vigyaan, armaan and samman.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Which Bihar district consistently leads in Gross District Domestic Product and per capita income?
questions.e: Patna leads Bihar in GDDP and per capita income, followed by Begusarai and Munger, according to the Economic Survey 2025–26.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: The 'Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi' announced in the Bihar Budget 2026–27 is meant to do what?
o: Boost farmers' income through direct support
questions.e: Named after Bharat Ratna Karpoori Thakur, the scheme provides direct income support to farmers, complementing central PM-KISAN transfers.

questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: Bihar's tax revenue for 2026–27 is projected at approximately what amount in the state budget?
questions.e: The budget projects tax revenue of around Rs 65,800 crore for 2026–27, indicating a steadily widening state revenue base.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bihar's geographical area is 94,163 sq km; what is its rank among Indian states by area?
questions.e: At 94,163 sq km Bihar is the 12th largest state of India by area, though it is the third most populous.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: How many districts and administrative divisions does Bihar have?
questions.e: Bihar has 38 districts grouped into 9 divisions (Patna, Tirhut, Saran, Darbhanga, Kosi, Purnia, Bhagalpur, Munger, Magadh).

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The northernmost district of Bihar is West Champaran; which is the southernmost district?
questions.e: Jamui is Bihar's southernmost district, while Kishanganj is the easternmost and Kaimur (Bhabua) the westernmost.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The river Kosi, called the 'Sorrow of Bihar', joins the Ganga near which place?
questions.e: After its long shifting course through north Bihar, the Kosi meets the Ganga near Kursela in Katihar district.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Gandak river joins the Ganga at which place in Bihar?
questions.e: The Gandak (Narayani), rising in Nepal, joins the Ganga near Hajipur–Sonepur opposite Patna.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Son river, rising at Amarkantak, joins the Ganga near which place?
questions.e: The Son flows north through the Kaimur–Rohtas region and joins the Ganga near Maner, just west of Patna.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Gogabil lake, declared Bihar's first community reserve for wetland birds, is located in which district?
questions.e: Gogabil in Katihar district, an oxbow lake of the Ganga–Mahananda system, was notified as Bihar's first community reserve.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary, India's only sanctuary for the Gangetic dolphin, lies in which district?
questions.e: The 60-km sanctuary stretch of the Ganga at Bhagalpur, notified in 1991, protects the endangered Gangetic dolphin, India's national aquatic animal.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Kabar Tal, Bihar's largest freshwater oxbow lake and a Ramsar site, is in which district?
questions.e: Kabar Tal in Begusarai district was declared a Ramsar site in 2020; the Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries in Jamui became Bihar's other Ramsar sites.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The famous Kakolat waterfall is located in which Bihar district?
questions.e: Kakolat falls on the Kakolat hill in Nawada district is a noted picnic and pilgrimage spot in south Bihar.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Which soil type dominates the vast north Bihar plain, making it highly fertile?
questions.e: The north Bihar plain is covered with fertile Gangetic alluvium deposited by the Himalayan rivers, supporting intensive paddy–wheat cultivation.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Rajgir hills, among the oldest hill ranges in India, lie in which district?
questions.e: The Rajgir hills in Nalanda district — Vaibhara, Vipula, Ratna, Udaya and Shanti — ring the ancient capital Rajagriha.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Punpun river joins the Ganga at which place associated with the pind-daan rituals?
questions.e: The Punpun meets the Ganga at Fatuha near Patna; pilgrims en route to Gaya perform rituals along its banks.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: Bihar's average annual rainfall is approximately what, concentrated in the June–September monsoon?
questions.e: Bihar receives roughly 100–125 cm of rain annually, almost entirely from the southwest monsoon; the Terai foothills get the heaviest showers.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Ghaghara (Sarayu) river meets the Ganga near which Bihar town?
questions.e: The Ghaghara joins the Ganga at Revelganj near Chhapra in Saran district after flowing along Bihar's western border with UP.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If 12 men can complete a work in 15 days, in how many days can 20 men complete the same work?
questions.e: Total work = 12 × 15 = 180 man-days; 180 ÷ 20 = 9 days. More workers finish the same work in fewer days.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What comes next in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.e: Each term is the previous term doubled plus one (5×2+1=11 … 95×2+1=191).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A train 240 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: In a code, DELHI is written as EFMIJ. How is PATNA written in that code?
questions.e: Each letter shifts forward by one (D→E, E→F…), so PATNA becomes QBUOB.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: The ratio of two numbers is 4:7. If their sum is 132, what is the smaller number?
questions.e: 4 + 7 = 11 parts = 132, so one part = 12; the smaller number is 4 × 12 = 48.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A shopkeeper marks goods 40% above cost and gives a 25% discount. What is his profit percent?
questions.e: Let cost = 100; marked price = 140; selling price = 140 × 0.75 = 105; profit = 5%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If DOG is coded as 26, how is CAT coded?
questions.e: Each letter is coded by its alphabetical position and the positions are added: DOG = 4 + 15 + 7 = 26, so CAT = 3 + 1 + 20 = 24.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A's age is twice B's age. Five years ago, A was three times as old as B. What is B's present age?
questions.e: Let B = x, A = 2x; then 2x − 5 = 3(x − 5), giving x = 10. So B is 10 and A is 20.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A sum of Rs 5,000 amounts to Rs 6,500 in 3 years at simple interest. What is the annual rate of interest?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A is B's brother. B is C's sister. C is D's father. How is A related to D?
questions.e: A and B are siblings and B is C's sister, so A is C's brother; since C is D's father, A is D's uncle.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A man walks 6 km north, then 8 km east. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.e: The path forms a right triangle; distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: The average of 7 consecutive even numbers is 26. What is the largest number?
questions.e: The average of an odd count of consecutive even numbers is the middle one (26); three steps of 2 above the middle gives 26 + 6 = 32.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If 35% of a number is 140, what is the number?
questions.e: Since 35% of the number equals 140, dividing 140 by 0.35 gives 400; checking back, 35% of 400 is indeed 140.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Find the next term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.e: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10; the next is 12, so 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Two pipes fill a tank in 20 and 30 hours respectively. Together, how long to fill it?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 per hour, so 12 hours.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A number when divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. What remainder when twice the number is divided by 7?
questions.e: Let the number be 7k + 3; twice is 14k + 6, which leaves remainder 6 on division by 7.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Book is to Chapter as Building is to what?
questions.e: A chapter is a division of a book, just as a floor is a division of a building.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: What is the average of the first 20 multiples of 5?
questions.e: The multiples form an arithmetic series from 5 to 100; average = (5 + 100) ÷ 2 = 52.5.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A cricketer's average after 20 innings is 45. How many runs must he score in the 21st innings to raise the average to 46?
questions.e: Runs so far = 20 × 45 = 900; needed total = 21 × 46 = 966; required = 966 − 900 = 66.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: If EARTH is coded as 52134, what is the code for HATER?
questions.e: From EARTH → 52134, the codes are E=5, A=2, R=1, T=3, H=4; applying them gives HATER = 4-2-3-5-1 = 42351.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide between 3 pm and 6 pm?
questions.e: Hands coincide every 65 5/11 minutes; between 3 and 6 pm they meet near 3:16, 4:21 and 5:27 — three times.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: The LCM of 12, 18 and 24 is what?
questions.e: Prime factors: 12 = 2²×3, 18 = 2×3², 24 = 2³×3; LCM = 2³ × 3² = 72.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: A sum doubles in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it triple?
questions.e: Doubling in 8 years means interest equals principal in 8 years (rate 12.5%); tripling needs twice the interest, i.e. 16 years.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: Which number replaces the question mark: 7, 14, 28, ?, 112?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 40% are girls. How many boys are in the class?

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary at Bhagalpur protects which species, declared India's National Aquatic Animal?
questions.e: The Gangetic dolphin (Platanista gangetica), India's National Aquatic Animal, is protected in the 60-km Vikramshila sanctuary stretch of the Ganga at Bhagalpur.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which two wetlands in Jamui district, Bihar, were declared Ramsar sites?
questions.e: The Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries in Jamui district joined Kabar Tal (Begusarai, 2020) as Bihar's Ramsar wetlands of international importance.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Dolphin, launched for the conservation of both riverine and marine dolphins, was announced in which year?
questions.e: Project Dolphin was launched in 2020 on the lines of Project Tiger, covering the Gangetic dolphin and the Indus river dolphin.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The principal bench (headquarters) of the National Green Tribunal is located in which city?
questions.e: The NGT's principal bench sits in New Delhi, with zonal benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which international protocol, adopted in 1987, mandated the phase-out of ozone-depleting substances like CFCs?
questions.e: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs and halons; the ozone hole is now slowly recovering, making it the most successful environmental treaty.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Red Data Book' listing threatened species worldwide is published by which organisation?
questions.e: The IUCN Red List (Red Data Book) assesses extinction risk; the Gangetic dolphin is listed as Endangered on it.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following is a primary greenhouse gas but NOT covered as a major target under the Kyoto Protocol's first commitment period?
questions.e: Kyoto targeted CO2, methane, nitrous oxide and fluorinated gases; water vapour, though the largest greenhouse contributor, is driven by natural cycles and was not a Kyoto target.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Chipko movement of the 1970s, a landmark in Indian environmentalism, began in which present-day state?
questions.e: Chipko began in 1973 at Mandal village in Chamoli (then UP, now Uttarakhand), with villagers hugging trees to stop commercial felling.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Kaziranga National Park, famed for the one-horned rhinoceros, lies in which state?
questions.e: Kaziranga in Assam holds the world's largest population of the greater one-horned rhinoceros and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, India's first major water-pollution law, was enacted in which year?
questions.e: The Water Act of 1974 created the Central and State Pollution Control Boards; the Air Act followed in 1981.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which committee's report led to the creation of the Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAMPA) mechanism in India?
questions.e: The Supreme Court's Central Empowered Committee recommended the CAMPA fund, where money collected for diverted forest land is used for compensatory afforestation.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In the context of the Kosi floods, the Kosi Barrage at Bhimnagar was built primarily through an agreement between India and which country?
questions.e: The 1954 Kosi agreement with Nepal led to the barrage at Bhimnagar (completed in the early 1960s) to tame the river called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which gas is mainly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.e: Chlorine released from CFCs catalytically destroys ozone molecules in the stratosphere, creating the Antarctic ozone hole.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The term 'biodiversity hotspot' was coined by which scientist?
questions.e: Norman Myers coined 'biodiversity hotspots' in 1988; India hosts four — Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, the Gangetic dolphin is listed in which Schedule giving it the highest protection?
questions.e: The Gangetic dolphin is a Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, affording it the highest legal protection against hunting.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Eutrophication of lakes like Kabar Tal is primarily caused by excess of which nutrients?
questions.e: Runoff rich in nitrogen and phosphorus from fertilisers triggers algal blooms that deplete oxygen — eutrophication — threatening wetland ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's updated climate pledge includes reaching net-zero emissions by which year?
questions.e: At COP26 (Glasgow, 2021) India pledged net zero by 2070, alongside 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 under the Panchamrit goals.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird, is mainly found in which habitat?
o: Desert grasslands of Rajasthan and Gujarat
questions.e: Fewer than 200 Great Indian Bustards survive in the desert grasslands of Rajasthan and Gujarat; power-line collisions are a major threat.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which forest type covers the largest area in Bihar, concentrated in the Terai and Kaimur regions?
questions.e: Bihar's forests are predominantly tropical dry deciduous (sal-dominated), found in West Champaran's Terai belt and the Kaimur plateau.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Aravalli Green Wall' project, frequently in news for checking desertification, aims to create a green buffer across which states?
questions.e: The Aravalli Green Wall spans the Aravalli range across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi to halt the eastward march of the Thar desert.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: ISRO's GISAT-1A (EOS-05) Earth-observation satellite was launched in early September 2026 aboard which rocket?
questions.e: GSLV-F17 carried GISAT-1A (EOS-05) to geostationary orbit in September 2026, ending a nearly seven-month launch pause after the PSLV-C62 failure in January 2026.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The Gaganyaan crew module's safe splashdown relies on how many parachutes of how many types?
questions.e: The module uses 10 parachutes of 4 types deployed in sequence: 2 apex-cover separation, 2 drogue, 3 pilot and 3 main parachutes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: VIKRAM3201, developed by ISRO with the Semi-Conductor Laboratory, is significant as what?
questions.e: VIKRAM3201 is India's first fully indigenous space-qualified 32-bit microprocessor for launch vehicles, fabricated at SCL Chandigarh.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: DRDO signed a Technology Development Fund agreement with start-up Zero mK India to build an indigenous dilution refrigerator for which national mission?
questions.e: The 20-millikelvin dilution refrigerator, essential for quantum computers, supports the National Quantum Mission's goal of cryogenic self-reliance.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: ISRO's new Advanced Radar Research Facility (IARRF), whose foundation was laid in September 2026, is coming up at which place?
questions.e: The ISTRAC Advanced Radar Research Facility at Chandrapur in Kamrup Metropolitan district, Assam, will strengthen satellite tracking and space situational awareness in the Northeast.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: NISAR, the NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite, was launched in which year?
questions.e: NISAR, launched jointly by NASA and ISRO in July 2025, maps the Earth’s surface with dual-band (L- and S-band) synthetic aperture radar.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: INS Nipun, launched on 31 August 2026 for the Indian Navy, belongs to which class of vessels?
questions.e: INS Nipun is the second Nistar-class Diving Support Vessel, built by Hindustan Shipyard at Visakhapatnam for deep-sea diving and submarine rescue.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission failure in January 2026 ended whose streak of successful launches?
questions.e: The 12 January 2026 PSLV-C62 failure broke ISRO's run of successful launches and caused the nearly seven-month pause ended by GISAT-1A in September 2026.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Desidustat, in the news as a novel oral drug, is used in the management of anaemia associated with which condition?
questions.e: Desidustat is an oral hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor developed in India for anaemia in chronic kidney disease patients.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: An international consortium published a comprehensive human brain-cell atlas in 2026 mapping gene activity in which brain region across the lifespan?
questions.e: The atlas analysed nuclei from over 6.3 million brain cells of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, illuminating neurodevelopment, ageing and psychiatric disease.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: India's third LCA Tejas Mk1A assembly line, operationalised by HAL, raised annual production capacity to how many jets?
questions.e: HAL's third Tejas Mk1A line, operationalised in October 2025, raised annual capacity to 24 jets, alongside a second line for the HTT-40 trainer.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The KALPANA3201 microprocessor, flight-tested by ISRO, is notable for being what?
o: A SPARC V8-based space chip with open-source-compatible toolsets
questions.e: KALPANA3201 is a 32-bit SPARC V8 (IEEE 1754) RISC flight-tested microprocessor developed with SCL, with open-source-compatible software toolsets, complementing VIKRAM3201 in India's space-electronics self-reliance push.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A pilot plant for sintered Neodymium-Iron-Boron permanent magnets, critical for EVs and wind turbines, was commissioned in March 2026 at which institution?
questions.e: The International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), Hyderabad, commissioned the rare-earth magnet pilot plant.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down on the Moon on 23 August 2023; the landing site is named what?
questions.e: The landing site near the lunar south pole was named Shiv Shakti Point; 23 August is observed as National Space Day.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: India's National Space Day is observed on 23 August to commemorate which achievement?
o: Chandrayaan-3's soft landing on the Moon
questions.e: 23 August marks Chandrayaan-3's 2023 soft landing near the lunar south pole, making India the first country to land there.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Exercise Veer Guardian-2026, the India–Japan bilateral air exercise held 9–22 September 2026, took place at which air force station?
questions.e: The IAF hosted the Japan Air Self-Defence Force at Jodhpur; India fielded Tejas, Su-30 MKI and Rafale while Japan flew F-2A fighters. The first edition was in Japan in January 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: As per the BPSC exam calendar 2026, the 72nd Integrated CCE preliminary examination is scheduled on which date, with how many vacancies?
questions.e: The 72nd CCE prelims is set for 25 October 2026 with 1,189 vacancies; the 71st CCE had 1,298 posts with mains results expected around August–September 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt. 15/2026) opened applications on 25 September 2026 for how many teacher posts, with the last date on 26 October 2026?
questions.e: TRE 4.0 notified 32,388 school teacher posts (Advt. 15/2026, superseding 14/2026); the application fee of Rs 100 must be paid by 25 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Mata Sita Women's University approved by the Bihar cabinet in September 2026 is significant because it is what?
questions.e: Approved on 23 September 2026 under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026, it will be Bihar's first women's university, covering women's colleges in Patna outside Patna University's jurisdiction.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar' University approved in September 2026 will be set up at which place?
questions.e: The cabinet approved the Dinkar University at Begusarai on the poet's birth anniversary, with jurisdiction over colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In September 2026, Bihar and Jharkhand signed an MoU ending their longstanding dispute over sharing the waters of which river?
questions.e: The two states signed a water-sharing agreement for the Sone river in the presence of the Union Home Minister, resolving a decades-old dispute.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which free trade agreement was finalised by India in September 2026, as reported in current-affairs round-ups?
questions.e: The India–New Zealand FTA, signed on 27 April 2026, was formally ratified on 21 September 2026 and enters into force on 20 October 2026, with 100% of Indian goods entering New Zealand duty-free.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY completed eight years on 23 September 2026; when was the scheme launched?
questions.e: Launched by the Prime Minister on 23 September 2018, PM-JAY remains the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme at Rs 5 lakh cover per family per year.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Delhi government's DURGA scheme approved on 23 September 2026 provides what to women and transgender persons?
questions.e: The Driving Upliftment and Rozgar for Women/Transgender Green e-Auto (DURGA) scheme provides 1,300 pink e-autos for safe, green livelihoods in the capital.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 18th edition of the India–Mongolia joint exercise 'Nomadic Elephant', begun in September 2026, is being held at which place?
questions.e: Both contingents of 45 personnel each are training at Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, on counter-insurgency drills under a UN mandate, including drone operations.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's GDP grew by what rate in Q1 of FY 2026–27, led by manufacturing and financial services?
questions.e: Q1 FY2026–27 GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year, led by manufacturing, financial services, real estate and professional services.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In the November 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, the BJP emerged as the single largest party with how many seats?
questions.e: The BJP won 89 seats (up from 74 in 2020) and the JD(U) 85, as the NDA swept about 202 of 243 seats with a 46.7% vote share.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: As of June 2026, Production Linked Incentive schemes across 14 sectors had attracted Rs 2.6 lakh crore in investment and created how many jobs?
questions.e: PLI schemes generated Rs 23.8 lakh crore in production and sales and 14.6 lakh jobs as of June 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's crude steel production rose from 81.7 million tonnes in 2014–15 to what level in 2025–26?
questions.e: National steel output more than doubled to 170.0 million tonnes in 2025–26, reflecting the infrastructure and manufacturing push.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: As of September 2026, who is the Leader of the Opposition in the 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly?
questions.e: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav is the Leader of the Opposition in the 18th Assembly, where the Mahagathbandhan holds 35 of 243 seats.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who became the first woman IPS officer to hold charge as Director General of Police in Bihar in September 2026?
questions.e: 1991-batch IPS officer Preeta Verma was given additional charge of DGP after incumbent Vinay Kumar took VRS on 27 September 2026 to become Chief Information Commissioner - making her the first woman IPS officer to head Bihar Police.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: In September 2026 the Bihar cabinet approved the purchase of 50 drones (Rs 24.50 crore) under which scheme?
questions.e: The 23 September 2026 cabinet cleared 50 drones for Rs 24.50 crore under the centrally sponsored Police Modernisation Scheme - for crowd control, riverine and anti-Naxal operations and disaster management - along with Rs 336.85 crore for police strengthening.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Rs 126.07-crore dairy projects approved for Supaul, Madhepura and Saharsa in September 2026 will be implemented under which cooperative union?
questions.e: The 23 September 2026 cabinet approved the projects - a yoghurt plant, premium ice cream plant and milk chilling facilities - under the Kosi Milk Producers Cooperative Union as part of Saat Nischay-3.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar' University at Begusarai will have jurisdiction over constituent and affiliated colleges in which districts?
questions.e: Approved on 23 September 2026 (Dinkar's birth anniversary) under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026, the university covers all constituent and affiliated colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria; colleges of Kameshwar Singh Sanskrit University, Darbhanga are excluded.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Under TRAI's Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, telecom operators must offer:
o: 30-day recharge plans renewable monthly and voice/SMS-only plans
A ban on bundled data packs
Free unlimited roaming for all users
questions.e: The 2026 amendment requires at least one 30-day special tariff voucher renewable on the same date each month - reducing 13 yearly recharges to 12 - and voice-and-SMS-only plans for users who do not need data.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: At the Asian Games 2026, Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase with a national record of:
questions.e: Parul Chaudhary clocked 9:08.67 - a personal best and national record - on 27 September 2026, her second Asian Games medal in the event after silver at Hangzhou 2023. Gold went to Bahrain's Winfred Yavi (9:04.36).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In September 2026, which state launched the 'Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram' scheme gifting a 1-gram, 22-carat gold ring to every newborn delivered in a government hospital?
questions.e: Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister launched 'Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram' in September 2026: every newborn in a government hospital gets a 1-gram 22-carat gold ring, with retrospective coverage for babies born from 22 June 2026. The first phase includes 1.28 lakh rings.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Under Bihar's 2026 One-Time Settlement scheme for brick kilns, the interest waiver applies to owners who settle principal dues within which window?
questions.e: The Mines and Geology Department's three-month OTS window runs 21 September to 20 December 2026, waiving accumulated interest for owners paying principal dues. Around 6,000 kilns are covered; Rs 289.38 crore of Rs 316.66 crore total dues was outstanding.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Under BPSC TRE 4.0 Advertisement 15/2026, the online application window for 32,388 school teacher posts is:
questions.e: Advertisement 15/2026 (dated 22 September 2026) superseded Adv 14/2026; applications run 25 September–26 October 2026 for 32,388 posts across Classes 1–12.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The last date for examination fee payment under BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advertisement 15/2026) is:
questions.e: The fee payment deadline is 25 October 2026; the application itself closes on 26 October and the correction window runs till 28 October.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who was appointed Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in September 2026?
questions.e: The ACC approved Mandeep K. Bhandari (2001-batch AGMUT IAS), earlier Principal Secretary to the J&K Lieutenant Governor, as CBSE Chairperson.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In its September 2026 Interim Economic Outlook, the OECD raised India’s GDP growth forecast for FY27 to:
questions.e: The September 2026 Interim Outlook ‘Weathering Successive Shocks’ raised FY27 growth by 80 basis points to 7.1% from 6.3%.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, Esha Singh won the silver medal in which event on 28 September 2026?
questions.e: Esha Singh finished second in the women’s 25m pistol final, losing a shoot-off to China’s Xiao Jiaruixian.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India secured its best-ever finish at the WorldSkills competition at Shanghai 2026 by placing:
questions.e: India placed 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 with six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence — its best show ever.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Livestock Insurance Portal of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying was launched on 28 September 2026 by:
questions.e: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh), holding Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, launched the portal in New Delhi.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Who resigned as the Chairperson of the Bihar Legislative Council on 28 September 2026?
questions.e: BJP MLC Awadhesh Narain Singh, Chairperson since 23 July 2024, resigned on 28 Sep 2026, submitting his resignation to Deputy Chairperson Ram Bachan Rai. Under the NDA understanding the Council Chairperson's post goes to the JD(U) while the Assembly Speaker (Prem Kumar) is with the BJP.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.q: The Gandak River at Dumaria Ghat was reported on 28 September 2026 to be flowing how far above the danger mark?
questions.e: During CM Samrat Choudhary's aerial survey of flood-hit Vaishali, Saran, East Champaran and Gopalganj, officials reported the Gandak near Dumaria Ghat at about 1.5 m above the danger mark, expected to rise another 50 cm overnight.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Bihar D.El.Ed Result 2026, declared by BSEB on 28 September 2026, is available for download at:
questions.e: Declared on 28 Sep 2026 for the 2025–27 (first year) and 2024–26 (second year) batches of the two-year face-to-face D.El.Ed programme; candidates need their roll code and roll number.
