questions.subject: Bihar Economy
questions.q: As per the 28 September 2026 review by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, how many of Bihar's 38 districts are covered by the City Gas Distribution network?
questions.e: 28 of 38 districts are covered, with 1,52,686 domestic PNG connections live (about 40.44% of the March 2026 target); Kaimur is targeted for gasification by November 2026.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: Ram Bachan Rai, whom JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar favours as the next Bihar Legislative Council Chairperson, currently holds which post?
o: Deputy Chairperson of the Legislative Council
Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly
questions.e: The 82-year-old JD(U) leader is the Deputy Chairperson to whom Awadhesh Narain Singh submitted his resignation; his MLC term ends 16 March 2027.

questions.subject: Bihar Polity
questions.q: The biennial elections to eight Graduate and Teachers' constituencies of the Bihar Legislative Council, whose sitting members' terms expire on 16 November 2026, are scheduled for:
questions.e: The elections cover Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi Graduates' constituencies and Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran Teachers' constituencies; JD(U), RJD and Jan Suraaj have announced candidates.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: In September 2026, the BPSC received zero applications for 218 Head of Department posts in government polytechnics. These posts belonged to which department?
o: Department of Science, Technology and Technical Education
questions.e: The 218 HoD posts across 16 disciplines were advertised on 26 August 2025 under the Department of Science, Technology and Technical Education; with no applications even after re-advertisement, BPSC returned the requisitions.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Among the 218 polytechnic Head of Department posts that drew zero applications, which discipline had the largest share of posts?
questions.e: Civil Engineering had 45 posts, the largest discipline share, followed by CSE (43), Electrical (42) and Electronics (39).

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: After 932 posts were added in September 2026, the total number of teacher vacancies under BPSC TRE-4.0 became:
questions.e: 493 posts were added for Classes 9–10 (now 4,370) and 439 for Classes 11–12 (now 16,540), taking the TRE-4.0 total to 32,388.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: On 29 September 2026, TRE-4 aspirants protesting in Patna demonstrated outside the residence of:
questions.e: TRE-4 aspirants gathered outside Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari's residence demanding that CTET-2026-appearing candidates also be allowed in the recruitment, on par with STET-appearing candidates.

questions.subject: Education
questions.q: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 is reported to be held on:
questions.e: The reported schedule is 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 with 31 January as a buffer; registration at jeemain.nta.nic.in is expected to begin soon.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nandan Nilekani-led task force on NTA examination reforms, which consulted K. Radhakrishnan on 29 September 2026, has how many members?
questions.e: The seven-member task force headed by Nandan Nilekani met former ISRO chief K. Radhakrishnan, whose 2024 committee had made 101 recommendations on exam reforms.

questions.subject: Education
questions.q: From the 2026–27 academic year, NTA will allot exam cities for JEE, NEET and CUET on the basis of:
o: The address on the candidate's Aadhaar card
The distance from the nearest metro city
questions.e: NTA announced that from 2026–27, exam cities will be allotted on the basis of the candidate's Aadhaar address, with no choice of cities; only candidates awaiting Aadhaar enrolment may choose.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) notifies 32,388 school-teacher posts. Online applications close on:
questions.e: TRE 4.0: 32,388 posts (Classes 1-12); apply 25 September-26 October 2026 on bpsc.bih.nic.in; fee Rs 100 per category.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Flood threat looms over Bihar and eastern UP after heavy Nepal rains and a reported breach in the embankment of which river?
questions.e: The Gandak (Narayani), a left-bank tributary of the Ganga rising in Nepal, saw a reported embankment breach raising flood threats in Bihar.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Kavach 4.0 was approved for 614.75 route km of which railway division at Rs 223 crore on 29 September 2026?
questions.e: Rs 223 crore for Kavach 4.0 (indigenous automatic train protection) across 614.75 route km of the Varanasi Division.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: On 29 September 2026 the Supreme Court quashed the NSA preventive detention of Mulla Afroz in the Sambhal case and imposed Rs 10 lakh costs on:
questions.e: The Court set aside the Allahabad High Court ruling, holding a custodial confession alone cannot ground NSA preventive detention.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's Index of Industrial Production grew 8.0% year-on-year in August 2026; manufacturing grew by:
questions.e: IIP: 8.0% YoY in August 2026; manufacturing 9.0% - a strong print ahead of the festive quarter.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Neeru Dhanda won the women's individual trap gold at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming:
o: The first Indian woman to win individual Asian Games gold in trap
A double gold winner at the Games
questions.e: Neeru Dhanda's trap gold was the first individual Asian Games gold for an Indian woman in the event.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Vithya Ramraj won 400m hurdles bronze in 54.75 seconds, breaking a 55.42-second national record from 1984 held by:
questions.e: Vithya Ramraj broke P.T. Usha's 1984 national record of 55.42 seconds.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The 30 September 2026 Bihar vigilance case against the bureaucrat couple was registered under:
o: Only the Prevention of Corruption Act
Prevention of Corruption Act and BNS Section 61(2)
questions.e: The case was registered on 25 September under the Prevention of Corruption Act and Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Ceigall India's Nawada stone-mining project awarded on 30 September 2026 is valued at:
questions.e: The five-year project at Bhadokhara, Nawada carries a cumulative value of Rs 214.52 crore, awarded via e-reverse auction.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Gandak river hit a record level of _____ on 30 September 2026 before breaching embankments in West Champaran:
questions.e: The river's level reached a record high of 91.25 metres following heavy rainfall in Nepal; breaches occurred at Khairtwa and Phuliyakhad.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history at the age of:
questions.e: Eleven-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history.

questions.subject: Defence & IR
questions.q: The 9th India-Kazakhstan joint exercise KAZIND began on 30 September 2026 at:
questions.e: The 9th edition of exercise KAZIND began at Oskemen, Kazakhstan.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The Indian Army's 145th Technical Graduate Course (July 2027) notification was issued on 30 September 2026; applications close on:
questions.e: The full TGC-145 notification was issued 30 September 2026; applications close 29 October 2026 on joinindianarmy.nic.in.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The 30 September 2026 aerial survey by CM Samrat Choudhary covered flood-hit areas of:
questions.e: The CM surveyed Bagaha, Bathna (Bairia), Machhargawan (Yogapatti), Shivrajpur and Bankatwa (Nautan) in West Champaran, and the Haijalpur area of Saran's Maker block.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The fresh Gandak breach at Sheetalpur in Gopalganj district was reported over a stretch of:
questions.e: The Bandhauli-Sheetalpur-Faizullahpur zamindari bund was breached over about six metres at Sheetalpur village around 6 am on 30 September.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: At Valmikinagar Gandak Barrage, the discharge fell between 4 am and 7 am on 30 September from 1,39,400 cusecs to:
questions.e: Discharge at Valmikinagar fell from 1,39,400 cusecs at 4 am to 1,31,500 cusecs at 7 am; 1,04,100 was the steady Kosi figure and 1,19,960 the Sone figure at 7 am.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: India's women's compound archery team equalled the world record of 238 with its 238-234 win over China; the record was originally set by:
questions.e: The trio equalled the world record of 238 set by Korea at Incheon 2014.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The PM-DHARA scheme approved on 1 October 2026 has an outlay of:
questions.e: The Cabinet approved Rs 1.86 lakh crore for intra-state transmission networks with battery storage.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: For the 2027-28 marketing year, the MSP for wheat was raised by Rs 25 to:
questions.e: The wheat MSP is now Rs 2,610 per quintal; pulses and oilseeds got hikes of up to Rs 675 per quintal.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026), the total number of school teacher posts is:
questions.e: The notification lists 32,388 posts: Primary 3,847; Middle 8,563; Secondary 3,877; Higher Secondary 16,101.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The last date to apply online for BPSC TRE 4.0 is:
questions.e: Applications are open 25 September–26 October 2026; the application fee must be paid by 25 October.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In BPSC TRE 4.0, the largest share of 16,101 posts is for which level?
questions.e: Higher Secondary (classes 11–12) has the largest share at 16,101 posts, including Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Political Science and other subjects.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The BPSC Project Manager preliminary examination scheduled for 4 October 2026 was:
questions.e: BPSC postponed the Project Manager (Industries Department, Advt 109/2025) preliminary exam citing administrative reasons; a new date will be announced.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'People's Plan Campaign 2026-27' launched via the 2 October gram sabhas is titled:
questions.e: The campaign 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas' asks gram panchayats to prepare Gram Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The 46th Chess Olympiad, where India won Open silver, was held at:
questions.e: The 46th Chess Olympiad was held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, in September 2026; Open gold went to hosts Uzbekistan.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Ahead of the 5–7 October 2026 MPC meeting, the repo rate is:
questions.e: The repo rate is 5.25%; the Reuters poll expects a 25 bps hike to 5.50% — the first since February 2023.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 57th GST Council recommended raising the GST prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to:
questions.e: The Council proposed the higher bar alongside removal of GST officers' arrest powers.

questions.subject: Education
questions.q: Which state was declared India's sixth fully literate state in October 2026?
questions.e: Uttarakhand joined Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim under the ULLAS programme.

questions.subject: Health
questions.q: Each JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) team comprises:
o: 5 NCC cadets and 5 MY Bharat volunteers
questions.e: The teams work under a designated Class-I officer; phase one covers 55 districts in 11 states.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The new captain of the Indian women's cricket team is:
questions.e: Smriti Mandhana succeeded Harmanpreet Kaur as captain.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: The Delhi government raised monthly ASHA incentives from Rs 3,000 to:
questions.e: The hike covers 6,690 ASHA workers in Delhi.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The Japan Open 2026 men's singles title was won by:
questions.e: Alcaraz beat Jiri Lehecka 7-6(4), 6-4 in Tokyo for his second straight Japan Open title; Djokovic won the China Open in Beijing.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Ganga enters Bihar at which place?
questions.e: The Ganga enters Bihar at Chausa in Buxar district and exits at Katihar, bisecting the state west to east.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Which river is called the “Sorrow of Bihar”?
questions.e: The Kosi is called the Sorrow of Bihar for its history of shifting course and devastating floods.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: How many districts does Bihar have?
questions.e: Bihar has 38 districts grouped into 9 divisions.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: How many seats are there in the Bihar Vidhan Sabha?
questions.e: The Bihar Legislative Assembly has 243 seats; the Vidhan Parishad has 75.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, India's first President, was born in which Bihar village?
questions.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was born at Ziradei in Siwan district, Bihar.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Nalanda University was founded during the reign of which ruler?
questions.e: Nalanda was founded under the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I; Vikramshila came later under the Pala king Dharmapala.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Vikramshila University was established by which Pala king?
questions.e: The Pala king Dharmapala founded Vikramshila in present-day Bhagalpur region.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, was born at which place in Bihar?
questions.e: Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali; he attained nirvana at Pawapuri.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Buddha attained enlightenment at which site in Bihar?
questions.e: The Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya under the Bodhi tree.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The first Buddhist council was held at which place?
questions.e: The first Buddhist council met at Rajgir; the second was held at Vaishali.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Sher Shah Suri, who built the Grand Trunk Road and introduced the rupiya, belonged to which Bihar town?
questions.e: Sher Shah Suri was from Sasaram; his tomb there is a landmark of Indo-Islamic architecture.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Battle of Buxar, which gave the East India Company the Diwani of Bengal, was fought in which year?
questions.e: Buxar (1764) was the decisive battle; the Diwani of Bengal followed in 1765.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, against the tinkathia system, was launched at which place in 1917?
questions.e: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Kunwar Singh, who led the 1857 revolt in Bihar past the age of 80, belonged to which place?
questions.e: The octogenarian Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur near Arrah led Bihar's 1857 uprising.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Bihar Diwas is celebrated on which date?
questions.e: Bihar Diwas is 22 March, marking the 1912 carving of Bihar & Orissa out of Bengal.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on which date?
questions.e: Jharkhand was formed on 15 November 2000, bifurcating Bihar.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Patna High Court was established in which year?
questions.e: The Patna High Court was established in 1916, one of India's oldest high courts.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.e: Sri Krishna Sinha became Bihar's first Chief Minister; Jairamdas Daulatram was the first Governor.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Chhath, Bihar's defining festival, is dedicated to which deity?
questions.e: Chhath is dedicated to Surya, the Sun god, observed in the month of Kartik.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Sonepur Mela, among Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held at the confluence of which rivers?
questions.e: Sonepur Mela (Saran) is held at the Ganga–Gandak confluence near Hajipur.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Which traditional Bihar craft holds a GI tag and is painted by Maithil women?
questions.e: Madhubani (Mithila) painting holds a GI tag; Sikki grass work is another GI-tagged Bihar craft.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Bihar is India's largest producer of which of the following?
questions.e: Bihar's Mithila region is India's #1 makhana producer; makhana holds a GI tag.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: The Muzaffarpur belt of Bihar is famous as India's top producer of which fruit?
questions.e: Bihar is India's #1 litchi producer, centred on the Muzaffarpur belt.

questions.subject: Daily Practice
questions.q: Which of these is a north-bank, Himalayan-origin river of Bihar?
questions.e: North-bank Himalayan rivers — Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Bagmati, Kosi, Mahananda — are flood-prone; Son, Punpun and Falgu are seasonal south-bank rivers.

questions.subject: Persons
questions.q: 11 October 2026 ko UNICEF India ne ___ ko apna celebrity advocate banaya. / On 11 October 2026, UNICEF India named ___ as its celebrity advocate.
questions.e: Ghoshna International Day of the Girl par hui; Mandhana usi saptah Bharat ki mahila cricket team ki kaptan bani thi. / Announced on the International Day of the Girl; Mandhana had been appointed India women's cricket captain earlier that week.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: 12 October 2026 ko Kuno National Park mein jo aath mahine ka cheetah cub mrit paya gaya, woh Namibian cheetah ___ ka tha. / The eight-month-old cheetah cub found dead at Kuno on 12 October 2026 was born to Namibian cheetah ___.
questions.e: February 2026 mein janme paanch cubs mein se ek; maut ka karan post-mortem ke baad pata chalega. / One of five born around February 2026; the cause awaits the post-mortem report.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: SAREX-2026 ka theme kya tha? / What was the theme of SAREX-2026?
o: Leveraging Technology to Strengthen SAR Preparedness and Maritime Safety
questions.e: 7–8 October 2026 ko Paradip (Odisha) mein 12vi Rashtriya Samudri Khoj-Bachav Exercise; 30 deshon ke 32 paryavekshak. / 12th National Maritime Search & Rescue Exercise at Paradip (Odisha) on 7–8 October 2026; 32 observers from 30 countries.

questions.subject: Bihar
questions.q: For how many total posts did BPSC advertise the School Teacher TRE 4.0 recruitment (Advt 15/2026) after the October 2026 revision?
questions.e: BPSC raised TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) vacancies from 32,388 to 33,320 (announced 7 October 2026). Online applications run 25 September – 26 October 2026 for classes 1–12. Eligibility includes graduation/PG in the subject plus B.Ed, STET, CTET or D.El.Ed.

questions.subject: Bihar
questions.q: BSEB released the second dummy admit card for Bihar STET 2026 on:
questions.e: BSEB released the 2nd dummy admit card for Bihar STET 2026 on 1 October 2026, with corrections allowed during 1–7 October 2026 (Advt P.R.183/2026). The exam is a computer-based test for classes 9–12.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: At which airbase did Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 conclude on 13 October 2026?
questions.e: Tarang Shakti 2026 concluded on 13 October 2026 at Jodhpur Airbase, Rajasthan — its second edition, with eight nations participating and ~150 aircraft flying 600+ sorties.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Supreme Court’s 12 October 2026 clarification on Form 6 related to its earlier judgment upholding which exercise in Bihar?
o: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
questions.e: On 12 October 2026 the Supreme Court clarified it had neither approved nor disapproved the ECI’s revised Form 6, since its May 2026 judgment upholding the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls pre-dated the form’s changes. Challenges will be heard on 27 October 2026.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Which India–UAE joint military exercise is underway at Chaubatia, Uttarakhand from 5–18 October 2026?
questions.e: The India–UAE joint exercise Mountain Guardian 2026, 3rd edition, runs 5–18 October 2026 at the Foreign Training Node, Chaubatia, Uttarakhand, with 92 personnel from both armies focusing on sub-conventional mountain operations.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In the 12 October 2026 governor reshuffle, Braj Mohan Ram was appointed Governor of:
questions.e: Braj Mohan Ram became Governor of Odisha. Others: Dr Sudha Yadav to Karnataka, Dr Dhal Singh Bisen to Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim; Om Prakash Mathur shifted Sikkim to Kerala; R. V. Arlekar to Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Madras High Court's 13 October 2026 ruling on Tamil Nadu MLAs concerned the resignations of:
questions.e: The Court upheld the Speaker's acceptance of the resignations of six AIADMK MLAs as genuine, directing disqualification proceedings to be completed within two months.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Telugu Ganga project, discussed by TN CM Joseph Vijay with AP CM Chandrababu Naidu on 13 October 2026, carries water from which river to Chennai?
questions.e: The meeting in New Delhi sought additional Krishna water for Chennai's drinking supply through the Telugu Ganga project.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: Special Campaign 6.0 on 14 October 2026 involves the Ministry of Panchayati Raj conducting:
o: A cleanliness drive and disposal of pending cases
questions.e: On 14 October 2026 the Ministry of Panchayati Raj will run a cleanliness drive and dispose of pending cases under Special Campaign 6.0.

questions.subject: General Studies
questions.q: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan was launched on:
questions.e: PM GatiShakti was launched on 13 October 2021 and completed five years on 13 October 2026.

questions.subject: General Studies
questions.q: ULLAS, under which Lakshadweep became India’s first 100% literate UT, stands for:
o: Universal Literacy and Learning Advancement Scheme
Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society
Union Literacy and Learning Assessment System
Upliftment of Learners through Literacy and Skills
questions.e: ULLAS = Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society, the adult-education programme under the Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram.

questions.subject: General Studies
questions.q: As per DARPG’s September 2026 report, the CPGRAMS grievance disposal rate was:
questions.e: 2,38,579 grievances were redressed in September 2026 — a disposal rate exceeding 104% — with pendency down to 85,687.

questions.subject: General Studies
questions.q: Who won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.e: Canadian author Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature for her bold, inventive oeuvre in dialogue with the classical tradition.

questions.subject: General Studies
questions.q: Who was appointed Deputy Election Commissioner in October 2026?
questions.e: Prakash Rajpurohit, a 2010-batch Rajasthan-cadre IAS officer, was appointed Deputy Election Commissioner till 8 April 2030.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: On which date did BPSC issue the notice postponing the 72nd CCE Prelims 2026 (which was scheduled for 25 October 2026)?
questions.e: The postponement notice was issued on 12 October 2026; the revised exam date is yet to be announced.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: How many posts does the BPSC 72nd Combined Competitive Examination 2026 cover after the corrigendum?
questions.e: 1,186 posts - the initial 1,230 was reduced after 44 Sugarcane Officer vacancies were removed.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: When was the BPSC 72nd CCE 2026 notification released, and when were applications accepted?
questions.e: Notification on 5 May 2026; online applications 7-31 May 2026 with a Rs 100 fee for all candidates.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The October 2026 boat tragedy in which at least 13 children died occurred in which Bihar district?
questions.e: The boat capsized in the Ganga under Raghopur police station area of Vaishali district on 13 October 2026 night.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: How many Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) posts are included in the BPSC 72nd CCE 2026?
questions.e: 20 DSP posts are included (SDO/SDM 100, Assistant Commissioner State Tax 76, Rural Development Officer 65).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Union Cabinet on 15 October 2026 continued the National Social Assistance Programme (2026–27 to 2030–31) with a ₹53,428 crore outlay. The programme's pension assistance to the elderly, widows and persons with disabilities flows from which constitutional provision?
questions.e: The National Social Assistance Programme operationalises the Directive Principle in Article 41 of the Constitution (right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Under which Centralised Employment Notification did the RRB open applications on 15 October 2026 for 1,688 NTPC undergraduate posts?
questions.e: The RRB opened applications under CEN No. 07/2026 on 15 October 2026 for 1,688 NTPC undergraduate posts (700 Commercial-cum-Ticket Clerk, 200 Accounts Clerk-cum-Typist, 600 Junior Clerk-cum-Typist, 188 Trains Clerk), with the last date on 13 November 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: What is the minimum educational qualification prescribed for the RRB NTPC Undergraduate recruitment (CEN 07/2026)?
questions.e: Candidates applying for the RRB NTPC Undergraduate recruitment (CEN 07/2026) must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination from a recognised board; the age limit is 18–30 years as on 1 January 2027.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Which of the following milestones is correctly associated with Bihar in the history of panchayati raj in India?
o: 50% reservation for women in panchayats in 2006
33% reservation for women in panchayats in 1993
questions.e: Bihar became the first state in India to reserve 50% of seats for women in panchayati raj institutions in 2006 — a landmark affirmative-action step later emulated by several states.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: ICAI has announced that the CA Intermediate September 2026 examination results are likely to be declared by the evening of:
questions.e: ICAI's Examination Department, in its announcement dated 14 October 2026, said the CA Intermediate September 2026 results are likely to be declared by the evening of 22 October 2026 at caresults.icai.org, accessible with the Registration Number and Roll Number.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Supreme Court Bench ruled on 15 October 2026 that religious conversion does not automatically confer backward-class reservation benefits under Article 16(4)?
o: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar
Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih
Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan
CJI Surya Kant and Justice (retd) on the panel
questions.e: A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar held on 15 October 2026 that a person converting from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim affirmative action under Article 16(4) merely on the basis of pre-conversion social backwardness, dismissing the Tamil Nadu government's appeal.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 9 MW Hanu project, dedicated along with four other Ladakh projects on 15 October 2026, is a:
questions.e: The 9 MW Hanu Hydroelectric Project with associated power-transmission infrastructure was among the five Ladakh projects worth about Rs. 3,350 crore dedicated on 15 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: 15 October 2026 marked the 10th anniversary of the Kigali Amendment. It amends which protocol?
questions.e: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol (adopted 15 October 2016, in force from 1 January 2019) schedules the phasedown of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: अक्टूबर 2026 में RBI की मौद्रिक नीति समिति ने रेपो दर में कितनी वृद्धि की और नई रेपो दर क्या है? (What did the RBI MPC do to the repo rate in October 2026?)
questions.e: 7 अक्टूबर 2026 को MPC ने रेपो दर 25 बेसिस पॉइंट बढ़ाकर 5.50% की — यह फरवरी 2023 के बाद पहली वृद्धि है — और रुख 'neutral' से 'calibrated tightening' कर दिया। (Dated: 7 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: IDBI बैंक में सरकार की 60.72% हिस्सेदारी किस संस्था द्वारा लगभग ₹52,878 करोड़ में खरीदी जा रही है?
questions.e: Fairfax Financial Holdings IDBI Bank में ₹52,878 करोड़ में 60.72% हिस्सेदारी खरीद रही है — यह भारत का सबसे बड़ा वित्तीय-क्षेत्र FDI सौदा बताया गया है। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: IBSAMAR IX नौसैनिक अभ्यास में भाग लेने वाला भारतीय नौसेना का जहाज कौन-सा है, और यह अभ्यास किन देशों के बीच होता है?
o: INS Tarkash — भारत, ब्राज़ील, दक्षिण अफ्रीका
questions.e: INS Tarkash नौवें IBSAMAR (भारत–ब्राज़ील–दक्षिण अफ्रीका) नौसैनिक अभ्यास में दक्षिण अफ्रीका में भाग ले रहा है। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: विश्व खाद्य दिवस (World Food Day) प्रतिवर्ष किस तिथि को मनाया जाता है और यह किस संस्था की स्थापना का स्मरण करता है?
questions.e: विश्व खाद्य दिवस 16 अक्टूबर को FAO (1945) की स्थापना की याद में मनाया जाता है; यह पहली बार 1981 में मनाया गया था। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: 31 अक्टूबर 2026 को वायु सेना प्रमुख (Chief of the Air Staff) का पदभार कौन संभालेंगे?
questions.e: एयर मार्शल आशुतोष दीक्षित 31 अक्टूबर 2026 को वायु सेना प्रमुख बनेंगे। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: NEET-PG 2026 के संबंध में 15 अक्टूबर 2026 को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने क्या निर्देश दिया?
o: उत्तर कुंजी पारदर्शिता याचिका पर केंद्र से जवाब मांगा
questions.e: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने NEET-PG 2026 उत्तर कुंजी और उत्तर प्रकटीकरण में पारदर्शिता की मांग वाली याचिका पर केंद्र सरकार से जवाब मांगा। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Bihar GK
questions.q: JD(U) MLA Anant Singh, who stirred a political controversy on 16 October 2026 over remarks linked to the MLC elections, represents which Bihar Assembly constituency?
questions.e: Anant Singh is the JD(U) MLA from Mokama. On 16 October 2026 he made sensational claims about his loyalty to former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar amid his opposition to the JD(U)'s Patna Graduates MLC candidate Neeraj Kumar, backing Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Singh instead.

questions.subject: Bihar GK
questions.q: BPSC TRE-4 (2026) aims to fill how many school teacher vacancies in Bihar?
questions.e: BPSC's Teacher Recruitment Examination TRE-4 (2026) aims to fill 32,388 vacancies: 3,847 for Classes 1-5, 8,563 for Classes 6-8, 3,877 for Classes 9-10 and 16,101 for Classes 11-12. Applications close on 21 October 2026 on bpsc.bih.nic.in.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Sauj Jheel, designated a Ramsar site on 15 October 2026, is located in which district?
questions.e: Sauj Jheel is in Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh. With its designation, Mainpuri became the only district in Uttar Pradesh with two Ramsar sites, the other being Saman Bird Sanctuary.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The election for the Patna Graduates' constituency seat of the Bihar Legislative Council, at the centre of the JD(U)-Anant Singh row in October 2026, is scheduled for:
questions.e: The Patna Graduates' MLC election is scheduled for 23 October 2026. JD(U) has fielded Neeraj Kumar, while MLA Anant Singh is backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: As per the Consortium of NLUs notification, the Common Law Admission Test (CLAT) 2027 will be held on which date?
questions.e: CLAT 2027 is scheduled for 6 December 2026 (2:00 PM–4:00 PM, offline pen-and-paper). Registration closes on 31 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Samrat Choudhary muretha vow
capsules.body: As state BJP chief, Samrat Choudhary vowed to keep wearing the muretha (traditional turban) until Nitish Kumar was out of power. After Nitish rejoined the NDA in January 2024, Choudhary offered the turban at Ram Janmabhoomi in Ayodhya in July 2024, two years before he himself became Bihar's first BJP chief minister in April 2026.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan 2026 target
capsules.body: India's first crewed spaceflight, Gaganyaan, is targeted for 2026, with four Indian astronauts in training. Uncrewed test missions precede the crewed flight. Success will make India the fourth nation with independent human spaceflight capability.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Chandrayaan-4 sample return
capsules.body: Chandrayaan-4, targeted for 2028, will attempt to bring lunar soil and rock samples back to Earth using multiple launches and in-space docking. The sample-return mission is designed as a technology bridge toward future crewed missions to the Moon.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Chandrayaan-5 with JAXA
capsules.body: Chandrayaan-5, planned after 2028, is a joint ISRO-JAXA mission formerly called LUPEX. An Indian lander will deploy a Japanese 350-kg rover to explore the lunar south pole region, a science-heavy step toward human exploration of the Moon.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO moon roadmap 2040
capsules.body: ISRO aims to land an Indian astronaut on the Moon by 2040 and raise India's share of the global space economy from about 2% to 10% this decade. Private industry is being brought into roles earlier handled only by ISRO, from launches to satellite building.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India 4th on Global Firepower, 85th on Henley Passport Index
capsules.body: The Global Firepower Index 2025 ranked India's conventional military strength 4th in the world, after the US, Russia and China, with defence spending third at about USD 76.6 billion. Separately, the Henley Passport Index placed India 85th, with visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 59 countries. The World Press Freedom Index 2025 ranked India 151st of 180, classified under a 'very serious' media situation.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Makhana Board announced
capsules.body: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Makhana Board in Bihar to improve production, processing, value addition and marketing of makhana. Makhana producers will be organised into Farmer Producer Organisations with handholding and training, ensuring they receive benefits of all relevant government schemes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Union Budget Bihar sops
capsules.body: The 2025-26 Union Budget announced a National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management in Bihar, expansion of IIT Patna, expansion of Patna airport, a brownfield airport at Bihta, facilitation of greenfield airports, and financial support for the Western Koshi Canal project benefiting over 50,000 hectares in Mithilanchal, under the Poorvodaya scheme.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Makhana economy push
capsules.body: Makhana is cultivated over about 15,000 hectares in Bihar, mainly in the Mithila region. The new Makhana Board will give farmers training, technology and market linkages so the fox-nut economy scales up with better processing and branding.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Global Soft Power Index 2025: India ranked 30th
capsules.body: The Brand Finance Global Soft Power Index 2025 ranked India 30th, measuring cultural influence, diplomacy and global perception, and placing it among the top emerging soft-power nations. India's soft power was credited to its culture, diplomacy and economy. The index result is frequently paired in exam revision with India's GII 2025 rank of 38th and Global Firepower rank of 4th as markers of its rising comprehensive national profile.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Madhav National Park declared India's 58th tiger reserve
capsules.body: On 9 March 2025, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav declared Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district, Madhya Pradesh, as India's 58th tiger reserve, with a core of about 375 sq km within a 1,751 sq km landscape. This made Madhya Pradesh, the 'Tiger State', host to nine tiger reserves, the most in India. The reserve strengthens a critical corridor linking Ranthambore (Rajasthan) with Kuno National Park, and tigers were reintroduced there from 2023.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Jnanpith 2024 Vinod Kumar Shukla
capsules.body: Hindi novelist and poet Vinod Kumar Shukla received the 59th Jnanpith Award for 2024, announced in March 2025. The Chhattisgarh writer, known for Naukar Ki Kameez, was the first from his state and the 12th Hindi recipient of the honour.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Jnanpith facts
capsules.body: The Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honour instituted in 1961, carries Rs 11 lakh, a bronze Saraswati statue and a citation. The first recipient was G. Sankara Kurup in 1965 and the first woman was Ashapurna Devi in 1976. Only works in Indian languages are eligible.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Indus Waters Treaty placed in abeyance after Pahalgam attack
capsules.body: Following the 22 April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in 'abeyance' on 23 April 2025, citing Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism. India then launched Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025 against terror infrastructure across the border. The MEA reiterated in June 2026 that the treaty stays suspended, with Baglihar Dam gates closed, and India rejected an August 2026 Court of Arbitration ruling in The Hague that the treaty remained in force.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Similipal Tiger Reserve notified as a national park
capsules.body: On 24 April 2025, the Odisha government notified Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district as a national park covering 845.70 sq km, making it India's 107th national park and Odisha's second after Bhitarkanika. Similipal, also a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and elephant reserve, is globally famous as the only wild home of melanistic (black) tigers, alongside about 40 Bengal tigers, a quarter of Odisha's elephant population and over 360 bird species.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Inaugural WAVES summit held in Mumbai
capsules.body: The first World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit (WAVES) was held from 1 to 4 May 2025 at the Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai, inaugurated by PM Modi, with participants from over 90 countries and 10,000-plus delegates. Covering films, broadcasting, AVGC-XR, gaming and AI in media, the summit's WAVES Bazaar recorded business deals worth over Rs 1,300 crore, and the Global Media Dialogue concluded with a WAVES declaration adopted by representatives of 77 countries.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Khelo India Youth Games in Bihar
capsules.body: Bihar hosted the seventh Khelo India Youth Games from May 4 to 15, 2025, its first major multi-discipline event. Prime Minister Modi virtually inaugurated it at the Patliputra Sports Complex, Patna. Twenty-seven medal sports plus e-sports as a demonstration event drew over 8,500 athletes, with venues in Patna, Rajgir, Gaya, Bhagalpur, Begusarai and Delhi.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: HDR 2025: India ranks 130th on Human Development Index
capsules.body: The UNDP Human Development Report 2025 placed India 130th out of 193 countries on the Human Development Index with a value of 0.644, in the medium human development category. The HDI combines health, education and standard-of-living indicators. The report also showed India improving on the Gender Inequality Index to 108th from 122nd in 2021, though gender gaps remain significant.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: KIYG 2025 final tally
capsules.body: Maharashtra topped the 2025 Khelo India Youth Games table, followed by Haryana and Rajasthan, while hosts Bihar finished 15th. Twenty-six records were set during the Games, including 13 national youth weightlifting records, marking a successful debut hosting for the state.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Vridhjan pension raised to 1100
capsules.body: The Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojana gives Rs 1,100 every month to all residents above 60, effective from June 2025, up from Rs 400-500 earlier. The amount is credited by DBT on the 10th of every month; the September 2026 instalment was credited on September 10. Old-age, widow and disability pensions are covered under the same window.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India's 2025 social rankings: happiness, gender gap, SDGs
capsules.body: The World Happiness Report 2025 (UN SDSN) ranked India 118th out of 147 countries, with Finland first, based on life-satisfaction surveys. The Global Gender Gap Report 2025 placed India 131st. The Sustainable Development Goals Index 2025 ranked India 99th, while the Global Peace Index 2025 ranked it 115th with Iceland the most peaceful. Together these paint the mixed social-development picture examiners often ask about.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: 17th BRICS Summit in Rio adopts Rio de Janeiro Declaration
capsules.body: BRICS leaders met in Rio de Janeiro on 6-7 July 2025 for the 17th BRICS Summit themed 'Strengthening Global South Cooperation for a More Inclusive and Sustainable Governance', adopting the Rio de Janeiro Declaration with 126 commitments across 31 points. The declaration strongly condemned the Pahalgam terror attack and backed zero tolerance of terrorism. Indonesia attended its first summit as a full member, leaders supported India's bid to host COP33 in 2028, and PM Modi announced India would define BRICS in 2026 as 'Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability'.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement signed
capsules.body: India and the UK signed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) on 24 July 2025 at Chequers, in the presence of PM Modi and UK PM Keir Starmer, concluding three years of talks that began in January 2022. It gives duty-free access for 99% of Indian exports to the UK, cuts Scotch whisky tariffs from 150% to 75%, eases visas for Indian professionals, and entered into force on 15 July 2026. Bilateral trade of USD 56 billion is targeted to double by 2030.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Divya Deshmukh world champion
capsules.body: Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup on July 28, 2025, in Batumi, Georgia, beating Koneru Humpy 2.5-1.5 in rapid tiebreaks. She became India's 88th Grandmaster and only the fourth Indian woman to earn the title, with a $50,000 prize and qualification for the 2026 Candidates tournament.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NISAR launched
capsules.body: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite was launched on July 30, 2025, from Sriharikota aboard GSLV-F16, the first joint ISRO-NASA mission of its kind. It is the world's first satellite carrying both L-band (NASA) and S-band (ISRO) synthetic aperture radars, weighing 2,392 kg in sun-synchronous orbit.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NISAR capabilities
capsules.body: NISAR provides all-weather, day-and-night Earth observation with a 12-day repeat cycle, detecting centimetre-scale movement of land and ice. It will support disaster response, infrastructure monitoring and agriculture, with data made freely available. It was also the first time GSLV placed a satellite in sun-synchronous polar orbit.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: GSLV firsts with NISAR
capsules.body: NISAR flew on the 18th GSLV mission and the 12th flight with the indigenous cryogenic upper stage. It was the heaviest payload the rocket had carried to sun-synchronous polar orbit, marking a new benchmark for India's launch capability.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana: 72 lakh jobs in first year
capsules.body: The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, launched 1 August 2025 and implemented through EPFO, completed its first year on 1 August 2026 with over 72 lakh first-time employees joining the formal workforce, nearly 30% of them women. The Rs 99,446-crore scheme runs to 31 July 2027 targeting over 3.5 crore jobs: first-time employees can receive up to Rs 15,000, while employers get up to Rs 3,000 per month per additional eligible employee.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Pratyaya Amrit chief secretary
capsules.body: Pratyaya Amrit took charge as Bihar's Chief Secretary on September 1, 2025, succeeding Amrit Lal Meena. A 1991-batch IAS officer, he was Development Commissioner and ACS for Health and Disaster Management. He won the Prime Minister's Award for Excellence in Public Administration in 2011 for turning around the Bihar State Bridge Construction Corporation.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: C.P. Radhakrishnan elected India's 15th Vice President (9 September)
capsules.body: NDA nominee C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected India's 15th Vice President on 9 September 2025, defeating the INDIA bloc's Justice B. Sudershan Reddy 452-300. Turnout was 98.2% - 767 of 781 eligible MPs, with 752 valid ballots. The poll was necessitated by Jagdeep Dhankhar's resignation on 21 July 2025.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Global Innovation Index 2025: India climbs to 38th
capsules.body: In the Global Innovation Index 2025 released by WIPO, India rose to 38th among 139 economies, up from 39th in 2024, and retained its lead in Central and Southern Asia with strengths in ICT services exports (1st), late-stage venture capital deals (4th) and unicorn valuation (11th). Switzerland topped the index for the 15th consecutive year, while China entered the top 10 for the first time at 10th place.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Saudi Arabia–Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement
capsules.body: On 17 September 2025 Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement under which aggression against one is treated as aggression against both — a NATO-style collective-defence clause. Exam significance: the mutual-defence wording; a likely question on West Asian security alignments.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 56th GST Council: 12% and 28% slabs scrapped (GST 2.0)
capsules.body: The 56th GST Council (3–4 September, New Delhi) scrapped the 12% and 28% slabs, creating a two-tier structure of 5% (merit) and 18% (standard), plus a 40% demerit rate for sin and luxury goods; individual life and health insurance were exempted. Effective 22 September 2025, it is dubbed the 'GST 2.0' reform. Exam structure: 5% + 18% + 40% demerit; insurance exempt.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI delists 474 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties
capsules.body: The Election Commission delisted 474 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties on 22 September 2025 for failing to contest any election in the preceding six years, part of its periodic clean-up of dormant outfits. Exam facts: 474 RUPPs delisted; reason = no contest in six years.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Ladakh protests (September)
capsules.body: September saw fresh protests in Ladakh demanding Sixth Schedule constitutional safeguards and statehood. Violence erupted in Leh on 24 September, including the torching of a BJP office, prompting tear-gas use. The agitation centres on constitutional protection for Ladakh's land, jobs and culture.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Mukhya Mantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana
capsules.body: PM Modi transferred the first instalment of Rs 7,500 crore on 25 September under the Bihar Mukhya Mantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana. A major Bihar-centric scheme delivering direct benefits to women - high priority for Bihar-specific exams.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: IAF retires its last MiG-21s (26 September)
capsules.body: The Indian Air Force retired its last MiG-21s on 26 September 2025, decommissioning No. 23 (Panthers) and No. 3 (Cobras) squadrons and ending the type's 62-year Indian service. The phase-out closes a long chapter in IAF fighter history.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana on September 26, 2025. In phase one, over 1.5 crore women receive a one-time Rs 10,000 through DBT to start businesses. Those who use it can get up to Rs 2 lakh in phase two. The scheme runs through BRLPS/JEEViKA, with the portal mmry.brlps.in (urban self-registration at mmryurban.brlps.in).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Mahila Rojgar phase two conditions
capsules.body: Phase two of the Mahila Rojgar Yojana requires the beneficiary to have invested the first Rs 10,000 in a business, run it for at least six months, and submit a utilisation certificate. Physical verification and regular self-help group attendance are needed, along with e-KYC. The government will also help market the products of beneficiary women.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India win Asia Cup 2025 (28 September, Dubai)
capsules.body: India won the Asia Cup 2025 in Dubai on 28 September, beating Pakistan by five wickets in the final. Tilak Varma's unbeaten 69 and Kuldeep Yadav's 4/30 powered a record-extending ninth title, with India unbeaten across all seven matches.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NISAR sends its first Earth images (30 September)
capsules.body: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite NISAR sent its first Earth images on 30 September 2025 as it readied for full operations. The joint mission marks a landmark in India-US space cooperation in Earth observation.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025 begins (30 September)
capsules.body: The ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025 began on 30 September 2025, co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India misses the September 2025 deadline for new NDC submission
capsules.body: India failed to submit its new or updated Nationally Determined Contribution by the 30 September 2025 deadline set under the Paris Agreement's five-year ambition cycle, a gap flagged by the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025. Only 64 parties, covering 63% of global emissions, had submitted new NDCs by then. India's existing NDC targets 50% cumulative electric power from non-fossil sources by 2030 and net zero by 2070, and the delay drew scrutiny ahead of COP30.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds repo rate at 5.5% (MPC, October 2025)
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee held the repo rate at 5.5% on 1 October 2025 — a second consecutive pause with a neutral stance. Governor Sanjay Malhotra's panel raised the FY26 GDP growth forecast to 6.8% (from 6.5%) and cut the CPI inflation projection to 2.6% (from 3.1%). Exam trio: repo 5.5%, GDP 6.8%, CPI 2.6%.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Bihar gains three new Ramsar sites in 2025
capsules.body: Bihar secured three new Ramsar designations in 2025: Gogabeel Lake in Katihar (October), and Gokul Jalashay and Udaipur Jheel (both September). Gogabeel is Bihar's first notified community reserve and an important oxbow lake of the Kosi river system, sheltering migratory ducks, geese and the endangered Indian skimmer. These additions significantly strengthen wetland conservation in the Gangetic plains of north Bihar.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Severe Cyclonic Storm Shakhti over the Arabian Sea
capsules.body: Severe Cyclonic Storm Shakhti formed over the northeast Arabian Sea and remained active from 1 to 7 October 2025, making it one of two named cyclonic storms in the Indian seas that October. It tracked near the Gujarat and Pakistan coasts, prompting IMD cyclone advisories and heavy-rainfall warnings for coastal Saurashtra and Kutch. Shakhti's relatively long six-day life marked an active post-monsoon cyclone phase in the Arabian Sea.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Global Hunger Index 2025: India at 102nd in 'serious' category
capsules.body: The Global Hunger Index 2025, released by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, ranked India 102nd out of 123 countries, placing it in the 'serious' hunger category. The index is computed from undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality. India's rank underscores persistent nutrition challenges despite its economic growth, a point frequently tested in competitive examinations.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar Assembly election schedule announced (6 October)
capsules.body: The Election Commission announced the Bihar Assembly election schedule on 6 October 2025: 243 seats, phase-wise polling on 6 and 11 November (121 seats first, 122 next), with counting on 14 November 2025.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna Metro first phase opens
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the first phase of the Patna Metro on October 6, 2025. The 3.45-km priority corridor links Patliputra Bus Terminal (ISBT), Zero Mile and Bhoothnath. Fares are Rs 15 and Rs 30, trains run 8 am to 10 pm at 20-minute intervals with 40-42 trips daily, coaches carry Madhubani artwork, and BSAP jawans guard the stations.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna Metro full plan
capsules.body: The Patna Metro project costs Rs 13,925.5 crore, funded by JICA with the Centre and the state. The Red Line spans 16.86 km and the Blue Line 14.56 km, covering 24 stations in all. Line 1 runs East-West from Danapur to Khemnichak and Line 2 North-South from Patna Junction to New ISBT, with interchanges at Patna Junction and Khemnichak.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel 2025 overview medicine
capsules.body: The 2025 Nobel Prizes were announced from October 6 to 13, with the ceremony on December 10. The Medicine prize went to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells, with applications in autoimmune disease and transplantation.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel physics chemistry
capsules.body: The Physics Nobel went to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret and John M. Martinis for discovering macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit. The Chemistry prize went to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), porous materials used in gas storage, separation and catalysis.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel literature peace economics
capsules.body: The Literature Nobel went to Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai. The Peace Prize was awarded to Venezuela's Maria Corina Machado for her work for democratic rights and a just, peaceful transition from dictatorship to democracy. The Economics prize went to Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt for explaining innovation-led growth and creative destruction.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Cochin Shipyard delivers 'Mahe' to the Navy
capsules.body: On 24 October, Cochin Shipyard handed over 'Mahe' to the Indian Navy - a lead vessel of an entirely home-designed class of shallow-water anti-submarine warships. The delivery adds a domestically built ASW platform for guarding coastal waters and sea lanes.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: US sanctions Colombian President Gustavo Petro
capsules.body: The United States sanctioned Colombian President Gustavo Petro on 24 October, escalating a counternarcotics standoff between Washington and Bogota. A notable international-relations flashpoint over drug policy and sovereignty.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Cyclone Montha batters the Andhra coast (28 October)
capsules.body: Severe Cyclone Montha made landfall near Kakinada on the Andhra Pradesh coast on 28 October 2025, with winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph. Crops across 38,000-plus hectares were damaged in the storm's wake.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Severe Cyclonic Storm Montha strikes Andhra Pradesh coast
capsules.body: Severe Cyclonic Storm Montha developed over the southwest Bay of Bengal during 25-30 October 2025 and crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast between Machilipatnam and Kalingapatnam, near Kakinada, on 28 October with sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph. Orange alerts were issued for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and adjoining south Odisha. Montha was the Bay of Bengal's first September-October named storm in the region since Gulab in 2021.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2025 flags massive finance shortfall
capsules.body: The UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2025 reported that global adaptation finance stood at only about USD 26 billion a year, while developing nations will need USD 310-365 billion annually by the mid-2030s. It noted that 172 countries now have at least one national adaptation framework, but implementation remains weak and debt-heavy funding dominates. For India, the report flagged vulnerabilities to heat stress, erratic monsoons and coastal flooding alongside its National Adaptation Fund and state action plans.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Gahirmatha seven-month fishing ban (1 Nov–31 May)
capsules.body: Odisha enforces its annual seven-month fishing ban at Gahirmatha from 1 November to 31 May to protect nesting Olive Ridley turtles, which arrive here for mass nesting in one of the world's largest arribadas. Exam link: Gahirmatha (Odisha) = Olive Ridley conservation; ban window Nov–May.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: India's first digital Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum in Chhattisgarh
capsules.body: India's first fully digital museum on tribal freedom fighters is coming up in Chhattisgarh, ahead of the state's 25th foundation day on 1 November. It will showcase tribal heroes of the independence struggle through interactive digital exhibits. Exam first: maiden digital tribal-freedom-fighter museum; state = Chhattisgarh.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025: 'Off Target'
capsules.body: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2025, titled 'Off Target', found global greenhouse gas emissions rose 2.3% in 2024 to 57.7 gigatonnes of CO2 equivalent, with India and China recording the largest absolute increases though India's per-capita emissions stayed below the world average. It warned emissions must fall 55% by 2035 to stay on a 1.5 degC path, and noted that by the 30 September 2025 deadline only 64 parties had submitted new or updated NDCs, while G20 members accounted for 77% of global emissions.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Survey vessel 'Ikshak' commissioned at Kochi (6 November)
capsules.body: The Navy's third survey vessel of her class, 'Ikshak', was commissioned at Kochi on 6 November 2025, strengthening India's hydrographic survey and ocean-mapping capacity.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Tropical Forest Forever Facility and ARISE launched at COP30
capsules.body: During the COP30 World Leaders' Summit (6-7 November 2025), Brazil launched the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, a dedicated funding mechanism to reward tropical forest conservation. The Climate Investment Funds launched the ARISE programme for least developed countries and small island states, with Germany and Spain committing USD 100 million combined. Separately, the Democratic Republic of Congo launched a National Digital Carbon Credit Registry to regulate its carbon-market projects.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Uttarakhand observed its Foundation Day on 9 November 2025
capsules.body: Uttarakhand observed its Foundation Day on 9 November 2025. The hill state was carved out of Uttar Pradesh in the year 2000 as the 27th state of India.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Blast near Delhi's Red Fort (10 November 2025)
capsules.body: On 10 November 2025 a Hyundai i20 exploded near Gate 1 of the Red Fort Metro Station in Delhi, killing 13 people. The case was registered under the UAPA and the Explosives Act, with a multi-agency investigation launched. Exam anchors: Red Fort Metro Gate 1, 13 deaths, UAPA + Explosives Act.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: COP30 in Belem adopts the Belem Package of 29 decisions
capsules.body: The 30th UN climate conference (COP30) was held at Belem, Brazil, from 10 to 21 November 2025, the first COP in the Amazon. All 195 Parties adopted the Belem Package: a call to mobilise at least USD 1.3 trillion per year in climate finance by 2035, a commitment to triple adaptation finance by 2035, conclusion of the Baku Adaptation Roadmap, 59 voluntary indicators to track the Global Goal on Adaptation, and a new Just Transition Mechanism. Critics noted the package lacked a firm commitment on transitioning away from fossil fuels.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar election 2025 results
capsules.body: The NDA won 202 of 243 seats in the 2025 Bihar Assembly election. The BJP won 89, JD(U) 85, LJP (Ram Vilas) 19, HAM(S) 5 and RLM 4. The Mahagathbandhan managed 35, with the RJD at 25 and the Congress at 6. Nitish Kumar took oath for a record tenth term as Chief Minister on November 20, 2025, at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, in the presence of Prime Minister Modi.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: COP31 awarded to Antalya, Turkiye for November 2026
capsules.body: After a rare bidding standoff at COP30, a deal brokered on 19 November 2025 gave COP31 to Antalya, Turkiye (9-20 November 2026), with Turkiye holding the presidency under Minister Murat Kurum and Australia leading negotiations as vice-president; a pre-COP will be held in a Pacific island nation. The incoming presidency launched the Antalya Pledge on AI-energy alignment and the 35x35 initiative to raise electricity's share of final energy use to 35% by 2035.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Nitish tenth oath at Gandhi Maidan
capsules.body: Nitish Kumar was sworn in for a record tenth term as Chief Minister on November 20, 2025, at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah present. The 26-member ministry included two deputy chief ministers, and Governor Arif Mohammed Khan administered the oath, marking another NDA tenure for the veteran leader.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: CAQM tightens GRAP schedule for Delhi-NCR pollution
capsules.body: On 21 November 2025, the Commission for Air Quality Management revised the Graded Response Action Plan for Delhi-NCR, making it more stringent by pulling measures one stage earlier: curbs once reserved for Stage IV (Severe+) now apply at Stage III (AQI 401-450), and so on down the ladder. GRAP Stage III was invoked on 13 December 2025 when AQI touched 401, bringing construction bans, BS-III petrol/BS-IV diesel four-wheeler restrictions and hybrid classes up to Class 5; Stage IV was invoked again in January 2026.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: COP30 text acknowledges climate disinformation for the first time
capsules.body: For the first time in UN climate negotiations, the COP30 Belem Package text acknowledged the need to tackle climate disinformation, pledging to promote information integrity and counter narratives that undermine science-based action. The conference also launched the Belem Health Action Plan to strengthen health systems against climate impacts, and the Global Implementation Accelerator plus the Belem Mission to 1.5C to help countries deliver their NDCs and national adaptation plans.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Cyclones Senyar and Ditwah close out 2025; costliest NIO season on record
capsules.body: Cyclonic Storm Senyar formed over the Strait of Malacca (25-27 November 2025) while Cyclonic Storm Ditwah churned over the southwest Bay of Bengal off Sri Lanka (26 November-3 December 2025). Together with Shakhti and Montha, they capped the 2025 North Indian Ocean season, which became the costliest on record, surpassing the 2020 season, after a series of deep depressions also brought extreme monsoon rainfall to Kolkata and coastal states.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: US boycotts Johannesburg G20; South Africa disinvited from 2026 summit
capsules.body: The US skipped the closing events of the G20 summit in Johannesburg on 22-23 November 2025, the first G20 ever held in Africa, and on 26 November 2025 President Trump announced South Africa would not be invited to the 2026 summit, citing alleged human-rights violations against white farmers and mishandling of the presidency handover. President Ramaphosa called the exclusion 'regrettable and punitive', and Germany and Japan raised concerns over the precedent of excluding a founding member.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: FIDE Chess World Cup, Goa: Sindarov youngest-ever champion
capsules.body: Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, aged 19, got the better of China's Wei Yi in the tiebreaks to win the FIDE Chess World Cup in Goa (31 Oct-27 Nov 2025), becoming the youngest-ever champion. The trophy was renamed the Viswanathan Anand Cup, and the top three finishers qualified for the 2026 Candidates Tournament.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 56th IFFI (Goa, 20-28 November)
capsules.body: At the 56th International Film Festival of India in Goa (20-28 November 2025), the Vietnamese film Skin of Youth, directed by Ash Mayfair, received the Golden Peacock for Best Film.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Eleven new Ramsar sites in 2025; first designations for three states
capsules.body: India added eleven Ramsar sites in 2025: Sakkarakottai and Therthangal (Tamil Nadu), Khecheopalri (Sikkim), Udhwa Lake (Jharkhand), Khichan and Menar (Rajasthan), Gokul Jalashay, Udaipur Jheel and Gogabeel (Bihar), Siliserh (Rajasthan) and Kopra Jalashay (Chhattisgarh). Notably, Chhattisgarh, Sikkim and Jharkhand received their first-ever Ramsar designations, while Tamil Nadu's total rose to 20, the highest for any Indian state.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: United States assumes G20 presidency; 2026 summit set for Miami
capsules.body: The United States assumed the G20 presidency on 1 December 2025 and will host the Leaders' Summit on 14-15 December 2026 at Trump National Doral in Miami, Florida, coinciding with America's 250th anniversary. The US agenda emphasises economic prosperity through deregulation, affordable and reliable energy, and pioneering new technologies like AI and quantum computing. The first Sherpa meeting under the US presidency was held in Washington on 15-16 December 2025.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Parliament passes VB–G Ram G Bill, replacing MGNREGA
capsules.body: Parliament passed the VB–G Ram G Bill on 18 December 2025, replacing MGNREGA with the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission. It guarantees 125 days of rural wage employment (up from MGNREGA's 100), funded 60:40 by the Centre and states (90:10 for northeastern/Himalayan states and UTs). Exam facts: 125 days; replaces MGNREGA; 60:40 / 90:10 funding.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Parliament passes SHANTI Bill on nuclear energy
capsules.body: Parliament passed the SHANTI Bill — Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India — on 18 December 2025. It replaces the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, opens civil nuclear energy to regulated Indian private participation, and grants the AERB statutory status. Exam core: two Acts replaced; private entry into nuclear; AERB statutory.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: ICGS 'Samudra Pratap' dedicated to the nation (Jan 5)
capsules.body: ICGS 'Samudra Pratap', India's first indigenous pollution-control vessel built by Goa Shipyard Limited, was dedicated to the nation on 5 January 2026. The ship gives the Indian Coast Guard a dedicated platform for marine pollution response.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: CSIR-NPL's National Environmental Standard Laboratory inaugurated (Jan 5)
capsules.body: CSIR-NPL's National Environmental Standard Laboratory was inaugurated on 5 January 2026 - the world's second and Asia's first facility for testing and certifying air-pollution monitoring devices. It directly supports the National Clean Air Programme's need for reliable, standardised pollution measurement.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 55 scholarly works in classical languages released (Jan 6)
capsules.body: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan released 55 scholarly works in classical languages on 6 January 2026, covering Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Odia and Tamil classics, along with a 45-episode sign-language series on the Tirukkural.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: US withdraws from 66 international bodies including India-led ISA (Jan 7)
capsules.body: Through an executive order under its 'America First' review, the United States withdrew from 66 international bodies on 7 January 2026 - including the India-led International Solar Alliance, IRENA, IPCC, IUCN, UNFCCC, UNFPA and UN Water - and formally exited the WHO after 78 years of membership.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India becomes the world's first country to commercially produce bio-bitumen
capsules.body: India became the world's first country to commercially produce bio-bitumen, announced on 7 January 2026 by Minister Nitin Gadkari. The CSIR-developed technology converts paddy straw through pyrolysis; 15% blending in bitumen can save roughly Rs 4,500 crore in foreign exchange while giving farmers value for crop residue.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New hexapod Lepidocampa sikkimensis described from Sikkim
capsules.body: ZSI scientists described Lepidocampa sikkimensis, a new species of Diplura, a primitive wingless group of soil-dwelling hexapods, from near Ravangla in Sikkim, with findings published on 7 January 2026 in the journal Zootaxa. It was the first time an Indian research team formally described a Diplura species, ending a nearly 50-year domestic research gap on the group. The discovery highlights the eastern Himalaya's poorly documented soil biodiversity.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visits India
capsules.body: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited India on 12–13 January 2026, travelling to Ahmedabad and Bengaluru. The two sides signed 19 strategic agreements covering defence technology, critical minerals, supply chains and clean energy. Exam facts: Chancellor Merz, two cities, 19 pacts across four sectors.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO's PSLV-C62 mission faces third-stage anomaly
capsules.body: ISRO's PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission, the 64th PSLV flight, suffered a third-stage anomaly on 12 January 2026. It carried DRDO's strategic surveillance satellite Anvesha plus 15 co-passengers (seven from Dhruva Space), and was NSIL's ninth dedicated commercial launch; mission data is under analysis. Exam core: 64th flight, Anvesha, third-stage snag.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: 2023, 2024 and 2025 confirmed as the three warmest years on record
capsules.body: Copernicus C3S data confirmed that 2023, 2024 and 2025 are the three warmest years on record globally, extending a streak of monthly temperatures above the 1.5 degC Paris Agreement threshold. Analysts project the long-term 1.5 degC limit, once expected around 2045, could now be reached as early as May 2029 on current trends. The finding raised the stakes for COP31's review of the 2035 NDCs submitted ahead of COP30.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: UN High Seas Treaty enters into force
capsules.body: The UN High Seas Treaty — the first legally binding agreement covering ocean areas beyond national jurisdiction — entered into force on 17 January 2026 after ratification by 60+ countries. It governs marine biodiversity, environmental impact assessments and benefit-sharing on the high seas. Exam core: BBNJ treaty; 60+ ratifications; in force January 2026.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: India's first sleeper Vande Bharat flagged off
capsules.body: India's first sleeper Vande Bharat Express was flagged off on 17 January 2026 on the Howrah–Kamakhya (Guwahati) route, departing from Malda Town in West Bengal. Unlike existing chair-car Vande Bharats, it has berths for overnight journeys. Exam first: maiden sleeper Vande Bharat; route Howrah–Kamakhya.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: High Seas Treaty (BBNJ) enters into force
capsules.body: The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), popularly the High Seas Treaty, entered into force on 17 January 2026 after crossing 60 ratifications in September 2025. Adopted in June 2023 under UNCLOS 1982, it is the first legally binding treaty for marine biodiversity in international waters, built on four pillars: marine genetic resources and benefit-sharing, area-based management tools including marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments, and capacity-building and technology transfer. India signed in 2024 but had not ratified by entry into force.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Rare red aurora over Hanle, Ladakh
capsules.body: A rare red aurora appeared over Hanle, Ladakh, on 19–20 January 2026, triggered by an X-class solar flare and a 1,700 km/s coronal mass ejection. The resulting G4 geomagnetic and S4 solar-radiation storm was the fiercest since 2003 — India's first well-documented red aurora. Exam science: X-class flare + CME → aurora at unusually low latitudes; Hanle observatory.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Responsible Nations Index: India ranked 16th
capsules.body: Former President Ram Nath Kovind launched the Responsible Nations Index on 19 January, in which India ranked 16th with a score of 0.551513. Singapore topped the index, ahead of France, the US and China. Exam data: India 16th (0.551513); top = Singapore.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma Awards 2026: 131 honours
capsules.body: The Padma Awards 2026 - 131 honours announced on Republic Day eve (25 January): 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri. Maharashtra topped the state tally with 15 awardees.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma Awards 2026 announced
capsules.body: The Padma Awards 2026, announced on January 25, conferred 131 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri, including two duo cases. Among them were 19 women, six foreigners/NRI/PIO/OCI recipients and 16 posthumous awardees, keeping the annual tradition of recognising excellence across fields.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma Vibhushan Bhushan names
capsules.body: Padma Vibhushan went posthumously to actor Dharmendra and former Kerala chief minister V. S. Achuthanandan. Padma Bhushan recipients included singer Alka Yagnik, tennis great Vijay Amritraj, actor Mammootty, banker Uday Kotak and adman Piyush Pandey, with Shibu Soren and V. K. Malhotra honoured posthumously.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma Shri sportspersons
capsules.body: Cricketers Rohit Sharma and Harmanpreet Kaur were among the Padma Shri recipients for 2026, alongside actor R. Madhavan, actor Prosenjit Chatterjee and late actor Satish Shah. The honours recognised sporting excellence in a year India won two cricket world titles.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma unsung heroes
capsules.body: Forty-five unsung heroes were honoured with Padma awards for grassroots work in literature, social work, tribal welfare, animal husbandry, traditional medicine and the environment. They include Anke Gowda (literature) and Techi Gubin (social work), drawn from marginalised communities, Divyangjan, women, children and tribal groups.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 77th Republic Day 2026 celebrated on Jan 26
capsules.body: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day on 26 January 2026 with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa as the chief guests. The theme was '150 Years of Vande Mataram'. The parade was the first held after Operation Sindoor, featured about 10,000 special guests, and Delhi Metro travel was free that day.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: EU leaders attend India's Republic Day as chief guests for the first time
capsules.body: European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen attended India's Republic Day celebrations on 26 January 2026 as chief guests, described as an unprecedented first, before the 16th India-EU Summit concluded the historic FTA the next day. PM Modi noted bilateral trade had reached 180 billion euros and over eight lakh Indians reside in EU countries, underlining the people-to-people pillar of the partnership.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: India-EU Free Trade Agreement concluded ('Mother of All Deals')
capsules.body: At the 16th India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026, India and the European Union concluded their Free Trade Agreement, hailed as the 'Mother of All Deals'. It is among the most significant trade pacts India has signed, cementing the economic partnership forged with the EU.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: India's first-ever Defence & Security Partnership with the EU
capsules.body: Alongside the FTA at the 16th India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026, India signed its first-ever Defence and Security Partnership with the European Union. The pact opens the EU's SAFE defence financing instrument to Indian companies, deepening defence-industrial cooperation between the two sides.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-EU Free Trade Agreement concluded after two decades
capsules.body: On 27 January 2026, at the 16th India-EU Summit in New Delhi, PM Modi with European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, hailed as India's biggest trade deal. Negotiations ran from 2007 to 2013 and were relaunched in 2022. Von der Leyen said it would cut up to 4 billion euros in annual tariffs. A Security and Defence Partnership and a mobility framework for Indian professionals were also agreed.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India the world's 4th largest economy; EU its biggest goods trade partner
capsules.body: A 27 January 2026 PIB release on the India-EU FTA described India as the world's 4th largest economy, having overtaken Japan in nominal GDP during 2025. India's bilateral goods trade with the EU stood at USD 136.53 billion in 2024-25 (exports USD 75.85 billion), making the EU India's largest goods trading partner, accounting for about 17% of India's total exports. Over 99% of Indian exports are set to gain preferential entry into the EU under the FTA.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-Dhand join Ramsar list, January 2026
