capsules.body: Ahead of World Wetlands Day 2026, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced two new Ramsar sites on 30 January 2026: Patna Bird Sanctuary in Etah, Uttar Pradesh (108.9 ha), and Chhari-Dhand in Kutch, Gujarat (about 22,700 ha). Chhari-Dhand is one of India's largest saline wetlands, famed for flamingos and migratory waterbirds, and ranks among the biggest recent Indian additions by area.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Union Budget 2026-27 presented on 1 February
capsules.body: Nirmala Sitharaman presented her ninth consecutive Union Budget on 1 February 2026 — the first budget delivered from Kartavya Bhawan. Framed around three Kartavyas (accelerating growth, meeting aspirations, access for all), it targets a fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP and provides capex of Rs 12.2 lakh crore. Exam anchors: 9th straight budget, Kartavya theme trio, 4.3% deficit, Rs 12.2 lakh crore capex.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Alcaraz career Grand Slam
capsules.body: Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic 2-6, 6-2, 6-3, 7-5 in the Australian Open final on February 1, 2026. At 22 years 272 days he became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, with seven major titles, and denied Djokovic a 25th major.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Economic Survey 2025-26 tabled
capsules.body: Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav presented the 20th Bihar Economic Survey 2025-26 in the Assembly on February 2, 2026, covering 2024-25. It was prepared by the Bihar Institute of Public Finance and Policy. The Survey shows Bihar growing faster than the national average for the third straight year, driven mainly by manufacturing and construction, with the secondary sector's share of GSVA climbing sharply.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar GSDP nears 10 lakh crore
capsules.body: Bihar's GSDP in 2024-25 stood at Rs 9,91,997 crore at current prices and Rs 5,31,372 crore at constant (2011-12) prices. Growth was 13.1% at current prices and 8.6% at constant prices, compared with India's 9.8% and 6.5%. The figures confirm Bihar outperformed the national economy for a third consecutive year on both nominal and real measures.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Per capita GSDP rises to 76490
capsules.body: Bihar's per capita GSDP reached Rs 76,490 at current prices in 2024-25, up from Rs 66,828 the previous year, and Rs 40,973 at constant prices, up from Rs 36,333. Net State Domestic Product was Rs 8,99,020 crore. Per capita NSDP at constant prices was Rs 36,342, only 31.7% of the all-India average, showing the gap with national income levels remains wide.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sectoral shift in Bihar economy
capsules.body: In 2024-25, the tertiary sector held 54.8% of Bihar's GSVA, the secondary sector rose to 26.8% from 21.1% in 2020-21, and the primary sector stood at 18.3%. At constant prices the secondary sector grew 11.1%, tertiary 8.9% and primary 4.1%. At current prices they grew 15.5%, 13.5% and 9.6% respectively, signalling a clear tilt toward manufacturing and construction.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Manufacturing boom in Bihar
capsules.body: The Survey notes that Bihar's above-average growth came chiefly from manufacturing and construction within the secondary sector, which grew 15.5% at current prices in 2024-25. Gross Fixed Capital Formation nearly doubled from Rs 17,416 crore to Rs 34,905 crore over five years, indicating a strong investment push into the state's industrial base.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar fiscal position 2024-25
capsules.body: Bihar's total expenditure in 2024-25 was Rs 2,81,939 crore. Outstanding debt stood at Rs 3,74,134 crore, or 37.7% of GSDP. The fiscal deficit was 4.2% of GSDP, while the state carried only a small revenue deficit of Rs 357 crore. Finance Minister Yadav described the state's finances as in good shape while tabling the Survey.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Three-year growth outperformance
capsules.body: Bihar has beaten national growth for three years running. At current prices its GSDP grew 17.9% in 2022-23 and 14.9% in 2023-24, against India's 14.0% and 12.0%. In 2024-25 Bihar grew 13.1% nominally versus India's 9.8%. Commenting on the figures, the government claimed the state was growing 3.3 percentage points faster than the national average.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Crop pattern in Bihar
capsules.body: In Bihar's cereal production, rice accounted for 40.7%, wheat for 32.1% and maize for 27.1%. Maize production rose 12.6% in 2024-25. The Survey highlights these shares while reporting the primary sector grew 9.6% at current prices and 4.1% at constant prices during the year.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Human development indicators
capsules.body: For 2019-23, life expectancy in Bihar was 68.9 years for males and 69.7 for females, roughly matching the national trend. The state's literacy rate stood at 61.8%, while per capita health spending rose to Rs 2,206. The figures form the human-development baseline of the 2025-26 Survey.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar district rankings
capsules.body: Patna, Begusarai and Munger ranked highest on district GDP and per capita income, while Sheohar, Araria and Sitamarhi were at the bottom. Patna also recorded the highest consumption of petrol, diesel and LPG among districts. The Survey presents these contrasts as a measure of regional disparity within the state.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Employment structure in Bihar
capsules.body: Employment in Bihar was dominated by the primary sector with 54%, while the secondary sector employed 24% and the tertiary sector 22%. The overall unemployment rate was 3% under the PLFS for 2023-24. The data underline how jobs remain concentrated in agriculture even as manufacturing-led output growth accelerates.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Banking and roads in Bihar
capsules.body: Bihar's credit-deposit ratio was 56.3%, with bank deposits of Rs 5.27 lakh crore and advances of Rs 2.97 lakh crore. On infrastructure, the state held 5.5% of India's road network, and the transport sector grew at 13.4% annually over the last decade, supporting the wider economic expansion.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Growth 3.3 percent above national average
capsules.body: Bihar's growth of 13.1% at current prices in 2024-25 stood 3.3 percentage points above the national average of 9.8%. Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav credited the visionary role of Prime Minister Modi and Nitish Kumar for Viksit Bihar while tabling the Survey, terming the state's finances in good shape.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 16th Finance Commission retains states' vertical devolution at 41% (2026-31)
capsules.body: The 16th Finance Commission retained the states' share in the vertical devolution of central taxes at 41% for 2026-31, announced on 3 February 2026. Urban local body grants rise 230% to Rs 3.56 trillion, and Rs 1.4 lakh crore was announced for states in the budget.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Budget 2026-27 outlay
capsules.body: Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav presented Bihar's largest-ever budget on February 3, 2026, with total expenditure of Rs 3,47,589.76 crore. It was about Rs 30,000 crore higher than the previous year's Rs 3.17 lakh crore budget. The budget consolidates schemes under Saat Nischay-3 (2025-2030) with the declared theme of a developed Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar fiscal targets 2026-27
capsules.body: The budget projects GSDP of Rs 13,09,155 crore with 15% nominal growth. The fiscal deficit is estimated at Rs 39,111.80 crore, or 2.99% of GSDP, within the 3% FRBM limit. The revenue account stays in surplus at Rs 1,143.19 crore, or 0.09% of GSDP, despite the record spending outlay.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Top budget allocations
capsules.body: Education received the highest allocation of Rs 60,204 crore, followed by Health at Rs 21,270 crore, Home at Rs 20,132 crore and Energy at Rs 18,737 crore. Schemes for social justice and welfare got Rs 7,724 crore under the principle of Nyay ke Saath Vikas (development with justice).

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Budget expenditure breakup
capsules.body: Establishment and committed expenditure was put at Rs 2,25,434.34 crore, the annual scheme outlay at Rs 1,22,155.42 crore and revenue expenditure at Rs 2,84,133.92 crore. Development expenditure of Rs 2,31,267 crore makes up 66.53% of total spending, against 33.47% for non-development spending.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar debt projections
capsules.body: Outstanding public debt is projected at Rs 3,88,554 crore (29.68% of GSDP) by end-2026-27, and total debt including public account liabilities at Rs 4,46,326 crore (34.09%). The budget states these stay within the limits prescribed by the 15th Finance Commission.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Infrastructure announcements
capsules.body: The budget proposes five new expressways, more than 2,000 public EV charging stations, and conversion of public buses to CNG and electric vehicles. Solar energy expansion, affordable housing for the poor, and tourism development were also announced, with industry bodies calling the outlay industry-friendly.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Education and health proposals
capsules.body: The budget proposes model schools and degree colleges in every block of Bihar. District hospitals are to be upgraded into superspecialty facilities, and health and education infrastructure receive top billing as the state pushes its human-development agenda under Saat Nischay-3.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Agriculture roadmap four
capsules.body: The fourth agricultural roadmap gets budget backing alongside support for dairy, fisheries, animal husbandry and the makhana industry. Haat-bazaars are proposed to market local products. The Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi aims to raise farmers' incomes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Budget vision five pillars
capsules.body: The budget rests on five pillars named imaan, gyaan, vigyaan, armaan and samman, standing for integrity, knowledge, science, aspiration and self-respect. It targets Viksit Bihar with priorities of education, technology, innovation, social justice, women, farmers, youth and entrepreneurs.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Other budget announcements
capsules.body: The budget proposes Industrial Manufacturing Cluster phase-2 at Gaya, affordable housing, home-based healthcare for the elderly, and doorstep property-registration services. Sports infrastructure and the film-policy push also received provisions, consolidating the state's welfare-to-growth pipeline.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: One crore jobs target by 2030
capsules.body: In his address to the joint sitting before the budget, the Bihar Governor set a target of creating one crore jobs and employment opportunities in the state by 2030. The target anchors the budget's emphasis on youth, startups and entrepreneurship.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Capital spending in budget
capsules.body: The budget provides capital outlay of Rs 39,377.06 crore and total capital expenditure of Rs 63,455.84 crore. Interest payments are estimated at 8.89% of revenue receipts, and the state's own tax revenue is expected to contribute about Rs 65,800 crore.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: JEEViKA Lakhpati Didis
capsules.body: Bihar has 43 lakh Lakhpati Didis, with a target of creating one crore more through JEEViKA (BRLPS). The rural livelihood mission works in all 38 districts and 534 blocks, and underpins the Mahila Rojgar Yojana and other women-entrepreneurship programmes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Two lakh to eligible women
capsules.body: Presenting the budget, the Finance Minister reiterated that eligible women will receive Rs 2 lakh under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, and the process has already begun. The pledge links the budget to the scheme launched by the Prime Minister in September 2025.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Godavari-Krishna link DPR circulated; other links in pipeline
capsules.body: A February 2026 Rajya Sabha reply recorded that the DPR for the modified Godavari (Inchampalli)-Krishna (Nagarjunasagar) link was circulated to party states in January 2024, with a draft memorandum of agreement shared in April 2024. The Krishna (Nagarjunasagar)-Pennar (Somasila) link also saw progress. While Ken-Betwa remains the only ILR link under implementation, these peninsular links show the National Water Development Agency's inter-basin transfer programme advancing beyond the first project.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Tarique Rahman becomes Bangladesh's 11th Prime Minister
capsules.body: Tarique Rahman became Bangladesh's 11th Prime Minister on 17 February 2026 after his BNP swept 212 of 299 parliamentary seats. Exam facts: 11th PM of Bangladesh; party = Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP); 212/299 seats.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: MILAN 2026: 74 nations at Visakhapatnam
capsules.body: The Navy's multilateral exercise MILAN 2026 ran from 15–25 February at Visakhapatnam with 74 participating nations — its largest edition — featuring the International Fleet Review on 18 February. India also assumed the IONS chairmanship for 2026–28. Exam numbers: 74 nations; Visakhapatnam; IONS chair 2026–28.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Joint exercises: Khanjar XIII, Dharma Guardian 7th, Vajra Prahar 16th
capsules.body: February 2026 packed three major bilateral drills: KHANJAR-XIII, the 13th India-Kyrgyzstan exercise at Missamari (4-17 Feb); DHARMA GUARDIAN 7th edition with Japan at Chaubattia (24 Feb-9 Mar); and VAJRA PRAHAR 16th edition with the United States at Bakloh (23 Feb-15 Mar).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Vayushakti-26 at Pokhran; INS Anjadip commissioned; CTS Krishna launched
capsules.body: The IAF's Vayushakti-26 firepower demonstration took place at Pokhran on 27 February 2026. On the naval side, INS Anjadip - the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft built by GRSE - was commissioned, and the CTS 'Krishna' was launched at L&T Kattupalli.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India wins T20 World Cup 2026
capsules.body: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the final on March 8, 2026, at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, to win the ICC Men's T20 World Cup. It was India's third title after 2007 and 2024. India became the first team to successfully defend the T20 World Cup and the first host to win it. Suryakumar Yadav captained the side; India and Sri Lanka jointly hosted.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: T20 WC 2026 records
capsules.body: The 2026 edition set tournament records: India's 255 for 5 in the final was the highest score in a knockout match, the 96-run win was the biggest knockout-margin victory, India hit 106 sixes (first team past 100 in one edition), and seven centuries were scored (most in an edition). The tournament had 20 teams, 55 matches, and India took home USD 3 million in prize money.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: T20 WC individual feats
capsules.body: Pakistan's Sahibzada Farhan set a single-edition record with 383 runs. Sanju Samson was Player of the Tournament with a strike rate of 199.38. New Zealand's Finn Allen hit the fastest T20 World Cup century off 33 balls, and Jasprit Bumrah and Varun Chakravarthy shared 14 wickets each to top the bowling charts.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Oscars 2026 winners
capsules.body: The 98th Academy Awards were held on March 15, 2026, hosted by Conan O'Brien. One Battle After Another won Best Picture, and Paul Thomas Anderson won Best Director, with the film taking six Oscars including the first-ever Academy Award for Casting. Michael B. Jordan won Best Actor for Sinners and Jessie Buckley Best Actress for Hamnet.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Oscars India connection
capsules.body: India's official entry Homebound was shortlisted but did not make the final Oscar nominations. Documentaries by Geeta Gandbhir earned two nominations, and Priyanka Chopra presented an award. Sinners, with a record 16 nominations, won four Oscars; Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman of colour to win cinematography, and Sean Penn and Amy Madigan won supporting acting honours.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Jnanpith 2025 Vairamuthu
capsules.body: Tamil poet and lyricist R. Vairamuthu was selected for the 60th Jnanpith Award for 2025. He is the third Tamil recipient after Akilan (1975) and Jayakanthan (2002). With more than 7,000 film songs to his credit, he previously won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2003, the Padma Shri in 2003 and the Padma Bhushan in 2014.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31
capsules.body: On 18 March 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs 2,584.60 crore to install about 1,500 MW of small hydro projects (1-25 MW each), especially in hilly and north-eastern states. Central assistance reaches Rs 3.6 crore per MW in the North-East and international-border districts and Rs 2.4 crore per MW elsewhere, and is expected to leverage Rs 15,000 crore of investment using fully indigenous plant and machinery.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Modified UDAN approved with Rs 28,840 crore outlay
capsules.body: On 25 March 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Regional Connectivity Scheme - Modified UDAN for ten years (FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36) with a total outlay of Rs 28,840 crore. It proposes developing 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips, O&M support for around 441 aerodromes, and modern helipads, targeting underserved and unserved areas to boost Tier-2 and Tier-3 connectivity, tourism and emergency healthcare access.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Shekha Jheel, Aligarh declared India's 99th Ramsar site
capsules.body: Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary in Aligarh district, Uttar Pradesh, was designated India's 99th Ramsar site in April 2026, shortly before Surha Tal became the 100th. A shallow seasonal wetland on the Central Asian Flyway, it hosts large congregations of bar-headed geese, northern pintails and other migratory ducks each winter. The back-to-back additions in early 2026 pushed Uttar Pradesh's tally to 13 Ramsar sites, second only to Tamil Nadu.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Taragiri commissioned
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commissioned INS Taragiri, an advanced stealth frigate, at Visakhapatnam on 3 April 2026. The 6,670-tonne Project 17A warship, built by Mazagon Dock, carries over 75% indigenous content.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Samrat Choudhary first BJP CM
capsules.body: Samrat Choudhary took oath on April 15, 2026, as the 24th Chief Minister of Bihar and the state's first BJP chief minister. The oath was administered by Governor Lt Gen (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain at Lok Bhavan. Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav of the JD(U) were sworn in as deputy chief ministers. Nitish Kumar had resigned and taken oath as a Rajya Sabha MP on April 10, 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Samrat Choudhary profile
capsules.body: Born in 1968, Samrat Choudhary is the son of Shakuni Choudhary, a six-time MLA from Tarapur, and Parvati Devi. He began in politics with the RJD before joining the BJP in 2018, and served as Bihar's Deputy Chief Minister before his elevation as the first BJP chief minister of the state.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Three-member Bihar cabinet
capsules.body: The new ministry began with three members: BJP's Samrat Choudhary as Chief Minister and two JD(U) deputy chief ministers, Vijay Kumar Choudhary (seven-time MLA) and Bijendra Prasad Yadav (nine-time MLA). A cabinet expansion is expected in the first week of May 2026, after the West Bengal and Tamil Nadu elections.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Syed Ata Hasnain Bihar governor
capsules.body: Lt Gen (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain is the Governor of Bihar and administered the oath to Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary in April 2026. He succeeded Arif Mohammed Khan, who had administered the oath to Nitish Kumar's ministry in November 2025, in the governor's office.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: PM Modi visits Sikkim (Apr 27-28)
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Sikkim on 27-28 April 2026 and inaugurated development projects worth about Rs 4,000 crore in the state.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Suvendu Adhikari sworn in as West Bengal Chief Minister on 9 May 2026
capsules.body: Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in as West Bengal Chief Minister on 9 May 2026, ending 15 years of Trinamool Congress rule and - a state first - installing a BJP-led government after a landslide victory.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: BIS notifies IS 19850:2026 — India's first fuel standard beyond E20
capsules.body: BIS notified IS 19850:2026 (Gazette 18 May; effective 15 May 2026) — India's first fuel-quality standard for petrol blends beyond E20, covering E22, E25, E27 and E30. It lays down specifications as the country moves past the 20% ethanol-blending milestone. Exam first: IS 19850:2026; blends E22–E30.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: V. D. Satheesan sworn in as Kerala Chief Minister
capsules.body: V. D. Satheesan was sworn in as Kerala Chief Minister on 18 May 2026 as the UDF returned to power after a decade, winning 102 of 140 assembly seats with the Congress alone securing 63. Exam facts: CM = V. D. Satheesan; UDF 102/140; Congress 63.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Lt Gen N. S. Raja Subramani appointed India's third Chief of Defence Staff
capsules.body: Lt Gen N. S. Raja Subramani took over as India's third Chief of Defence Staff on 31 May 2026, additionally serving as Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Royal Challengers Bengaluru won IPL 2026 on 31 May
capsules.body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru won the IPL 2026 on 31 May, defeating Gujarat Titans by five wickets at Ahmedabad. Under Rajat Patidar's captaincy, Virat Kohli's unbeaten 75 led the side home.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: RCB retains IPL title
capsules.body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru beat Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the IPL final on May 31, 2026, at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. Chasing 156, Virat Kohli made an unbeaten 75 off 42 balls with the fastest IPL final fifty off 25. RCB became only the third team to defend the title after CSK and MI, earning Rs 20 crore in prize money under captain Rajat Patidar.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Surha Tal becomes India's 100th Ramsar site
capsules.body: The Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary, better known as Surha Tal in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh, was designated as India's 100th Ramsar site in June 2026. A natural oxbow lake on the Ganga's floodplain, Surha Tal is a major wintering ground for migratory waterfowl and supports threatened species like the Egyptian vulture and greater spotted eagle. The milestone underscores India's position as the country with the largest Ramsar network in South Asia.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: R Praggnanandhaa became the first Indian to win Norway Chess (5 June 2026)
capsules.body: R Praggnanandhaa became the first Indian to win Norway Chess on 5 June 2026, defeating top-ranked Magnus Carlsen twice and sealing the title with a final-round win over Vincent Keymer.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: The Land Port Management System 'VINIMAY' launched on 9 June 2026
capsules.body: The Land Port Management System 'VINIMAY', a digital platform for managing India's land ports, was launched on 9 June 2026, aimed at streamlining cross-border passenger and cargo movement at land borders.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Narendra Modi becomes longest-serving continuously elected PM
capsules.body: On 10 June 2026 Narendra Modi completed 4,399 days in office, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's elected-tenure record of 4,398 days to become India's longest-serving continuously elected Prime Minister (PIB). The count spans his uninterrupted tenure since May 2014. Exam margin: just one day — 4,399 vs 4,398.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Mizoram leads electoral-roll digitisation at 68.05%
capsules.body: Mizoram topped all states in electoral-roll form digitisation at 68.05% as of 12 June 2026, the highest among states during the Special Intensive Revision exercise. Exam stat: top state = Mizoram (68.05%).

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Jharkhand receives 11 GI tags in one go
capsules.body: On 14 June 2026, Jharkhand received Geographical Indication tags for 11 traditional products in a single announcement: Bhoya Saree and Fabric, Kuchai Silk Saree, Kesaria Kalakand, Dokra Craft, Tumka Chadar, Baroni Paintings, Munda Jewellery, Jharkhand Bamboo Craft, Tussar Silk and Sarees, Jadopatia Painting, and Pancho Saree and Fabric. The recognition is expected to protect the state's tribal crafts and give artisans and weavers better access to national and international markets.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Kavach 4.0 expansion approved
capsules.body: The expansion of Kavach 4.0 — India's indigenous automatic train protection system — was approved on 15 June 2026. Kavach automatically applies the brakes if a loco pilot overshoots a signal, preventing collisions. Exam line: Kavach = indigenous automatic train protection; 4.0 expansion approved June 2026.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Heli-tourism scheme in Bihar
capsules.body: Bihar's cabinet approved the Mukhyamantri Bihar Heli-Tourism and Air-Tourism Seva Yojana on June 17, 2026. Phase one runs July 15, 2026 to January 15, 2027 through the Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation. Weekend services link Patna with Rajgir (Rs 4,000), Valmikinagar (Rs 5,000) and Karmchat Dam in Kaimur (Rs 6,000), plus a 10-minute Patna joy ride at Rs 2,100 per seat.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: NEET-UG 2026 re-examination held on 21 June
capsules.body: The NEET-UG 2026 re-examination was held smoothly on 21 June 2026 with over 20 lakh candidates; the NTA reported no paper-leak complaints. It followed the cancellation of the original 3 May exam, announced on 12 May. Exam chain: 3 May exam → cancelled 12 May → re-exam 21 June; 20 lakh+ appeared.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: New service chiefs take charge on 1 July
capsules.body: In the 1 July 2026 tri-services reshuffle, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit became Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Jasvir Singh Mann took over as AOC-in-C of Southern Air Command, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh became Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (CISC), and Lt Gen Rajesh Pushkar assumed command of the Army's Southern Command. Exam drill: Dixit = VCAS, Mann = Southern Air Command, Tejinder Singh = CISC, Pushkar = Southern Command.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Balika Inter Protsahan 2026
capsules.body: Under the Mukhyamantri Balika (Intermediate) Protsahan Yojana 2026, unmarried girls who pass Class 12 through the Bihar School Examination Board receive a one-time Rs 25,000. It is part of the Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana. Applications are made on the Medhasoft portal, with the amount paid to an Aadhaar-linked bank account.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna Metro extended to Malahipakri
capsules.body: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the Patna Metro's extension to Malahipakri on July 2, 2026, adding Khemnichak station to the route. The operational corridor from ISBT to Malahipakri is now about 6 km long. The Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety had inspected the stretch on April 27, 2026, before approval.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Australia wins women's T20 WC
capsules.body: Australia beat England by seven wickets in the final on July 5, 2026, at Lord's to win the ICC Women's T20 World Cup for a record seventh time. Led by Sophie Molineux, Australia chased 151 with 17 balls to spare, the highest successful chase in a Women's T20 World Cup final. England hosted the tournament with 12 teams and 33 matches.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Beth Mooney record double
capsules.body: Beth Mooney was Player of the Match with 64 off 49 in the final and also Player of the Tournament, becoming the first to win the tournament award twice (2020 and 2026) and the first to win Player of the Match in two finals (2023 and 2026). England's Danni Wyatt-Hodge scored 302 runs, the first 300-run edition by any batter.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: PM Modi's three-nation tour: Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand (7-11 July)
capsules.body: PM Modi undertook a three-nation tour of Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand from 7-11 July 2026 - the first Indian prime-ministerial visit to New Zealand in 40 years. Ties with New Zealand were raised to the level of a Strategic Partnership anchored in a 'Roadmap to 2030', targeting doubled bilateral trade of Rs 35,000 crore by 2030 and fast-tracking FTA talks.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: PM Modi conferred 'Bintang Adipurna'
capsules.body: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto conferred Indonesia's highest civilian honour, the Bintang Adipurna, on PM Modi in Jakarta on 7 July 2026 for strengthening India-Indonesia relations; Modi dedicated it to the people of India.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: MSME ZED certification crosses 9.49 lakh registrations
capsules.body: As of 7 July 2026, about 9.49 lakh MSMEs had registered under the MSME Sustainable (ZED - Zero Defect Zero Effect) Certification Scheme, with over 6.67 lakh Bronze, 6,700 Silver and 4,800 Gold certifications awarded. The scheme promotes high-quality, environmentally sustainable manufacturing, and women-owned MSMEs receive a 100% subsidy on certification cost, aligning with green and inclusive industrialisation goals.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Telangana to host KIYG 2026
capsules.body: Telangana will host the eighth Khelo India Youth Games in November 2026, announced by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya. More than 8,000 athletes and officials are expected. The announcement also marked the start of the national build-up toward the 2030 Commonwealth Games and 2036 Olympics.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: NABARD facilitates GI tags for 28 products including Bihar's Bawanbuti and Pattharkatti
capsules.body: On 10 July 2026, NABARD announced it had facilitated Geographical Indication registration for 28 products, taking its supported tally to 176. The batch included Nalanda Bawanbuti Saree and Fabrics and Gaya Pattharkatti Stone Craft from Bihar, Kuchai Silk Saree and Fabrics from Jharkhand, Ba Shilp (bamboo craft) and Bihu Pepa from Assam, Himachal Wood Carving Craft, and Khajuraho Metal Craft from Madhya Pradesh, spanning handlooms, handicrafts, metalwork, pottery and musical instruments.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Wimbledon 2026: Sinner retains title, Noskova wins women's crown
capsules.body: Jannik Sinner retained the Wimbledon men's singles title, defeating Alexander Zverev 6-7, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the 12 July final. Linda Noskova won the women's crown, beating Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 on 11 July. Doubles titles went to Heliovaara/Patten (men), Guo Hanyu/Mladenovic (women) and Arevalo/Ostapenko (mixed).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: England's first-ever T20 series win over India
capsules.body: England recorded their first-ever T20I series victory over India, winning 4-0 with the Chester-le-Street opener washed out. India were bowled out for 76 at Trent Bridge, and the final T20I was played at Southampton on 12 July 2026. Exam notes: maiden T20 series win for England over India; India's 76 all out.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Sinner retains Wimbledon
capsules.body: Jannik Sinner defeated Alexander Zverev 6-7(7/9), 7-6(7/2), 6-3, 6-4 in the Wimbledon final on July 12, 2026, to retain his title. It was Sinner's fifth Grand Slam title and his 100th win at the majors, extending his reign as the dominant men's player.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India–UK CETA comes into force
capsules.body: The India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) came into force on 15 July 2026. Described as a 'gold standard' deal, it has the UK eliminating or reducing tariffs on 98.8% of its tariff lines; the Double Contribution Convention (DCC) on social security also took effect. Exam numbers: 98.8% tariff lines; DCC = Double Contribution Convention.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Tribal protests continue against Ken-Betwa dam construction
capsules.body: On 17 July 2026, farmers and tribal communities staged Jal Satyagraha and Chita Andolan protests in Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh, against displacement by the Ken-Betwa Link Project's Daudhan Dam. The reservoir is expected to submerge around 9,000 ha, including over 5,800 ha inside Panna Tiger Reserve's landscape, and fell lakhs of trees. A 2019 Central Empowered Committee report had questioned the project's wildlife clearance, and NGT petitions on environmental clearance remained pending in 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Spain win FIFA World Cup 2026
capsules.body: Spain won the FIFA World Cup 2026, defeating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 19 July final at MetLife Stadium, New Jersey — Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute. It was Spain's second title (first since 2010) and made them the first country to hold the men's and women's World Cups simultaneously. Kylian Mbappe claimed the Golden Boot. Exam set: Spain's 2nd title; 1-0 AET; MetLife; Golden Boot Mbappe.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: England win ODI series 2-1 against India
capsules.body: England clinched the ODI series 2-1 against India — their first bilateral ODI series win over India since 2018. Ben Duckett's 141 at Lord's on 19 July became the highest ODI innings at the venue, surpassing Viv Richards' 138* in the 1979 World Cup final; Rohit Sharma made 138 for India. Exam record: Duckett 141 > Richards 138* at Lord's.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Spain wins FIFA World Cup
capsules.body: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the FIFA World Cup final on July 19, 2026, at the New York New Jersey Stadium (MetLife). Ferran Torres scored the winner in the 106th minute. It was Spain's second World Cup title, and Spain became the first nation to hold the men's and women's titles simultaneously. Argentina failed to register a single shot in regulation, a first for any finalist.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: FIFA 2026 awards and records
capsules.body: Kylian Mbappe won the Golden Boot with 10 goals, his second straight, and became the World Cup's all-time top scorer with 22. Rodri took the Golden Ball, Unai Simon the Golden Glove, and Pau Cubarsi the Young Player award. Spain kept seven clean sheets and conceded just one goal all tournament, both records. The 48-team event drew a record 7 million spectators.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Vande Mataram gets legal protection on par with national anthem
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, extending the 1971 Act's protection to the national song Vande Mataram. Intentional obstruction of its singing or disruption of assemblies engaged in singing it is now a criminal offence, punishable with up to three years' imprisonment and/or fine; repeat convictions carry a minimum one-year term. The government said it gives the song due respect, while the Opposition called it against secularism.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Samudra Manthan: National Offshore Exploration Scheme launched
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet on 31 July 2026 approved Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with a Phase-I outlay of Rs 84,084 crore up to FY 2030-31. The Central Sector Scheme covers offshore seismic surveys, drilling of 60 deepwater exploration wells, common offshore infrastructure and oil-and-gas manufacturing zones, with government support covering up to 50% of eligible deepwater drilling cost subject to a Rs 675-crore-per-well ceiling.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: CWG 2026 India tally
capsules.body: India finished fourth at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with 39 medals: 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze. The scaled-down 10-sport edition had India's 122 athletes; boxing delivered a record seven gold and three silver. Gulveer Singh was India's only double medallist. Australia (171) topped, ahead of England (110) and Canada (62).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: CWG 2026 Indian highlights
capsules.body: Neeraj Chopra won javelin silver and Yashvir Singh bronze at Glasgow 2026. Of India's 39 medals, women won 8 gold, 4 silver and 4 bronze, while men won 5 gold, 13 silver and 5 bronze. Boxing produced a record haul of seven gold medals, powering India to fourth place.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Ahmedabad to host CWG 2030
capsules.body: Ahmedabad will host the centenary Commonwealth Games in 2030, as announced at the Glasgow 2026 closing ceremony. Neeraj Chopra carried the Indian flag alongside IOA president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi to receive the Commonwealth Games flag.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: CWG boxing golds
capsules.body: India's record boxing haul at Glasgow 2026 included golds for Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Arundhati Choudhary, Sachin Siwach and Ankush Panghal. Jadumani Singh, Lovlina Borgohain and Narender Berwal added silver, making boxing India's best-performing sport.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds the repo rate at 5.25% (MPC, 3-5 August)
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (3-5 August 2026) held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance. The GDP forecast for FY27 was raised to 6.7% and the CPI forecast trimmed to 5.0%; Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited resilient demand and easing supply disruptions, flagging deficient monsoon and volatile crude as risks.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25% in August policy
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee unanimously kept the repo rate at 5.25% in its August 2026 review, the fourth consecutive pause, retaining a neutral stance. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said headline inflation was driven mainly by fuel and food while core inflation stayed benign. The SDF remained at 5% and MSF/Bank Rate at 5.5%. FY27 CPI inflation was projected around 4.6-5%, with risks peaking in Q3 on food and fuel.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: GOBARdhan: National Circular Bioenergy Scheme approved
capsules.body: On 6 August 2026, the Union Cabinet approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with an outlay of Rs 23,731 crore for FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36. The integrated framework aims to grow domestic Compressed Biogas (CBG) production nearly ten-fold through assured offtake, stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline connectivity and credit support, converting cattle dung, agri residue, press mud and municipal organic waste into clean fuel, organic manure and rural income.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Senior bureaucratic reshuffle (10 August 2026)
capsules.body: A 10 August 2026 bureaucratic reshuffle appointed Deepti Gaur Mukerjee as Higher Education Secretary, Pallavi Jain Govil as Corporate Affairs Secretary, and Sunil Paliwal as Youth Affairs Secretary. Exam drill: match each officer to the ministry — Mukerjee = Higher Education, Govil = Corporate Affairs, Paliwal = Youth Affairs.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Ken-Betwa: only river-link project under implementation among 30 identified
capsules.body: In a Rajya Sabha reply on 10 August 2026, the Jal Shakti Ministry said the Ken-Betwa Link Project is the only one of 30 identified interlinking-of-rivers projects (16 peninsular, 14 Himalayan under the National Perspective Plan) to have entered implementation. Foundation stone was laid by PM Modi at Khajuraho on 25 December 2024. Estimated at Rs 44,605 crore, it will irrigate 10.62 lakh ha, give drinking water to about 62 lakh people, and generate 103 MW of hydropower plus 27 MW of solar power, with completion targeted by March 2030.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Polavaram: the other national project with a river-link component
capsules.body: The same August 2026 parliamentary reply noted that the Polavaram Irrigation Project in Andhra Pradesh, incorporating the Godavari (Polavaram)-Krishna (Vijayawada) link, is classified as a national project executed by the state with the Polavaram Project Authority. It envisages irrigation to about 7.2 lakh acres, diversion of 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna basin, drinking water to 28.5 lakh people in 611 villages, and 960 MW of hydropower.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: PM Modi releases Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography
capsules.body: PM Modi released former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles', at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi, on 12 August 2026. Exam recall: author = India's 14th President (2017–22); memorise the full title.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Parliament's Monsoon Session 2026 ends: 11 Bills passed, low productivity
capsules.body: Parliament's Monsoon Session 2026 closed in August after passing 11 Bills in both Houses, including laws on Vande Mataram's protection, paper-leak reform, judges' strength, birth-death registration, MSME payments, bankers' evidence and Kerala's name change. Only one Bill got a full debate. Lok Sabha productivity was 19% and Rajya Sabha 39%, with Question Hour never completed even once in the Lower House. The Foreign Contributions (Regulation) Amendment Bill was sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Anti-paper-leak law strengthened with fast-track courts
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, amending the 2024 Act that covers UPSC, SSC, RRB, IBPS and NTA exams. It mandates investigation within two months and trial within three months, empowers states to set up Special Fast Track Courts, allows Special Public Prosecutors, enables Central Special Task Forces, raises penalties, and creates a time-bound appeal before a Division Bench of the High Court. It was the only Bill debated in both Houses this session.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Kerala's name change cleared by Parliament
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, clearing the way for the state to be renamed Keralam. It was among the 11 Bills passed by both Houses during the Monsoon Session 2026, most of which went through within minutes amid disruptions. For BPSC aspirants, note the parallel with earlier state renamings (Madras to Tamil Nadu, Bangalore to Bengaluru) and the constitutional process under Article 3, where Parliament alone can alter a state's name.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Supreme Court judges' strength and birth-death registration Bills passed
capsules.body: Two notable laws cleared the Monsoon Session 2026: the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, replacing an ordinance and revising the sanctioned strength of the apex court; and the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which tightens delayed registration — 1-to-2-year delays now need an Executive Magistrate's approval, and delays beyond two years need a Judicial Magistrate (First Class). Both passed with minimal debate amid House disruptions.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bankers' Books Evidence Bill modernises banking records law
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, replacing the colonial-era framework on bank records. It formally recognises electronic and digital banking records — online transfers, UPI trails, electronically stored ledgers — as admissible evidence in legal proceedings. It passed in about five minutes in the Lok Sabha. The older Bankers' Books Evidence Act dated back to 1891, making this a major update for India's digital-first banking system.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 79th Independence Day: 'Naya Bharat' theme, record 103-minute address
capsules.body: India marked its 79th Independence Day on 15 August 2026 with the themes 'Naya Bharat', '150 Years of Vande Mataram' and 'Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047'. PM Modi delivered a record 103-minute, 13th consecutive Red Fort address covering the Emergency, Operation Sindoor, 'Made in India' defence, semiconductors, critical minerals, women's empowerment and the RSS centenary. Highlights: Flying Officer Rashika Sharma assisted the flag-hoisting; two Mi-17s showered petals — one bearing the national flag, the other an Operation Sindoor flag; 2,500 NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers formed the 'Naya Bharat' logo.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: National Sports Awards 2025
capsules.body: The National Sports Awards for 2025, announced on August 18, 2026, named no Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, only the third time since 1991 after 2008 and 2014. Seventeen athletes received Arjuna Awards, including Tejaswin Shankar (athletics), Vidit Gujrathi (chess), Divya Deshmukh (chess), Narender (boxing), and Lalremsiami and Rajkumar Pal (hockey).

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Dronacharya and lifetime awards
capsules.body: The Dronacharya regular awards went to Parveer Singh (athletics), Chhote Lal Yadav (boxing) and Neha Chavan (shooting); the lifetime honours to Dharmendra Singh Yadav and Virender Kumar. I Arumainayagam, the 1962 Asian Games gold-winning footballer, received the Arjuna (Lifetime) award, and the Army Paralympic Node, Pune, got the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Para and deaf Arjuna winners
capsules.body: The 2026 Arjuna list included para sportstars Rudransh Khandelwal (para shooting) and Ekta Bhyan (para athletics), and deaf shooter Dhanush Srikanth. Notably, no cricketer featured among the 17 Arjuna recipients this year.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge
capsules.body: The Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Yojana, launched at Gyan Bhawan, Patna, on August 26, 2026, gives seed funding of Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh to around 2,100 selected women entrepreneurs. It is one of three women-focused schemes unveiled at the same event, alongside the Abhaya Brigade and the Balika PhD fellowship.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: CM Balika PhD Fellowship
capsules.body: The Chief Minister Balika PhD Fellowship gives about 1,000 women research scholars Rs 10,000 every month for four years. Announced on August 26, 2026, it aims to keep women in higher education and research, complementing the state's push on women's entrepreneurship and safety.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Abhaya Brigade for women police
capsules.body: The Abhaya Brigade provided 4,700 bicycles and two-wheelers to women police personnel for patrolling and responding to complaints involving women and girls. Bihar has about 40,000 women police personnel, the highest among states. The emergency 112 response time was reported below 10 minutes, with a target of 5-7 minutes.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India win the Test series 1-0 in Sri Lanka
capsules.body: India won the Test series 1-0 in Sri Lanka as the second Test at Colombo ended in a draw on 27 August 2026. Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133, scored while following on, saved Sri Lanka after India declared at 503-9. Debutant spinner Saransh Jain was among India's wicket-takers.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India's Q1 FY27 GDP grows 7.8%, beating RBI estimate
capsules.body: NSO data released 31 August 2026 showed real GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026), beating the RBI's 7% projection. Real GVA rose 8.2% and nominal GDP 10.3%. Manufacturing grew 9.2%, services 10% (financial, real estate and professional services 12.1%), gross fixed capital formation 11.9% and exports 12%. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said reforms were bearing results; former NITI Aayog CEO Amitabh Kant called it ahead of expectations.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New blind fish genus from Indo-Gangetic aquifers in Bihar
capsules.body: Scientists described Gangaichthys indonepalicus, a new genus and species of miniature blind earthworm eel (family Chaudhuriidae), from alluvial aquifers of the Indo-Gangetic plain in Bihar in 2026 (ZooKeys). The 4-cm fish has skin-covered reduced eyes, a translucent unpigmented body and no ribs — adaptations to life in total darkness. It is the first stygobitic (subterranean) fish recorded from the Gangetic basin; the name honours the Ganga and its India-Nepal range.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Forex reserves around $700 billion, says Finance Minister
capsules.body: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said at the G20 meetings in Asheville, North Carolina, that India's foreign exchange reserves stood at slightly over $700 billion in early September 2026. The buffer — among the world's largest — supports the rupee amid crude-price volatility and the RBI's liquidity management, which includes absorbing large FCNR(B)-driven dollar inflows.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New vine snake genus Proahaetulla antiqua found in southern Western Ghats
capsules.body: IISc Bengaluru researchers discovered Proahaetulla antiqua in the southern Western Ghats, a new vine snake species that also represents an entirely new genus, believed to have diverged around 26 million years ago. Reported in 2026, the find adds to the Western Ghats' reputation as a global biodiversity hotspot with high reptile endemism and shows how cryptic lineages persist in one of India's most surveyed yet still surprising landscapes.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO's GSLV-F17 launches EOS-05, India's first geo-orbit imaging satellite
capsules.body: ISRO launched GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05 (GISAT-1A) from Sriharikota's Second Launch Pad at 2:55 am on 4 September 2026. The 2,367-kg satellite — the heaviest GSLV Mk II has lifted — is India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit (~36,000 km), offering strategic real-time data, full Indian landmass coverage every 30 minutes and 5-minute imaging of chosen areas. It was the 107th Sriharikota launch and 19th GSLV flight; PM Modi hailed it as a proud national moment.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: EOS-05: India's heaviest GSLV Mk II payload at 2,367 kg
capsules.body: EOS-05, weighing 2,367 kg, is the heaviest satellite the GSLV Mark II has placed in space, ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan confirmed after the 4 September 2026 launch. The mission was the 107th launch from Sriharikota and the 19th GSLV flight, and it followed the failed GSLV-F10/EOS-03 mission of 2021 and PSLV failures in 2025-26 — making the success a programme-level recovery for ISRO.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NITI Aayog launches PACT and ZET marketplace for freight electrification
capsules.body: NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba launched the PACT and ZET marketplace on 7 September 2026, urging strategic electrification of India's freight sector. Heavy trucks are just 3-4% of the vehicle fleet but cause over one-third of transport-sector carbon emissions; only about 800 heavy-duty electric trucks were sold in 2025, while 70% of India's freight moves by road. The platforms aim to accelerate zero-emission trucking.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Financial Fraud Risk Indicator stopped Rs 5,000 crore fraud
capsules.body: The Department of Telecommunications' Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), launched under the Digital Intelligence Platform, has prevented suspected cyber-fraud transactions worth over Rs 5,000 crore, the Communications Ministry announced on 8 September 2026. FRI flags suspicious mobile numbers linked to fraud so banks and payment firms can block dubious transactions before money is lost — a key cyber-safety tool as UPI and digital payments expand.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: PM-SETU: Rs 735.70 crore approved for ITI transformation
capsules.body: The 5th National Steering Committee of PM-SETU approved Skill Investment Plans worth Rs 735.70 crore on 8 September 2026 to strengthen industry-led transformation of Industrial Training Institutes. PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) aims to align vocational training with industry demand, a key plank of India's skilling architecture.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Kharif sowing area crosses 1086.31 lakh hectares
capsules.body: All-India kharif area coverage stood at 1086.31 lakh hectares as on 4 September 2026, the Agriculture Ministry reported on 8 September. The healthy sowing footprint, alongside a normal monsoon, matters for food-inflation control — a key RBI watch item, with CPI inflation at 4.82% in August and upside risks flagged from weather disruptions affecting food prices.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Coal gasification scheme Round 1 gets seven applications
capsules.body: Round 1 of the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects concluded with seven applications from leading public and private companies, the Coal Ministry announced on 8 September 2026. The scheme aims to convert coal into cleaner syngas, methanol and chemicals, cutting dependence on imported crude and gas while reducing the environmental footprint of domestic coal.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: PM Modi launches Rs 35,000 crore projects in Vadodara
capsules.body: PM Modi laid foundation stones and inaugurated development projects worth more than Rs 35,000 crore in Vadodara, Gujarat, on 8 September 2026 (PIB Release ID 2307800). The package covered infrastructure, industry and public services, underlining Gujarat's role as a manufacturing and investment hub ahead of the BRICS Summit hosted in New Delhi days later.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: PIB backgrounder on jute, India's golden fibre
capsules.body: PIB published a backgrounder on 7 September 2026 on jute, 'India's golden fibre', noting the crop's economic and ecological importance. India is the world's largest jute producer (West Bengal, Assam and Bihar lead), and jute's biodegradability makes it central to the plastic-substitution and circular-economy agenda — linking to the World Circular Economy Forum hosted in Gandhinagar the same month.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: 'Ghost Flower' orchid discovered in Arunachal Pradesh
capsules.body: A new leafless orchid, Gastrodia keyiensis, was described from Keyi Panyor district, Arunachal Pradesh, in the journal Phytotaxa on 9 September 2026. The species lacks leaves and chlorophyll, surviving on soil fungi (holomycotrophy). Locally called 'Oram Opuh' (Ghost Flower) in the Nyishi dialect, only five flowering individuals were found, and it is classified Data Deficient. The discovery reinforces Arunachal's tag as India's 'Orchid Paradise' with ~600 documented orchid species.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Egyptian President El-Sisi arrives for BRICS Summit
capsules.body: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi arrived in New Delhi on 11 September 2026 for the 18th BRICS Summit, received by Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth. Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also reached the capital for the summit, making it one of the largest diplomatic gatherings India has hosted.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 18th BRICS Summit held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
capsules.body: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12-13 September 2026 under its fourth chairship. The theme was 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. Leaders of all 11 members adopted the 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration on global-governance reform, de-escalation, trade, payments and development cooperation. A BRICS Business Forum preceded it on 11 September, and over 350 chairship meetings were held across 25+ Indian cities during 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Commemorative BRICS stamps released marking 20 years
capsules.body: On 12 September 2026, India Post released two commemorative postage stamps on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit, marking two decades of BRICS cooperation (2006-2026). The stamps carried the inscription 'BRICS: Two Decades of Cooperation, 2006-2026' and reflected India's chairship theme and its 'Humanity First', people-centric vision. BRICS now comprises 11 members accounting for roughly 49.5% of world population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of world trade.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New caecilian species Gegeneophis chandgadi discovered in Maharashtra
capsules.body: On 12 September 2026, the Zoological Survey of India announced a new species of subterranean, legless amphibian, Gegeneophis chandgadi, discovered at Buzawade village in Chandgad, Kolhapur district of Maharashtra's northern Western Ghats. Named after the local Chandgadi dialect of Marathi, the caecilian was found in residential and agricultural landscapes rather than inside protected forests, underlining hidden subterranean biodiversity in human-dominated areas.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India hosts World Circular Economy Forum 2026 in Gandhinagar
capsules.body: India became the first South Asian country to host the World Circular Economy Forum, held 15-18 September 2026 at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar. Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Gujarat CM Bhupendrabhai Patel inaugurated it under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity'. Organised by CPCB with Finland's Sitra fund, MoEFCC and Gujarat, it released guides on reuse of treated sewage and India's circular-economy and EPR initiatives.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Ministries gear up for Special Campaign 6.0 from 2 October
capsules.body: CBIC, the Departments of Expenditure, Financial Services, CBDT, Pensions and Pensioners' Welfare and the Home Ministry began preparations in September for Special Campaign 6.0 (2-31 October 2026), the Centre's annual drive for swachhata, disposal of pending references, record management and workplace improvement. The Finance Ministry also scheduled a 18-19 September conference of State Finance Ministers and Secretaries on 'Financing India's Journey towards Viksit Bharat' in New Delhi.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Trump signs Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act authorising 100% tariffs
capsules.body: US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law on 18 September 2026. The Act empowers the President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or natural gas, targeting buyers including India and China. India's MEA said it is monitoring developments and remains 'firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people'.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 43rd Indian Coast Guard Commanders' Conference held
capsules.body: The 43rd Indian Coast Guard Commanders' Conference was held in New Delhi from 17 September 2026, with the Raksha Rajya Mantri calling on the ICG to keep pace with rapid technological advancements and emerging maritime challenges. The Coast Guard, under the Defence Ministry, guards India's 7,516-km coastline and exclusive economic zone.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: HAL hands over LCA trainers, HTT-40 and Dhruv NG helicopters
capsules.body: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited handed over 2 LCA FOC twin-seat trainers and 3 HTT-40 basic trainers to the IAF, and 4 Dhruv NG helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited, in the presence of the Raksha Mantri and Civil Aviation Minister on 18 September 2026. The indigenous deliveries strengthen IAF training capacity and civil helicopter operations, showcasing HAL's production ramp-up.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) 2026 concludes
capsules.body: The Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) Programme 2026 concluded at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi, on 18 September 2026. CORE is a tri-services forum for reviewing operational preparedness and jointness, reflecting the armed forces' push towards integrated theatre-level planning.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NLMC board reviews accelerated asset monetisation
capsules.body: The 21st Board meeting of the National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC) on 19 September 2026 reviewed the Centre's asset monetisation programme and pushed for acceleration, alongside investor meets ahead of the RINL land e-auction. NLMC is the government's dedicated vehicle for monetising surplus land and non-core assets of CPSEs and departments under the National Monetisation Pipeline.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Keel laid for first Next Generation Missile Vessel at Cochin Shipyard
capsules.body: Cochin Shipyard Limited laid the keel of the first Next Generation Missile Vessel (NGMV) for the Indian Navy on 19 September 2026, a day after steel-cutting began for the second NGMV. The NGMVs will replace ageing missile vessels with modern, stealthier platforms, advancing the Navy's indigenous shipbuilding drive under Atmanirbhar Bharat. Raksha Rajya Mantri attended the 43rd Indian Coast Guard Commanders' Conference the same week.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: 20th Asian Games open in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan
capsules.body: The 20th Asian Games opened on 19 September 2026 in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, running till 4 October. Over 11,000 athletes from 45 countries plus the OCA Refugee Team compete in 469 events across 43 sports. India sent 495 athletes in 36 sports; Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat were the flag-bearers at the opening ceremony. India's previous best was 107 medals (28 gold, 38 silver, 41 bronze) at Hangzhou 2023.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games Aichi Nagoya
capsules.body: The 20th Asian Games run from September 19 to October 4, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with 43 sports and 469 events. India's 495 athletes compete in 36 sports, with Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat as flag bearers. As of September 25, India had 23 medals (2 gold, 9 silver, 12 bronze).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Semicon India 2026 concludes showcasing India's chip push
capsules.body: Semicon India 2026 concluded successfully by 20 September 2026, underlining India's growing role in the global semiconductor ecosystem. The conference capped a month of electronics push that also saw BIS expand mandatory quality certification to more electronic goods, with smartphone screen protectors to need BIS certification (IS 19348:2025) from 1 April 2027, covering strength, durability, optical clarity and adhesive quality.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Unemployment rate down from 6% to 3.2%, says Minister
capsules.body: Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan said on 20 September 2026 that India's unemployment rate had declined from 6% to 3.2%, crediting the government's major schemes and employment push. The claim was reported by PIB-aligned competitive-exam compilations; official periodic labour force survey data is the benchmark BPSC aspirants should cross-check before using the figure in answers.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: SLINEX-26: annual India-Sri Lanka maritime exercise
capsules.body: The India-Sri Lanka annual bilateral maritime exercise SLINEX-26 was announced on 20 September 2026, continuing the long-running naval engagement between the two neighbours. It came in the same week that Indian Naval ships Sahyadri and Kulish arrived at Subic Bay, Philippines, for the ADMM-Plus Joint Combined Action exercise, and INS Trishul made a port call at Alexandria, Egypt, before joining Exercise Varuna in Toulon, France.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Elavenil Valarivan leads India's early shooting medals
capsules.body: India's shooting campaign at the Asian Games opened with Elavenil Valarivan's silver in the women's 10m air rifle individual event on Day 1, followed by silver in the women's team event with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. The men's 10m air rifle team (Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon, Parth Mane) also won silver, with Patil and Dhillon adding individual medals — building a haul of seven shooting medals by 25 September.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India wins its first-ever Asian Games medal in MMA
capsules.body: Suchika Tariyal won bronze in the traditional 60 kg MMA event, securing India's first-ever Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts. Her podium finish marked the entry of Indian combat-sport athletes into a new discipline at the continental level, as MMA's profile grows within the Asian Games programme.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM-AJAY accelerates Scheduled Caste socio-economic development
capsules.body: The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) is accelerating the socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities, PIB reported around 20 September 2026. The scheme converges income-generating, infrastructure and social-development projects for SC populations, fitting the government's broader saturation-approach welfare delivery model alongside PM-JAY, PM Surya Ghar and PM-SETU.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Nitin Gadkari announces UHPFRC flyover at Indora-Dighori
capsules.body: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari announced completion of the Indora-Dighori flyover using Ultra-High Performance Fibre Reinforced Concrete (UHPFRC) technology, cutting travel time from about an hour to 10-15 minutes. Reported on 20 September 2026, the project showcases advanced construction materials in Indian highway infrastructure.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Suryakiran Aerobatic Team flies over Meerut for first time
capsules.body: The IAF's Suryakiran Aerobatic Team performed over Meerut skies for the first time on 20 September 2026, thrilling spectators with formation aerobatics. The display came amid a busy IAF week that included a joint air defence exercise with Japan and HAL's handover of new trainer aircraft and helicopters.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Central Bureau of Narcotics ties up with Brahma Kumaris
capsules.body: The Central Bureau of Narcotics signed an MoU with the Brahma Kumaris on 21 September 2026 to strengthen preventive drug awareness, youth empowerment and community outreach. It complements the NCB's enforcement-led 3rd ANTF Conference held the same week, adding a social-awareness pillar to the drug-free India by 2029 goal.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: DRI seizes over 845 kg of contraband in intensified crackdown
capsules.body: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence seized more than 845 kg of contraband drugs across various locations in an intensified crackdown on drug trafficking, reported on 21 September 2026. The seizure follows the Centre's sharpened anti-narcotics push, including the 3rd ANTF conference and the CBN-Brahma Kumaris outreach MoU in the same week.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Nomadic Elephant 2026: 18th India-Mongolia exercise begins
capsules.body: The 18th India-Mongolia joint military exercise NOMADIC ELEPHANT commenced on 21 September 2026 at the Foreign Training Node, Pithoragarh (Uttarakhand), running till 3 October. Forty-five personnel each from the Indian Army and Mongolian Armed Forces train in counter-insurgency operations under a UN mandate in semi-urban and mountainous terrain. Drills cover cordon-and-search, room intervention, special heliborne ops, cyber security, and drones and counter-drone systems.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: IAF holds joint air defence exercise with Japan
capsules.body: The Indian Air Force conducted a joint air defence exercise with Japan on 21 September 2026, deepening air-power interoperability between the two Quad partners. The week also saw the Suryakiran Aerobatic Team fly over Meerut skies for the first time (20 September), and the Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) Programme 2026 conclude at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi (18 September).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Indian naval ships reach Subic Bay for ADMM-Plus exercise
capsules.body: Indian Naval ships Sahyadri and Kulish arrived at Subic Bay, Philippines, on 21 September 2026 for the ADMM-Plus Joint Combined Action exercise. The deployment reflects India's Act East engagement with ASEAN-centred defence platforms, paralleling the 24th Varuna exercise with France in the Mediterranean and SLINEX-26 with Sri Lanka in the Indian Ocean.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's women's cricket team wins first gold at Asian Games
capsules.body: India won its first gold medal of the Asian Games 2026 in the women's cricket final, defeating their opponents to top the podium early in the Games. The triumph marked the second straight Asian Games gold for Indian women's cricket, giving the 495-strong contingent a strong opening before shooting, weightlifting and wrestling added further medals.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: DISHA 2.0 regional workshop held in Goa
capsules.body: The Department of Justice organised a regional workshop on the DISHA 2.0 scheme in Goa on 21 September 2026. DISHA (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) aims to make justice delivery accessible at the grassroots through tele-law, legal literacy and pro-bono legal services, aligning with the government's access-to-justice mission.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: MoD inks Rs 586 crore contract for tank auxiliary power units
capsules.body: The Ministry of Defence signed a Rs 586 crore contract on 21 September 2026 to procure auxiliary power units for T-72 and T-90 main battle tanks. APUs let armoured vehicles run electronics and start engines without the main engine, improving battlefield endurance and fuel efficiency — part of the Army's ongoing fleet-modernisation programme.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Fisheries package for SC ST EBC
capsules.body: Bihar's 2026-27 fisheries special package for SC, ST and EBC applicants offers up to 80% subsidy. The Pond Fisheries Scheme gives 70% on unit cost up to Rs 10.10 lakh, and the Plateau Area Scheme gives 80% on unit cost up to Rs 16.70 lakh (maximum Rs 13.36 lakh). The minimum water area is 0.4 acre, covering pumpsets, solar pumps, sheds, aerators and inputs.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NPCI revises UPI MDR framework
capsules.body: NPCI revised the UPI MDR framework: a 0.4% charge applies to merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 per transaction. Person-to-person UPI transfers remain free. Exam numbers: 0.4%; Rs 2,000 threshold; Rs 300 cap; P2M only.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cabinet raises EPFO wage ceiling to Rs 25,000
capsules.body: The Cabinet raised the EPFO wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 (effective 17 September 2026), lifting the EPS pension contribution cap to Rs 2,080 per month and bringing more workers under EPF coverage. Exam figures: Rs 15,000 → Rs 25,000; EPS cap Rs 2,080.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Indian Oil approves Rs 2,449 cr Kochi–Thoothukudi gas pipeline
capsules.body: Indian Oil approved a Rs 2,449-crore, 424.65-km natural gas pipeline from Kochi to Thoothukudi, boosting gas connectivity across the southern states. Exam numbers: Rs 2,449 crore; 424.65 km; Kochi–Thoothukudi.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: HAL hands over Tejas trainers, HTT-40 'Ankur' and Dhruv NG
capsules.body: HAL handed over LCA Tejas FOC trainers, HTT-40 'Ankur' trainers and Dhruv NG helicopters — the Dhruv NG being India's first indigenous civil helicopter with AS-4 compliance, opening up civilian markets. Exam first: Dhruv NG = first indigenous civil helicopter; AS-4 compliant.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Adani Power's 3,200 MW plant at Dhubri, Assam
capsules.body: Adani Power is building a 3,200 MW ultra-supercritical thermal plant at Dhubri, Assam, with a Rs 48,000-crore investment — the Northeast's largest power asset. Ultra-supercritical technology burns coal more efficiently with lower emissions. Exam numbers: 3,200 MW; Rs 48,000 crore; Dhubri, Assam.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Asia's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
capsules.body: Asia's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, with about Rs 5,500 crore in investment and 18,000+ jobs, under a DoT–MP MoU signed in July 2026. Exam first: Asia's first telecom manufacturing zone; Gwalior; 18,000+ jobs.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India targets world's No. 1 silk producer by 2028-29
capsules.body: India aims to become the world's No. 1 silk producer by 2028-29; output has climbed from 26,000 MT in 2014 to about 42,000 MT now, with Karnataka leading production. Exam trajectory: 26,000 → 42,000 MT; top state Karnataka; No. 1 target by 2028-29.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: FCRA (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
capsules.body: The FCRA (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 provides that assets created from foreign funds vest in a government-appointed authority if an NGO's FCRA registration is cancelled or lapses. Since 2015, 22,496 NGO registrations have been cancelled. Exam numbers: asset-vesting clause; 22,496 cancellations since 2015.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: LPG biometric authentication mandatory from 1 Oct 2026
capsules.body: Biometric authentication for LPG becomes mandatory from 1 October 2026: 27.43 crore consumers (89.9%) are already verified, while unverified customers will have to pay the market price for cylinders. The drive targets duplicate and ghost connections in the subsidy system. Exam figures: 27.43 crore (89.9%); deadline 1 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: IAF to host 2nd edition of Tarang Shakti at Jodhpur
capsules.body: The IAF will host the second edition of Tarang Shakti — its multinational air exercise — at Jodhpur from 26 September to 12 October 2026, featuring complex air-combat drills with foreign air forces. Exam facts: 2nd edition; Jodhpur; 26 Sep–12 Oct 2026.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Exercise Nomadic Elephant: 18th India–Mongolia edition
capsules.body: The 18th edition of Exercise Nomadic Elephant — the India–Mongolia joint military exercise — began at Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand. The annual drill builds interoperability in counter-insurgency and mountain warfare. Exam pair: Nomadic Elephant = India–Mongolia; venue Pithoragarh.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: SLINEX-26
capsules.body: The 13th edition of SLINEX, the India-Sri Lanka bilateral naval exercise, was conducted off Visakhapatnam. INS Kavaratti and the fleet tanker INS Jyoti represented India. Such bilateral drills build interoperability between the two navies and sustain India's maritime engagement in the Indian Ocean region.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: India's first indigenous long-range OWA drone 'KAL' tested at Pokhran
capsules.body: India flight-tested its first home-grown long-range one-way-attack (kamikaze) drone, KAL, at Pokhran. The platform can strike targets about 1,000 km away, remain airborne for seven to eight hours, and carry a 50-kg payload. It gives India an indigenous loitering-strike option and strengthens the Make-in-India defence push.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: WMO State of Global Water Resources 2025
capsules.body: The World Meteorological Organization's State of Global Water Resources 2025 reports that 34% of monitored groundwater stations sat below normal levels. Parts of India showed persistent groundwater depletion through 2022-25. The finding matters for India's irrigation and drinking-water security; expect map/table questions on depletion zones.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: 20th Asian Games opened in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan
capsules.body: The 20th Asian Games opened in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, under the theme 'Harmonic Heart Beat'. Shooter Manu Bhaker and kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat carried India's flag at the opening ceremony, and teqball made its Asian Games debut. India now chases medals at the Japan-hosted Games.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Savita Punia becomes India's most-capped women's hockey player
capsules.body: Veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia earned her 321st senior cap, passing Vandana Katariya's 320 to become the most-capped player in Indian women's hockey history. Hockey India marked the record with a Rs 10 lakh reward - a landmark for the national women's hockey programme.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India makes first farm-level soil carbon payments
capsules.body: In a first for Indian agriculture, 2,550 farmers in Punjab and Haryana received over Rs 2.9 crore in farm-level soil carbon payments under the 'Aadi' programme, covering roughly 50,000 verified carbon credits. Farmers were paid for carbon sequestered in their soils - a landmark for agri carbon markets in India.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Deep-sea mining push
capsules.body: India now holds three exploration contracts with the International Seabed Authority covering about 95,000 sq km of ocean floor, advancing its deep-sea mining ambitions. Under the Deep Ocean Mission, the crewed submersible MATSYA-6000 is also under development. The ISA governs mineral extraction in international waters.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New orchid 'Gastrodia keyiensis' discovered in Arunachal Pradesh
capsules.body: Botanists have described a new leafless orchid, Gastrodia keyiensis - nicknamed the 'Ghost Flower' - found along the Keyi River in Arunachal Pradesh. The discovery paper appeared in the journal Phytotaxa on 9 September 2026. It underlines the Eastern Himalayas as a biodiversity hotspot.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New cat species 'Leopardus tilcayo' identified in Bolivia
capsules.body: Scientists identified Leopardus tilcayo, a new wildcat species from Bolivia - the first new living feline species described in over a century. A rare mammalian-taxonomy breakthrough likely to feature in environment and biology current-affairs sets.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI publishes final Bihar electoral roll after Special Intensive Revision
capsules.body: The Election Commission published Bihar's final electoral roll after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), concluded after a 22-year gap ahead of the 2026 Assembly polls. About 65 lakh names were deleted from the draft roll (deceased, relocated or duplicate entries).
