The Supreme Court ordered on 8 September that Aadhaar be accepted as identity proof for additions (not as citizenship proof); the final hearing is on 7 October. Patna district gained 1,63,600 voters over the draft; Muzaffarpur 88,108; Nawada 30,491.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: August CPI inflation rises to 4.82%; rate-hike talk builds
capsules.body: India's retail inflation climbed to 4.82% in August 2026 from 4.45% in July, staying above the RBI's 4% target. ICRA expects it to cross 5% in September; Elara sees FY27 average inflation at 4.9%, with risks in H2 as base effects fade. Most brokerages expect the repo rate to stay at 5.25% through 2026, with a 25 bps hike possible in early 2027. Wholesale price inflation hit 9.92% in August on food and fuel.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New parasitic wasp species found in Assam's Dibru-Saikhowa
capsules.body: ZSI researchers Rupam Debnath and K. Rajmohana described a new parasitic wasp, Oxyserphus narendrani, from Dibru-Saikhowa National Park, Assam, in a study published September 2026. The 3.3-mm insect is the first recorded occurrence of the genus Oxyserphus in India and the first described species of the genus in the Oriental region. Named after late taxonomist Dr T.C. Narendran, it was collected in November 2024 with a yellow pan trap.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Periyar Tiger Reserve survey records six new species
capsules.body: A four-day faunal survey at Periyar Tiger Reserve, Kerala (Thekkady), reported on 22 September 2026, recorded six species previously undocumented in the reserve: one bird, one butterfly and four odonates. The golden-headed cisticola (Cisticola exilis) took the reserve's bird count to 347, and the common onyx butterfly (Horaga onyx) took its butterfly tally to 284, with 174 bird and 192 butterfly species documented during the exercise.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: PM Modi calls India a key custodian of the greater one-horned rhino
capsules.body: On World Rhino Day (22 September), PM Modi said India is among the world's most important custodians of the greater one-horned rhinoceros, which thrives mainly in Assam's Kaziranga and other northeastern protected areas. The statement underlines India's conservation success — Assam hosts over two-thirds of the world's wild one-horned rhinos — and the role of protected-area management in species recovery.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 72nd National Film Awards held outside Delhi for first time
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu conferred the 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on 22 September 2026 — the first time in the awards' 72-year history the ceremony moved out of Delhi. Kevadia (renamed Ekta Nagar) is home to the Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue at 597 feet. The 11-member jury was headed by filmmaker Jayaraj; entries spanned 161 films across 24 languages.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Article 370 named Best Feature Film; Yami Gautam Best Actress
capsules.body: At the 72nd National Film Awards, Article 370 was named Best Feature Film and its lead Yami Gautam won Best Actress. Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Direction for Amaran. Kalki 2898 AD received Best Popular Film providing wholesome entertainment, while Captain Miller (Dhanush) was named Best Feature Film promoting national, social and environmental values. Awards covered 22 feature and 23 non-feature categories from 561 total entries.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Kartik Aaryan and Mammootty share Best Actor honour
capsules.body: The Best Actor award at the 72nd National Film Awards was shared by Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion and Malayalam superstar Mammootty for Bramayugam — a first National Award for Aaryan. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Film of a Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. Veteran actor Anant Nag received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. Beyond Eighth Schedule languages, Garhwali film Dholi, Tulu film Imbu and Santhali film Aangen were also recognised.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: VP inaugurates 9th Indian International Water Week
capsules.body: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 9th Indian International Water Week 2026 in New Delhi on 22 September, a flagship event on water security, irrigation efficiency and river rejuvenation. It ran alongside the World Circular Economy Forum week, making mid-September 2026 a notable moment for India's environment and water diplomacy — India also announced it would host International Water Week 2026 events.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Final Bihar voter list published after 22-year SIR gap
capsules.body: The Election Commission released Bihar's final voter list after the Special Intensive Revision on 22 September 2026, the first such revision in 22 years. The exercise, done under Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, deleted about 65 lakh entries (deceased, shifted, duplicates). The Supreme Court is hearing petitions against SIR, with a final hearing scheduled for 7 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI's bond sales & FX intervention halve liquidity surplus
capsules.body: RBI's bond sales and foreign-exchange interventions cut the banking system's liquidity surplus to Rs 4.92 trillion on 21 September - down 55% from the record Rs 11.16 trillion. The central bank sold Rs 750 billion of bonds in a week with Rs 250 billion more planned; a diaspora deposit scheme had earlier raised $133 billion. ANZ expects three 25-basis-point hikes from October 2026, taking the repo rate to 6.00% by end-FY27.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI extends simplified KYC certification for FPIs at co-operative banks
capsules.body: From 18 September 2026, foreign portfolio investors registered with urban and rural co-operative banks get simplified KYC certification, putting them on par with NRIs/PIOs - no physical in-person verification under PMLA norms. The RBI move eases FPI access through smaller banking channels.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI bulk-deposit rate disclosure rules from 1 Oct 2026
capsules.body: Banks must publish bulk-deposit interest rates on their websites from 1 October 2026, with a 10-minute grace period after the 10 am daily deadline. An RBI transparency measure for deposit-rate disclosure.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SEBI pushes banks into commodity derivatives; RBI/IRDAI hold back
capsules.body: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey pushed for banks and pension funds to enter commodity derivatives to deepen liquidity and hedging depth; the RBI and IRDAI are holding back. MCX shares fell 3.4% on the commentary. Remember: commodity derivatives are regulated by SEBI.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Tarang Shakti 2026: F-35s to fly with IAF for the first time
capsules.body: The second edition of multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti runs 26 September-12 October 2026 at Jodhpur. US F-35s will fly alongside the IAF for the first time; seven friendly air forces bring assets (France's Rafales, UAE's F-16s, plus Germany, Australia, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka), with 32 nations as observers. It was announced by Vice Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: First-ever V4+India Foreign Ministers' Meeting
capsules.body: The first-ever V4+India Foreign Ministers' Meeting took place on 21 September in New York on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA. EAM S. Jaishankar met counterparts from Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia; the sides agreed on an annual ministerial meeting and business forum, and the V4 backed India's bid for a permanent UNSC seat.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Ireland fines Google EUR 403 million over location-data privacy
capsules.body: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google EUR 403 million on 21 September for GDPR breaches involving Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy data (2018-20). Google must comply within six months; it is the regulator's fourth-largest fine. A landmark data-privacy enforcement case for GDPR questions.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 72nd National Film Awards presented at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu presented the 72nd National Film Awards on 22 September at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat - the first ceremony held outside Delhi. Dadasaheb Phalke Award 2024 went to Anant Nag. Best Feature Film: Article 370; Best Actress: Yami Gautam; Best Actor (shared): Mammootty (Bramayugam) and Kartik Aaryan (Chandu Champion); Best Director: Rajkumar Periasamy (Amaran); Best Popular Film: Kalki 2898 AD; Best Non-Feature: Bhangaar; a Santhali film was honoured for the first time.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's first gold at Asian Games 2026
capsules.body: India's first gold at the 2026 Asian Games came in women's cricket: India beat Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the T20 final at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin, on 22 September (216/3 vs 69). Smriti Mandhana's 79 off 45 took her past 11,000 international runs - a first for a woman batter. India's tally then: 1 gold, 4 silver, 2 bronze.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Suchika Tariyal wins bronze in MMA
capsules.body: Suchika Tariyal won India's first-ever Asian Games medal in MMA - bronze in the women's traditional 60kg category on 21 September - after losing her semifinal to Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Men's 10m air rifle team silver
capsules.body: The men's 10m air rifle team of Rudrankksh Patil, Parth Mane and Himanshu Dhillon won silver at the Asian Games on 21 September.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Amit Shah sets drug-free India target for December 2029
capsules.body: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi on 22-23 September 2026. Organised by the Narcotics Control Bureau on the theme 'United Resolve, Shared Responsibility', it implements the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029), targeting a drug-free India by 31 December 2029 under the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, using a whole-of-government approach against trafficking networks.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Jaishankar flags India's concerns over US Russia-sanctions law to Rubio
capsules.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York on 23 September 2026 during UNGA 81's High-Level Week, reiterating India's 'interests and concerns' over the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), signed by President Trump on 18 September. The law authorises up to 100% tariffs on the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas — a direct threat to India's energy security, as Russian crude forms over 30% of its oil imports.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India meets Italy's Tajani on defence, AI, space cooperation
capsules.body: On the sidelines of UNGA 81 in New York, EAM Jaishankar met Italian leaders including Antonio Tajani to advance the India-Italy strategic partnership across defence, security, AI, space, critical technologies and energy. Jaishankar also joined a Global South meeting, stressing deeper economic, technological and environmental cooperation among developing countries and reform of multilateral institutions.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Deep depression over Bay of Bengal crosses near Kalingapatnam
capsules.body: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal approached the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast and was expected to cross near Kalingapatnam on the night of 23 September 2026, with sustained winds of 52-61 kmph and heavy to very heavy rainfall forecast for Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Fishermen were advised to stay off the seas. Kalingapatnam is an ancient port town in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Mirabai Chanu wins weightlifting silver at Asian Games
capsules.body: Mirabai Chanu won the silver medal in weightlifting at the Asian Games 2026, adding to India's tally on 23 September. Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan congratulated her. The medal continued Chanu's record as one of India's most decorated weightlifters, following her Olympic and World Championship honours.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: WAVES 2026 success; next edition in October 2027
capsules.body: Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the next edition of WAVES (World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit) will be held in October 2027, after the success of the 2026 edition. He noted the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies has about 380 students across 13 industry-aligned courses and that the Prime Minister has approved 15,000 creative labs across the country. The National Film Awards ceremony will henceforth travel to leading tourist destinations in states.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Karnataka seeks central drought relief; writes to PM
capsules.body: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar wrote to PM Modi seeking interim drought relief and advance SDRF funds, reported on 24 September 2026. The request highlights the federal disaster-relief architecture — the State Disaster Response Fund and National Disaster Response Fund — and comes as weather risks (floods in the east, dry spells in the south) test monsoon-season management.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Textile stocks fall on SRIA tariff fears
capsules.body: Indian textile stocks dropped up to 5% in September 2026 as the US sanctions law (SRIA) raised fears of up to 100% tariffs on exports tied to Russian-energy purchases. The episode shows how geopolitical sanctions can spill into specific export sectors, with textiles — a major employer — flagged as vulnerable even as Delhi and Washington negotiate a trade deal.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Creative economy push: 15,000 creative labs approved
capsules.body: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry said on 22-23 September 2026 that the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies has about 380 students enrolled across 13 industry-aligned courses, and that the Prime Minister has approved 15,000 creative labs across the country. The push anchors the creative-economy agenda alongside WAVES (next edition October 2027) and the National Film Awards' move to state venues.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Integrated Chaur Development
capsules.body: The Mukhyamantri Integrated Chaur Development Scheme (2026-27) offers up to 50% subsidy to make low-lying chaur land productive. Fish farming is integrated with agriculture, horticulture or agroforestry, in two models: beneficiary-based and entrepreneur-based. It is run by the Department of Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: MoD signs Rs 810.79 crore SAT-SAAW deal with BDL
capsules.body: The Defence Ministry signed an Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Ltd on 23 September 2026 for 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) for the IAF under the Buy Indian (IDDM) route, in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. The DRDO-designed precision glide bomb carries 60% indigenous content and will arm Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30MKI aircraft, with deliveries from 2027-28 to 2028-29.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: DRDO's 30kW laser anti-drone weapon moves toward production
capsules.body: DRDO is moving its indigenous 30kW-class truck-mounted laser weapon toward production and will seek an industry partner. It can engage drone swarms and UAVs up to 5 km away. Part of Project Sudarshan Chakra, with 50kW and 100kW variants in the works - a big step for directed-energy air defence.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 (22nd edition)
capsules.body: India and US troops held joint artillery drills at the Mahajan Field Firing Range, Rajasthan, on 23 September during the 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas - using M777 ultra-light howitzers, Dhanush guns, Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launchers, L70 air-defence guns and M-LIDS, focused on interoperability of fire planning. The exercise spans Rajasthan and Uttarakhand.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Tata's defence plant inaugurated in Berrechid, Morocco
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Morocco's Defence Minister Abdelatif Loudyi inaugurated Tata Advanced Systems' 20,000 sq-m facility at Berrechid, Morocco, on 23 September. It will build 150 WhAP 8x8 armoured vehicles for the Royal Moroccan Army over three years - the largest contract ever for Indian-made armoured vehicles and a landmark defence-export win.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SEBI Board meets 24 Sept with major reforms on the agenda
capsules.body: At its 24 September meeting, the SEBI Board lined up major reforms: a PMS overhaul including a new mutual-fund-only PMS (Rs 25 lakh minimum investment vs Rs 50 lakh; Rs 2 crore net worth vs Rs 5 crore), a common advertisement code for regulated entities, settlement-rule changes, eased FPI norms for non-agri commodity derivatives, corporate-debt reforms (Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt securities), depository receipts for REITs/InvITs, and vault-manager rules.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SEBI's net-settlement proposal: comments close 24 Sept
capsules.body: SEBI's 3 September consultation paper proposes net settlement of funds (with gross securities settlement) for mutual-fund cash-market trades at the individual scheme level; public comments closed on 24 September 2026. A market-microstructure reform to cut settlement friction.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Motilal Oswal gets SEBI nod for custodial services
capsules.body: Motilal Oswal Custodial Services got SEBI approval on 24 September to offer custodial services - safekeeping, trade settlement, corporate actions and regulatory reporting - to AIFs, portfolio managers, mutual funds, insurers and pension funds; operations begin in Q4 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 3-day nationwide bank strike from 28 Sept 2026
capsules.body: The United Forum of Bank Unions (seven unions covering about 90% of bank staff) called a three-day nationwide strike for 28-30 September. SBI advised customers to finish branch work by 25 September, while ATMs, YONO, internet/mobile banking and UPI stay functional. Demands: a five-day banking week, pension updation, a uniform DA formula and an NPS-to-OPS switch option; a continuous strike from 26 October was also announced.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: PIB Fact Check busts fake UPI/ATM rumours
capsules.body: On 23 September the Finance Ministry clarified via PIB Fact Check that rumours of UPI/ATM charges are false: person-to-person UPI stays free, merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 stay free, and a 0.4% MDR applies only on specified person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. About 96% of merchant transactions remain unaffected.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: EPFO wage ceiling raised to Rs 25,000
capsules.body: The Cabinet approved raising the mandatory EPF wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, effective 17 September 2026 (Vishwakarma Jayanti) - the first revision in about 12 years (since September 2014). Around 51 lakh more employees are expected to come under EPF coverage, with an annual government outgo of roughly Rs 11,339 crore.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI rate-hike buzz returns
capsules.body: The repo rate has held at 5.25% since August - a fourth straight pause - with the MPC next meeting on 5-7 October. S&P expects a 25-bps hike to 5.5% in FY27, Fitch sees 5.5% in October and 5.75% in early 2027, and SBI Research also recommends two hikes.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India co-sponsors inaugural P4M Summit at the UN
capsules.body: EAM S. Jaishankar co-chaired the first-ever 'Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity (P4M)' Summit on 21 September in New York with leaders of Australia, Barbados, Brazil, Canada and Kenya. He stressed transparent decision-making and action on the '4F' crisis of fuel, food, fertiliser and finance.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Roshibina Devi wins wushu silver
capsules.body: On 24 September, Naorem Roshibina Devi lost the women's 60kg sanda final 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu and took silver - becoming the first Indian to medal at three successive Asian Games (bronze 2018, silver Hangzhou 2022, silver 2026). India's tally moved to 14: 1 gold, 6 silver, 7 bronze.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Satnam Singh & Salman Khan row to bronze
capsules.body: The Indian pair of Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won bronze in men's double sculls on 24 September (6:13.25), finishing behind China and Uzbekistan.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Five medals on Day 4 (23 Sept)
capsules.body: India won five medals on 23 September: Mirabai Chanu took silver in women's 49kg weightlifting (total 198 kg: 87 snatch + 111 clean & jerk), ending India's 28-year wait since Karnam Malleswari's 1998 Bangkok silver; Jay Meena won bronze in men's singles soft tennis - India's first-ever Asian Games soft-tennis medal; bronzes also came in men's and women's skeet team events and the men's badminton team (lost 1-3 to China in the semifinal).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Elena Rybakina wins US Open women's singles
capsules.body: Elena Rybakina (Kazakhstan) beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in the US Open women's singles final on 12 September, denying Sabalenka a three-peat. It is Rybakina's third Grand Slam title, after the 2026 Australian Open and Wimbledon 2022.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Ayushman Bharat turns 8
capsules.body: On 23 September, PM Modi said Ayushman Bharat - now eight years old - covers over 60 crore beneficiaries with Rs 5 lakh annual health insurance, the world's largest healthcare scheme. Key stats: 48.54 crore Ayushman cards issued, over 13 crore people treated, Rs 2 lakh crore+ of care through 38,000+ empanelled hospitals, and 500+ crore visits at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: 20th Rozgar Mela
capsules.body: On 19 September, PM Modi handed out 51,000+ appointment letters across 45 locations at the 20th Rozgar Mela - about 12.75 lakh appointment letters in total through the Mela series. He spotlighted the new Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (around Rs 1 lakh crore outlay, about 2 crore first-time youth, Rs 15,000 incentive for first-time job seekers plus employer incentives).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Exercise Veer Guardian 2026 concludes at Jodhpur
capsules.body: The second edition of Exercise Veer Guardian - the IAF-Japan Air Self-Defence Force bilateral air drill - concluded on 22 September at Air Force Station Jodhpur after 14 days. The IAF fielded Su-30MKI, Rafale and the indigenous LCA Tejas; Japan's F-2A fighters made their first-ever visit to India. On Distinguished Visitor's Day, JASDF Chief Gen. Takehiro Morita and IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh both flew the Tejas. The inaugural edition was at Hyakuri, Japan, in January 2023.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Fitch, S&P and ADB raise India's FY27 GDP forecast
capsules.body: On 23 September, Fitch raised India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.9% (from 6.4%) and S&P to 7% (from 6.6%), after stronger-than-expected 7.8% growth in the June quarter; the ADB also lifted its forecast to 7% (from 6.6%). All three expect at least a 25-bps RBI hike - Fitch sees 5.5% in October and 5.75% in early 2027, while S&P projects FY27 consumer inflation averaging 5.1%.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Luke Lindberg appointed WFP Executive Director
capsules.body: On 18 September, the UN appointed US agriculture official Luke Lindberg as Executive Director of the World Food Programme, on the joint recommendation of Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and FAO DG Qu Dongyu after Executive Board confirmation. He succeeds Cindy McCain (Carl Skau served as acting ED) for a five-year term - the youngest person ever to lead the agency. Lindberg was previously USDA Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs and was nominated by US President Donald Trump. WFP is headquartered in Rome and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India becomes first South Asian country to host WCEF
capsules.body: India became the first South Asian country to host the World Circular Economy Forum: WCEF 2026 (15-18 September) was inaugurated at the Mahatma Mandir Convention and Exhibition Centre, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Gujarat CM Bhupendrabhai Patel. Theme: 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity'; organised by the CPCB with Finland's Sitra, MoEFCC and the Gujarat government.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO-ESA cooperative agreement extended to 8 January 2032
capsules.body: The ISRO-ESA cooperative agreement was extended to 8 January 2032, widening collaboration on space weather and human/robotic exploration. In parallel, India's National Quantum Mission is expanding - C-DOT's 14 indigenous quantum products and IISc Bengaluru's Foundation for Quantum Computing Innovation are recent milestones.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISTRAC's Advanced Radar Research Facility to come up in Assam
capsules.body: ISRO will set up an Advanced Radar Research Facility (IARRF) at Chandrapur, Assam, under ISTRAC - strengthening satellite tracking, telemetry and command coverage from the Northeast to support the rising launch cadence, including Gaganyaan and navigation-satellite missions.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: 9th Molecular Virology Meeting (MVM 2026) at New Delhi
capsules.body: The 9th Molecular Virology Meeting (MVM 2026) concluded on 18 September at BRIC-National Institute of Immunology (BRIC-NII), New Delhi - a gathering of about 200 clinicians, researchers and students on viral biology, vaccines, therapeutics and public health. The annual forum, started in 2009, was hosted with ICGEB and the Regional Centre for Biotechnology.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: MY Bharat crosses 3 crore registered youth
capsules.body: The Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform, launched in 2023, has crossed 3 crore registered youth users - a key metric for questions on government youth-engagement initiatives.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Bharat Taxi launched in five UP cities
capsules.body: On 23 September, UP CM Yogi Adityanath flagged off Bharat Taxi - a cooperative-led ride-hailing service with zero commission on a 'Driver is the Owner' model (Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Ltd) - in Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj. About 40,000 drivers ('Saarthis') registered across the five cities; nationally, over 10 lakh Saarthis have joined since the service began in February 2026.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: UP's Krishak Samriddhi Yojana portal and two apps launched
capsules.body: At the same 23 September programme, the CM launched the Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana e-portal - long-term farm loans through the UP Cooperative Rural Development Bank at 6% interest, down from 11%, targeting 5 lakh small and marginal farmers - plus the Urvarak Setu mobile app (Cooperation Department) and the UPCDC app (UP Cooperative Database Centre).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: India's solar capacity nears 165 GW
capsules.body: India's installed solar capacity has risen to nearly 165 GW, with the PM Surya Ghar scheme empowering over 51 lakh families - headline numbers for renewable-energy current affairs.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Rajat Sharma re-elected NBDA President
capsules.body: The News Broadcasters & Digital Association board unanimously re-elected India TV Chairman & Editor-in-Chief Rajat Sharma as NBDA President for 2026-27 on 23 September. NBDA is the apex body of 29 leading news broadcasters running 130+ news channels and digital platforms; Jayant Mammen Mathew (MM TV) joined the board.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: BJP appoints in-charges for 36 states and UTs
capsules.body: On 24 September the BJP named in-charges and co-in-charges for all 36 states and UTs: national general secretary Smriti Irani gets Haryana and Chhattisgarh, while vice-president Ram Madhav gets Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: WION Iconic Tourism Summit & Awards 2026
capsules.body: The WION Iconic Tourism Summit & Awards 2026 was held on 23 September at ITC Maurya, New Delhi, presented by VFS Global in association with Red Hat Communications. Sessions covered the future of global mobility, biometric travel and AI in tourism, closing with the Iconic Awards honouring travel and tourism contributors.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI defends SIR 'logical discrepancies' net widened to 11 categories
capsules.body: Amid the SIR controversy, the ECI clarified that its 'logical discrepancies' checks expanded from 4 categories used earlier in West Bengal to up to 11 in Phase 3 across Karnataka, Haryana, Delhi and Telangana. Tests include age gaps under 15 years between voter and parent, under 40 years between voter and grandparent, more than six siblings linked to one parent, and name-spelling variations between revisions. The Indian Express argued on 24 September that the exercise 'must be rethought or abandoned'.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI: no documents needed with Form 6/8 citizenship declaration
capsules.body: The Election Commission clarified on 24 September that its SIR orders — for Bihar (June 2025), 12 states/UTs (October 2025) and 19 states/UTs (May 2026) — all unanimously approved, require an additional citizenship declaration form (Annexure D) along with Form 6 (new registration) or Form 8 (shifting from outside the state), but those submitting it need not furnish any other document. The exercise is conducted under Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Centre cuts customs duty on edible oils ahead of festivals
capsules.body: The Centre cut basic customs duty on edible oils with effect from 24 September 2026: crude palm and soyabean oil from 10% to 5%, refined palm and soyabean from 32.5% to 27.5%, crude sunflower oil from 10% to nil, and refined sunflower oil from 32.5% to 22.5%. Total import duty on crude palm/soya falls to 11%. The move aims to cool retail prices — sunflower oil retailed at Rs 194/kg in late September — before Navratri and Diwali, and to favour domestic refining.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI reports 18% credit growth; new Executive Director appointed
capsules.body: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said bank credit grew around 18% year-on-year till June 2026, with healthy growth across agriculture, industry, housing and MSME lending. Monisha Chakraborty took charge as a new Executive Director of the RBI in September 2026. The central bank also flagged rising foreign-exchange inflows — about $136 billion under its special swap facility by 31 August, mostly via FCNR(B) deposits — pushing core liquidity above Rs 8 lakh crore.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: ADB raises India's GDP forecast to 7% on strong Q1
capsules.body: The Asian Development Bank raised India's GDP growth forecast to 7% in September 2026, citing stronger-than-expected Q1 FY27 performance of 7.8%. India's forex reserves stood around $700 billion, the Finance Minister noted at the G20 in Asheville, North Carolina. Union Bank of India separately projected a possible RBI rate-hike cycle from December 2026, taking the repo rate to 5.75-6% in H2 FY27 to curb inflation and absorb excess liquidity.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Trishul reaches Toulon for 24th India-France Exercise Varuna
capsules.body: INS Trishul arrived in Toulon, France, for the 24th edition of the bilateral India-France maritime exercise Varuna, reported on 24 September 2026. The guided-missile frigate had made a port call at Alexandria, Egypt, earlier (19 September). The same week, Defence Minister-chaired events saw HAL hand over 2 LCA FOC twin-seat trainers, 3 HTT-40 basic trainers to the IAF and 4 Dhruv NG helicopters to Pawan Hans.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: TDB-DST signs Rs 63.84 crore deal with Galax-E for satellite tech
capsules.body: The Technology Development Board under the Department of Science and Technology signed an Rs 63.84 crore RDI assistance agreement with Galax-E on 24 September 2026 for developing next-generation multi-sensor satellite technology. The deal reflects the growing public-private model in India's space ecosystem, where private firms increasingly partner with ISRO and government agencies on advanced space hardware.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO advanced radar facility foundation laid in Assam
capsules.body: The foundation was laid in Assam for an advanced ISRO radar facility in September 2026, reported in competitive-affairs compilations on 24 September. The facility will strengthen India's space-based surveillance, tracking and weather-monitoring infrastructure, complementing the EOS-05 geo-imaging milestone achieved earlier in the month.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India reaffirms 2030 goal to eliminate Hepatitis B and C
capsules.body: At a UNGA 81 side event, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava reaffirmed India's goal to eliminate Hepatitis B and C as public-health threats by 2030. The strategy covers prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and long-term care. India also highlighted progress on Universal Health Coverage, sickle-cell care and hepatitis elimination at the General Assembly, positioning health as a diplomatic theme.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India deepens economic and digital ties with Caribbean nations
capsules.body: India is looking to deepen economic and digital ties with Caribbean nations, reported in national headlines on 24 September 2026. The outreach extends India's Global South engagement — digital public infrastructure cooperation being a recurring offer — alongside its active UNGA 81 diplomacy with the US, Italy, France and developing-country partners.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Lavrov: Russia will not pause operations for Ukraine talks
capsules.body: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said at the UN on 24 September 2026 that Russia would not pause military operations for Ukraine negotiations, amid the ongoing West Asia conflict that has also roiled crude markets. India has navigated this geopolitics by diversifying energy sourcing, while flagging the SRIA sanctions law's risks to its imports and exports with the US.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY turns eight
capsules.body: Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana turned eight in September 2026, continuing as the world's largest health assurance scheme covering crores of families with up to Rs 5 lakh annual hospitalisation cover. Health Minister J.P. Nadda inaugurated Arogya Manthan 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan on 24 September to review the scheme's progress, even as India highlighted Universal Health Coverage and sickle-cell care achievements at UNGA 81.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: MY Bharat platform crosses 3 crore registered youth
capsules.body: The MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) platform crossed 3 crore registered youth since its 2023 launch, reported on 24 September 2026. Conceived as a single-window platform for youth volunteering, internships and national-building activities, it has become one of the world's largest youth-engagement platforms. Education Minister Pralhad Joshi also inaugurated the Seva Pratham Innovation Challenge at IISc Bangalore the same week.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM Surya Ghar empowers over 51 lakh families; solar nears 165 GW
capsules.body: India's installed solar capacity rose to nearly 165 GW, with PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana empowering over 51 lakh families, the government highlighted around 24 September 2026. The rooftop-solar scheme gives households subsidised panels and free electricity units, cutting bills and emissions — a flagship of India's energy-transition and household-welfare agenda.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Railways approves Vadodara ROB, new Kanpur-Anand Vihar train
capsules.body: Indian Railways approved construction of a Road Over Bridge in Alkapur, Vadodara Division, costing Rs 166.5 crore, and sanctioned a new daily train service between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar Terminal, PIB reported on 24 September 2026. The same month, KAVACH 4.0 was commissioned for the first time on South Central Railway — 108 route km between Malkajgiri and Kamareddi (Telangana) — improving train-location accuracy and automatic braking.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Arogya Manthan 2026 inaugurated by Health Minister
capsules.body: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda inaugurated Arogya Manthan 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, on 24 September. The annual conclave reviews Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, bringing together states, insurers and hospitals to strengthen the world's largest health assurance scheme as it completed eight years.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India showcases health achievements at UNGA 81
capsules.body: At UNGA 81, India highlighted its progress in Universal Health Coverage, hepatitis elimination and sickle-cell disease care, per PIB-linked compilations on 24 September 2026. The Union Health Secretary separately reaffirmed the 2030 target for eliminating Hepatitis B and C as public-health threats, making health a visible strand of India's multilateral diplomacy alongside the energy-security debate.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar assembly polls: final roll numbers by district
capsules.body: Bihar's final electoral roll after SIR shows district-wise changes versus the draft: Patna gained 1,63,600 voters, Muzaffarpur 88,108 and Nawada 30,491, while statewide about 65 lakh names were removed. The roll will be used for the 2026 Bihar Assembly elections, with physical copies distributed to District Election Officers-cum-District Magistrates and shared with recognised political parties.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: CS reviews law and order
capsules.body: Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit chaired a law-and-order review on September 24, 2026, ahead of the festival season. He directed stronger patrolling with visible policing, fixed accountability on SPs for field visits down to subdivision level, overnight stays by headquarters officers in districts, and tighter surveillance of anti-social elements.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Trishul arrives at Toulon for 24th Exercise VARUNA
capsules.body: The Indian Navy's guided-missile stealth frigate INS Trishul reached Toulon, France, on 22 September for the 24th edition of Exercise VARUNA - the bilateral naval drill with France that began in 2001. The harbour and sea phases (cross-deck visits, operational interactions, sports) build interoperability; the deployment followed a 14-17 September port call at Alexandria, Egypt, with a PASSEX alongside ENS Bernees.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Yudh Abhyas 2026: US Ambassador Sergio Gor witnesses the drill
capsules.body: US Ambassador Sergio Gor visited Rajasthan to witness the 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas, under way at the Mahajan Field Firing Range and across Uttarakhand, where Indian and US troops have already done joint artillery drills with M777 howitzers, Dhanush guns, Pinaka MBRLs and M-LIDS.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: CDS stresses integration of technology, data and industry
capsules.body: Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani stressed that integrating technology, data and industry is central to strengthening India's defence ecosystem - the triad driving the armed forces' modernisation doctrine.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SEBI Board approves sweeping reforms at 215th meeting (24 Sept)
capsules.body: SEBI's 215th board meeting in Mumbai on 24 September overhauled the framework. New Portfolio Managers Regulations, 2026 allow PMS to deploy money into IPOs, primary-market debt and foreign securities, and introduce a mutual-fund-only PMS with about Rs 25 lakh minimum versus Rs 50 lakh. FPIs get wider non-agri commodity-derivative access, but physically-settled positions must close at least three days before expiry. Other moves: depository receipts for listed REITs/InvITs abroad; a common ad code (celebrities may promote brands, not specific products); 9% annual disgorgement interest; a Rs 75 crore net-worth floor for vault managers; wider accredited-investor norms; and easier corporate-debt rules.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bank strike 28-30 Sept: today is the last full working day
capsules.body: The United Forum of Bank Unions, seven unions covering roughly 90% of the banking workforce, has called a three-day nationwide strike from 28 to 30 September, with a further continuous strike from 26 October on notice. SBI advised customers to complete branch work by 25 September; ATMs, YONO, internet and mobile banking and UPI will stay functional. Key demands are a five-day banking week, pension updation, a uniform DA formula, and an option to switch from NPS to the old pension scheme.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Jaishankar chairs 2nd FIPIC Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New York
capsules.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar presided over the second ministerial gathering of the Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation on 24 September in New York, on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly. The grouping, launched by India in Fiji in 2014, reviewed the 12-Point Action Plan announced by PM Modi in 2023. Discussions covered renewable energy, climate action, disaster resilience, education, healthcare and capacity building. Jaishankar endorsed the Pacific Islands Forum's 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent and proposed tailored capacity-building programmes for Pacific professionals.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: FSSAI proposes ban on analogue paneer sold as 'paneer'
capsules.body: The Food Safety and Standards Authority has proposed, through draft amendment regulations notified on 22 September and gazette-published on 23 September, adding 'paneer made of constituents not derived from milk' to restricted products. Items already licensed under the 'Analogue in Dairy Context' category must drop the word 'paneer' from their nomenclature, labelling and marketing. Objections and suggestions are invited within 60 days of gazette publication. At least eight states - Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat among them - have already moved against analogue paneer at their own level.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 sent to Cabinet
capsules.body: The Power Secretary confirmed the draft National Electricity Policy 2026, prepared by the Power Ministry, is now before the Cabinet for approval. Once cleared, the document will set the country's overarching power-sector strategy covering generation, transmission, distribution and related areas. No details of the draft's contents were disclosed in the announcement; exam focus is on the fact that a new draft policy has reached the Cabinet stage.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Railways: 2nd Saraighat rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra
capsules.body: Railways will build a second rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra at Saraighat in Assam, alongside doubling of the Agthori-Kamakhya track, both falling under the Northeast Frontier Railway zone. Separately, the ministry approved a Rs 166.5 crore four-lane rail overbridge at Alkapuri in Vadodara and a new daily overnight train between Kanpur and Anand Vihar. The new Brahmaputra crossing strengthens the existing Saraighat bridge, a vital connectivity link for the Northeast.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: India meets 99.2% of domestic mobile phone demand
capsules.body: Electronics Secretary S. Krishnan announced that 99.2% of the mobile phones India needs are now made within the country - a landmark for electronics self-reliance. The near-total import substitution in handsets is among the biggest successes of the Make-in-India push in electronics, with almost the entire domestic market now supplied locally.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: NEET-PG 2026 results declared
capsules.body: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences declared NEET-PG 2026 results on 24 September for the exam held on 30 August, taken by 2,63,544 candidates, plus a Jaipur re-exam on 5 September for 2,416 candidates hit by a power failure. Category cut-offs: General/EWS 262 (50th percentile), General-PwBD 244 (45th), SC/ST/OBC 226 (40th). Ranks rest on actual marks with tie-breaking criteria; individual scorecards and answer keys will be released on natboard.edu.in in October. The Board found none of the questions technically incorrect.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 6: five medals, India at 17
capsules.body: India collected five medals on day six of the Asian Games 2026 (24 September) - two silver and three bronze - taking the tally to 17 (1 gold, 6 silver, 10 bronze), though the country slipped to 15th while China crossed 100 medals. Silver went to the mixed 4x400m relay team and wushu star Roshibina Devi (women's 60kg). Bronze came from Seema Kumari in the women's 10,000m (India's first athletics medal of the Games), the skeet mixed team of Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Anantjeet Singh Naruka, and the men's double sculls pair Satnam Singh and Salman Khan (6:13.25).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey: India thrash South Korea 8-2
capsules.body: India's men's hockey team routed South Korea 8-2, the country's biggest-ever win over the Koreans in Asian Games history. In kabaddi, the women's team thumped Japan 50-25 to reach the semifinal while the men beat Chinese Taipei to top their group; both squads have assured India of medals.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India-New Zealand FTA to enter into force on 20 Oct 2026
capsules.body: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will enter into force on 20 October 2026 after ratification by both countries. The pact, formalised on 27 April 2026 at Bharat Mandapam by Goyal and NZ Trade Minister Todd McClay, the pact gives 100% of India's exports to New Zealand - textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods and processed foods - duty-free access. India also gains duty-free inputs such as wooden logs, coking coal and metal scrap. The aim is to double bilateral trade to Rs 35,000 crore within five years.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Fitch raises India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.9%
capsules.body: Fitch Ratings raised India's FY27 growth forecast by 50 basis points to 6.9%, citing stronger-than-expected expansion and resilient investment. India grew 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 despite the energy-price shock from the US-Iran conflict. Fitch expects headline inflation to rise to 5.5% by December 2026, easing to 4.2% by end-2027.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: MoD signs Rs 810.79 crore contract with BDL for 160 SAT-SAAW systems
capsules.body: The Defence Ministry signed a Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited on 23 September in New Delhi for 160 SAT-SAAW systems, under the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category. The Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapon, a DRDO-developed air-to-ground precision glide bomb, with 60% indigenous content, launchable from Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30 MKI aircraft. Deliveries in 2027-28 and 2028-29 will strengthen the Indian Air Force's precision-strike capability.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Nomadic Elephant 2026: 18th India-Mongolia joint exercise begins
capsules.body: The 18th edition of the India-Mongolia joint military exercise Nomadic Elephant began at Pithoragarh in Uttarakhand, with 45 personnel from each side. Training centres on counter-insurgency drills conducted under a UN mandate, alongside drone operations, cybersecurity and cordon-and-search drills.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: 3rd ANTF Conference; Amit Shah sets drug-free India target for 2029
capsules.body: Home Minister Amit Shah addressed the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force heads of states and UTs in New Delhi on 22-23 September, organised by the Narcotics Control Bureau with 36 states/UTs on the theme 'United Resolve, Shared Responsibility'. The conference will implement the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029), targeting a drug-free India by 31 December 2029 in line with Viksit Bharat 2047. Shah also released four anti-narcotics TVCs, launched the revamped NCB website and laid foundation stones for NCB zonal complexes at Lucknow and Dehradun.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: OneSCD: India co-hosts global sickle-cell partnership at UNGA81
capsules.body: India co-launched OneSCD, a global sickle-cell partnership, on 23 September in New York alongside Nigeria, WHO, UNICEF, Africa CDC, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and the World Coalition on Sickle Cell Disease. The partnership aims to close global gaps in diagnosis, treatment and survival for sickle cell disease. India showcased its National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (2023, elimination target 2047): over 72.9 million screened, 2 million-plus carriers identified, 2.5 lakh diagnosed and 49.3 million Sickle Cell Cards issued.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: AB PM-JAY completes 8 years with 60+ crore beneficiaries
capsules.body: The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana completed eight years with 60+ crore beneficiaries. Launched by PM Modi on 23 September 2018 at Ranchi and run by the Health Ministry, it is the world's largest government-funded public health insurance scheme, offering Rs 5 lakh annual cover per family for secondary and tertiary care. It is centrally sponsored with 60:40 Centre-state funding (90:10 for Northeastern states, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and J&K).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance renamed ICICI Life Insurance
capsules.body: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company was renamed ICICI Life Insurance effective 22 September 2026 after Registrar of Companies approval. Prudential plc of the UK will shift from promoter status to passive investor as it plans to acquire a controlling stake in Bharti Life Insurance.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: BIS certification made mandatory for smartphone screen protectors
capsules.body: The Electronics Ministry brought smartphone screen protectors under the Compulsory Registration Order, 2021, making BIS certification mandatory from 1 April 2027. They must conform to IS 19348:2025, covering thickness, dimensions, light transmission, visual defects and strength, before manufacture, import or sale. Screen protectors become the 66th category in the framework, alongside smartphones, laptops, chargers, LED TVs and set-top boxes.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Pune to host UCI Road World Championships 2032
capsules.body: At the UCI's 195th Congress in Montreal, Pune was announced as host of the 2032 UCI Road World Championships - cycling's road world championships coming to India for the first time. Pune's bid, driven jointly by Maharashtra's government and the Cycling Federation of India, beat Groningen/Drenthe of the Netherlands in the final round.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Jay Meena: India's first-ever Asian Games soft-tennis medal
capsules.body: Jay Meena, a 26-year-old from Dewas in Madhya Pradesh, took bronze in men's singles soft tennis on 23 September - India's first-ever Asian Games medal in the sport. A 2-4 semifinal defeat to Japan's Takuya Kurosaka followed after beating Pakistan's Arain Hussain 4-0 in the group stage and the Philippines' Sherwin Nuguit 4-3 in a seven-game quarterfinal thriller.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Delhi Cabinet approves DURGA scheme: 1,300 pink e-autos
capsules.body: The Delhi Cabinet cleared the DURGA scheme (Driving Upliftment and Rozgar for Women/Transgender Green E-Auto), giving 1,300 pink e-autos for dignified self-employment: 1,170 for women and 130 for transgender persons, with district-level caps of 90 and 10 respectively. Eligibility covers women aged 20-40 who are Delhi residents with voter ID, LMV licence and PSV badge, and family income up to Rs 5 lakh. A three-year vehicle lock-in applies.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Tejashwi Yadav demands cancellation of five state polls over SIR row
capsules.body: RJD working president and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on 25 September 2026 demanded cancellation of the recent elections in five states, including Bihar, alleging the Special Intensive Revision was excluding eligible voters. He cited reports that Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected repeatedly to poll-panel decisions. The ECI countered that all SIR orders were unanimously approved by CEC Gyanesh Kumar and both Commissioners, calling later objections an afterthought.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Premier Energies commissions India's largest solar cell facility
capsules.body: Premier Energies commissioned India's largest solar cell manufacturing facility in September 2026, a milestone for domestic solar supply chains. It coincides with India's installed solar capacity nearing 165 GW and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana empowering over 51 lakh families, data the government highlighted around 24 September. The facility strengthens India's import-substitution push in renewables manufacturing.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: PLI schemes boost pharma, API and medical device making
capsules.body: PIB reported on 25 September 2026 that Production-Linked Incentive schemes are strengthening India's pharmaceutical, active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and medical devices manufacturing sectors. The PLI push reduces import dependence in critical drug inputs — a strategic lesson from supply-chain disruptions — and complements the broader Atmanirbhar Bharat manufacturing agenda.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Defence Ministry signs Rs 810.79 crore deal with BDL for anti-airfield weapons
capsules.body: The Ministry of Defence signed an Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited on 25 September 2026 for anti-airfield weapons. Days earlier (21 September), it had inked a Rs 586 crore contract for auxiliary power units for T-72 and T-90 tanks. Both deals fit the indigenisation push, while the HAL handover of LCA trainers, HTT-40 trainers and Dhruv NG helicopters on 18 September underscored domestic aerospace output.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: TRAI launches Digital Connectivity Rating Platform
capsules.body: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India launched its Digital Connectivity Rating Platform on 25 September 2026, a PIB-reported initiative to rate buildings and areas on digital connectivity quality. The platform aims to make connectivity a measurable, comparable parameter — relevant as India pushes 5G/6G readiness, smart-city infrastructure and work-from-home resilience.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-France reaffirm cooperation in the electricity sector
capsules.body: India and France reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation in the electricity sector on 25 September 2026, per PIB. The energy partnership complements the broader India-France strategic agenda — defence (Exercise Varuna's 24th edition in Toulon), space, and clean-energy cooperation — making France one of India's key European partners.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet win shooting gold with Asian record
capsules.body: On 25 September 2026, Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team final at the Asian Games, India's second gold of the Games. The pair set an Asian record of 484.6 points, beating South Korea by 6.6 points (Iran took bronze with 415.8). The same day, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudrankksh Patil and Niraj Kumar won silver in the men's 50m rifle 3-positions team event with 1762-94x.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India adds relay silver and athletics medals at Asian Games
capsules.body: India's medal rush continued: the mixed 4x400m relay team won silver at the Asian Games 2026. Seema claimed bronze in the women's 10,000m, Naorem Roshibina Devi won silver in the women's 60 kg wushu final, and Satnam Singh and Salman Khan earned bronze in the men's doubles sculls rowing event. The men's badminton team also secured bronze, and Anantjeet Singh Naruka with Parinaaz Dhaliwal won skeet mixed-team bronze.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India 12th in Asian Games medal tally; China leads
capsules.body: As of 25 September 2026, India stood 12th in the Asian Games medal table with 2 gold, 9 silver and 12 bronze (23 total). China dominated with around 98 golds, followed by host Japan and South Korea. With the Games running till 4 October, India's shooting and wrestling contingents remained key medal hopes, while the men's cricket team began its campaign from the quarter-finals on 28 September.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: GI-tagged Gulbarga Toor Dal exported to Maldives
capsules.body: APEDA facilitated the export of GI-tagged Gulbarga Toor Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives, reported on 25 September 2026. Gulbarga (Kalaburagi) tur dal received its Geographical Indication tag for its distinctive quality, and the Maldives shipment showcases India's agri-export push through value-added, origin-branded products.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Pensions Department launches SCDPM 6.0
capsules.body: The Department of Pensions and Pensioners' Welfare launched the Special Campaign for Clearance of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6.0 on 25 September 2026, targeting disposal of pension-related grievances and pending references. It runs parallel to the government-wide Special Campaign 6.0 for swachhata and record management (2-31 October 2026).

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Amit Shah inaugurates 4th UP International Trade Show
capsules.body: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the 4th edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show in Greater Noida on 25 September 2026, per PIB. The show promotes UP's MSMEs, ODOP (One District One Product) crafts and export potential, supporting the state's $1 trillion-economy aspiration.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: BIS expands mandatory quality-mark list for electronic goods
capsules.body: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) expanded its list of electronic products requiring mandatory quality certification in September 2026, adding to the existing list of smartphones, laptops, chargers, LED televisions, microwave ovens, printers and set-top boxes. BIS, established on 1 April 1987 and headquartered in New Delhi, functions as India's National Standards Body under the Department of Consumer Affairs.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India golds at Asiad
capsules.body: India's golds at the Aichi Asian Games came from the women's cricket T20 team, which beat Sri Lanka in the final, and the 10m air pistol mixed team of Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet on September 25. Both golds arrived in the opening week of the Games.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asiad shooting medals
capsules.body: Elavenil Valarivan won 10m air rifle silver plus team silver, Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon and Parth Mane took men's 10m air rifle team silver, the men's 50m rifle 3P team added silver, and both skeet mixed pairs won bronze. India had already confirmed its 100th Asiad shooting medal before the Aichi edition.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Mirabai Chanu Asiad silver
capsules.body: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49kg weightlifting at Aichi with 198kg (87kg snatch, 111kg clean and jerk), her first Asian Games medal. It ended India's 28-year wait for an Asiad weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari's 1998 bronze. North Korea's Ri Song-gum took gold with a 215kg world record.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asiad athletics medals
capsules.body: Gulveer Singh won silver in the men's 10,000m (28:29.38) and Seema Kumari bronze in the women's race. The mixed 4x400m relay took silver in 3:14.46, 36-year-old Manpreet Kaur won shot put bronze at 17.17m, and Baranica Elangovan's 4.15m pole vault bronze was India's first Asiad medal in the event.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asiad other Indian medals
capsules.body: Roshibina Devi won wushu silver (women's 60kg), her third Asiad medal. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan's rowing double-sculls bronze was India's first in the event. Jay Meena took soft tennis bronze, Suchika Tariyal MMA bronze, and the men's badminton team bronze. In hockey, Deepika Sehrawat scored nine goals against Thailand, an Asiad record.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India debutants at Asiad
capsules.body: At Aichi 2026, Jay Meena won soft tennis bronze, Suchika Tariyal MMA bronze, and Manush Shah-Diya Chitale table tennis mixed doubles bronze, marking podium finishes in newer Asiad disciplines. The women's cricket gold also kept India on course in team sports.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Biometric Aadhaar authentication mandatory for subsidised LPG refills
capsules.body: Biometric Aadhaar authentication will be mandatory for subsidised domestic LPG refills from 1 October 2026, reported in PIB-linked compilations on 20 September. The move aims to curb diversion and duplicate connections in the LPG subsidy system, extending Aadhaar-based verification to cooking-gas delivery.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: 25th SCO Summit held in Tianjin
capsules.body: The 25th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit was held in Tianjin, China, on 31 August–1 September 2025. The Tianjin Declaration condemned terrorism in all forms, opposed unilateral tariffs and protectionism, and called for cooperation in AI, energy security and sustainable development. Leaders backed reform of global governance. Kyrgyzstan assumed the SCO presidency for the next term.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Yudh Abhyas 2025 begins in Alaska
capsules.body: The India-US joint military exercise Yudh Abhyas 2025 began on 1 September at Fort Wainwright and the Yukon Training Area in Alaska, running till 14 September. Troops of the Indian Army's Madras Regiment trained alongside the US Army's 11th Airborne Division in high-altitude and cold-climate warfare, focusing on UN peacekeeping operations and interoperability.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: VIKRAM3201: India's first indigenous 32-bit space-grade processor
capsules.body: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw unveiled VIKRAM3201, India's first fully indigenous 32-bit microprocessor for space applications, at Semicon India 2025 in New Delhi. Developed by ISRO's Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and fabricated by the Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) on 180 nm CMOS technology, the chip is designed for launch-vehicle avionics and other strategic systems.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: US Open 2025: Alcaraz and Sabalenka triumph
capsules.body: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Jannik Sinner 6-2, 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 to win the US Open men's singles, his sixth Grand Slam title, regaining the world No. 1 ranking. Aryna Sabalenka beat Amanda Anisimova 6-3, 7-6 to retain the women's crown, becoming the first woman since Serena Williams (2014) to win back-to-back US Open titles. It was her fourth major.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: India win Men's Hockey Asia Cup in Rajgir
capsules.body: India defeated South Korea 4-1 in the final at Rajgir, Bihar, to win the Men's Hockey Asia Cup 2025. The victory, India's fourth Asia Cup title, secured direct qualification for the 2026 FIH Men's Hockey World Cup. The tournament was hosted at the Rajgir Hockey Stadium in Nalanda district.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Gen-Z protests topple Nepal government
capsules.body: Mass Gen-Z-led protests against a social-media ban and corruption forced Nepal Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli to resign on 9 September 2025. The agitation, which saw violent clashes and arson in Kathmandu, was triggered by the government's ban on platforms including Facebook, X and YouTube. The unrest marked one of Nepal's worst political crises in years.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India to host 5th Coast Guard Global Summit in Chennai in 2027
capsules.body: India will host the 5th Coast Guard Global Summit (CGGS) in Chennai in 2027, coinciding with the Golden Jubilee of the Indian Coast Guard. The decision was taken unanimously at the 4th CGGS in Rome (11–12 September), attended by delegates from 115 countries. India assumed the CGGS presidency from Italy; DG ICG Paramesh Sivamani led the Indian delegation.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: PM Modi visits Manipur
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Manipur on 13 September 2025, his first visit to the state since ethnic violence erupted in May 2023. In Churachandpur he laid foundation stones for projects worth over ₹7,300 crore, and in Imphal he inaugurated projects worth ₹1,200 crore, signalling a push for peace and development in the strife-torn state.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Purnea Airport terminal inaugurated
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the new terminal building of Purnea Airport on 15 September 2025 and flagged off the first Purnea–Kolkata flight. The airport, developed as a civil enclave at the Purnea airbase, boosts air connectivity for the Seemanchal and Kosi regions of Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: ₹36,000 crore development package for Purnea
capsules.body: At Purnea on 15 September, PM Modi launched development projects worth about ₹36,000 crore for Bihar. Key components include the 3×800 MW Pirpainti thermal power project (~₹25,000 crore) in Bhagalpur and Kosi–Mechi river-link Phase I (over ₹2,680 crore), aimed at power security and irrigation in north Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: National Makhana Board launched
capsules.body: PM Modi launched the National Makhana Board at Purnea on 15 September 2025. Headquartered in Bihar, which accounts for roughly 90% of India's makhana (fox nut) production, the Board will promote cultivation, processing, value addition and export of makhana, a major cash crop for Mithila and Seemanchal farmers.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Swasth Nari Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan launched
capsules.body: The Swasth Nari Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan, a nationwide women's health campaign, was launched on 17 September 2025. The initiative focuses on screening and awareness for anaemia, non-communicable diseases, and maternal and child health, with special health camps organised across aspirational districts.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: ₹5,000 cloth aid to 16 lakh Bihar construction workers
capsules.body: The Bihar government released ₹802.46 crore as cloth assistance of ₹5,000 each to 16.05 lakh registered construction workers on 17 September 2025. The direct benefit transfer, routed through the Bihar Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, targeted workers registered under the state's labour welfare schemes.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: US imposes $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions
capsules.body: US President Donald Trump signed a proclamation on 19 September 2025 imposing a one-time $100,000 payment on specified new H-1B visa petitions filed on or after 21 September. Existing visa holders and renewals were excluded. The move, aimed at curbing alleged abuse of the skilled-worker programme, directly affects Indian IT professionals, the largest H-1B beneficiaries.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: ICGS Adamya commissioned at Paradip
capsules.body: Indian Coast Guard Ship Adamya, the first of eight Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels, was commissioned at Paradip, Odisha, on 19 September 2025. The 51-metre, 320-tonne vessel, capable of 28 knots, is armed with a 30 mm CRN-91 gun and will be based at Paradip under ICG Region (North-East) for maritime security on the eastern seaboard.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2023) announced for Mohanlal
capsules.body: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023 was announced for Malayalam cinema legend Mohanlal on 20 September 2025. The 55th recipient of India's highest film honour — and the youngest ever at 65 — Mohanlal is a Padma Shri (2001) and Padma Bhushan (2019) awardee. President Droupadi Murmu presented the award at the 71st National Film Awards ceremony on 23 September.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: ₹25,000 tablet aid for Bihar Vikas Mitras
capsules.body: The Bihar government announced tablet assistance of ₹25,000 each for over 10,000 Vikas Mitras on 21 September 2025, to digitise grassroots service delivery. Their travel allowance was raised from ₹1,900 to ₹2,500 per month and the stationery allowance from ₹900 to ₹1,500, strengthening the Mahadalit outreach workforce.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: World Athletics Championships conclude in Tokyo
capsules.body: The World Athletics Championships concluded in Tokyo on 21 September 2025 with India returning without a medal. Javelin thrower Sachin Yadav finished fourth (86.27 m) and high jumper Sarvesh Kushare sixth (2.28 m) — India's best performances. The championships were dominated by the United States in the medal tally.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: ₹10,000 smartphone aid for Shiksha Sevaks
capsules.body: Bihar announced smartphone assistance of ₹10,000 each for over 30,000 Shiksha Sevaks and Talimi Markaz workers on 22 September 2025. The support aims to help literacy volunteers and minority-education workers use digital tools for teaching and reporting under the state's adult-education and madrasa-modernisation programmes.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 71st National Film Awards presented
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu presented the 71st National Film Awards in New Delhi on 23 September 2025. '12th Fail' won Best Feature Film; Shah Rukh Khan ('Jawan') and Vikrant Massey ('12th Fail') shared the Best Actor award; Rani Mukerji ('Mrs. Chatterjee vs Norway') won Best Actress. Mohanlal received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2023).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: TASL's defence plant inaugurated in Morocco
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Morocco's Abdelatif Loudyi jointly inaugurated Tata Advanced Systems' defence manufacturing facility at Berrechid, Morocco, on 23 September 2025. The 20,000 sq.m plant — the first overseas defence factory by an Indian private company in Africa — will produce the DRDO–TASL co-developed WhAP 8×8 armoured platform for the Royal Moroccan Army.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Agni-Prime tested from rail-based launcher
capsules.body: DRDO and the Strategic Forces Command successfully test-fired the Agni-Prime intermediate-range ballistic missile from a rail-based mobile launcher on 24 September 2025, in a full operational scenario. The canisterised missile, with a range up to 2,000 km, can be launched with short reaction time and reduced visibility, putting India among select nations with rail-mobile launch capability.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Jaishankar addresses 80th UNGA session
capsules.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the 80th session of the UN General Assembly in New York on 27 September 2025. He called for reformed multilateralism, condemned terrorism, and highlighted India's contributions to UN peacekeeping, climate action and digital public infrastructure, while holding bilateral meetings on the summit sidelines.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar SIR final roll: 7.42 crore electors
capsules.body: The Election Commission published Bihar's final electoral roll after the Special Intensive Revision on 30 September 2025, listing about 7.42 crore electors. Around 21.53 lakh names were added after the draft roll and 3.66 lakh deleted after scrutiny, concluding the contentious revision ahead of the Assembly elections.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Southwest monsoon 2025 ends at 108% of LPA
capsules.body: The southwest monsoon ended on 30 September 2025 with all-India rainfall at 108% of the Long Period Average — an above-normal season. Northwest India received 127%, central India 115% and the southern peninsula 110%, while east and northeast India got only 80%. Bihar remained rainfall-deficient despite the surplus elsewhere.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement in force
capsules.body: The India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement entered into force on 1 October 2025. Signed with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, the TEPA commits the bloc to $100 billion in investment and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years, in return for tariff concessions — India's first FTA with a European bloc.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: 6.9-magnitude earthquake strikes Cebu, Philippines
capsules.body: A 6.9-magnitude earthquake struck off Cebu in the Philippines on 30 September 2025, killing at least 72 people and damaging buildings and churches. The shallow quake in the seismically active Pacific Ring of Fire triggered landslides and disrupted power, with rescue operations continuing into October.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Assam–Nagaland border violence
capsules.body: Around 100 houses were torched in communal clashes along the Assam–Nagaland border on 2 October 2025, amid long-standing inter-state boundary disputes. Security forces were deployed and both state governments ordered inquiries, reviving attention on the unresolved border demarcation in the Northeast.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar hikes DA to 58%
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 3 October 2025 raised dearness allowance/dearness relief for state employees and pensioners from 55% to 58%, effective 1 July 2025. The hike, following the Centre's decision, will cost the exchequer ₹917.78 crore in FY26 and was among 129 proposals cleared in the government's last cabinet meeting before the Assembly polls.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar doubles school scholarships
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 3 October 2025 doubled annual scholarships for government-school students: Classes 1–4 from ₹600 to ₹1,200, Classes 5–6 from ₹1,200 to ₹2,400, and Classes 7–10 from ₹1,800 to ₹3,600. The hike covers government and aided schools, including minority institutions, madrasas and Sanskrit schools.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Stipend for new advocates, jobless allowance in Bihar
capsules.body: Bihar's 3 October cabinet approved a ₹5,000 monthly stipend for newly enrolled advocates for three years, and a ₹1,000 monthly unemployment allowance for graduate youth aged 20–25 for five years. It also cleared a state film and theatre institute, in a pre-poll package of 129 decisions.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: ₹2,500 crore to 25 lakh women under Mahila Rozgar Yojana
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar disbursed ₹2,500 crore to 25 lakh women beneficiaries under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana in Patna on 3 October 2025. Under the scheme, one woman per family receives ₹10,000 as seed support for self-employment, with up to ₹2 lakh additional assistance linked to enterprise progress.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2025
capsules.body: The Ministry of AYUSH conferred the National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2025 on 3 October. The awardees — Prof. Banwari Lal Gaur, Vaidya Neelakandhan Mooss E.T. and Vaidya Bhavana Prasher — were honoured for contributions to Ayurveda education, traditional knowledge and research, among the highest recognitions in the field.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI constitutes Payments Regulatory Board
capsules.body: The Reserve Bank of India constituted a six-member Payments Regulatory Board (PRB) headed by the RBI Governor to oversee payment systems. Proposed by the Watal Committee in 2017, the board will regulate and supervise digital payments, prepaid instruments and payment aggregators as India's cashless ecosystem expands.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Cabinet approves National Pulses Mission (2025–31)
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet approved the National Pulses Mission (2025–31) on 3 October 2025 to achieve self-sufficiency in pulses and cut import dependence. The mission focuses on quality seed distribution, expanded procurement at MSP, and incentives for tur, urad and masoor cultivation under an Atmanirbhar Bharat push.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's best-ever show at World Para Athletics
capsules.body: India recorded its best-ever medal haul at the World Para Athletics Championships, which concluded in New Delhi on 5 October 2025, winning 22 medals — 6 gold, 9 silver and 7 bronze — to finish tenth in the standings. The home championships marked a breakthrough for India's para-sport programme.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Israel–Hamas Gaza ceasefire deal signed
capsules.body: Israel and Hamas signed a Gaza ceasefire and hostage-release agreement at Sharm el-Sheikh on 9 October 2025, based on a 20-point peace plan. The ceasefire took effect on 10 October; Hamas released 20 surviving hostages on 13 October while Israel freed 1,968 Palestinian prisoners. A Gaza peace summit followed with 20+ world leaders.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Sonali Ghosh wins Kenton R. Miller Award
capsules.body: Dr. Sonali Ghosh, Field Director of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, became the first Indian to win the Kenton R. Miller Award for innovation in sustainable protected-area management on 10 October 2025. Presented by IUCN's World Commission on Protected Areas at the World Conservation Congress in Abu Dhabi, she shared it with Ecuador's Roque Simón Sevilla Larrea.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: NDA announces Bihar seat-sharing
capsules.body: The NDA announced its seat-sharing for the Bihar Assembly elections on 12 October 2025: the BJP and JD(U) will contest 101 seats each, Chirag Paswan's LJP (Ram Vilas) 29, and Upendra Kushwaha's RLM and Jitan Ram Manjhi's HAM (Secular) 6 each, for the 243-member House. Smaller allies publicly grumbled about their allocations.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: LEAPS 2025 logistics awards launched
capsules.body: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade launched the Logistics Excellence, Advancement, and Performance Shield (LEAPS) 2025 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 13 October, marking four years of PM GatiShakti.
