The national awards across 13 categories will benchmark logistics performance under the National Logistics Policy (2022).

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India elected to UN Human Rights Council
capsules.body: India was elected to the 47-member UN Human Rights Council for the 2026–28 term on 14 October 2025, securing 177 votes in the UN General Assembly. It will be India's seventh term on the Geneva-based body, which reviews human-rights records through the Universal Periodic Review mechanism.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: First transgender member of SC-appointed panel
capsules.body: Transgender rights activist Akkai Padmashali became the first transgender person appointed to a Supreme Court-constituted committee on 17 October 2025. Headed by former Delhi High Court judge Justice Asha Menon, the panel will draft a National Equal Opportunity Policy for transgender persons' protection and welfare.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Madagascar gets transitional president after Gen-Z uprising
capsules.body: Colonel Michael Randrianirina was sworn in as Madagascar's transitional president on 17 October 2025 after Gen-Z-led protests over shortages and corruption forced President Andry Rajoelina to flee on 14 October; parliament impeached Rajoelina the next day. The episode echoed Nepal's September upheaval.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: DRDO begins stratospheric airship trials
capsules.body: DRDO began the second phase of trials of its Stratospheric Airship Platform at Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh, on 18 October 2025, with further tests on 19, 25 and 26 October. The helium-filled unmanned airship, which reached 17 km in its May 2025 maiden flight, will test long-endurance surveillance and atmospheric sensors in the 15–20 km band.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Chhath 2025: four-day festival begins
capsules.body: Bihar's grand festival Chhath began with Nahay Khay on 25 October 2025, followed by Kharna (26th), Sandhya Arghya (27th) and Usha Arghya (28th). Devotees offered arghya to the setting and rising sun at ghats along the Ganga and other rivers, with the state government making elaborate cleanliness, safety and traffic arrangements.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Patrick Herminie sworn in as Seychelles President
capsules.body: Dr. Patrick Herminie was sworn in as the sixth President of Seychelles on 26 October 2025 at Unity Stadium, Victoria, after winning the presidential election with 52.7% of the vote. He succeeded Wavel Ramkalawan in the Indian Ocean island nation, a key partner in India's SAGAR maritime vision.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI announces SIR Phase II in 12 states/UTs
capsules.body: The Election Commission on 27 October 2025 announced Phase II of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories, covering about 51 crore electors. Enumeration runs 4 November–4 December 2025, with final rolls due 7 February 2026, extending the Bihar SIR model nationwide.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: ₹37,952 crore NBS subsidy for Rabi 2025–26
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet on 28 October 2025 approved ₹37,952.29 crore under the Nutrient-Based Subsidy scheme for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers — including DAP and NPKS grades — for Rabi 2025–26 (1 October 2025–31 March 2026). The subsidy keeps farm-gate prices affordable, supporting food security and stable input costs.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India pull off record chase in Women's World Cup semifinal
capsules.body: India chased down 339 against Australia in the ICC Women's ODI World Cup semifinal on 30 October 2025, reaching 341/5 in 48.3 overs — the highest successful chase in Women's World Cup history. Jemimah Rodrigues struck an unbeaten 127 and captain Harmanpreet Kaur 89, scripting a famous win.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Patel
capsules.body: India marked the 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on 31 October 2025, observed as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas). The 'Iron Man of India', who integrated 562 princely states, was honoured with unity runs, pledges and tributes at the Statue of Unity in Kevadia, Gujarat.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: LVM3-M5 launches CMS-03, India's heaviest satellite
capsules.body: ISRO's LVM3-M5 launched the 4,410 kg CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) into geosynchronous transfer orbit from Sriharikota on 2 November 2025 — the heaviest satellite ever launched from Indian soil. Costing ₹1,589 crore, the secure communications satellite will serve the Indian Navy, succeeding the decade-old GSAT-7.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India win maiden Women's ODI World Cup
capsules.body: India won their maiden ICC Women's ODI World Cup on 2 November 2025, beating South Africa by 52 runs in the final — 298/7 versus 246. Shafali Verma scored 87, while Deepti Sharma starred with 58 and 5/39. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur lifted the trophy, ending India's long wait for a women's world title.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Zohran Mamdani elected New York City mayor
capsules.body: Zohran Mamdani was elected New York City's mayor on 4 November 2025, becoming the city's first Muslim and first South Asian mayor-elect — and its youngest since 1917. The 34-year-old democratic socialist takes office on 1 January 2026, marking a generational shift in America's largest city.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Phase I voting held
capsules.body: The first phase of the Bihar Assembly elections was held on 6 November 2025, covering 121 of the 243 constituencies. Elaborate security and central forces were deployed across sensitive booths as the NDA and the Mahagathbandhan faced off in a high-stakes contest.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 150 years of Vande Mataram commemorated
capsules.body: A year-long commemoration of 150 years of 'Vande Mataram' was launched on 7 November 2025. Composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterji in 1875 and later adopted as India's national song, the occasion was marked with a commemorative coin and postage stamp honouring its role in the freedom movement.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sonepur Mela begins
capsules.body: The historic Harihar Kshetra Sonepur Mela began on 9 November 2025 in Saran district, at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak. The month-long fair (till 10 December), one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, draws traders, pilgrims and tourists to the Hariharnath temple town.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: SWAYAM green defence manufacturing initiative launched
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched SWAYAM (Sustainable and Green Defence Manufacturing) on 10 November 2025 while inaugurating the DPSU Bhavan in New Delhi. Anchored in the Comprehensive Energy Efficiency Action Plan (2023), it pushes energy efficiency, renewables and lower emissions across defence PSUs, tracked via the SWARNA dashboard. Four DPSUs — MIL, AVNL, IOL and HSL — were granted Miniratna Category-I status.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Sergio Gor sworn in as US Ambassador to India
capsules.body: Sergio Gor was sworn in as the United States Ambassador to India on 10 November 2025 in Washington, in a ceremony presided over by President Donald Trump. He will concurrently serve as Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, underlining the strategic weight of the India-US partnership.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar records highest turnout since 1951
capsules.body: The second phase of Bihar polling on 11 November 2025 saw the state record its highest-ever voter turnout of 66.91% — the best since 1951. Women outvoted men at 71.6% versus 62.8%, across 45,399 polling stations in Phase II, signalling deep democratic engagement.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules notified
capsules.body: The government notified the final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, on 13 November. Data Protection Board provisions take effect immediately, consent-manager rules after 12 months, and principal compliance obligations after 18 months, operationalising India's first comprehensive data-privacy law.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Jharkhand marks 25 years of statehood
capsules.body: Jharkhand observed its 25th Foundation Day on 15 November 2025, marking a quarter-century since its carving out of Bihar on 15 November 2000. The silver-jubilee celebrations highlighted the tribal-dominated state's mineral wealth and development journey.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Kolkata's 'On the Edge?' wins CIMUSET Award
capsules.body: Science City Kolkata's climate-change gallery 'On the Edge?' won the CIMUSET Award on 15 November 2025 at the 27th ICOM General Conference in Dubai. Developed by the National Council of Science Museums under the Ministry of Culture, the interactive gallery highlights climate change and sustainability.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 16th Finance Commission submits report
capsules.body: The 16th Finance Commission, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, submitted its report for 2026–31 to President Droupadi Murmu on 17 November 2025, under Articles 280 and 281. The report recommends the vertical and horizontal devolution of taxes between the Centre and states for the next five-year award period.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: First Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Awards conferred
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu conferred the first Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Awards and the 6th National Water Awards (2025) at Vigyan Bhawan on 18 November 2025. The JSJB awards honour community-led water conservation under the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain campaign. In the National Water Awards, Maharashtra was adjudged Best State, followed by Gujarat and Haryana.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish gives up Home portfolio to BJP after 20 years
capsules.body: A day after the oath-taking, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar allocated cabinet portfolios on 21 November 2025, giving up the Home department to ally BJP for the first time since he came to power in 2005. Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary (BJP) became Home Minister, while Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Sinha got Land and Revenue. Nitish retained General Administration, Cabinet Secretariat and Vigilance.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Four labour codes come into force
capsules.body: The four labour codes — on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations (2020), Social Security (2020), and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (2020) — came into force on 21 November 2025, consolidating 29 central labour laws. The overhaul modernises definitions of wages, working hours, and social-security coverage including gig workers.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: G20 Leaders' Summit held in Johannesburg
capsules.body: The first G20 Leaders' Summit on African soil was held in Johannesburg on 22–23 November 2025 under South Africa's theme of 'Solidarity, Equality and Sustainability'. The leaders' declaration addressed disaster resilience, debt relief, just energy transitions and critical minerals, though the US boycott dispute shadowed proceedings.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Justice Surya Kant becomes 53rd CJI
capsules.body: Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025, succeeding Justice B.R. Gavai. His tenure runs till 9 February 2027. Elevated to the Supreme Court in 2019, he has presided over key constitutional benches.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Justice Vikram Nath to head NALSA
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu nominated Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath as Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), effective 24 November 2025. He succeeds Justice Surya Kant, who vacated the post on becoming CJI. CJI Kant separately nominated Justice J.K. Maheshwari as Chairman of the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar cabinet approves AI Mission, one-crore jobs target
capsules.body: In its first meeting on 25 November 2025, the new Bihar cabinet approved the Bihar State AI Mission and a target of one crore jobs and employment opportunities over five years. It also cleared 11 greenfield townships, 25 new sugar mills (and revival of nine closed ones), plus plans for a defence corridor and semiconductor park.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: South Africa win Test series in India 2–0
capsules.body: South Africa completed a 2–0 Test series win in India on 26 November 2025 — their first series victory in India since 2000. They won the second Test at Guwahati by 408 runs, with off-spinner Simon Harmer taking 17 wickets in the match, as India's home dominance crumbled.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Q2 FY26 GDP grows 8.2%
capsules.body: India's real GDP grew 8.2% in Q2 FY26 (July–September 2025), sharply up from 5.6% a year earlier, as per NSO estimates released 28 November. Manufacturing grew 9.1%, construction 7.2% and the tertiary sector 9.2%, cementing India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 29 women elected to Bihar Assembly
capsules.body: Twenty-nine women were elected as MLAs in the 2025 Bihar Assembly — up from 26 in 2020, though below the record 34 of 2010. Twenty-six belong to the NDA and three to the RJD, reflecting incremental gains in women's political representation.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 26th Hornbill Festival begins
capsules.body: The 26th Hornbill Festival began on 1 December 2025 at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, Nagaland, running till 10 December. Named after the hornbill bird, the ten-day cultural extravaganza showcases Naga tribes' music, dance, cuisine and indigenous games, and is a flagship tourism event of the Northeast.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Ramakrishnan Chander appointed LIC MD
capsules.body: The Ministry of Finance appointed Ramakrishnan Chander as Managing Director of the Life Insurance Corporation of India on 1 December 2025. LIC, India's largest insurer, manages assets worth trillions and plays a systemic role in the country's financial markets.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Konark and Sand Art festivals inaugurated
capsules.body: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi inaugurated the 15th International Sand Art Festival and the 36th Konark Festival on 1 December 2025 at the Konark Sun Temple heritage site. The twin festivals, running till 5 December, celebrate Odisha's art, dance and sculpture traditions.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Usha Janakiraman appointed RBI Executive Director
capsules.body: The Reserve Bank of India appointed Usha Janakiraman as Executive Director with effect from 1 December 2025, assigning her the Department of Supervision (Risk, Analytics and Vulnerability Assessment). A former Chief General Manager-in-charge of the Department of Regulation, she brings over three decades of experience in banking supervision.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 'Rage Bait' is Oxford Word of the Year 2025
capsules.body: Oxford University Press named 'rage bait' — content designed to provoke anger for online engagement — as its Word of the Year 2025 on 1 December. The choice reflects the lexicon of the attention economy, where outrage-driven posts dominate social-media algorithms and discourse.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Prem Kumar elected Bihar Assembly Speaker
capsules.body: Senior BJP leader Prem Kumar was unanimously elected the 18th Speaker of the Bihar Legislative Assembly on 2 December 2025. The nine-term Gaya Town MLA's unopposed election — the first since 2015 — reflected the NDA's comfortable majority in the new House.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: 14th EKUVERIN exercise begins in Kerala
capsules.body: The 14th edition of EKUVERIN, the annual bilateral military exercise between the Indian Army and the Maldives National Defence Force, commenced at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, on 2 December 2025, running till 15 December. The exercise focuses on counter-insurgency and humanitarian assistance drills.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Central Excise (Amendment) Bill passed
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025, on 3 December, raising excise duties on tobacco products. Introduced in the Lok Sabha on 1 December, the amendment aims to discourage tobacco consumption while boosting revenue, aligning with public-health objectives.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Putin visits India for 23rd Annual Summit
capsules.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi on 4 December 2025 for a two-day state visit — his first since 2021 — for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit. Talks with PM Modi covered defence, trade, energy, civil nuclear cooperation and labour mobility, reaffirming the 'special and privileged' strategic partnership.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Assembly session: Deputy Speaker elected, ₹37,498 cr budget
capsules.body: Bihar's five-day Assembly session concluded on 5 December 2025 with Narendra Narayan Yadav elected Deputy Speaker. The House passed a second supplementary budget exceeding ₹37,498 crore, including ₹24,050 crore for rural development, setting the new government's spending priorities.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI cuts repo rate to 5.25%
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee cut the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.25% on 5 December 2025, retaining a neutral stance. The SDF stands at 5.00% and the MSF/Bank Rate at 5.50%. The central bank raised the FY26 growth forecast to 7.3% and projected inflation at 2.0%.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Raj Bhavans renamed Lok Bhavan
capsules.body: On a Ministry of Home Affairs directive, Raj Bhavans were redesignated as Lok Bhavan and Raj Niwas as Lok Niwas, with the PMO complex renamed Seva Teerth (from Executive Enclave). Twenty states — including Bihar — renamed their Raj Bhavans, while J&K and Ladakh adopted Lok Niwas, signalling a 'citizen-first' governance ethos.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Trump receives inaugural FIFA Peace Prize
capsules.body: US President Donald Trump received the inaugural 'FIFA Peace Prize — Football Unites the World' on 5 December 2025 from FIFA President Gianni Infantino at the Kennedy Center, Washington D.C., during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final Draw ceremony. The new award recognises contributions to global peace through football.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NASA loses contact with MAVEN Mars orbiter
capsules.body: NASA lost communication with the MAVEN spacecraft on 6 December 2025 after normal operations, ending over a decade in Mars orbit. Launched in 2013, the Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution mission studied how the Red Planet lost its atmosphere, reshaping understanding of Martian climate history.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: India International Science Festival held in Panchkula
capsules.body: The India International Science Festival (IISF) 2025 was held at Panchkula, Haryana, from 6–9 December, co-organised by the Ministry of Earth Sciences. The festival brought together scientists, students and innovators to celebrate India's scientific achievements and promote a culture of inquiry.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Simranpreet Kaur wins ISSF World Cup Final gold
capsules.body: India's Simranpreet Kaur Brar, 21, won gold in the women's 25m pistol at the ISSF World Cup Final 2025 in Doha on 8 December, scoring 41/50 to equal the junior world record. She beat China's Yao Qianxun (silver) and Germany's Doreen Vennekamp (bronze) for her maiden World Cup Final medal.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar creates three new departments
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 9 December 2025 created three new departments — Youth, Employment & Skill Development; Higher Education; and Civil Aviation — to sharpen governance focus. The restructuring separates higher education from the school-education department and gives dedicated attention to jobs and aviation infrastructure.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Rajnath Singh inaugurates 125 BRO projects
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated 125 Border Roads Organisation infrastructure projects — 28 roads, 93 bridges and four others, worth ₹5,000 crore — from Ladakh in December 2025, the highest single-day BRO rollout. Key assets include the 920-metre Shyok Tunnel on the Durbuk–Shyok–Daulat Beg Oldie road along the LAC. He also virtually inaugurated the Galwan War Memorial honouring the 2020 clash heroes.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Handicraft Awards 2023–24 conferred
capsules.body: The Ministry of Textiles conferred the National Handicraft Awards for 2023 and 2024 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, on 9 December 2025, as part of National Handicrafts Week celebrations. The awards honour master craftspersons for preserving and innovating India's traditional crafts.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Germany win Junior Hockey World Cup
capsules.body: Germany won their eighth FIH Men's Junior Hockey World Cup on 10 December 2025, beating Spain 3–2 in a shoot-out after a 1–1 draw in the final. Hosts India defeated Argentina 4–2 to claim bronze. The tournament was co-hosted by Chennai and Madurai in Tamil Nadu.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar portfolio allocation notified
capsules.body: Bihar's portfolio notification on 12 December 2025 assigned Youth, Employment & Skill Development to Sanjay Singh 'Tiger' and Higher Education to Sunil Kumar, while Chief Minister Nitish Kumar retained Civil Aviation. The allocation operationalised the three new departments created on 9 December.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: DHRUV64: India's first 1 GHz indigenous microprocessor
capsules.body: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) launched DHRUV64 on 15 December 2025 — India's first fully indigenous 1.0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core microprocessor, developed under MeitY's Microprocessor Development Programme. With open-source architecture and zero licensing costs, it targets 5G, IoT, automotive and industrial-automation applications.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: ₹476-crore makhana scheme rolled out
capsules.body: The National Makhana Board held its first meeting on 15 December 2025, rolling out a ₹476-crore Central Sector Scheme (2025–31) for the holistic development of the makhana sector — covering research, seed production, farmer training, value addition, branding and exports. Bihar, producing ~90% of India's makhana, is the chief beneficiary.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM-SETU: five National Centres of Excellence for skilling
capsules.body: Under the PM-SETU skilling reform, five National Centres of Excellence were announced — at Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur and Ludhiana — with Singapore partnering for advanced manufacturing at Chennai. Component I will upgrade 1,000 government ITIs on a hub-and-spoke model with mandatory industry partnership, addressing India's low formal-skilling rate.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar approves Saat Nishchay-3 (2025–30)
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 16 December 2025 approved Saat Nishchay-3, the state's development agenda for 2025–30, spanning employment and income, industry, agriculture, education, health, infrastructure and ease of living. It targets one crore youth opportunities, prioritises 94 lakh poor families, and aims to double average per-capita income.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Ashwini Tewari re-appointed SBI MD
capsules.body: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved the re-appointment of Ashwini Kumar Tewari as Managing Director of the State Bank of India on 16 December 2025. His extended tenure will run from 27 January 2026 to 31 December 2027, ensuring leadership continuity at India's largest bank.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Navy commissions INAS 335 'Ospreys'
capsules.body: The Indian Navy commissioned INAS 335 'Ospreys' — its MH-60R Seahawk helicopter squadron — at INS Hansa, Goa, on 17 December 2025. Presided over by Admiral Dinesh K. Tripathi, the squadron boosts anti-submarine, anti-surface and search-and-rescue capabilities on the Western seaboard.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India–Oman CEPA signed in Muscat
capsules.body: India and Oman signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in Muscat on 18 December 2025, covering goods, services, investment and professional movement. The pact, concluded during PM Modi's visit marking 70 years of diplomatic ties, deepens economic engagement with the key Gulf partner.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: PM Modi receives Oman's highest civilian honour
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred the First Class of the Order of Oman — the Sultanate's highest civilian honour — by Sultan Haitham bin Tarik on 18 December 2025 in Muscat. It was his 29th international award, coinciding with 70 years of India–Oman diplomatic relations.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: PM Modi visits Assam and West Bengal
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Assam and West Bengal on 20–21 December 2025, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for highways, airport and fertiliser projects. In Guwahati he opened India's first nature-themed airport terminal at LGBI Airport and unveiled an 80-foot statue of Assam's first CM Gopinath Bordoloi, and laid the foundation for an ammonia-urea plant at Dibrugarh.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Shashwat Sharma to head Airtel India
capsules.body: Shashwat Sharma was appointed Managing Director and CEO of Airtel India on 20 December 2025, effective 1 January 2026, for a five-year term. He succeeds Gopal Vittal, who moves to Executive Vice Chairman after a 13-year tenure as CEO, in a planned leadership transition at India's second-largest telecom operator.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: IOL–Safran pact for navigation systems
capsules.body: India Optel Ltd (IOL) signed an agreement with Safran Electronics & Defense on 22 December 2025 in New Delhi for manufacturing the SIGMA 30N inertial navigation system and CM3-MR direct-firing sight in India. Signed by CMD Tushar Tripathi and Safran's Alexandre Ziegler, it builds on a January 2024 MoU for artillery, air-defence and anti-drone systems.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India–New Zealand FTA concluded
capsules.body: India and New Zealand concluded a comprehensive Free Trade Agreement on 22 December 2025 — among India's fastest FTAs with a developed country, wrapped up in nine months over five rounds. Indian exports get zero-duty access on 100% of NZ tariff lines; India liberalised ~70%, excluding dairy, sugar and edible oils. It offers post-study work visas, 5,000 professional visas and a $20-billion investment commitment.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 359th Prakash Parv at Patna Sahib
capsules.body: The 359th Prakash Parv (birth anniversary) of Guru Gobind Singh concluded at Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib, Patna Sahib, on 27 December 2025. Born in Patna in 1666, Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699; the celebrations drew devotees from across the world to his birthplace.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Rithvik Sanjeevi wins National Badminton title
capsules.body: Rithvik Sanjeevi won the men's singles title at the 87th Senior National Badminton Championship in Vijayawada on 28 December 2025, beating Bharat Raghav 21–16, 22–20 in the final after overcoming Kiran George in the semifinals. The tournament featured 128 players.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Lav Aggarwal appointed DGFT
capsules.body: Lav Aggarwal, a 1996-batch IAS officer of the Andhra Pradesh cadre, was appointed Director General of Foreign Trade on 30 December 2025. Formerly Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Women and Child Development, his ACC-approved appointment puts him at the helm of India's export-promotion regime.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 43 IPS officers promoted in Bihar; Kundan Krishnan elevated to DGP rank
capsules.body: The Bihar Home Department notified the promotion of 43 IPS officers effective January 1, 2026. Kundan Krishnan (1994 batch), serving as ADG (Headquarters) and on central deputation, was elevated to the rank of Director General of Police. Shalin (2001 batch) rose from IG to ADG. Eight DIGs of the 2008 batch, including Manoj Kumar, Sanjay Kumar, Vivekananda and Vikash Burman, were promoted to Inspector General, while five more 2008-batch officers on central deputation received conditional IG promotions subject to Phase-IV Mid-Career Training.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor takes charge as Vice Chief of Air Staff
capsules.body: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor took charge as Vice Chief of the Air Staff on January 1, 2026, succeeding Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari. Commissioned into the fighter stream in December 1986, he has 3,400+ flying hours on MiG-21 and MiG-29 aircraft and played a key role in inducting the PC-7 Mk II trainer. He served as Defence Attache to Pakistan and as Senior Air Staff Officer at Central Air Command. He holds the VSM, AVSM, PVSM and the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal awarded for his role in Operation Sindoor.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish inaugurates two-day state police conference in Patna
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated a two-day state-level police conference at the Police Headquarters, Sardar Patel Bhawan, Patna, on January 12, 2026, with Home Minister Samrat Choudhary and DGP Vinay Kumar present. For the first time, officers of every level, from the DGP down to station house officers, interacted simultaneously with the Chief Minister, with district officers joining via video conferencing. The agenda covered curbing rising crime, police modernisation, cyber and digital crime, technology use in policing, and rebuilding police-public trust.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish cabinet approves 41 proposals on jobs and infrastructure
capsules.body: The first cabinet meeting of 2026, chaired by CM Nitish Kumar on January 13, approved 41 proposals focused on job generation and infrastructure. Key decisions: Rs 33.29 crore for a 220 KV DC transmission line to supply uninterrupted power to the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster at Gaya via the Bihar State Power Transmission Company; creation of 694 posts in the Agriculture Department (534 Plant Protection Supervisor and 160 Plant Protection Inspector) under the Bihar Agriculture Subordinate Service (Category-05); and a temporary ex-cadre post of Forest and Environment Advisor for three years.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: ACC appoints new Directors General of NIA, BSF and ITBP
capsules.body: On January 14, 2026, the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved new Directors General for three security agencies. Rakesh Aggarwal (1994-batch, Himachal Pradesh cadre) became DG of the National Investigation Agency till August 31, 2028. Praveen Kumar (1993-batch, West Bengal cadre) became DG of the Border Security Force till September 30, 2030, succeeding Daljit Singh Chawdhary. Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor (1990-batch, Haryana cadre; former Haryana DGP) became DG of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police till October 31, 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: National Startup Day 2026 marks 10 years of Startup India
capsules.body: National Startup Day was observed on January 16, 2026, marking a decade of the Startup India initiative launched on January 16, 2016 by DPIIT. India now has over 2,00,000 DPIIT-recognised startups, 6.6 lakh+ portal users, 240+ incubators under the Seed Fund Scheme and Rs 27,000+ crore of funding mobilised. About 53% of startups are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, 48% have at least one woman director, and 32 states/UTs have startup policies. The day was declared in 2022; the PM highlighted the milestone at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ICMR developing improved indigenous Kyasanur Forest Disease vaccine
capsules.body: The Indian Council of Medical Research is developing an improved indigenous vaccine for Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD), a tick-borne viral haemorrhagic fever endemic to the Western Ghats (Karnataka, Kerala, Goa, Maharashtra) and transmitted by Haemaphysalis ticks. The existing vaccine has limited efficacy and needs annual boosters; the improved version aims at stronger immunogenicity and longer protection, supporting the One Health approach to zoonotic diseases.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India and Germany sign Joint Declaration of Intent on telecom cooperation
capsules.body: In January 2026, India and Germany signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on Telecommunications Cooperation, deepening the digital partnership alongside Chancellor Friedrich Merz's January 12-13 visit to India. The cooperation covers 5G/6G, digital public infrastructure, cybersecurity and supply-chain resilience, complementing the India-EU free trade agreement and the first-ever India-EU defence and security partnership concluded in the same month.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Parakram Diwas 2026: 129th birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
capsules.body: Parakram Diwas was observed on January 23, 2026, the 129th birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose (born January 23, 1897, in Cuttack). The Day of Valour recalls the Indian National Army, the provisional Azad Hind government of 1943 and his call of 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'. The day was instituted in 2021 ahead of the 125th birth anniversary.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: National Voters' Day 2026 observed on January 25
capsules.body: National Voters' Day was observed on January 25, 2026, commemorating the foundation day of the Election Commission of India (established January 25, 1950). Celebrated since 2011, the day honours voters, encourages youth enrolment and strengthens democratic values. The ECI is a permanent constitutional body under Article 324; current focus areas include electoral-roll purity, EPIC-Aadhaar linkage and accessible polling.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Maharashtra Deputy CM Ajit Pawar dies in aircraft crash at Baramati
capsules.body: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and NCP leader Ajit Pawar died in an aircraft crash at Baramati, Pune district, on January 28, 2026. A six-time MLA from Baramati and the state's finance minister, he dominated Maharashtra politics for three decades through cooperative-sector politics and led the 2023 NCP split that aligned his faction with the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar doubles SC/ST pre-matric scholarships after 15 years
capsules.body: The January 29 cabinet doubled the Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe students, the first revision since 2011. Effective FY 2025-26, annual rates are Rs 1,200 (Classes 1-4), Rs 2,400 (Classes 5-6), Rs 3,600 (Classes 7-10) and Rs 6,000 for hostel students. Around 27 lakh students benefit at a state expenditure of Rs 519.64 crore. Grants and income limits for backward-class scholarship and hostel schemes were also enhanced.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Ustad Bismillah Khan music college approved for Dumraon, Buxar
capsules.body: The state cabinet approved a music college at Dumraon in Buxar district, named after Bharat Ratna Ustad Bismillah Khan, with a fresh sanction of Rs 87.81 crore under the state plan (an earlier Rs 14.52 crore sanction was cancelled). Funds cover the college building, furniture, internal roads and boundary wall; the college will offer education in various disciplines of music.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar to recruit 17,000 retired Army and CAPF personnel on contract
capsules.body: The January 29 cabinet cleared the contractual recruitment of 17,000 retired personnel from the Indian Army and Central Paramilitary Forces in FY 2026-27 to strengthen law and order, combat crime and curb extremism. It also raised the honorarium of Special Armed Police (SAP) personnel with immediate effect. The move follows the January 12-13 state police conference on force modernisation.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Budget 2026-27: Biopharma SHAKTI and Semiconductor Mission 2.0
capsules.body: In her ninth consecutive budget, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced Biopharma SHAKTI with Rs 10,000 crore over five years to make India a global biopharma manufacturing hub. Semiconductor Mission 2.0 will focus on industry-led research, equipment and materials, full-stack Indian IP and supply-chain fortification. The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme outlay was raised to Rs 40,000 crore, and dedicated Rare Earth Corridors will come up in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu for mining, processing, research and manufacturing.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Budget 2026-27: Rs 12.2 lakh crore capex and 7 high-speed rail corridors
capsules.body: The Union Budget raised the Centre's capital expenditure by nearly 9% to Rs 12.2 lakh crore for FY 2026-27 (from Rs 11.21 lakh crore). Seven high-speed rail corridors were announced, including Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri. Also announced: 20 new National Highways, 20 new national waterways, a Rs 10,000 crore container-manufacturing scheme over five years, Mega Textile Parks in challenge mode, an integrated textile programme, the Mahatma Gandhi Gram Swaraj initiative for khadi and handloom, and a sports-goods manufacturing push.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Budget 2026-27: Income Tax Act 2025 from April 1; buyback taxed as capital gains
capsules.body: The Income Tax Act, 2025 will come into force on April 1, 2026, with simplified rules and redesigned forms. Share buybacks will be taxed as capital gains for all shareholders to curb promoter misuse: corporate promoters pay an additional buyback tax (effective 22%), non-corporate promoters 30%. TCS on scrap and minerals was rationalised to 2%, and TCS on LRS remittances for education and medical treatment cut from 5% to 2%. Municipal bonds get a Rs 100 crore incentive for a single issuance above Rs 1,000 crore.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Budget 2026-27: record Rs 2,761.80 crore for fisheries
capsules.body: The budget gave the highest-ever budgetary support of Rs 2,761.80 crore to fisheries, with the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana receiving Rs 2,500 crore. The integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars will strengthen the fisheries value chain with startups, women-led groups and Fish Farmer Producer Organisations. Fish catch by Indian vessels in the EEZ and high seas was made duty-free, foreign port landings treated as exports, and the duty-free import limit for seafood-processing inputs raised from 1% to 3%.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Union Budget's Bihar push: high-speed rail, waterways, Patna ship repair
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar welcomed the Union Budget 2026-27 for Bihar's connectivity and jobs: the Varanasi-Siliguri high-speed rail corridor will benefit the state; 20 new national waterways include a ship-repair and maintenance facility at Patna (land already allotted) and a water metro route from Bihar to Varanasi; a Patna-Varanasi freight corridor was announced. Mega Textile Parks and the Rs 40,000 crore semiconductor support are expected to create youth employment, alongside five new tourist destinations and Buddhist-site development.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Major gubernatorial reshuffle across states and Union Territories
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu effected a major reshuffle of governors and lieutenant governors in March 2026: Jishnu Dev Varma (former Telangana Governor) became Governor of Maharashtra; Taranjit Singh Sandhu (former Ambassador to the US) became Lieutenant Governor of Delhi; Vinai Kumar Saxena (former Delhi LG) became LG of Ladakh, replacing Kavinder Gupta. The reshuffle aimed at administrative continuity ahead of upcoming assembly elections.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi reappointed Drugs Controller General of India
capsules.body: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet reappointed Dr Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi as Drugs Controller General of India at the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation on a one-year contract from March 1, 2026, until a regular incumbent is appointed. The DCGI heads India's apex drug regulator, clearing new drugs, clinical trials and vaccines.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: B.P. Singh takes charge as Director General of Naval Armament
capsules.body: Shri B.P. Singh assumed charge as Director General of Naval Armament at Naval Headquarters, New Delhi. As DGONA he is the Navy's apex officer for weapon management, overseeing armament policy, procurement and life-cycle management of naval weapons.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Wildlife Day 2026 observed on March 3
capsules.body: World Wildlife Day 2026 was observed on March 3 with the theme 'Medicinal and Aromatic Plants: Conserving Health, Heritage and Livelihoods'. The National Zoological Park, New Delhi, organised a marathon under the motto 'Each Step Towards Wildlife Conservation'. The day marks the 1973 adoption of CITES, the convention regulating international wildlife trade.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: WEF President and CEO Borge Brende resigns
capsules.body: Borge Brende, President and Chief Executive Officer of the World Economic Forum, resigned in March 2026. The Geneva-based WEF, founded in 1971 by Klaus Schwab, hosts the annual Davos meeting that brings together global political leaders, business heads and policymakers.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Fino Payments Bank MD and CEO Rishi Gupta arrested for tax evasion
capsules.body: Rishi Gupta, Managing Director and CEO of Fino Payments Bank, was arrested under provisions of the CGST and SGST Acts, 2017, for alleged tax evasion, a rare instance of a bank chief being arrested under GST law. Fino is a listed payments bank focused on underbanked customers.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nand Kishore Yadav appointed Governor of Nagaland
capsules.body: Former Bihar Assembly Speaker and BJP leader Nand Kishore Yadav was appointed Governor of Nagaland in the March 2026 gubernatorial reshuffle. A veteran Bihar politician with long legislative experience, his posting brings administrative steadiness to the strategically sensitive northeastern state.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: International Women's Day 2026 observed on March 8
capsules.body: International Women's Day 2026 was observed on March 8 with the UN theme 'Rights. Justice. Action. For ALL Women and Girls.' The global 'Give to Gain' campaign was launched to accelerate gender parity through mentorship and collective support; the UN flagged that women hold only 64% of the legal rights men enjoy worldwide. In India, a 'Shakti Walk' (#SheLeadsBharat) was organised on Kartavya Path, New Delhi.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Delhi Metro expansion: two corridors opened, three more launched
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated two new Delhi Metro corridors and laid the foundation for three more lines on March 8, 2026, alongside projects worth Rs 33,500 crore under the GPRA redevelopment plan, among the largest urban-transit and government-housing pushes in the capital.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Museum-Patna Museum tunnel project launched at Rs 542 crore
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the construction of a tunnel connecting the Bihar Museum and the Patna Museum at an estimated cost of Rs 542 crore on March 8, 2026. The tunnel will allow seamless visitor movement between the modern Bihar Museum (opened 2015) and the colonial-era Patna Museum (established 1917, the 'Jadu Ghar'), famed for its Mauryan and Gupta-era sculptures, ancient coins, terracotta and a 200-million-year-old fossilised tree.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish launches Rs 569.36 crore projects in Supaul during Samriddhi Yatra
capsules.body: During his Samriddhi Yatra, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 213 development projects worth Rs 569.36 crore in Supaul on March 10, 2026: foundation stones for 84 projects (Rs 434.47 crore) and inauguration of 129 projects (Rs 134.90 crore). He cited central support including the Makhana Board and a new Bihar airport announced in the Union Budget.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Jose Antonio Kast sworn in as 38th President of Chile
capsules.body: Jose Antonio Kast Rist, founder and leader of Chile's Republican Party, was sworn in as the 38th President of Chile for a four-year term after winning the 2025 presidential election, marking a rightward shift in Latin American politics.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: New plant species Osbeckia zubeengargiana discovered in Manas
capsules.body: Scientists discovered Osbeckia zubeengargiana, a new flowering plant species, in Manas National Park, Assam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and major tiger-elephant reserve. Such discoveries in protected areas strengthen biodiversity documentation and conservation planning in the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India wins five medals at World Boxing Futures Cup in Bangkok
capsules.body: India finished the World Boxing Futures Cup 2026 in Bangkok with a total of five medals, underlining the country's growing bench strength in international boxing beyond its Olympic medalists.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: BCCI Naman Awards 2026 held in New Delhi
capsules.body: The BCCI Naman Awards 2026 were held in New Delhi on March 15, 2026, to honour excellence in Indian cricket, coming a week after India's T20 World Cup triumph on March 8.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gujarat launches its first sounding rocket near Dholera
capsules.body: Gujarat successfully launched its first sounding rocket from near Dholera on March 15, 2026, a milestone for the state's space ecosystem around the Dholera special investment region. Sounding rockets carry scientific instruments on sub-orbital flights for atmospheric and microgravity research.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India tops World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026 with 208 medals
capsules.body: India finished first at the World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026 held in New Delhi with a record tally of 208 medals, showcasing the country's remarkable depth in para-sports ahead of major international championships.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Kimi Antonelli wins Chinese Grand Prix for maiden F1 victory
capsules.body: Kimi Antonelli won the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix, claiming his first Formula 1 victory and announcing the arrival of the sport's new generation at the front of the grid.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: K.V. Ramana Murty appointed SEBI whole-time member
capsules.body: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved the appointment of Kompella Venkata Ramana Murty as Whole-Time Member of the Securities and Exchange Board of India, strengthening the market regulator's leadership for securities-market oversight.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Manjeet Singh named ECI Special Observer for Assam Assembly election
capsules.body: The Election Commission of India appointed Manjeet Singh, retired IAS officer of the 1988 batch (Rajasthan cadre), as Special Observer for the 2026 Assam Legislative Assembly election, a standard ECI mechanism to ensure free and fair polls in sensitive states.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: William Dalrymple wins Mark Lynton History Prize 2026
capsules.body: Historian William Dalrymple won the Mark Lynton History Prize 2026 for 'The Golden Road: How Ancient India Transformed the World', which traces ancient India's cultural and economic influence across Asia.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Bhumika Shrestha becomes Nepal's first transgender woman MP
capsules.body: Bhumika Shrestha, a 37-year-old LGBTQ rights activist, became Nepal's first transgender woman Member of Parliament, a historic milestone for inclusion and marginalised representation in South Asia, weeks before Balendra Shah became Nepal's youngest prime minister.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Diwas 2026: 114th foundation day celebrated
capsules.body: Bihar celebrated its 114th foundation day from March 22 to 24 at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on the theme 'Unnat Bihar, Ujjwal Bihar'. Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the three-day event. Bihar was carved out of the Bengal Presidency on March 22, 1912, and Bihar Diwas has been celebrated as a statewide festival since 2010. Cultural performances featured Sona Mohapatra, Shaan and Papon; President Droupadi Murmu extended greetings to the state.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Fifth phase of Samriddhi Yatra begins; projects for Jehanabad
capsules.body: Chief Minister Nitish Kumar commenced the fifth phase of his 'Samriddhi Yatra' on March 23, 2026, visiting Jehanabad, where he inaugurated 88 development schemes worth Rs 70 crore and laid foundation stones for 73 projects worth Rs 182 crore. At a Jan Samvad public dialogue, he reaffirmed the resolve of a 'Developed Bihar' and interacted with beneficiaries of rural-development programmes.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti takes charge as NCBC Chairperson
capsules.body: Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti assumed charge as Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes. The NCBC is a constitutional body under Article 338B, inserted by the 102nd Amendment in 2018, which advises on OBC welfare and examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the Central OBC list.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Balendra Shah sworn in as Nepal's youngest Prime Minister
capsules.body: Balendra Shah (35), leader of the Rastriya Swatantra Party and a former rapper, was sworn in as the youngest Prime Minister of Nepal after a landslide electoral victory, marking a generational shift in Himalayan politics that is being closely watched in New Delhi.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-EU working arrangement on industrial aviation production
capsules.body: India signed a working arrangement with the European Union in the field of industrial aviation production to strengthen bilateral cooperation, deepening the strategic embrace that followed the January 2026 conclusion of the India-EU free trade agreement and defence-security partnership.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish unveils 1,373 projects worth Rs 1,056 crore for Patna
capsules.body: During the Samriddhi Yatra, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 1,373 development projects worth Rs 1,056 crore in Patna district: 761 projects (Rs 473 crore) inaugurated and 612 (Rs 583 crore) foundation-laid. He distributed Rs 519.26 crore in bank loans to 2,06,989 Jeevika self-help-group women and reviewed the 10.5 km AIIMS-Janipur stretch of the Bihta-Sarmera-Patna Ring Road project.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: T.N. Natarajan takes charge as SAIL Director (Commercial)
capsules.body: Shri T.N. Natarajan assumed charge as Director (Commercial) of Steel Authority of India Limited, the Maharatna steel PSU, a key leadership post for steel marketing and sales strategy.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Krishna Kumar Thakur takes charge as NMDC Director (Personnel)
capsules.body: Krishna Kumar Thakur, a 1998-batch officer of the Indian Railway Personnel Service, assumed charge as Director (Personnel) of NMDC Limited, India's largest iron-ore producer, overseeing human resources for the Navratna miner.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BSEB Class 10 result 2026: 81.79% pass; both board results out in March
capsules.body: The Bihar School Examination Board declared the Class 10 (Matric) result on March 29, 2026: 81.79% pass, with 15,10,928 students appearing (7,84,871 girls, 7,26,057 boys) and 12,35,743 passing. Class 12 results were also declared within March, making Bihar the only state to declare both board results in March. Class 10 evaluation finished in just 12 days using barcoded OMR sheets, lithocodes, CCTV surveillance and two-level frisking. The result was announced by Education Minister Sunil Kumar with BSEB Chairman Anand Kishor.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NHAI raises FASTag Annual Pass fee to Rs 3,075 from April 1
capsules.body: The National Highways Authority of India raised the FASTag Annual Pass fee to Rs 3,075 effective April 1, 2026, a change relevant for frequent highway users and toll-revenue estimates.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NASA's Artemis II launches: first crewed lunar mission since 1972
capsules.body: NASA's Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026, the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years. The roughly 10-day, 1.12-million-km Orion flight carries four astronauts on a lunar flyby without landing, testing life-support and navigation systems for the Artemis III landing mission.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Record Rs 2.42 lakh crore GST collection in April 2026
capsules.body: Goods and Services Tax collections hit a record Rs 2.42 lakh crore in April 2026, signalling strong consumption and compliance momentum at the start of FY 2026-27.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Aridaman commissioned: India's third nuclear ballistic submarine
capsules.body: On April 3, 2026, the Indian Navy commissioned INS Aridaman, India's third SSBN (nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine), after extensive trials; it was handed over at a naval base in Kerala. SSBNs provide the sea leg of India's nuclear triad, underpinning the no-first-use doctrine with an assured second-strike capability.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO launches Mission MITRA in Leh for Gaganyaan astronaut training
capsules.body: On April 4, ISRO launched Mission MITRA (Mission for Integrated Technology Research and Application) in Leh at altitudes of 3,500 to 5,000 metres, running till April 9. A Mars- and Moon-like environment with hypoxia, low temperature and isolation trains astronauts' physical and mental health for Gaganyaan, with a Human Spaceflight Support System set up on the ground.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: MoD signs Rs 810.79 crore BDL contract for 160 SAT-SAAW glide bombs
capsules.body: The Ministry of Defence signed a Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited for 160 SAT-SAAW precision glide bombs for the Indian Air Force. The indigenous stand-off weapon boosts air-to-surface strike capability under Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan: ISRO conducts second Integrated Air Drop Test
capsules.body: ISRO successfully conducted the second Integrated Air Drop Test (IADT-02) of the Gaganyaan-1 crew module at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, on April 10, 2026, validating parachute-based deceleration, a critical crew-safety milestone for India's human spaceflight programme.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Bicentenary celebrations of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule begin
capsules.body: India began commemorating the 200th birth anniversary of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule (born April 11, 1827): founder of India's first girls' school in 1848 at Pune with Savitribai Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873, and a pioneering crusader against caste discrimination and gender inequality.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Skills Outcomes Fund launched by Skill Development Ministry
capsules.body: Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Jayant Chaudhary launched the Skills Outcomes Fund in New Delhi, an outcomes-based financing initiative that links skilling payouts to actual employment results, aligning training with industry demand.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BSEB releases Class 10 and 12 compartment and special exam schedule
capsules.body: The Bihar School Examination Board released the schedule for the Class 10 and 12 special and compartment examinations: theory papers from May 2 to May 11, 2026, in two shifts daily (9:30 am to 12:45 pm and 2 pm to 5:15 pm). The exams give students who failed or seek improvement another chance to clear the academic year.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish Kumar resigns as Bihar CM after 20-year tenure
capsules.body: On April 14, 2026, Nitish Kumar resigned as Chief Minister of Bihar, ending a 20-year tenure as the state's longest-serving CM. His 'Sushasan' era closed with the NDA's sweeping 2025 assembly mandate of 202 of 243 seats and the record Rs 3.47 lakh crore budget for 2026-27. He resigned after being elected to the Rajya Sabha.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nitish Kumar elected to the Rajya Sabha
capsules.body: Former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April 2026, necessitating his resignation from the chief ministership on April 14 and the dissolution of his cabinet. His move to Parliament paved the way for BJP leader Samrat Choudhary to become Bihar's first BJP chief minister.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Karnataka wins Khelo India Tribal Games 2026
capsules.body: Karnataka emerged as champions of the Khelo India Tribal Games 2026, the national platform showcasing tribal athletes across indigenous and mainstream sporting disciplines.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar portfolio allocation: Samrat keeps 29 departments including Home
capsules.body: In the initial portfolio allocation after the April 15 swearing-in, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary retained 29 departments, including Home, General Administration, Cabinet Secretariat and Vigilance, with unallocated departments also under him. Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Chaudhary received 10 departments including Water Resources, Parliamentary Affairs, Education and Rural Development. The BJP, with 89 of 243 MLAs, leads the state's first BJP-led government.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung's state visit to India
capsules.body: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung paid a state visit to India from April 19 to 21, 2026, advancing the Special Strategic Partnership in semiconductors, defence, shipbuilding and resilient supply chains.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Seismological observatory in Kishtwar, Doppler radar in Doda announced
capsules.body: Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh announced a seismological observatory at Kishtwar and a Doppler Weather Radar at Doda in Jammu and Kashmir, strengthening earthquake monitoring in the seismically active Chenab valley and improving weather forecasting for the region.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: India-Egypt special forces exercise Cyclone-IV held
capsules.body: The fourth edition of Exercise Cyclone, the India-Egypt special forces drill, was held in April 2026, deepening counter-terrorism and desert-warfare cooperation between the two armies.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Samrat's first cabinet: 11 greenfield townships; land deals frozen in 11 cities
capsules.body: In its first meeting on April 22, the Samrat Choudhary cabinet approved 22 proposals, headlined by 11 greenfield townships with designated special and core areas. Land sale, purchase, transfer and construction were frozen in Patna, Sonepur, Gayaji, Darbhanga, Saharsa, Purnea and Munger till March 31, 2027, and in Muzaffarpur, Chhapra, Bhagalpur and Sitamarhi till June 30, 2027, under the Bihar Urban Planning and Development Act, 2012, to notify masterplans.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Samrat's first cabinet: Police Didi scooters, IIT Patna grant, NFSU campus
capsules.body: The April 22 cabinet approved 1,500 scooters (Rs 18.75 crore) for women police personnel under the 'Police Didi' initiative plus over 4,000 two-wheelers overall; a Rs 305 crore grant to IIT Patna; Rs 172.80 crore for the Emergency Response Support System building and state police data centre at Rajiv Nagar, Patna; about 50 acres at Punpun for a National Forensic Sciences University off-campus centre and Central Forensic Science Laboratory (Rs 287.16 crore); and a Rs 3,615 crore skill-upgrade plan.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: National Panchayati Raj Day observed on April 24
capsules.body: National Panchayati Raj Day was observed on April 24, 2026, commemorating the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992), which came into force on April 24, 1993, and gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions as the third tier of governance.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Laureus World Sports Awards 2026: Alcaraz and Sabalenka honoured
capsules.body: Carlos Alcaraz was named Laureus World Sportsman of the Year and Aryna Sabalenka Sportswoman of the Year for 2026, following Alcaraz's career Grand Slam completed at the Australian Open in February.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement signed
capsules.body: India signed a Free Trade Agreement with New Zealand on April 27, 2026, expanding market access for goods and services and deepening Indo-Pacific economic ties, weeks after the conclusion of the India-EU free trade agreement.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25%, projects 6.9% GDP growth for FY27
capsules.body: In its April 2026 monetary policy, the Reserve Bank of India kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% with a neutral stance, projecting FY 2026-27 GDP growth of 6.9% and inflation of 4.6%.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 negatived in Lok Sabha
capsules.body: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was negatived, or defeated, in the Lok Sabha in April 2026. Constitutional amendments require a special majority under Article 368, and government defeats on such bills are rare, making the outcome constitutionally significant.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Census 2027 mascots Pragati and Vikas unveiled
capsules.body: The mascots for Census 2027, India's first digital census, were unveiled as 'Pragati' and 'Vikas' in April 2026, aimed at popularising the exercise and boosting engagement between enumerators and citizens.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Meghalaya adopts Khasi and Garo as official languages
capsules.body: Meghalaya adopted Khasi and Garo as the state's official languages, formally recognising its two dominant tribal languages and strengthening linguistic federalism in the Northeast.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Five new districts created in Ladakh; total now seven
capsules.body: The Centre created five new districts in the Union Territory of Ladakh, taking the total to seven, improving administrative reach across the vast and strategically sensitive Himalayan region.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: WPI inflation hits multi-month high of 8.3% in April 2026
capsules.body: Wholesale Price Index inflation rose to 8.3% in April 2026, a multi-month high, even as consumer inflation stayed near target, a divergence policymakers watch for pass-through risks to retail prices.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: IIP base year revised to 2022-23
capsules.body: The government revised the base year of the Index of Industrial Production to 2022-23, updating the item basket and weights to reflect the current industrial structure for more accurate measurement of industrial growth.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PMGSY-III extended till March 2028 with Rs 83,977 crore outlay
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet extended the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana-III till March 2028 with an outlay of Rs 83,977 crore, continuing rural road connectivity with a focus on unconnected habitations, farm-to-market links and bridge works.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: OCI cards extended to sixth-generation Sri Lankan Tamils
capsules.body: The government extended Overseas Citizen of India card eligibility to sixth-generation Sri Lankan Tamils, deepening diaspora outreach to the community affected by the island's civil conflict.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India submits updated NDCs for 2031-35 under Paris Agreement
capsules.body: India submitted its updated Nationally Determined Contributions for 2031-35 under the Paris Agreement, charting the next decade of targets on emission-intensity reduction, non-fossil power capacity and carbon sinks.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India targets 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047
capsules.body: India set a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, anchoring long-term clean baseload electricity for the Viksit Bharat vision alongside the small modular reactor programme.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Ashok Lahiri appointed NITI Aayog Vice Chairperson
capsules.body: Economist Ashok Lahiri was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog, the government's premier policy think tank chaired by the Prime Minister, to steer the Viksit Bharat strategy.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: April GST mop-up hits record Rs 2.43 lakh crore
capsules.body: Gross GST collections touched a record Rs 2.43 lakh crore in April 2026, up 8.7% year-on-year, data released on 1 May showed. Import-linked GST surged 25.8% to Rs 57,580 crore while domestic revenue grew 4.3% to Rs 1.85 lakh crore. After refunds of Rs 31,793 crore, net collections stood at Rs 2.11 lakh crore. The previous record was Rs 2.23 lakh crore in April 2025.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Marta Kostyuk wins Madrid Open women's title
capsules.body: Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk defeated Russia's Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-3 in the Madrid Open final on 2 May 2026 to win her first WTA 1000 title. It was her third career WTA title and her second in two weeks after Rouen. The world No. 23 beat fifth seed Jessica Pegula and 13th seed Linda Noskova en route, and celebrated with her signature backflip.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Press Freedom Day observed
capsules.body: World Press Freedom Day was observed on 3 May 2026. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 1993 on UNESCO's recommendation, the day defends media independence and honours journalists who lost their lives in the line of duty. The 2026 observance highlighted the safety of journalists covering conflict zones and elections worldwide.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Census 2027 houselisting phase underway
capsules.body: The houselisting and housing census phase of Census 2027, India's first fully digital census, continued through May 2026 after beginning in April. Enumerators are collecting housing and household data on digital devices, with a self-enumeration option for citizens. The population enumeration, which will include caste data, is scheduled for February 2027.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: UPI clocks 22.35 billion transactions in April
capsules.body: UPI processed 22.35 billion transactions worth Rs 29.03 lakh crore in April 2026, up 25% in volume year-on-year, NPCI data released in early May showed. The daily average touched 745 million transactions. The platform is now live in eight countries including the UAE, Singapore, France and Mauritius, aiding cross-border payments.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar AI Mission approved
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved the Bihar AI Mission on 6 May 2026, clearing artificial-intelligence training programmes for legislators and government officials. Partner institutions include the National University of Singapore, C-DAC Patna, IIT Patna, NIELIT Patna and CIMP, positioning Bihar among the early Indian states with a dedicated AI mission.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar cabinet expansion ahead of assembly polls
capsules.body: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary expanded the Bihar cabinet on 7 May 2026, inducting a fresh set of ministers months ahead of the assembly elections due later this year. The expansion balanced caste and regional representation across the NDA alliance partners governing the state.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: First anniversary of Operation Sindoor
capsules.body: 7 May 2026 marked the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor, the tri-services military operation India launched in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack of 22 April 2025. DRDO timed its 8 May Agni missile test with MIRV capability to coincide with the anniversary, underlining India's deterrence posture.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: DRDO tests Advanced Agni missile with MIRV
capsules.body: DRDO successfully flight-tested an Advanced Agni missile with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) capability from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha, on 8 May 2026. Multiple payloads struck spatially distributed targets across the Indian Ocean Region. The Defence Ministry confirmed all mission objectives were met; Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh congratulated DRDO, the Army and industry.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day
capsules.body: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day was observed on 8 May 2026, the birth anniversary of Henry Dunant, founder of the International Committee of the Red Cross. The day recognises the volunteers and staff of the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement across 192 national societies.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Migratory Bird Day
capsules.body: World Migratory Bird Day was observed on 9 May 2026, the second Saturday of May. The UN-backed campaign raises awareness about protecting migratory birds and their habitats along global flyways, including the Central Asian Flyway that passes over India.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: National Technology Day
capsules.body: National Technology Day was observed on 11 May 2026, commemorating the 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests. On the same day in 1998, India also test-fired the Trishul missile and flew the indigenous Hansa-3 aircraft. The day celebrates India's scientists, engineers and technological self-reliance.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: International Nurses Day
capsules.body: International Nurses Day was observed on 12 May 2026, the birth anniversary of Florence Nightingale. Coordinated by the International Council of Nurses since 1974, the day honours the contribution of nurses to public health systems, patient care and universal health coverage.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar raises dearness allowance to 60%
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet raised dearness allowance for state government employees and pensioners from 58% to 60% under the Seventh Pay Commission, effective 1 January 2026. The hike, cleared in mid-May, benefits around nine lakh employees and pensioners and adds to the state's salary expenditure.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan G1 mission clears key review
capsules.body: ISRO's Gaganyaan G1 mission received key review clearance in May 2026, moving India's first human spaceflight programme closer to flight. G1 is the first of three planned uncrewed missions that will validate human-rated launch systems, the crew escape system and the crew module before Indian astronauts fly.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Sikkim's 51st Statehood Day
capsules.body: Sikkim observed its 51st Statehood Day on 16 May 2026. The former Himalayan kingdom became India's 22nd state on 16 May 1975 following a referendum. The day is marked by official ceremonies in Gangtok celebrating the state's merger with the Indian Union.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: International Day of Light
capsules.body: The International Day of Light was observed on 16 May 2026. Led by UNESCO, the day marks the anniversary of the first successful laser operation in 1960 and promotes the role of light science and technology in sustainable development, from solar energy to optical communications.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: 79th World Health Assembly begins in Geneva
capsules.body: The 79th World Health Assembly was held in Geneva from 18 to 23 May 2026 under the theme 'Reshaping global health: a shared responsibility'. Delegations from WHO member states debated health financing, the WHO Pandemic Agreement's pathogen-access annex, antimicrobial resistance and reform of the global health architecture.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: International Museum Day
capsules.body: International Museum Day was observed on 18 May 2026. Coordinated by the International Council of Museums since 1977, the day highlights the role of museums in cultural exchange and education; museums across India, including Patna Museum, organised special exhibitions and outreach programmes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 100 acres free for NIFTEM in Vaishali
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved free transfer of 100 acres of land in Vaishali district for the National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM). The institute will boost food-processing education, research and industry linkage in a state where agriculture employs most of the workforce.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rural SP posts for five districts
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved creation of rural Superintendent of Police posts for East Champaran, Samastipur, Madhubani, Vaishali and Siwan districts. The move strengthens rural policing by separating law-and-order duties from urban police jurisdictions in five populous districts.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Bee Day
capsules.body: World Bee Day was observed on 20 May 2026. Proclaimed by the UN on the initiative of Slovenia, the day recognises the role of bees and other pollinators in food security and biodiversity. India is among the world's largest honey producers, with Bihar a significant contributor.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Anti-Terrorism Day
capsules.body: Anti-Terrorism Day was observed in India on 21 May 2026, the death anniversary of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, assassinated in 1991. Observed since 1992, the day promotes national unity against terrorism; government offices and educational institutions take an anti-violence pledge.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: International Day for Biological Diversity
capsules.body: The International Day for Biological Diversity was observed on 22 May 2026. The UN-designated day marks the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity in 1992. India, one of 17 mega-diverse countries, hosts four of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI approves record Rs 2.87 lakh crore dividend
capsules.body: The RBI's Central Board on 22 May 2026 approved a record surplus transfer of Rs 2,86,588 crore to the Central Government for 2025-26, the highest ever. The 623rd board meeting, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra in Mumbai, also raised the Contingent Risk Buffer to 6.5% of the balance-sheet size.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: UPSC Civil Services Prelims 2026 held
capsules.body: The UPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2026 was held on 24 May 2026 across India for 933 vacancies. New norms made face authentication mandatory at examination centres and barred serving IAS and IFS officers from reappearing. The mains examination is scheduled from 21 August 2026.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Football Day
capsules.body: World Football Day was observed on 25 May 2026. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2024 to mark the centenary of the first international football tournament at the 1924 Paris Olympics, the day celebrates football's role in peace, development and social inclusion.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar's revised EV policy targets 30% by 2030
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved a revised Electric Vehicle policy targeting 30% of new vehicle sales to be electric by 2030. The policy offers purchase incentives, charging-infrastructure support and manufacturing incentives as Bihar pushes cleaner urban transport and lower vehicular emissions.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Cashless treatment under Bihar Government Health Scheme
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved cashless inpatient treatment under the Bihar Government Health Scheme for state employees and pensioners. Beneficiaries can access cashless hospitalisation at empanelled hospitals, reducing out-of-pocket expenditure for the state's workforce.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: International Day of UN Peacekeepers
capsules.body: The International Day of UN Peacekeepers was observed on 29 May 2026. India is the largest cumulative troop contributor to UN peacekeeping, having deployed personnel across dozens of missions since 1948, with over 170 Indian peacekeepers having made the supreme sacrifice.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Q4 FY26 GDP grows 6.9%; full year at 7.4%
capsules.body: India's GDP grew 6.9% in the January-March quarter of FY26, government data released on 29 May 2026 showed, taking full-year FY26 growth to 7.4%. The print beat street estimates, driven by manufacturing, construction and services, even as the RBI flagged global headwinds for FY27.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Goa's 39th Statehood Day
capsules.body: Goa observed its 39th Statehood Day on 30 May 2026. Goa became India's 25th state on 30 May 1987, with Daman and Diu remaining a separate Union Territory. Konkani in the Devanagari script is the state's official language.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Hindi Journalism Day
capsules.body: Hindi Journalism Day was observed on 30 May 2026, marking the 1826 launch of Udant Martand, the first Hindi newspaper, from Calcutta. The day honours Hindi journalism's role in the freedom movement and in democratic discourse.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World No Tobacco Day
capsules.body: World No Tobacco Day was observed on 31 May 2026. The WHO campaign highlights the health risks of tobacco, which kills over 8 million people globally each year. India is the world's second-largest tobacco consumer, with COTPA, 2003 regulating its sale and advertising.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: UPI hits record 23.2 billion transactions in May
capsules.body: UPI hit a record 23.2 billion transactions worth Rs 29.90 lakh crore in May 2026, NPCI data released on 1 June showed, driven by summer travel and IPL-season spending.
