Volume grew 24% year-on-year. The May print surpassed April's 22.35 billion transactions, extending UPI's run of monthly records.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Telangana Formation Day
capsules.body: Telangana observed its Formation Day on 2 June 2026, marking the state's creation in 2014 as India's 29th state after bifurcation from Andhra Pradesh. Hyderabad, the shared capital for ten years after bifurcation, is now Telangana's exclusive capital.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: CM Medical Assistance Fund ceiling raised to Rs 4 lakh
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet raised the ceiling under the Chief Minister's Medical Assistance Fund from Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 4 lakh, expanding financial help for poor patients needing costly treatment at government and empanelled hospitals.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Bicycle Day
capsules.body: World Bicycle Day was observed on 3 June 2026. Declared by the UN in 2018, the day promotes cycling as a sustainable, healthy and affordable mode of transport and encourages member states to build cycling infrastructure.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Southwest monsoon sets in over Kerala
capsules.body: The southwest monsoon set in over Kerala on 4 June 2026, three days after its normal date of 1 June, the IMD announced. The department forecast below-normal seasonal rainfall at about 92% of the Long Period Average, citing an emerging El Nino and the ongoing West Asia conflict's effect on global weather patterns.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Environment Day: Climate Action
capsules.body: World Environment Day was observed on 5 June 2026 under the theme 'Climate Action' with the global campaign #NowForClimate, hosted by Azerbaijan. The day, led by UNEP since 1974, is the United Nations' principal platform for environmental outreach and awareness.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds repo at 5.25%; cuts FY27 GDP to 6.6%
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee on 5 June 2026 unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance, the third straight hold. Governor Sanjay Malhotra cut the FY27 GDP forecast to 6.6% from 6.9% and raised CPI inflation projection to 5.1%, citing the West Asia conflict and elevated crude prices.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: French Open 2026: Zverev and Andreeva win singles titles
capsules.body: Germany's Alexander Zverev won the French Open men's singles title and Russia's Mirra Andreeva won the women's crown at Roland Garros on 7 June 2026. Andreeva's triumph came five weeks after her Madrid Open final defeat, confirming her rise at the top of women's tennis.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Food Safety Day
capsules.body: World Food Safety Day was observed on 7 June 2026. Jointly led by WHO and FAO since 2019, the day draws attention to foodborne risks and the farm-to-table safety chain; FSSAI marked the day in India with its annual awareness campaign.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 31.30 crore Integrated Aqua Park in Bhojpur
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved a Rs 31.30 crore Integrated Aqua Park at the Banasur Fish Seed Farm in Bhojpur district, boosting quality fish seed production and aquaculture under the state's fisheries development push.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Oceans Day
capsules.body: World Oceans Day was observed on 8 June 2026. The UN-designated day highlights the ocean's role in climate regulation, food security and livelihoods, and supports India's blue-economy push along its long coastline and island territories.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 83.25 crore grain processing project in Madhubani
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet cleared a Rs 83.25 crore grain-based processing project in Madhubani, expected to generate 109 jobs and strengthen agro-processing and value addition in the Mithila region.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 164.51 crore for PMFME implementation
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved Rs 164.51 crore for implementing the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme in 2026-27, supporting micro food-processing units with credit-linked subsidy and capacity building.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Day Against Child Labour
capsules.body: The World Day Against Child Labour was observed on 12 June 2026. Led by the ILO since 2002, the day targets the elimination of child labour; India prohibits employment of children below 14 years under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World Blood Donor Day
capsules.body: World Blood Donor Day was observed on 14 June 2026, the birth anniversary of Karl Landsteiner, who discovered the ABO blood group system. Coordinated by WHO since 2004, the day thanks voluntary donors and promotes safe, sufficient blood supplies.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 483.51 crore beverage and solar project in Buxar
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved a Rs 483.51 crore beverage and solar project at Nawanagar in Buxar district, projected to create about 400 jobs and add renewable-energy capacity in the state.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought
capsules.body: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought was observed on 17 June 2026. Led by the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, the day focuses on land restoration; India has committed to restoring 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Five new private universities approved
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved the establishment of five new private universities, expanding higher-education capacity and choice for students under the Bihar Private Universities Act framework.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: 12th International Day of Yoga
capsules.body: The 12th International Day of Yoga was observed on 21 June 2026 under the theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'. Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the national celebration in Kolkata. Proposed by India, the UN proclaimed 21 June as Yoga Day in 2014.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Housing Board to buy land for satellite townships
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet authorised the Bihar State Housing Board to purchase land under the Bihar Raiyati Land Purchase Policy, 2026 for developing satellite townships, easing urban housing pressure around Patna and other fast-growing cities.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Sahitya Akademi Bal and Yuva Puraskar 2026
capsules.body: The Sahitya Akademi announced its Bal Sahitya Puraskar and Yuva Puraskar for 2026 on 23 June. Yuva Puraskar winners included Dheeraj Bismil for the Dogri drama collection 'Aalra' and Nighat Nasreen for the Kashmiri work 'Lalle Nilwath Tchali Na Zahn'; Balwan Singh Jamoria received the Bal Sahitya Puraskar for Dogri.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Olympic Day
capsules.body: Olympic Day was observed on 23 June 2026, marking the founding of the International Olympic Committee in 1894. The day promotes sport and the Olympic values of excellence, respect and friendship; India is preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI orders Special Intensive Revision of Bihar rolls
capsules.body: The Election Commission on 24 June 2026 ordered a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Bihar, the first such exercise since 2003. Around eight crore electors must submit enumeration forms, and those enrolled after 2003 need citizenship documents. The final roll is due on 30 September, ahead of the assembly polls.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar State Teacher Transfer Rules, 2026
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 24 June 2026 approved the Bihar State Teacher Transfer Rules, 2026, covering over 5.5 lakh teachers. Transfers will be processed through a transparent portal-based system with priority provisions for mutual transfers and medical grounds.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: 11th BRICS Energy Ministers' Meeting in Gurugram
capsules.body: The 11th BRICS Energy Ministers' Meeting was held in Gurugram on 25 June 2026 under India's BRICS chairship, themed 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. Ministers adopted a joint communique and launched the BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Samvidhan Hatya Diwas
capsules.body: Samvidhan Hatya Diwas was observed on 25 June 2026, marking the 51st anniversary of the Emergency imposed in 1975. Observed since 2024, the day recalls the suspension of constitutional rights during the 21-month Emergency proclaimed on 25 June 1975.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Scientific study of sand deposits in five rivers
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved a scientific study of sand deposits in five major rivers of the state, aiming to regulate sand mining, curb illegal extraction and protect river ecology through evidence-based mineral planning.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: World MSME Day
capsules.body: World MSME Day was observed on 27 June 2026. Designated by the UN in 2017, the day recognises micro, small and medium enterprises; India's Udyam-registered MSMEs number in crores and the sector contributes about 30% of GDP and significant employment.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 20,000 aid for Sindhu Darshan pilgrims
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved financial assistance of up to Rs 20,000 for pilgrims undertaking the Sindhu Darshan Yatra in Ladakh, supporting religious tourism from the state.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: National Statistics Day
capsules.body: National Statistics Day was observed on 29 June 2026, the birth anniversary of P.C. Mahalanobis, the father of Indian statistics. Observed since 2007, the day honours contributions to the national statistical system; Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical Institute.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: International Asteroid Day
capsules.body: International Asteroid Day was observed on 30 June 2026, marking the 1908 Tunguska event in Siberia. The UN-designated day raises awareness about asteroid impact hazards; ISRO tracks near-Earth objects through its space situational awareness programme, NETRA.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: National Doctors' Day
capsules.body: National Doctors' Day was observed on 1 July 2026, the birth anniversary of Dr Bidhan Chandra Roy, physician and former West Bengal chief minister. Observed in India since 1991, the day honours the service of doctors to society and the healthcare system.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Exercise Khaan Quest 2026 concludes in Mongolia
capsules.body: Exercise Khaan Quest 2026, the 23rd edition of the multinational peacekeeping exercise, concluded in Mongolia on 3 July 2026. Over 1,000 personnel from 18 countries trained in UN peace-support operations, tactical drills and humanitarian assistance; India participated with a contingent.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: India-France Exercise Shakti-VIII ends
capsules.body: The eighth edition of the India-France joint military exercise Shakti concluded on 3 July 2026. The 90-member Indian contingent trained alongside French troops in a 96-hour field exercise focused on joint tactical operations, interoperability and counter-terror drills.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rs 1,424 crore pension DBT to 97.84 lakh beneficiaries
capsules.body: The Bihar government transferred Rs 1,423.94 crore through DBT to about 97.84 lakh social-security pension beneficiaries in July 2026, at Rs 1,100 per beneficiary per month. The state announced that pensions will henceforth be credited by the 10th of every month.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Free JEE-NEET coaching in Patna model schools
capsules.body: Bihar launched free 'School Live Classes' for JEE and NEET coaching in 10 Patna model schools on 16 July 2026, enrolling 518 students in the first phase. The programme will extend to 155 model schools, offering free competitive-exam coaching to government school students.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 72nd National Film Awards announced
capsules.body: The 72nd National Film Awards were announced on 18 July 2026. 'Article 370' won Best Feature Film; Kartik Aaryan ('Chandu Champion') and Mammootty ('Bramayugam') shared Best Actor; Yami Gautam ('Article 370') won Best Actress; Rajkumar Periasamy ('Amaran') won Best Director; 'Kalki 2898 AD' won the wholesome-entertainment award; Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for 'Swatantrya Veer Savarkar'.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar legislature's Monsoon Session begins
capsules.body: The Bihar legislature's five-day Monsoon Session began on 20 July 2026 and ran till 24 July. The Assembly passed 20 bills, including legislation on urban development, gambling prohibition and ease of doing business, amid opposition protests over the NEET paper-leak issue.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Urban Development Bill, 2026 passed
capsules.body: The Bihar Assembly passed the Bihar Urban Development Bill, 2026 during the July monsoon session, overhauling the legal framework for municipal governance, town planning and urban infrastructure in the state's rapidly growing cities.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Gambling (Prohibition) Bill, 2026 passed
capsules.body: The Bihar Assembly passed the Bihar Gambling (Prohibition) Bill, 2026, banning gambling and betting, including online gaming for stakes, with penal provisions for organisers and participants.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Ease of Doing Business Bill, 2026 passed
capsules.body: The Bihar Assembly passed the Bihar Ease of Doing Business Bill, 2026, providing deemed approvals, single-window clearances and time-bound delivery of services to improve the state's investment climate.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Agricultural land conversion law repealed
capsules.body: The Bihar Assembly passed the Bihar Agricultural Land (Conversion for Non-Agricultural Purposes) (Repeal) Bill, 2026, scrapping the older conversion law and streamlining land-use change procedures for industry and housing projects.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Appropriation (No. 3) Bill authorises Rs 87,383 crore
capsules.body: The Bihar Assembly passed the Bihar Appropriation (No. 3) Bill, 2026, authorising withdrawal of over Rs 87,383 crore from the Consolidated Fund of the state to meet the year's expenditure.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: NEET-UG paper-leak protests rock Delhi and Patna
capsules.body: Student protests over alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks intensified in Delhi and Patna on 25 July 2026, with demonstrators demanding a CBI probe and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Police detained several protesters near Jantar Mantar as agitations spread to other cities.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns
capsules.body: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on 25 July 2026 amid nationwide student protests over alleged NEET-UG paper leaks and scrutiny of the examination's conduct. His exit marked one of the most significant ministerial casualties of the paper-leak controversy.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Kargil Vijay Diwas
capsules.body: Kargil Vijay Diwas was observed on 26 July 2026, marking the 27th anniversary of India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War. Tributes were paid at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras; the war ended on 26 July 1999 after Operation Vijay evicted Pakistani intruders from the heights of Kargil.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Tribunals Reforms Bill creates National Tribunals Commission
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill during the 2026 Monsoon Session, creating a National Tribunals Commission to oversee appointments, administration and uniform service conditions across central tribunals, addressing long-standing concerns about tribunal independence and vacancies.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: MSME Development (Amendment) Bill passed
capsules.body: Parliament passed the MSME Development (Amendment) Bill in the Monsoon Session, revising the definition and registration framework for micro, small and medium enterprises to reflect inflation and economic growth since the original 2006 Act.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Global Tiger Day
capsules.body: Global Tiger Day was observed on 29 July 2026. India hosts around 75% of the world's wild tigers, with the 2022 all-India estimate at 3,682. The day raises awareness for tiger conservation across the 13 tiger-range countries and reviews progress under the TX2 goal.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NCDC (Amendment) Bill passed
capsules.body: Parliament passed the National Cooperative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill in the Monsoon Session, expanding NCDC's lending and support mandate for cooperatives in dairy, fisheries, storage and new-generation farmer producer organisations.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: MMDR Amendment Bill passed
capsules.body: Parliament passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill in the Monsoon Session, further opening the mining sector by easing auction rules and expanding the list of critical minerals to encourage private exploration.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Student Credit Card scheme extended to 2030-31
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet extended the Bihar Student Credit Card scheme up to 2030-31, allocating Rs 950 crore for 2026-27. The scheme, which has benefited about 4.15 lakh students so far, offers education loans at low interest for higher studies.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI raises FY27 GDP forecast to 6.7%
capsules.body: The RBI's August monetary policy review kept the repo rate at 5.25% but raised the FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7% from 6.6%, citing resilient domestic demand. The stance remained neutral as upside risks to inflation from elevated crude prices persisted.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: National Handloom Day
capsules.body: National Handloom Day was observed on 7 August 2026, honouring the country's handloom weavers. The day marks the launch of the Swadeshi Movement on 7 August 1905; Bihar's Bhagalpuri silk and Bawanbuti weaves were showcased in state programmes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 50% private ITI seats through BCECEB
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet decided that 50% of seats in private Industrial Training Institutes will be filled through the Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB), bringing merit-based, transparent admissions to private ITIs.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sports science centre at Rajgir academy
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved a Sports Science, High Performance Training and Injury Centre at the State Sports Academy in Rajgir, providing scientific training, physiotherapy and injury management for the state's athletes.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: National Sports Governance Bill passed
capsules.body: Parliament passed the National Sports Governance Bill on 12 August 2026 - the Lok Sabha on 11 August and the Rajya Sabha on 12 August - creating India's first comprehensive sports law. It sets up a National Sports Board, a National Sports Tribunal and an election panel, with 12-year tenure caps and 30% women's representation in federations.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Free land for CBG plants in four cities
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved free allotment of 10 acres for 25 years for compressed biogas (CBG) plants at Gayaji, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur and Biharsharif, promoting biofuel production from agricultural waste under the SATAT initiative.

capsules.subject: Miscellaneous
capsules.title: Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
capsules.body: Partition Horrors Remembrance Day was observed on 14 August 2026, recalling the suffering of millions displaced during the 1947 Partition. Observed since 2021, the day honours the victims and survivors of one of history's largest migrations.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: BWF World Championships begin in New Delhi
capsules.body: The 30th BWF World Badminton Championships began in New Delhi on 17 August 2026, India's first hosting since Hyderabad 2009. PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen and the Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty pair led the home challenge at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 19 special courts for SC/ST atrocity cases
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved 19 exclusive special courts for cases under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act along with 171 supporting non-gazetted posts, speeding up justice delivery for atrocity victims.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: State support for PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved state support under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - Rs 10,000 per kW, capped at Rs 20,000 per consumer - with an estimated state expenditure of Rs 1,000 crore to accelerate rooftop solar adoption.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 16 medical colleges on PPP mode
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved operation of 16 government medical and dental colleges and hospitals on public-private partnership mode, appointing PwC as transaction adviser for Rs 8.27 crore to structure the concessions.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 300 B.Ed. colleges to become multidisciplinary
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved conversion of 300 stand-alone B.Ed. institutions into multidisciplinary degree colleges under NEP 2020, integrating teacher education with undergraduate programmes.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Kushal Yuva Programme extended to 2030-31
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet extended the Kushal Yuva Programme up to 2030-31, allocating Rs 430.08 crore for 2026-27. The skill-development scheme offers free soft-skills and computer training to youth aged 15-28.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nalanda Mahavihara: the ancient residential university
capsules.body: Nalanda, in present-day Nalanda district, was the world's first residential university, flourishing from the 5th to the 12th century CE under Gupta and Pala patronage. At its peak it hosted about 10,000 students and 2,000 teachers from across Asia, with the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang studying here in the 7th century. Excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India, the ruins were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Vikramashila: Pala-era seat of Tantric Buddhism
capsules.body: Vikramashila Mahavihara was founded in the 8th century by the Pala emperor Dharmapala near present-day Antichak in Bhagalpur district. It became a leading centre of Tantric Buddhist learning, headed by scholars like Atisha Dipankara, who later carried Buddhism to Tibet. Its excavated ruins reveal a massive cruciform stupa surrounded by 208 monastic cells.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Odantapuri: Bihar's forgotten third university
capsules.body: Odantapuri Mahavihara near Bihar Sharif was founded by the first Pala king, Gopala I, in the 8th century, completing Bihar's trio of great Buddhist universities with Nalanda and Vikramashila. It housed about a thousand monks and was a major centre of Mahayana scholarship. It was destroyed during Bakhtiyar Khilji's campaigns around 1200 CE.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Vaishali and the Lichchhavi republic
capsules.body: Vaishali, in present-day Vaishali district, was the capital of the Vajjian confederacy led by the Lichchhavis, often described as one of the world's earliest republics. Its assembly of 7,707 rajas governed through collective decision-making, a system the Buddha is said to have admired. The site holds an Ashokan pillar with a single lion capital and the relic stupa of the Lichchhavis.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
capsules.body: Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India was launched in Champaran against the tinkathia system, which forced peasants to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their holdings for European planters. Local ryot Raj Kumar Shukla travelled to Lucknow in 1916 to persuade Gandhi to visit Bihar. The movement's success led to the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 and established Gandhi's method of mass satyagraha.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Kunwar Singh and 1857 in Bihar
capsules.body: Veer Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur, nearly eighty years old, led the 1857 uprising in Bihar and recaptured Arrah from the British in July 1857. He later carried the revolt to Lucknow and Azamgarh before dying of his wounds in April 1858. Bihar remembers him as its foremost hero of the First War of Independence.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: The Barabar caves: India's oldest rock-cut architecture
capsules.body: The Barabar and Nagarjuni hill caves in Jehanabad district were excavated under Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE for the Ajivika sect, making them the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India. The Lomas Rishi cave carries the earliest rock-cut imitation of a wooden chaitya arch, complete with carved elephants. Their highly polished interiors display the famed Mauryan mirror finish.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Kesaria stupa: among the world's tallest
capsules.body: The Kesaria stupa in East Champaran, excavated by the ASI, rises about 31.5 metres and is counted among the largest Buddhist stupas in the world. Tradition links it to the Buddha's alms-bowl episode at Vaishali. Its terraced circular design influenced stupa architecture across Asia.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya
capsules.body: The Mahabodhi Temple marks the spot where Prince Siddhartha attained enlightenment around 531 BCE, becoming the Buddha. The present brick temple, largely in its 5th-6th century Gupta form, was first established by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002 and remains Buddhism's holiest shrine.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sonepur's Harihar Kshetra Mela
capsules.body: Held at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak near Sonepur, the month-long Harihar Kshetra Mela is famed as Asia's largest cattle fair. It begins on Kartik Purnima and draws traders of elephants, horses and cattle from across India. The fair is tied to the legend of Gajendra Moksha and the Hariharnath temple.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Chhath Puja: Bihar's great sun festival
capsules.body: Chhath, dedicated to Surya and Chhathi Maiya, is Bihar's most emotionally resonant festival, observed over four days including Nahay-Khay, Kharna and the two arghyas at sunrise and sunset. Devotees fast and offer prayers standing in rivers and ponds. Its observance has spread with Bihari migration to metros across India and to Nepal, Mauritius and Fiji.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Madhubani painting of Mithila
capsules.body: Madhubani (Mithila) painting originated as wall and floor art by women of the Mithila region, depicting gods, nature and social life in distinctive geometric styles like bharni, kachni and tantric. Artists such as Sita Devi carried it from village walls to paper and global galleries in the 1970s. It remains Bihar's most recognisable cultural export.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bhikhari Thakur: the Shakespeare of Bhojpuri
capsules.body: Bhikhari Thakur (1887-1971), a barber-turned-playwright from Saran, is called the Shakespeare of Bhojpuri for his socially charged nautanki plays. His masterpiece Bidesiya portrays the pain of migrant labourers leaving their wives behind, a theme that still resonates in Bihar. His works also attacked caste discrimination and the dowry system.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sharda Sinha and the 2025 Padma Vibhushan
capsules.body: Sharda Sinha, Bihar's beloved folk singer known as the voice of Chhath, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in the 2025 Padma awards. Her songs like those for Chhath and weddings made Maithili and Bhojpuri folk music familiar across India. She had earlier received the Padma Shri (1991) and Padma Bhushan (2018).

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Karpoori Thakur's Bharat Ratna (2024)
capsules.body: Karpoori Thakur, twice Chief Minister of Bihar and champion of backward-class reservation, was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024. As CM in 1978 he implemented the Mungeri Lal Commission's recommendations, pioneering OBC reservation in state jobs. He is remembered for his austere lifestyle and the slogan of social justice he embodied.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: JP's Sampoorna Kranti call (1974)
capsules.body: On 5 June 1974, Jayaprakash Narayan addressed a massive rally at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, giving the call for Sampoorna Kranti - Total Revolution against corruption and misrule. The Bihar student movement he led became the spearhead of the nationwide agitation that preceded the Emergency of 1975-77. JP, born at Sitab Diara in Saran, remains Bihar's tallest post-independence political figure.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rajendra Prasad: Bihar's gift to the republic
capsules.body: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, born at Ziradei in Siwan on 3 December 1884, was India's first President (1950-1962). A Gandhian who led the Champaran inquiry's legal work and the 1934 earthquake relief, he presided over the Constituent Assembly that framed the Constitution. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1962.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar's 50% quota for women in panchayats
capsules.body: In 2006 Bihar became the first Indian state to reserve 50% of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions, going beyond the 33% mandated by the 73rd Amendment. The move dramatically increased women's representation at the grassroots, with lakhs of elected women representatives. Several states later followed Bihar's 50% model.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Saat Nischay: Nitish Kumar's governance framework
capsules.body: Saat Nischay (Seven Resolves) is the Bihar government's flagship development programme, covering piped water (Har Ghar Nal Ka Jal), drainage, roads, electricity, youth skills, student credit and women's empowerment. Its Part 2, launched after the 2020 assembly election, added goals like women's employment and IT-enabled governance. It structures much of the state's budgetary spending.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Student Credit Card scheme
capsules.body: The Bihar Student Credit Card Yojana provides education loans up to Rs 4 lakh to students who have passed Class 12 from Bihar, for higher and technical education. The state acts as guarantor, easing access to credit for poor families. It is one of the three youth-focused schemes under Saat Nischay alongside the self-help allowance and Kushal Yuva Karyakram.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Kosi: the Sorrow of Bihar
capsules.body: The Kosi, descending from Nepal, is called the Sorrow of Bihar for its history of westward course-shifts and catastrophic floods across Supaul, Saharsa, Madhepura and Purnia. The 2008 breach at Kusaha in Nepal displaced over 30 lakh people in Bihar. The Kosi Barrage at Bhimnagar (1963), built under the 1954 Indo-Nepal agreement, seeks to tame the river.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Kanwar Lake: Bihar's Ramsar jewel
capsules.body: Kanwar (Kabar) Lake in Begusarai, an oxbow lake formed by the Gandak's meandering, is Bihar's first Ramsar site (designated 2020). It is counted among Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lakes and hosts tens of thousands of migratory waterbirds each winter. Siltation and encroachment remain its main conservation challenges.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Valmiki Tiger Reserve
capsules.body: Valmiki National Park in West Champaran, contiguous with Nepal's Chitwan, is Bihar's only national park and the core of the Valmiki Tiger Reserve. Its forests of sal and grasslands shelter tigers, leopards, sloth bears and the greater one-horned rhinoceros. The reserve is Bihar's flagship wildlife destination.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Gangetic dolphin: Bihar's aquatic heritage
capsules.body: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary at Bhagalpur is India's only protected area dedicated to the Gangetic river dolphin, the national aquatic animal. In 2024 Patna got India's first National Dolphin Research Centre to study the endangered species. The dolphin, blind and navigating by echolocation, is an indicator of Ganga's health.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
capsules.body: The 5.75-km Mahatma Gandhi Setu across the Ganga between Patna and Hajipur was India's longest river bridge when commissioned in 1982. After decades of deterioration it was rebuilt with a steel superstructure, with the western flank reopened in 2020 and full rehabilitation completed later. It remains the lifeline linking north and south Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna Metro project
capsules.body: Patna Metro's Phase-1 covers two corridors - a north-south corridor and an east-west corridor - being built through a special purpose vehicle with central assistance. It is Bihar's first metro rail project, aimed at decongesting one of India's most crowded state capitals. The project has faced the usual challenges of land acquisition and shifting timelines. [verify]

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: New Nalanda University campus (2024)
capsules.body: The new campus of Nalanda University at Rajgir was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 19 June 2024, reviving the ancient seat of learning as a modern international university. Established by a 2010 Act of Parliament following the East Asia Summit initiative, it offers postgraduate and doctoral programmes with a pan-Asian faculty. Its net-zero campus blends ancient architectural motifs with modern sustainability.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar hosts Khelo India Youth Games 2025
capsules.body: Bihar hosted the 7th Khelo India Youth Games in May 2025, the first time the state staged India's flagship youth multi-sport event. Competitions were spread across Patna, Gaya, Bhagalpur and other cities, giving Bihar's sports infrastructure its biggest showcase. The event aligned with the state's push to build athletic talent beyond cricket.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Mithila Makhana: GI tag and Makhana Board
capsules.body: Mithila Makhana received the GI tag in 2022, recognising the fox-nut cultivated in the wetlands of north Bihar, which accounts for the bulk of India's makhana output. The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a dedicated Makhana Board in Bihar to boost production, processing and marketing. Makhana has emerged as a high-value superfood in domestic and export markets.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Shahi litchi of Muzaffarpur
capsules.body: The Shahi litchi of Muzaffarpur, prized for its sweetness and juicy pulp, received the GI tag in 2018. Bihar is India's largest litchi producer, with Muzaffarpur at the heart of the orchard belt. The fruit's short shelf life makes cold-chain logistics the key constraint on its trade.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna University: Bihar's first university
capsules.body: Patna University, established in 1917, was the first university of Bihar and the seventh oldest in the Indian subcontinent. Its colleges, including Patna College (1863) and Patna Science College, have produced generations of scholars and administrators. The university has long sought central university status.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC: the state civil services gatekeeper
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission was constituted on 1 April 1949 to recruit for the state's civil services under the Government of India Act, 1935. [verify] Its Combined Competitive Examination is the gateway to the SDM/DSP and allied services, with the 70th CCE cycle drawing lakhs of aspirants. The Commission is headquartered at Patna.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Budget 2025-26
capsules.body: Bihar's state budget for 2025-26 was about Rs 3.17 lakh crore, presented by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Samrat Choudhary. [verify] It emphasised infrastructure, the Saat Nischay schemes and employment generation ahead of the assembly election cycle. The budget's size reflects the state's dependence on central transfers for over two-thirds of revenue.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Rajgir Zoo Safari
capsules.body: The Rajgir Zoo Safari, opened in 2022 in Nalanda district, is Bihar's first zoo safari and among the largest in India. Animals roam in large naturalistic enclosures while visitors tour in protected vehicles. It complements the region's Buddhist circuit of Rajgir, Nalanda and Bodh Gaya.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib, Patna
capsules.body: Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib at Patna Sahib marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, born in Patna in 1666. It is one of the five takhts of Sikhism and a major pilgrimage centre. The 350th Prakash Parv celebrations in 2017 drew Sikh devotees from across the world to Patna.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sher Shah Suri and Sasaram
capsules.body: Sher Shah Suri, the Afghan ruler who briefly displaced the Mughals (1540-1545), built his magnificent mausoleum in the middle of a lake at Sasaram in Rohtas district. His short reign gave India the rupiya currency, the dak-chowki postal system and the Sadak-i-Azam highway. He died in 1545 during the siege of Kalinjar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Chirand: Bihar's Neolithic window
capsules.body: Chirand in Saran district, on the Ganga's bank, is Bihar's most important Neolithic-Chalcolithic site, inhabited from around 2500 BCE. Excavations revealed bone and antler tools, charred grains and evidence of early rice cultivation. It shows the middle Ganga plain was a cradle of early farming long before the cities.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Pataliputra: from Pataligrama to imperial capital
capsules.body: Pataliputra began as Pataligrama, a fortified post founded by Ajatashatru against the Lichchhavis; his son Udayin made it the Magadhan capital. Under the Mauryas it became one of the ancient world's great cities, described by Megasthenes as surrounded by a wooden palisade with 570 towers. Kumhrar's excavated pillared hall is its most famous surviving monument.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sachchidananda Sinha and the Constituent Assembly
capsules.body: Sachchidananda Sinha, the veteran Bihar leader, was the interim president of the Constituent Assembly when it first met on 9 December 1946, as the seniormost member. A founder of the Bihar Provincial Congress and Patna University's early leadership, he bridged the nationalist and constitutional phases of the freedom movement. He later became Bihar's Finance Minister.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar's 2000 bifurcation
capsules.body: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 under the Bihar Reorganisation Act, taking the mineral-rich Chota Nagpur and Santhal Pargana regions. Bihar was left with 38 districts and lost most of its industry and mineral revenue. The split reshaped the state's economy around agriculture, services and remittances.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: The 1934 Bihar-Nepal earthquake
capsules.body: On 15 January 1934, an earthquake of about magnitude 8.0 devastated north Bihar and Nepal, killing over 10,000 people in Bihar alone. Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga and Motihari were among the worst-hit towns, with widespread sand-venting and building collapse. The relief effort, led by Rajendra Prasad, became a landmark of organised disaster response.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Sama-Chakeva: Mithila's winter festival
capsules.body: Sama-Chakeva is a winter folk festival of the Mithila region celebrating the affection between brothers and sisters. Clay idols of the sibling pair Sama and Chakeva are worshipped for about ten days in Kartik, with folk songs narrating their legend. The festival's bird motifs also mark the season of migratory birds in the region's wetlands.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Pitrapaksha Mela at Gaya
capsules.body: During the Pitrapaksha fortnight, lakhs of Hindus converge on Gaya to perform pind-daan for their ancestors at the Vishnupad temple on the Falgu river. The belief that offerings at Gaya liberate ancestral souls makes it Hinduism's foremost shraddha centre. The Bihar government organises the Mela with special pilgrim facilities each year.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Malmas Mela of Rajgir
capsules.body: The Malmas Mela at Rajgir is held once every three years during the intercalary month (Adhik Maas) of the Hindu calendar. Pilgrims bathe in Rajgir's hot springs and visit its temples and Buddhist sites. It is among the biggest periodic fairs of the Magadh region.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Vidyapati: the Adi Kavi of Maithili
capsules.body: Vidyapati (c. 1352-1448), court poet of the Oiniwar kings of Mithila, is honoured as the Adi Kavi of Maithili literature. His love songs on Radha-Krishna, written in Maithili, influenced Bengali Vaishnavism and were admired by Chaitanya. His Sanskrit works include treatises on law and the Ganga's glory.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Shri Krishna Sinha: Bihar Kesari
capsules.body: Shri Krishna Sinha, called Bihar Kesari, was the state's first Chief Minister (1946-1961) and its longest-serving. A Gandhian who led the Salt Satyagraha in Bihar, he abolished zamindari and built the state's early industrial base. With deputy Anugrah Narayan Sinha he shaped modern Bihar's institutions.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Anugrah Narayan Sinha
capsules.body: Anugrah Narayan Sinha was Bihar's first Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister, serving alongside Shri Krishna Sinha from 1946 to 1957. A Gandhian and educationist, he presented Bihar's early budgets and championed rural development. His birth anniversary is observed as a state function in Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana
capsules.body: The Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana gives staged cash support to Bihar's girls - from birth assistance through school uniforms, menstrual hygiene support and graduation incentives. It aims to check dropout, child marriage and female foeticide. The scheme converges benefits that earlier ran as separate programmes for the girl child.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Har Ghar Nal Ka Jal
capsules.body: Har Ghar Nal Ka Jal, the flagship resolve of Saat Nischay, promises piped drinking water to every rural household in Bihar. Implementation runs through panchayats with ward-level piped schemes. The programme's maintenance and water quality remain the key tests of its success.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Nagi and Nakti: Bihar's new Ramsar sites
capsules.body: Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries in Jamui district were added to the Ramsar list in 2024, taking Bihar's Ramsar tally to three with Kanwar Lake. [verify] These man-made reservoirs on the Nagi and Nakti rivers host large congregations of migratory ducks, geese and waders each winter. Their listing recognises community-supported wetland conservation in south Bihar.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Kesavananda Bharati and the basic structure
capsules.body: In Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973), a 13-judge bench held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure. The doctrine has since shielded judicial review, federalism, secularism and free elections from amendment. It remains the most-cited judgment in Indian constitutional law.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: The 42nd Amendment: the mini-constitution
capsules.body: The 42nd Amendment (1976), passed during the Emergency, is called the mini-constitution for its sweeping changes. It added Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble, inserted Fundamental Duties, and curtailed judicial review. Parts of it were undone by the 43rd and 44th Amendments after the Emergency.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: GST: the 101st Amendment
capsules.body: The 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016) introduced the Goods and Services Tax, replacing a maze of indirect taxes with a destination-based levy. It created the GST Council under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Finance Minister. GST completed eight years in 2025 as India's biggest tax reform since independence.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Nari Shakti Vandan: women's reservation
capsules.body: The 106th Amendment (2023), the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The reservation will take effect after the next delimitation, which follows the forthcoming Census. Within the women's quota, one-third of seats are reserved for SC/ST women.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: EWS reservation: the 103rd Amendment
capsules.body: The 103rd Amendment (2019) introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections among the unreserved categories in education and public employment. Its validity was upheld by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan (2022) by a 3:2 majority. The EWS quota breaches the 50% ceiling set in Indra Sawhney (1992).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: New criminal laws from July 2024
capsules.body: From 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced the IPC (1860), CrPC (1973) and Indian Evidence Act (1872). The overhaul adds offences like terrorism and mob lynching, mandates forensic investigation for serious crimes, and allows trials in absentia. It is the biggest recodification of criminal law since independence.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Caste enumeration in Census 2027
capsules.body: In April 2025 the government announced that the forthcoming Census - the first digital census, phased over 2026-27 - will enumerate castes. This will be the first caste count since 1931, with major implications for reservation policy and delimitation. The decision followed years of political demand, including after Bihar's 2022 caste survey.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: One Nation One Election: the Kovind panel
capsules.body: The high-level committee on simultaneous elections, chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind, submitted its report in March 2024 recommending synchronised Lok Sabha and assembly polls. Implementing bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024. The proposal needs constitutional amendments and broad political consensus.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: The collegium and the NJAC verdict
capsules.body: Judges of the higher judiciary are appointed through the collegium system flowing from the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges cases. Parliament's attempt to replace it with the National Judicial Appointments Commission was struck down in 2015 as violating judicial independence. The 99th Amendment inserting Article 124A thus became inoperative.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Anti-defection law: the Tenth Schedule
capsules.body: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), disqualifies legislators who defect from their party. The 91st Amendment (2003) removed the one-third split exemption, requiring two-thirds for a valid merger. The Speaker decides disqualification petitions, subject to judicial review after Kihoto Hollohan (1992).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Inter-State Council and Sarkaria
capsules.body: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council to coordinate Centre-State relations; it was established in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation. The Punchhi Commission (2010) later reviewed federal relations and suggested fixed tenures for Governors. Both commissions remain standard BPSC references on federalism.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Money Bill vs Financial Bill
capsules.body: A Money Bill, defined in Article 110, deals only with taxation, borrowing and expenditure from the Consolidated Fund. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha with the President's prior recommendation, and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days. The Speaker's certification of a Money Bill was contested in the Aadhaar case (2018).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
capsules.body: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, passed in April 2025, restructures the administration of waqf properties in India. [verify] It changes the composition of waqf boards and tribunals and tightens the process for declaring waqf property. The law was among the most debated legislations of 2025.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Delimitation freeze till 2026
capsules.body: The 42nd Amendment froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats to states at 1971 population levels till 2001; the 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze to 2026. The freeze was meant to not penalise states that controlled population growth. The coming delimitation after the 2027 Census will reopen the north-south representation debate.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: VVPAT: the paper trail of EVMs
capsules.body: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail units, attached to EVMs, let voters see a printed slip of their vote for seven seconds. VVPATs were used in all Lok Sabha constituencies for the first time in 2019. The Supreme Court has repeatedly upheld EVM-VVPAT integrity while ordering counting of five VVPATs per assembly segment.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Green Revolution and M. S. Swaminathan
capsules.body: The Green Revolution of the 1960s, led by M. S. Swaminathan with high-yielding wheat and rice varieties, made India food-secure. Swaminathan, awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024, later chaired the National Commission on Farmers whose report recommended MSP at 50% over cost. Punjab, Haryana and western UP were its epicentres.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 1991: the LPG reforms
capsules.body: The 1991 balance-of-payments crisis forced India to pledge gold and accept an IMF programme, triggering Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation under P. V. Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh. Industrial licensing was abolished for most sectors, the rupee was devalued, and foreign investment was opened. The reforms ended four decades of the licence raj.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI and monetary policy
capsules.body: The Reserve Bank of India, established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949, conducts monetary policy through the six-member Monetary Policy Committee. The flexible inflation-targeting framework (CPI inflation target of 4% within a 2-6% band) was formalised in 2016. The repo rate is the MPC's principal policy instrument.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NITI Aayog replaces the Planning Commission
capsules.body: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015, shifting from centralised five-year plans to cooperative federalism. Chaired by the Prime Minister with a Governing Council of Chief Ministers, it issues the SDG India Index and the Fiscal Health Index of states. The last Five Year Plan (12th) ended in March 2017.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Digital India and UPI
capsules.body: The Unified Payments Interface, launched by NPCI in 2016, made India the world leader in real-time digital payments. UPI transactions crossed a billion a month within years and the system has been exported to countries like France and Sri Lanka. It rests on the JAM trinity of Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: MSME: the employment engine
capsules.body: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises contribute about 30% of India's GDP and are the largest employers after agriculture. The 2020 revision raised the investment limits - micro up to Rs 1 crore, small Rs 10 crore, medium Rs 50 crore - and added turnover criteria. The Udyam portal is the single registration window for MSMEs.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: The FRBM framework
capsules.body: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (2003) commits the Centre to fiscal discipline, with the deficit targets reset periodically on expert advice. The N. K. Singh committee (2017) recommended a debt-to-GDP anchor of 60% (40% Centre, 20% states). Escape clauses permit deviation during national emergencies and economic shocks.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SEZs and the sunrise sectors
capsules.body: Special Economic Zones, enabled by the 2005 Act, offer tax and regulatory concessions to export-oriented units. The policy focus has shifted to sunrise sectors - semiconductors, EVs, green hydrogen and electronics manufacturing - through Production Linked Incentive schemes. India's electronics exports have surged on the back of mobile phone manufacturing.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI's gold and forex reserves
capsules.body: India's foreign exchange reserves, among the world's largest, are managed by the RBI for currency stability and import cover. The RBI has steadily raised the share of gold in reserves and repatriated part of its overseas gold holdings in 2024. Adequate reserves let India weather the 2024-25 global volatility.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: The 16th Finance Commission
capsules.body: The 16th Finance Commission, chaired by Arvind Panagariya and constituted in December 2023, recommends the tax devolution formula for 2026-31. The 15th Commission had kept states' share at 41% of the divisible pool. Its criteria - income distance, population, area, forest cover and demographic performance - shape every state's finances including Bihar's.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cooperative federalism in taxation
capsules.body: The GST Council, with the Union Finance Minister as chair and state ministers as members, decides tax rates by a three-fourths majority with the Centre holding one-third weight. Compensation to states for GST revenue loss was paid for five years till June 2022. The Council's consensus model is studied as an experiment in federal bargaining.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance
capsules.body: After the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, suspending data-sharing and talks with Pakistan. [verify] The World Bank-brokered treaty had survived three wars as a rare example of water cooperation. The move signalled a hardening of India's counter-terror posture.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Harappan town planning
capsules.body: The Harappan civilisation (c. 2600-1900 BCE) is famed for grid-pattern streets, covered drains and the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro. Dholavira in Gujarat, a UNESCO site, shows a three-part town division and sophisticated water reservoirs. Lothal had the world's earliest known dockyard.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Ashoka's dhamma administration
capsules.body: After the Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE), Ashoka propagated dhamma - a moral code of non-violence, tolerance and welfare - through rock and pillar edicts across the subcontinent. He appointed Dhamma-mahamattas in his 13th regnal year and sent missions abroad, including to Sri Lanka under Mahinda. The edicts, in Prakrit, Greek and Aramaic, are India's earliest deciphered royal inscriptions.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: The Gupta golden age debate
capsules.body: The Gupta period (4th-6th century CE) is called a golden age for its advances in mathematics (Aryabhata), astronomy, metallurgy (Mehrauli pillar) and art (Ajanta). Nalanda was founded under Kumaragupta I in this era. Historians now qualify the label, noting the age's gains were concentrated among elites.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Chola naval power
capsules.body: The Cholas of the 9th-13th centuries built India's greatest pre-modern navy, with Rajaraja I and Rajendra I projecting power to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia. Rajendra's 1025 expedition against Srivijaya secured trade routes across the Bay of Bengal. The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO site, commemorates Rajaraja's reign.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Bhakti and Sufi movements
capsules.body: The Bhakti movement (Alvars, Nayanars, Kabir, Nanak, Mirabai, Tulsidas) and the Sufi orders (notably the Chishtis under Nizamuddin Auliya) reshaped medieval Indian religion around devotion and equality. Both challenged caste hierarchy and ritualism, composing in regional languages. Their syncretic ethos peaked under Akbar's sulh-i-kul.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Akbar's administration
capsules.body: Akbar (1556-1605) built the Mughal administrative system: the mansabdari rank system, Todar Mal's zabti revenue assessment, and the division of the empire into subas. His policy of sulh-i-kul (universal peace) integrated Rajputs through matrimonial alliances. Fatehpur Sikri and the Agra Fort embody his architectural ambition.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Shivaji and Maratha administration
capsules.body: Shivaji (crowned 1674 at Raigad) built the Maratha state on the ryotwari assessment, a standing army paid in cash, and the Ashtapradhan council of eight ministers. His guerrilla tactics and fort network checkmated the Mughals and Bijapur. The Treaty of Purandar (1665) with Jai Singh I marked a key Mughal-Maratha settlement.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Battle of Buxar and the Diwani
capsules.body: The Battle of Buxar (22 October 1764) saw Hector Munro's Company forces defeat the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II. The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa - the constitutional beginning of British rule. Buxar is fought on Bihar's soil in present-day Buxar district.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Permanent Settlement of 1793
capsules.body: Lord Cornwallis's Permanent Settlement (1793) made zamindars proprietors of land in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in return for a fixed revenue demand. Intended to create a loyal landed class, it entrenched absentee landlordism and peasant misery. Bihar's agrarian agitations, from Champaran to the Kisan Sabha, grew from its inequities.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: 1857: the first war of independence
capsules.body: The 1857 uprising began with the Meerut sepoys on 10 May and Mangal Pandey's earlier defiance at Barrackpore. Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed emperor at Delhi while Rani Lakshmibai, Tantia Tope, Nana Sahib and Kunwar Singh led regional resistance. Its failure stemmed from lack of central leadership, limited spread and superior British organisation.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: The Deccan Riots and agrarian unrest
capsules.body: The Deccan Riots of 1875 saw Maharashtra's peasants attack moneylenders' account books, prompting the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act (1879). The earlier Indigo Revolt (1859-60) in Bengal and the Pabna agrarian leagues showed peasant resistance predating the Congress. These movements form the pre-history of Gandhian peasant mobilisation.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi
capsules.body: Curzon's 1905 partition of Bengal triggered the Swadeshi movement - boycott of foreign goods, national education and the rise of Extremists under Tilak, Pal and Lajpat Rai. Bengal was reunited in 1911 when the capital shifted to Delhi. The movement's techniques became the template for later Gandhian agitations.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Gandhi's movements: a timeline
capsules.body: Champaran (1917), Kheda and Ahmedabad (1918) were Gandhi's Indian apprenticeship; Non-Cooperation (1920-22), Civil Disobedience (1930-34) and Quit India (1942) were the national campaigns. Each ended with strategic retreat - Chauri Chaura, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, and wartime repression. Together they converted the Congress from an elite body into a mass movement.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: The INA and the RIN mutiny
capsules.body: Subhas Chandra Bose's Indian National Army, revived in 1943 with Japanese support, reached the Indo-Burma frontier with the slogan Dilli Chalo. The 1945-46 Red Fort trials of INA officers sparked nationalist outrage, followed by the Royal Indian Navy mutiny of February 1946. These shocks convinced Britain that India had become ungovernable.

capsules.subject: History
capsules.title: Mountbatten Plan and independence
capsules.body: The Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 accepted partition, with Punjab and Bengal divided and princely states given the choice of accession. The Indian Independence Act (July 1947) created the dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947. The Radcliffe Line, announced on 17 August, triggered the largest migration in human history.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: The Tropic of Cancer through India
capsules.body: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 deg N) passes through eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. It marks the northern limit of the Sun's overhead passage, dividing India into tropical and subtropical zones. The Mahi river is the only Indian river to cross the Tropic twice.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Western Ghats: a biodiversity hotspot
capsules.body: The Western Ghats, running 1,600 km along India's west coast, are one of the world's eight hottest biodiversity hotspots and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012). Anaimudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is their highest peak. They block the southwest monsoon, making the windward coast among the wettest places on earth.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: The Deccan Traps
capsules.body: The Deccan Traps of Maharashtra and adjoining states are among the world's largest volcanic provinces, formed by eruptions around 66 million years ago. Their basalt lava flows created the region's characteristic black regur soil, ideal for cotton. The lava-stepped landscape hosts the hill forts of the Marathas.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Chilika: Asia's largest brackish lagoon
capsules.body: Chilika Lake in Odisha is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon and India's first Ramsar site (1981). Its Nalabana island shelters migratory birds while Irrawaddy dolphins inhabit the outer channel. The lake supports the livelihoods of over a lakh fisherfolk.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: The Thar desert's extent
capsules.body: The Thar desert, spanning western Rajasthan into Pakistan, is the world's most densely populated desert. The Indira Gandhi Canal has greened parts of Ganganagar and Bikaner, though waterlogging and salinity are concerns. The desert's camel, khejri tree and desert national park (for the great Indian bustard) are its icons.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Sundarbans: the mangrove delta
capsules.body: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, straddles India and Bangladesh at the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta. The Indian side is a national park, tiger reserve and UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to the swimming Royal Bengal tiger. Sea-level rise and cyclones threaten its fragile islands.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Loktak Lake and Keibul Lamjao
capsules.body: Loktak Lake in Manipur is famous for phumdis - floating masses of vegetation and soil. Keibul Lamjao National Park, on the lake's southwestern part, is the world's only floating national park and the last refuge of the sangai (brow-antlered deer). The Ithai barrage altered the lake's hydrology, affecting the phumdis.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: The Chenab rail bridge
capsules.body: The Chenab rail bridge in Jammu and Kashmir, 359 metres above the riverbed, is the world's highest railway bridge - taller than the Eiffel Tower. Part of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla link, it was built to withstand earthquakes and high winds. It symbolises the engineering push to connect Kashmir by all-weather rail.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Project Tiger at 50-plus
capsules.body: Project Tiger, launched in 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park, now covers over 50 tiger reserves across India. The 2022 all-India estimation put the tiger population at 3,682, about 70% of the world's wild tigers. The NTCA oversees the reserves while the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, provides the legal backbone.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Cheetah reintroduction at Kuno
capsules.body: In September 2022 India reintroduced the cheetah - extinct in the country since 1952 - at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, with animals flown from Namibia and South Africa. The project, the world's first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation, tests whether cheetahs can reclaim their historic range. Breeding successes and cub births have marked its progress amid close monitoring.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: India's Ramsar network
capsules.body: India has over 90 Ramsar-listed wetlands, the largest network in South Asia, spanning from Chilika (1981) to recent additions like Nagi-Nakti in Bihar. [verify] The Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran) recognises wetlands of international importance for biodiversity and livelihoods. Amrit Dharohar, launched in 2023, targets their community-led conservation.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: The Aravalli green wall
capsules.body: The Aravalli Green Wall project aims to create a 1,400-km green corridor from Gujarat to Delhi to check the Thar desert's eastward march. Modelled on Africa's Great Green Wall, it involves afforestation across Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi. The Aravallis, among the world's oldest mountain ranges, are also threatened by mining.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Great Indian Bustard: a flagship in peril
capsules.body: The Great Indian Bustard, among the world's heaviest flying birds, survives in a few hundred individuals, mainly in Rajasthan's Desert National Park. Overhead power lines are its biggest killer, prompting Supreme Court-ordered undergrounding in priority habitats. Its plight illustrates the collision between renewable energy expansion and biodiversity.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Single-use plastic ban
capsules.body: India banned identified single-use plastic items - including carry bags below 120 microns, cutlery, straws and cigarette packets - from 1 July 2022. Extended Producer Responsibility rules make manufacturers accountable for plastic waste. Enforcement remains the challenge, with alternatives like compostable plastics scaling up slowly.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: National Green Hydrogen Mission
capsules.body: Launched in 2023 with an outlay of about Rs 19,744 crore, the National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 million tonnes of annual green hydrogen production by 2030. It aims to decarbonise steel, fertilisers and refineries while positioning India as an exporter. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysing water with renewable electricity.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: COP summits and India's stance
capsules.body: At COP26 (Glasgow, 2021) India announced the Panchamrit pledge - net zero by 2070, 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, and lifestyle for environment (LiFE). COP30 was hosted by Belem, Brazil, in November 2025. India consistently argues for equity and common but differentiated responsibilities in climate talks.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: E-waste and the new rules
capsules.body: India is among the world's largest generators of electronic waste, with the E-Waste Management Rules (2022) imposing extended producer responsibility on manufacturers. Formal recycling capacity lags the waste generated, with the informal sector handling much of it unsafely. The rules now cover over 100 electrical and electronic items.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: The leopard census 2024
capsules.body: India's leopard population was estimated at 13,874 in the 2024 census released in 2025, with Madhya Pradesh holding the most. [verify] Leopards, highly adaptable, increasingly range outside forests, raising human-wildlife conflict. The census used camera-trap data across tiger landscapes and adjoining areas.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan: India's human spaceflight
capsules.body: Gaganyaan is ISRO's mission to send Indian astronauts to low-earth orbit aboard an indigenous crew module, with uncrewed test flights preceding the crewed mission. Four IAF test pilots completed astronaut training, including stints abroad. The programme includes the HLVM-3 rocket, crew escape systems and a planned Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Chandrayaan-3's south-pole landing
capsules.body: On 23 August 2023 Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole, making India the first country to land there and the fourth to soft-land on the Moon. The Pragyan rover confirmed sulphur and other elements in the lunar soil. The landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Aditya-L1: India's sun observatory
capsules.body: Aditya-L1, launched in September 2023, is India's first solar observatory, stationed at the Sun-Earth Lagrange point L1, 1.5 million km from Earth. Its seven payloads study the solar corona, flares and space weather. Continuous solar monitoring protects satellites and power grids from solar storms.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: NISAR: the NASA-ISRO radar satellite
capsules.body: NISAR, the joint NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite launched in July 2025, is the costliest earth-observation mission the two agencies have built together. [verify] Its dual-band radar maps land deformation, ice sheets and forests every 12 days. Data will aid disaster response, agriculture and climate science.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Axiom-4: Shubhanshu Shukla's ISS flight
capsules.body: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station in June 2025 aboard Axiom Mission 4, becoming the first Indian to visit the ISS and the second Indian in space after Rakesh Sharma (1984). [verify] He conducted ISRO-designed experiments in microgravity during the two-week mission. The flight is a precursor to Gaganyaan.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: SpaDeX: India's docking milestone
capsules.body: ISRO's SpaDeX mission achieved satellite docking in January 2025, making India the fourth country to demonstrate space docking after the US, Russia and China. [verify] Docking technology is essential for building the planned Bharatiya Antariksh Station and for lunar sample-return missions. The two satellites, SDX01 and SDX02, were launched on a PSLV.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: DeepSeek R1 and the AI cost shock
capsules.body: China's DeepSeek released its R1 reasoning model in January 2025, claiming frontier-level performance at a fraction of Western training costs. The open-weight release triggered a sell-off in AI hardware stocks and a global debate on efficient AI. It accelerated India's own push for sovereign, low-cost AI models.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: India's semiconductor mission
capsules.body: The India Semiconductor Mission (2021), with about Rs 76,000 crore in incentives, aims to build chip fabrication and display units in India. Tata's Dholera fab with Taiwan's PSMC and the Assam packaging unit are the flagship projects. Semiconductors are the strategic choke-point of the digital economy, dominated by Taiwan and South Korea.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Quantum: the National Quantum Mission
capsules.body: The National Quantum Mission (2023), with an outlay of about Rs 6,000 crore, targets quantum computers of 50-1,000 qubits, quantum communication and sensing within eight years. Quantum technology promises unbreakable encryption and exponential computing for drug discovery and logistics. India joins the US, China and EU in the state-backed quantum race.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: The human genome and GenomeIndia
capsules.body: The GenomeIndia project sequenced 10,000 genomes to map India's genetic diversity for precision medicine. India's population harbours thousands of endogamous groups, making such a reference database globally unique. Findings will guide screening for rare diseases and pharmacogenomics.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Paris 2024: India's campaign
capsules.body: India sent 117 athletes to the Paris 2024 Olympics and finished 71st with six medals - one silver (Neeraj Chopra, javelin) and five bronze. Manu Bhaker won two shooting bronzes, becoming the first Indian to win two medals at a single Games since independence. The men's hockey team retained its bronze, and Aman Sehrawat (wrestling) became India's youngest Olympic medallist.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Champions Trophy 2025
capsules.body: India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 in Dubai, defeating New Zealand in the final on 9 March. Rohit Sharma's side went unbeaten through the tournament, with the spinners decisive on slow pitches. It was India's first Champions Trophy title since 2013 and a record third overall.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Gukesh: the youngest world chess champion
capsules.body: D. Gukesh defeated China's Ding Liren in December 2024 to become the World Chess Champion at 18, the youngest undisputed champion ever. The Chennai teenager broke Garry Kasparov's age record set in 1985. His triumph capped India's chess boom, with the country holding both the open and women's junior world titles around the same period.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Khelo India and the sports pyramid
capsules.body: The Khelo India programme - Youth Games, University Games and Winter Games - is the base of India's sporting pyramid, feeding the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). Bihar hosted the 7th Youth Games in May 2025. The 2028 Los Angeles Olympics are the next target for India's medal ambitions.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Neeraj Chopra's javelin reign
capsules.body: Neeraj Chopra, Tokyo 2020 gold medallist, took silver at Paris 2024 behind Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem in a historic South Asian one-two. He remains India's most decorated track-and-field athlete and the face of Indian athletics. His 2025 season included breaching the coveted 90-metre mark. [verify]

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India at the Asian Games
capsules.body: India won 107 medals at the Hangzhou 2022 Asian Games (held in 2023), crossing 100 for the first time. Athletics and shooting led the tally. The next Asian Games will be hosted by Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, in September-October 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Women's cricket's rise
capsules.body: India co-hosted the 2025 ICC Women's ODI World Cup with Sri Lanka, riding the momentum of the Women's Premier League. The WPL, launched in 2023, has professionalised women's cricket with top salaries and packed stadiums. Harmanpreet Kaur's side carries the nation's hopes for a first ICC women's title.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey's Olympic bronze double
capsules.body: India's men's hockey team won bronze at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, ending decades of Olympic medal drought. Goalkeeper P. R. Sreejesh's heroics made him a national icon before his retirement. Hockey India now targets a return to the gold-medal era of 1928-1980.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: IPL 2025: RCB's maiden title
capsules.body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru won their first IPL title in 2025, defeating Punjab Kings in the final and ending an 18-year wait. [verify] Virat Kohli finally lifted the trophy that had eluded him since 2008. The season also spotlighted teenage sensation Vaibhav Suryavanshi. [verify]

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's 2036 Olympic bid
capsules.body: India has formally expressed interest in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, with Ahmedabad projected as the centrepiece city and the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave as the hub. Hosting would follow the 2010 Commonwealth Games experience. The IOC's decision process runs through the 2020s, with competition from other bidders.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma awards 2025
capsules.body: The 2025 Padma awards honoured 139 personalities, with seven Padma Vibhushans including folk singer Sharda Sinha of Bihar (posthumous), violinist L. Subramaniam, nephrologist D. Nageshwar Reddy and former CJI Jagdish Singh Khehar. [verify] The Padma awards, announced every Republic Day eve, are India's highest civilian honours after the Bharat Ratna.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Bharat Ratna 2024: five recipients
capsules.body: In 2024 the Bharat Ratna was conferred on five personalities: Karpoori Thakur and M. S. Swaminathan (posthumous), and L. K. Advani, P. V. Narasimha Rao and Chaudhary Charan Singh. It was the largest single-year conferral, exceeding the usual three-person limit. The announcements spanned January to March 2024.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Prizes 2024
capsules.body: The 2024 Nobels recognised AI's scientific arrival: Physics to Hopfield and Hinton for neural networks, Chemistry to Baker, Hassabis and Jumper for protein structure prediction. Medicine went to Ambros and Ruvkun (microRNA), Peace to Japan's Nihon Hidankyo, Literature to Han Kang, and Economics to Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Dadasaheb Phalke Award
capsules.body: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, Indian cinema's highest honour, went to Mithun Chakraborty for 2022 (announced 2024). Named after the father of Indian cinema, it recognises lifetime contribution to film. Recent recipients include Waheeda Rehman (2021) and Asha Parekh (2020).

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Jnanpith Award
capsules.body: The Jnanpith, India's highest literary honour, was awarded to Gulzar and Jagadguru Rambhadracharya for 2023 (announced 2024) - only the second time it went to two recipients. It recognises outstanding contribution to Indian literature across languages. The award carries a cash prize, a bronze Saraswati and a citation.

capsules.subject: Awards
