capsules.title: Saraswati Samman and Vyas Samman
capsules.body: The Saraswati Samman (K. K. Birla Foundation) honours outstanding prose or poetry in Indian languages; the Vyas Samman specifically recognises Hindi literature. These sit below the Jnanpith in the literary awards hierarchy but carry significant prestige. BPSC often asks about their recent recipients.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: National Sports Awards
capsules.body: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour, followed by the Arjuna Award for consistent performance. The 2024 Khel Ratna went to chess champion D. Gukesh, shooter Manu Bhaker, hockey captain Harmanpreet Singh and para-athlete Praveen Kumar. [verify] The awards were renamed from Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2021.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Gallantry awards: Param Vir to Kirti
capsules.body: The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest wartime gallantry award, the Ashoka Chakra its peacetime equivalent. Wartime decorations descend through Mahavir Chakra and Vir Chakra; peacetime through Kirti Chakra and Shaurya Chakra. Subedar Major Sanjay Kumar (Kargil, 1999) is among the living Param Vir recipients.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Operation Sindoor (May 2025)
capsules.body: After the 22 April 2025 terror attack at Pahalgam killed 26 civilians, India launched Operation Sindoor on 7 May, striking terror camps in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir with stand-off weapons. Pakistan's retaliation and India's counter-strikes marked the sharpest India-Pakistan clash since 2019. An understanding to stop firing was reached on 10 May. [verify]

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-UK free trade agreement
capsules.body: India and the United Kingdom concluded a free trade agreement in May 2025 after three years of negotiation. [verify] The deal cuts tariffs on British whisky and cars while opening Indian services and textile access to the UK market. It is India's most significant trade pact with a developed economy.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: BRICS expansion
capsules.body: Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025, joining the 2024 intake of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia's partner status. [verify] The 2025 summit in Rio de Janeiro debated de-dollarisation and Global South finance. BRICS now represents nearly half the world's population.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: G20: from Delhi to Johannesburg
capsules.body: India's 2023 G20 presidency admitted the African Union as a permanent member - its signature achievement. Brazil hosted in 2024 and South Africa hosted the 2025 summit in Johannesburg, completing the Global South presidency troika. The forum remains the premier venue for global economic coordination.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: SCO summit at Tianjin
capsules.body: The 2025 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit at Tianjin, China, brought together the leaders of India, China, Russia and Central Asia. [verify] The SCO, founded in 2001, focuses on regional security and counter-terrorism. India's participation balances its Quad engagement with Eurasian diplomacy.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Trump's second term
capsules.body: Donald Trump began his second term as US President on 20 January 2025, pursuing an America First agenda of tariffs, immigration curbs and energy expansion. His tariff threats rattled global trade, including India-US negotiations. The term's foreign policy mixes deal-making with alliance pressure.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India-Middle East-Europe Corridor
capsules.body: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, announced at the 2023 G20, links India to Europe via the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Israel. Conceived as a counter to China's Belt and Road, it combines rail, shipping and digital links. Regional conflicts have slowed its implementation.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: The Quad's evolution
capsules.body: The Quad - India, the US, Japan and Australia - has grown from a 2007 naval exercise into a summit-level grouping for Indo-Pacific security and technology. Its agenda now spans critical minerals, undersea cables and maritime domain awareness. India hosted the Quad summit cycle amid careful balancing with Russia ties.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: UN@80 and Security Council reform
capsules.body: The United Nations turned 80 in 2025 amid stalled Security Council reform. India, with Brazil, Germany and Japan (the G4), demands permanent seats reflecting contemporary realities. The veto's paralysis over Ukraine and Gaza has renewed calls for change, though P5 resistance persists.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: COP30 at Belem
capsules.body: COP30, the 2025 UN climate summit, was hosted by Belem in Brazil's Amazon region - symbolically placing forests at the centre of climate action. [verify] The summit reviewed progress on the Global Stocktake and climate finance pledges. India's LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) mission featured in its national messaging.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup
capsules.body: The 2026 FIFA World Cup, hosted jointly by the USA, Canada and Mexico, will be the first with 48 teams and 104 matches. The expanded format adds a round of 32 to the knockout stage. It is the first World Cup hosted across three countries.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Maha Kumbh 2025 at Prayagraj
capsules.body: The Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj (13 January-26 February 2025) drew hundreds of millions of pilgrims to the Triveni Sangam, among the largest peaceful gatherings on earth. Held every 12 years, it rotates among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and Ujjain. The 2025 edition was the first branded as a UNESCO-recognised intangible heritage event cycle. [verify]

capsules.subject: National
capsules.title: Nobel Economics 2026: Hall & Woodford
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences went to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford — announced 12 Oct 2026 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

capsules.subject: National
capsules.title: Bank of India: programmable Digital Rupee
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Bank of India launched user-level programmable CBDC auto-issuance on 29 Sep 2026 — scheduled, purpose-bound Digital Rupee transfers; developed by Montran India.

capsules.subject: National
capsules.title: Diesel/ATF export levies cut from 1 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Diesel export levy ₹20→₹16/L and ATF ₹15→₹10.50/L from 1 Oct 2026; petrol levy unchanged at ₹0.50/L (Central Excise Notifications 52/2026, 53/2026 dated 30 Sep).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India beat West Indies by 14 runs in Indore
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — India won the T20I at Holkar Stadium, Indore, on 11 Oct 2026 by 14 runs — India 223/10 (Abhishek Sharma 69 off 30) beat West Indies 209/7.

capsules.subject: National
capsules.title: HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi MD & CEO from 27 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank's MD & CEO from 27 Oct 2026 — the bank's first external appointee to the role.

capsules.subject: National
capsules.title: New India Assurance gets new CMD
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Lavanya R Mundayur was appointed CMD of New India Assurance (order 30 Sep 2026); tenure till 31 May 2029; she was earlier CMD of the Agriculture Insurance Company of India.

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: Bihar MLC polls on 23 Oct: 8 seats, 164 candidates
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Biennial elections to 8 Bihar Legislative Council seats (Patna, Tirhut, Darbhanga, Kosi Graduates'; Patna, Tirhut, Darbhanga, Saran Teachers') on 23 Oct 2026; 164 candidates in fray; counting 27 Oct; special casual leave for voters (CEO Bihar).

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: Bihar: 1-crore entrepreneur target, Bihar-made purchase preference
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary announced a target of 1 crore entrepreneurs by 2030 and purchase preference for Bihar-made products in government procurement; ~7,000 Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana beneficiaries received instalments at Patna's Bapu Sabhagar (8 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: BSEB extends 2028 exam registration to 24 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — BSEB extended registration for the Matric and Intermediate 2028 exams to 24 Oct 2026 (was 10 Oct); Chairman Dr. Tyagarajan S.M. announced it in Patna (10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: NHRC camp sitting in Patna on 7–8 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The NHRC held a two-day open hearing and camp sitting in Patna on 7–8 Oct 2026; the full bench led by Chairperson Justice V Ramasubramanian heard pending Bihar cases.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Ashutosh Dixit: 29th Air Chief from 31 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 Oct 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh (PIB).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI hikes repo rate to 5.50%
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — RBI's MPC raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 — first hike since Feb 2023; stance 'calibrated tightening'; FY27 GDP 7.1%, CPI 5.2% (RBI).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Trishul reaches Plymouth for Konkan-2026
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — INS Trishul reached Plymouth, UK, for bilateral Exercise Konkan-2026 with the Royal Navy (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Sahyadri reaches Vladivostok for Indra-2026
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — INS Sahyadri reached Vladivostok, Russia, for bilateral Exercise Indra-2026 (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Navy to induct indigenous ASW vessel ‘Mangrole’
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The Indian Navy will induct the indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel ‘Mangrole’ (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: UPI-MDR from 15 Oct: 0.4% above ₹2,000
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — From 15 Oct 2026, specified UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 carry 0.4% MDR (capped at ₹300); railways, telecom, insurance and fuel get a flat ₹5; person-to-person transfers stay free.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Chennai: ₹13,000 cr projects; metro Phase II ₹4,900 cr
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — PM Modi launches Chennai projects worth over ₹13,000 crore on 11 Oct; the Chennai Metro Phase II Poonamallee–Vadapalani stretch (~₹4,900 crore) includes a 3.7-km double-decker structure (PMO, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Defence Secretary to visit Cyprus, Greece (12–15 Oct)
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The Defence Secretary will visit Cyprus and Greece from 12–15 Oct 2026 (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: UPSC Centenary: PM Modi to address gathering at Bharat Mandapam
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 1 October 2026 and address the gathering.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey: India beat Pakistan 4-3, reach Asian Games final
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — Defending champions India defeated Pakistan 4-3 in the men's hockey semifinal at the Asian Games 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Cricket: India vs Pakistan gold-medal final on 3 October
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — India beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the men's cricket semifinal; the gold-medal match against Pakistan is on 3 October.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: FASTag Annual Pass crosses 1 crore
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — FASTag Annual Pass issuances crossed one crore since the August 2025 launch; the ₹3,075 pass gives one-year validity or 200 toll crossings at about 1,150 plazas.

capsules.subject: Agriculture
capsules.title: Khet Bachao Abhiyan: 22 October–30 November 2026
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The Centre announced the Khet Bachao Abhiyan (22 October–30 November 2026) for soil health and balanced fertiliser use, with over ₹1,200 crore sanctioned under PM-RKVY to 10 states.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC to hear Ram Temple donation plea on 2 November
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court agreed to hear on 2 November a plea seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhooti Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai and others over alleged donation irregularities; the bench is headed by CJI Surya Kant.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar cabinet approves two new universities
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 23 September 2026 approved the establishment of Mata Sita Women's University at Patna and Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar' University at Begusarai under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026. The Patna university will be Bihar's first women's university, with jurisdiction over women's colleges in Patna outside Patna University; the Dinkar University will cover colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria. Rs 15 crore each was approved for establishment expenses.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar cabinet: 24 decisions including Nawada sugar mill
capsules.body: At its 23 September 2026 meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the Bihar cabinet took 24 decisions. Besides the two new universities, it approved a sugar mill for Nawada, revised allowances for chairpersons of state boards and commissions (monthly salary raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 65,000; daily allowance from Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,500), and a consolidated Rs 50,000 monthly payment for members of the Bihar State Fishermen Commission.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Samrat Choudhary: first BJP Chief Minister of Bihar
capsules.body: BJP leader Samrat Choudhary took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on 15 April 2026, becoming the first BJP leader to head a government in the state. His predecessor Nitish Kumar stepped down of his own accord and is now a Rajya Sabha MP. Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav serve as Deputy Chief Ministers.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: applications open for 32,388 teacher posts
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission opened applications on 25 September 2026 for the Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE) 4.0 under Advertisement No. 15/2026, which supersedes the earlier 14/2026. The drive will fill 32,388 school teacher posts (primary 3,847; middle 8,563; secondary 3,877; senior secondary 16,101). The last date to apply is 26 October 2026 and the fee deadline is 25 October 2026, with a uniform fee of Rs 100.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: 72nd BPSC CCE prelims on 25 October 2026
capsules.body: As per the BPSC exam calendar 2026, the 72nd Integrated Combined Competitive Examination prelims is scheduled for 25 October 2026 with 1,189 vacancies. The 71st CCE (1,298 posts, prelims 13 September 2025) has its mains results expected around August–September 2026. The 70th CCE had 2,035 posts.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bihar Budget 2026–27: Rs 3.47 lakh crore, largest ever
capsules.body: Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav presented the Bihar Budget 2026–27 on 3 February 2026 with a record outlay of Rs 3,47,589.76 crore, up from Rs 3.17 lakh crore in 2025–26. The fiscal deficit is targeted at Rs 39,111.80 crore (2.99% of GSDP), within the FRBM 3% ceiling, with a revenue surplus of Rs 1,143.19 crore. The guiding principle is 'nyay ke saath vikas' (development with justice).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bihar Budget 2026–27: education gets Rs 60,204 crore
capsules.body: Education received the highest allocation in the Bihar Budget 2026–27 at Rs 60,204 crore, followed by health (Rs 21,270 crore), home (Rs 20,132 crore) and energy (Rs 18,737 crore). Policy highlights include the Saat Nishchay-3 roadmap (2025–2030), the Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi for farmers, phase-2 of the Industrial Manufacturing Cluster at Gaya, five new expressways, and conversion of public buses to CNG/electric with 2,000+ charging stations.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana: Rs 10,000 to 1.5 crore women
capsules.body: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 highlighted the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana, under which Rs 10,000 each was transferred to the bank accounts of about 1.56 crore women to support livelihoods. The government plans up to Rs 2 lakh in further assistance for women who used the initial support to start businesses. The scheme, launched ahead of the 2025 Assembly elections, is credited with powering the NDA's women-led victory.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bihar Economic Survey 2025–26: 13.1% growth, still lowest per capita
capsules.body: The 20th Bihar Economic Survey 2025–26, tabled on 2 February 2026, reports GSDP growth of 13.1% at current prices (8.6% at constant prices) in 2024–25, beating the national 9.8% (6.5% real). GSDP touched Rs 9.92 lakh crore and per capita GSDP rose to Rs 76,490 — yet Bihar remains India's poorest state by per capita income (about Rs 70,000 a year). Literacy improved to 61.8%.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar–Jharkhand end Sone river water dispute
capsules.body: Bihar and Jharkhand signed an MoU in September 2026 on sharing the waters of the Sone river, ending a longstanding dispute between the two eastern states. The agreement was signed in the presence of the Union Home Minister. The Sone rises at Amarkantak and joins the Ganga near Maner, west of Patna.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 18th Bihar Assembly: NDA's 202-seat landslide
capsules.body: The 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly was constituted on 20 November 2025 after elections on 6 and 11 November 2025. The NDA won about 202 of 243 seats (BJP 89, JD(U) 85, LJP(RV) 19, HAM(S) 5, RLM 4) with a 46.7% vote share, against the Mahagathbandhan's 35. Prem Kumar is Speaker and Tejashwi Yadav (RJD) is Leader of the Opposition. Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj failed to win a seat in its debut.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Inter-district teacher transfers: three district choices [verify]
capsules.body: Teachers in Bihar can now give three district preferences for inter-district transfers, with postings finalised on preferred-district basis and District Education Officers empowered to transfer within districts — a relief for a long-pending teacher demand. [verify]

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: CMPDI sand-replenishment study in five Bihar rivers
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet sanctioned a Rs 2.58 crore post-monsoon sand-replenishment study by the Central Mine Planning & Design Institute (CMPDI) covering five rivers — Sone, Kiul, Falgu, Morhar and Chanan. The study measures sand deposits before and after the monsoon to curb illegal sand mining and ensure leaseholders pay revenue on the actual volume extracted.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Minor airports for six Bihar districts under UDAN [verify]
capsules.body: Bihar cleared minor airports for Madhubani, Veerpur, Munger, Valmikinagar, Muzaffarpur and Saharsa under the UDAN regional connectivity scheme, with the Airports Authority of India and the state government jointly overseeing development. [verify]

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Q1 FY2026–27: GDP grows 7.8%
capsules.body: India's GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY2026–27, led by manufacturing, financial services, real estate and professional services. GST collections stayed robust through the quarter, reflecting continued economic momentum.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Exercise Veer Guardian-2026: India–Japan air drill at Jodhpur
capsules.body: The India–Japan bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian-2026 was held at Air Force Station Jodhpur from 9 to 22 September 2026. The IAF fielded Tejas, Su-30 MKI and Rafale aircraft while the Japan Air Self-Defence Force flew F-2A fighters. The first edition was held in Japan in January 2023.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Yudh Abhyas 2026: India–US exercise near the LAC
capsules.body: The India–US joint military exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026, running since 2004 and alternating between the two countries, is underway close to the Line of Actual Control in one of its largest editions, with reported first-time deployment of the US MLIDS counter-drone system.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar Fishermen Commission members to get Rs 50,000 a month
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet on 23 September 2026 approved a consolidated monthly payment of Rs 50,000 for members of the Bihar State Fishermen Commission, covering honorarium, vehicle allowance and mobile recharge — part of a broader revision of board and commission allowances.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO launches GISAT-1A (EOS-05) on GSLV-F17
capsules.body: ISRO launched the GISAT-1A (EOS-05) Earth-observation satellite on GSLV-F17 in early September 2026 from Sriharikota, ending a nearly seven-month launch pause caused by the PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failure of 12 January 2026. The geostationary satellite will support disaster monitoring, agriculture and forestry, replacing the GISAT-1/EOS-03 lost in the 2021 GSLV-F10 failure.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan crew module: 10 parachutes of 4 types
capsules.body: ISRO detailed the Gaganyaan crew module's deceleration system: 10 parachutes of 4 types deployed in sequence — 2 apex-cover separation, 2 drogue, 3 pilot and 3 main parachutes — for a safe splashdown after re-entry. Suspension lines use high-strength Kevlar fibre, with heat-resistant Nomex and elastic nylon canopies. The mission will send three crew to a 400-km orbit for three days.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO's radar research facility at Chandrapur, Assam
capsules.body: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma laid the foundation stone for ISRO's Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) Advanced Radar Research Facility at Chandrapur in Kamrup Metropolitan district. The facility will strengthen satellite tracking, orbit determination and space situational awareness in the Northeast.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY completes eight years
capsules.body: The Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana completed eight years on 23 September 2026. Launched on 23 September 2018, it remains the world's largest government-funded health assurance programme, giving Rs 5 lakh cashless hospitalisation cover per family per year to eligible beneficiaries.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Delhi's DURGA scheme: 1,300 pink e-autos for women
capsules.body: The Delhi cabinet approved the DURGA (Driving Upliftment and Rozgar for Women/Transgender Green e-Auto) scheme on 23 September 2026, providing 1,300 pink electric autos to women and transgender persons for safe, green livelihoods in the capital.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: PLI schemes: Rs 2.6 lakh crore investment, 14.6 lakh jobs
capsules.body: Production Linked Incentive schemes across 14 sectors had attracted Rs 2.6 lakh crore in investment and generated Rs 23.8 lakh crore in production and sales as of June 2026, creating 14.6 lakh jobs — a key pillar of the manufacturing push.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India–New Zealand FTA: ratified 21 Sept, effective 20 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The India–New Zealand free trade agreement, signed on 27 April 2026, was formally ratified on 21 September 2026 and enters into force on 20 October 2026. New Zealand removes tariffs on 100% of Indian goods from day one, while India eliminates or cuts duties on 95% of its imports from New Zealand; dairy and key farm goods stay protected.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: VIKRAM3201 and KALPANA3201: India's space chips
capsules.body: ISRO and the Semi-Conductor Laboratory developed VIKRAM3201 — India's first space-qualified launch-vehicle microprocessor fabricated at SCL — and the open-source, flight-tested KALPANA3201 microprocessor, marking a leap in space-electronics self-reliance.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: DRDO's quantum push: indigenous dilution refrigerator
capsules.body: DRDO signed its first major deep-tech agreement under the Technology Development Fund scheme with start-up Zero mK India to build an indigenous 20-millikelvin dilution refrigerator. The cryogenic system, vital for quantum computers, supports the National Quantum Mission's goal of ending import dependence.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Rare-earth magnet pilot plant at ARCI Hyderabad
capsules.body: A pilot plant for sintered Neodymium-Iron-Boron (Nd-Fe-B) rare-earth permanent magnets was commissioned at ARCI Hyderabad in March 2026, supporting domestic supply chains for EVs, wind turbines and robotics — a strategic hedge against rare-earth import dependence.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: HAL's third Tejas Mk1A line: capacity now 24 jets a year
capsules.body: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited operationalised its third LCA Tejas Mk1A assembly line in October 2025, raising annual production capacity to 24 jets, alongside a second line for the indigenous HTT-40 basic trainer aircraft.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Steel output doubles to 170 million tonnes
capsules.body: India's crude steel production more than doubled from 81.7 million tonnes in 2014–15 to 170.0 million tonnes in 2025–26, reflecting the infrastructure and manufacturing push. India remains the world's second-largest steel producer.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Nipun: second Nistar-class diving support vessel
capsules.body: INS Nipun, the second ship of the Nistar-class Diving Support Vessel family, was launched on 31 August 2026 at the Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. Built by Hindustan Shipyard, Visakhapatnam, it will handle deep-sea diving, underwater intervention, salvage and submarine rescue for the Navy.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Human brain-cell atlas maps 6.3 million cells
capsules.body: An international consortium published a comprehensive human brain-cell atlas mapping gene activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex across life stages, analysing nuclei from over 6.3 million brain cells — fresh insight into neurodevelopment, ageing and neuropsychiatric conditions.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: ISRO warns of severe cyclone season Oct–Dec 2026
capsules.body: ISRO scientists warned that three high-intensity tropical cyclones could strike the North Indian Ocean between October and December 2026, with cumulative storm energy projected up to 83% above the 44-year average — a critical heads-up for coastal disaster management.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Andhra Pradesh Police launch AI Drone Portal, SafeStay app
capsules.body: Andhra Pradesh Police rolled out an AI Drone Portal for aerial surveillance and crime prevention and the SafeStay app for safety monitoring of hostels and paying-guest accommodations — a model of tech-led policing.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Messi retires from international football after 2026 World Cup final [verify]
capsules.body: Lionel Messi announced retirement from international football after Argentina's 1–0 loss to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, closing one of the sport's greatest international careers. [verify]

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar's Saat Nishchay-3: the 2025–2030 roadmap
capsules.body: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 unveiled Saat Nishchay-3, the third phase (2025–2030) of the seven-resolves programme, framed around the themes 'imaan, gyaan, vigyaan, armaan aur samman' (faith, knowledge, science, aspiration, dignity) under the guiding principle 'nyay ke saath vikas'.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi
capsules.body: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 announced the Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi to boost farmers' income through direct support, named after Bharat Ratna Karpoori Thakur, the 'Jannayak' who pioneered backward-class reservations in Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Gaya to host phase-2 Industrial Manufacturing Cluster
capsules.body: Phase-2 of the Industrial Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) will be developed at Gaya under the Bihar Budget 2026–27, anchoring manufacturing investment in south Bihar alongside five new expressways and 2,000+ EV charging stations.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bihar's capex share rises to 22.3%; revenue receipts double
capsules.body: Bihar's capital expenditure share rose from 15.8% of total outlay in 2020–21 to 22.3% in 2024–25, while revenue receipts grew from Rs 1.28 lakh crore to Rs 2.18 lakh crore — a structural shift toward asset-creating investment noted in the Economic Survey 2025–26.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Hotel Patliputra Ashok to become five-star via PPP [verify]
capsules.body: The Bihar cabinet approved redeveloping Patna's iconic Hotel Patliputra Ashok into a five-star hotel through a public-private partnership on a long lease, boosting the capital's hospitality infrastructure. [verify]

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Nitish Kumar: from CM to Rajya Sabha MP
capsules.body: Nitish Kumar served as Bihar Chief Minister from 1 December 2025 to 14 April 2026 after leading the NDA to its 2025 landslide, then stepped down of his own accord; he now represents Bihar in the Rajya Sabha while remaining the NDA's senior leader in the state.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar's women-led mandate: the new 'MY' formula
capsules.body: Prime Minister Modi described the NDA's 2025 Bihar victory as a new 'MY — Mahila and Youth' formula, crediting the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana (Rs 10,000 to about 1.25 crore women before the polls) for the women-powered mandate that buried the old 'MY' (Muslim–Yadav) arithmetic.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Vikramshila dolphin sanctuary and Project Dolphin
capsules.body: Bihar's Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary at Bhagalpur (notified 1991) protects the endangered Gangetic dolphin — India's National Aquatic Animal and a Schedule I species — under the umbrella of Project Dolphin (2020), modelled on Project Tiger.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Kabar Tal, Nagi–Nakti: Bihar's Ramsar wetlands
capsules.body: Kabar Tal in Begusarai (Ramsar, 2020), Bihar's largest freshwater oxbow lake, and the Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries in Jamui form the state's Ramsar wetland trio — critical wintering grounds for migratory birds on the Central Asian Flyway.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Makhana: Bihar's 90% share and the Makhana Board
capsules.body: Bihar produces about 90% of India's makhana (foxnut), centred on Darbhanga, Madhubani, Purnia and Saharsa; Mithila makhana holds a GI tag and the Union Budget 2025–26 announced a dedicated Makhana Board in Bihar — a direct prelims fact on the state's agro-economy.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Desidustat: India's oral drug for kidney-disease anaemia
capsules.body: Desidustat, a novel oral drug developed in India, treats anaemia in chronic kidney disease patients — an affordable alternative to injectable erythropoietin therapies, closely watched in pharma current affairs.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Bihar's OPRMC Phase-3: tech-led road maintenance
capsules.body: Bihar's Output and Performance-based Road Maintenance Contract (OPRMC) Phase-3 will deploy modern technology for road monitoring and upkeep, shifting the state's focus from construction-first to sustained maintenance of its road network — about 5.5% of India's total. [verify]

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Bharat Ratna 2024: Karpoori Thakur remembered in 2026 budget
capsules.body: The Bihar Budget 2026–27 named its flagship farmer income scheme after Jannayak Karpoori Thakur, who received the Bharat Ratna in 2024 for pioneering backward-class reservations and pro-poor governance as Bihar's Chief Minister in the 1970s.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Patna's JP Ganga Path and the riverfront push
capsules.body: The JP Ganga Path (Patna's Marine Drive) extensions continued through 2026, reshaping the capital's riverfront connectivity; AIIMS Darbhanga's construction and the Munger–Bhagalpur bridge projects also progressed as marquee infrastructure works. [verify]

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Rail Wheel Factory: 2.10 lakh wheels in 2025–26
capsules.body: The Rail Wheel Factory produced over 2.10 lakh wheels and 1.20 lakh wheelsets in 2025–26, underpinning the railways’ rolling-stock self-reliance alongside the Nuclear Fuel Complex’s eighth domestic batch of steam-generator tubes for 700 MW reactors.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Preeta Verma becomes Bihar's first woman acting DGP
capsules.body: Bihar DGP Vinay Kumar (1991-batch IPS) took voluntary retirement on 27 September 2026 and was appointed Chief Information Commissioner, a post vacant since 31 July. 1991-batch IPS officer Preeta Verma was given additional charge of DGP - the first woman IPS officer to hold the post in Bihar.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Cabinet: Rs 336.85 cr for police modernisation, 50 drones
capsules.body: At its 23 September 2026 meeting, the Bihar cabinet approved Rs 336.85 crore for strengthening district police, railway police, BSAP and the Prohibition and Narcotics Control Bureau, plus the purchase of 50 drones for Rs 24.50 crore under the centrally sponsored Police Modernisation Scheme - for crowd control, riverine and anti-Naxal operations and disaster management.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Dairy push: Rs 126.07 cr projects in Supaul, Madhepura, Saharsa
capsules.body: The 23 September 2026 cabinet approved dairy development projects in Supaul, Madhepura and Saharsa under the Kosi Milk Producers Cooperative Union - including a yoghurt plant, premium ice cream plant and milk chilling facilities - at Rs 126.07 crore, as part of Saat Nischay-3.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: amended Adv 14/2026, registration from 21 Sept
capsules.body: In the amended Advertisement 14/2026 for Teacher Recruitment Examination TRE 4.0, BPSC opened online registration from 21 September 2026 and added music-teacher posts to the recruitment drive, which originally announced 32,388 teacher vacancies across classes 1-12. The written exam is scheduled from 22 to 27 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games: India at 37 medals after Day 8 (27 Sept)
capsules.body: India took a seven-medal haul on 27 September 2026 to reach 37 medals (4 gold, 16 silver, 17 bronze), placed 12th. Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh won squash singles silvers; athletics added five medals - Sarvesh Kushare (silver, men's high jump, 2.25m), Ancy Sojan (silver, women's long jump, 6.53m), Parul Chaudhary (bronze, 3000m steeplechase, national record 9:08.67), Harita Bhadra (bronze, women's 200m) and Tejaswin Shankar (bronze, decathlon, 7,934 pts).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: TRAI: 30-day recharge plans, voice/SMS-only plans
capsules.body: Under the Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, operators must offer at least one 30-day special tariff voucher renewable on the same date every month - cutting the 13 annual recharges to 12 - plus voice-and-SMS-only plans for users who do not need data.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Brick-kiln OTS: interest waiver from 21 Sept to 20 Dec 2026
capsules.body: Bihar's Mines and Geology Department opened a three-month One-Time Settlement window (21 September to 20 December 2026) for brick kilns: owners who pay outstanding principal dues get the interest waived. About 6,000 kilns are covered; total dues were Rs 316.66 crore, with Rs 289.38 crore still outstanding.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Cabinet: e-Sushruta NX in 12 medical institutions, vet policy
capsules.body: The 23 September 2026 cabinet approved rollout of the e-Sushruta NX hospital information application in 12 medical institutions, gave in-principle approval to the Bihar Veterinary Infrastructure and Service Strengthening Policy, and cleared the Bihar Boiler (Inquiry, Adjudication and Appeal) Rules, 2026.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: Advertisement 15/2026 out; 32,388 posts, apply 25 Sep–26 Oct
capsules.body: BPSC issued Advertisement 15/2026 (dated 22 September 2026) for TRE 4.0, superseding the cancelled Adv 14/2026 (18 August). It offers 32,388 school teacher posts — 3,847 primary, 8,563 middle, 3,877 secondary and 16,101 senior secondary. Online applications run 25 September–26 October 2026; the fee (Rs 100, plus Rs 200 biometric charge if Aadhaar is not linked) must be paid by 25 October; the correction window stays open till 28 October. Selection is through a written MCQ examination with no interview.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Mandeep K. Bhandari appointed CBSE Chairperson
capsules.body: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved Mandeep K. Bhandari, a 2001-batch AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, as Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education. Earlier Principal Secretary to the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, he replaces Lokhande Prashant Sitaram, who held additional charge after Rahul Singh’s transfer in June 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: OECD raises India’s FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%
capsules.body: In its September 2026 Interim Economic Outlook ‘Weathering Successive Shocks’, the OECD raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast by 80 basis points to 7.1%, up from 6.3% projected in June, citing resilient domestic demand. It expects growth to moderate to 6.5% in FY28, with inflation averaging 4.7% in FY27 and 4.2% in FY28.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026: India reaches 39 medals on 28 September
capsules.body: India’s tally at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 reached 39 medals (4 gold, 17 silver, 18 bronze) on 28 September 2026, after Esha Singh’s silver in the women’s 25m pistol (lost a shoot-off to China’s Xiao Jiaruixian) and Pincky Balhara’s bronze in women’s -78kg kurash. Seven medals had come on 27 September. Central cash awards: Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver, Rs 10 lakh for bronze.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: WorldSkills Shanghai 2026: India finishes 10th, best ever
capsules.body: India placed 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 — its best performance ever at the global skills competition — winning six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence. It improved on 13th place at WorldSkills Lyon 2024, where the contingent had won four bronze medals.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Livestock Insurance Portal launched on 28 September
capsules.body: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) — holding the Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj portfolios — launched the Livestock Insurance Portal of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying in New Delhi on 28 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India–New Zealand FTA in force from 20 October 2026
capsules.body: The India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement comes into force on 20 October 2026, giving 100% duty-free access to Indian exports.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Legislative Council Chairman resigns
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — BJP MLC Awadhesh Narain Singh resigned as Bihar Legislative Council Chairperson on 28 September 2026, submitting his resignation to Deputy Chairperson Ram Bachan Rai. JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar favours the 82-year-old Rai, whose MLC term ends 16 March 2027, as the next Chairperson. Under the NDA understanding, with the Assembly Speaker (nine-time BJP MLA Prem Kumar of Gaya) held by the BJP, the Council Chairperson's post goes to the JD(U). Biennial elections to eight Graduate/Teachers' Council constituencies are due on 23 October 2026 (terms expire 16 November).

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Bihar DElEd Result 2026 declared
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — BSEB declared the Bihar D.El.Ed Result 2026 on 28 September 2026 for the two-year face-to-face programme's 2025–27 (first year) and 2024–26 (second year) batches. Scorecards are available at deledresult.biharboardonline.org; candidates need their roll code and roll number (as printed on the admit card) to download the marksheet.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: CM's aerial survey of flood-hit areas
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary conducted an aerial survey of flood-affected Vaishali, Saran (Hajipur–Maker), East Champaran and Gopalganj (Dumaria Ghat) on 28 September 2026. The Gandak at Dumaria Ghat is flowing about 1.5 metres above the danger mark and is expected to rise another 50 cm; he directed night patrolling of embankments and SDRF–NDRF coordination for flood relief camps and community kitchens.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bihar PNG network: 28 of 38 districts covered
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — A 28 September review chaired by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit noted that 28 of Bihar's 38 districts (about 74%) are now covered by the City Gas Distribution network, with 1,52,686 domestic PNG connections live — about 40.44% of the March 2026 target. Five districts were added recently (Sheohar and Sitamarhi on 27 August, Buxar on 2 September); Kaimur is targeted for gasification by November 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bank strike of 28–30 Sep deferred
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — The three-day bank strike planned for 28–30 September 2026 was deferred after talks between the Indian Banks' Association and the United Forum of Bank Unions on 27 September. A high-level committee will study the unions' demand for a five-day banking week (all Saturdays off; banks currently close only on the second and fourth Saturdays, a rule in place since 2015).

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: CM attends school PTM-2026
capsules.body: 29 Sep 2026 — Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary attended the Parent-Teacher Meeting (PTM)-2026, themed on NIPUN (foundational literacy and numeracy), at Rajkiya Madhya Vidyalaya, Ramjichak, Danapur, on 26 September 2026. He set students a target of scoring above 90%, cautioned against unnecessary mobile-phone use, and said coaching should be needed only in special circumstances.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC: zero applications for 218 polytechnic HoD posts
capsules.body: On 29 September 2026 the BPSC said it received zero applications for 218 Head of Department posts in government polytechnics under the Department of Science, Technology and Technical Education. Advertised on 26 August 2025 across 16 disciplines — Mechanical 33, Computer Science 43, Electrical 42, Civil 45, Electronics 39 — and re-advertised after nine earlier ads drew no response, the requisitions have now been returned to the department.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: TRE-4 and Group D aspirants protest in Patna
capsules.body: On 29 September 2026, TRE-4 aspirants demonstrated outside Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari's residence in Patna, demanding that candidates appearing for CTET 2026 also be allowed in the TRE-4 recruitment, on par with STET-appearing candidates. Group D aspirants marched from Gandhi Maidan toward the CM's residence; stopped at JP Golambar, about 500 sat in protest. The Gardanibagh sit-in has continued for about 30 days.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: TRE-4.0: 932 more posts added; total now 32,388
capsules.body: BPSC added 932 teacher posts to TRE-4.0 on 29 September 2026, taking total vacancies to 32,388 — Classes 9–10 up 493 to 4,370, Classes 11–12 up 439 to 16,540, with 3,847 primary and 8,563 middle-school posts. Applications under Advt 15/2026 run 25 September–26 October 2026 at bpsconline.bihar.gov.in, with a flat ₹100 fee.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bank strike of 28–30 September deferred after IBA–UFBU talks
capsules.body: The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its 28–30 September 2026 strike after talks with the IBA: banks agreed to five-day banking twice a month for non-field staff, with a further meeting in October. The strike would have affected about 8.5 lakh employees.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: JEE Main 2027 Session 1: 22–30 January; registration soon
capsules.body: NTA is expected to open JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration soon at jeemain.nta.nic.in. The session is reported for 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027, with 31 January as a buffer date — about 114 days from 29 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: Nilekani-led NTA reform panel consults K. Radhakrishnan
capsules.body: On 29 September 2026, the seven-member Nandan Nilekani-led task force on NTA exam reforms met former ISRO chief K. Radhakrishnan, whose 2024 committee made 101 recommendations on exam security, registration, admit cards, CBT and result systems. The new panel's report is yet to be submitted.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: NTA: exam cities from Aadhaar address from 2026–27
capsules.body: NTA will allot exam cities for JEE, NEET and CUET from the 2026–27 academic year on the basis of the address on the candidate's Aadhaar card, with no choice of cities; only candidates awaiting Aadhaar enrolment can choose. NEET will also move to Computer Based Test mode from next year.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: 32,388 teacher posts; apply by 26 October
capsules.body: BPSC's TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) notifies 32,388 school-teacher posts: 3,847 primary (Classes 1-5), 8,563 middle (6-8), 3,877 secondary (9-10) and 16,101 senior secondary (11-12). Apply online 25 September-26 October 2026 on bpsc.bih.nic.in; fee Rs 100 per category.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Gandak embankment breach raises flood threat
capsules.body: Heavy rainfall in Nepal and a reported breach in the Gandak embankment have raised flood threats in Bihar and eastern UP. The Gandak (Narayani) rises in Nepal and joins the Ganga in Bihar as a left-bank tributary.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Kavach 4.0 for Varanasi Division at Rs 223 crore
capsules.body: Indian Railways approved Kavach 4.0 - its indigenous automatic train protection system - across 614.75 route km of the Varanasi Division at Rs 223 crore on 29 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC quashes Mulla Afroz NSA detention; Rs 10 lakh costs on UP
capsules.body: On 29 September 2026 the Supreme Court quashed Mulla Afroz's NSA preventive detention in the Sambhal case, set aside the Allahabad High Court ruling and imposed Rs 10 lakh costs on Uttar Pradesh, holding a custodial confession alone cannot ground preventive detention.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: August IIP grows 8.0%; manufacturing 9.0%
capsules.body: India's Index of Industrial Production grew 8.0% year-on-year in August 2026, with manufacturing output up 9.0% - a strong print ahead of the festive quarter.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Neeru Dhanda: trap gold at Asian Games
capsules.body: Neeru Dhanda won the women's individual trap gold at the 2026 Asian Games - the first Indian woman to win individual Asian Games gold in the event.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Vithya Ramraj breaks P.T. Usha's 1984 record
capsules.body: Vithya Ramraj won 400m hurdles bronze in 54.75 seconds, breaking P.T. Usha's 55.42-second national record set in 1984.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Vigilance raids Bihar bureaucrat couple; ~Rs 80 lakh cash seized
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — The Bihar Vigilance Investigation Bureau searched four premises of Patna ADM (Supply) Ravindra Kumar Diwakar and his wife, Danapur Sub-Registrar Kumari Sweety, recovering nearly Rs 80 lakh in cash, jewellery worth Rs 52.6 lakh and 48 watches in a Rs 1.07 crore disproportionate-assets case registered on 25 September under the Prevention of Corruption Act and BNS Section 61(2).

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Ceigall India gets Rs 214.52 cr Bihar mining LoI for Nawada
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — Ceigall India received a Bihar government Letter of Intent on 30 September for stone-block mining at Bhadokhara, Nawada — a five-year, Rs 214.52 crore project with 20,96,500 cubic metres of total minable reserve, awarded by the Department of Mines and Geology via e-reverse auction.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Gandak at record 91.25 m; embankments breached in West Champaran
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — The Gandak breached embankments at Khairtwa (Bagaha-1) and Phuliyakhad (Bairia) in West Champaran on 30 September after hitting a record 91.25 m level following heavy Nepal rainfall; discharge stayed above 500,000 cusecs and CM Samrat Choudhary inspected Dumariaghat on 28 September.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: INDIA bloc: march to EC on 6 Oct; CEC removal motion ready
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — At its 30 September meeting in New Delhi, the INDIA bloc announced a march to the Election Commission office on 6 October and a New Delhi rally on 1 November, pressing for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged voter-list manipulation; a draft removal motion is ready for deliberation.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, becomes youngest Woman Grandmaster
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — Eleven-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history, as reported on 30 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India's first Blue Bond: Rs 600 cr + green shoe
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — Sagarmala Finance Corporation launched India's first Blue Bond on 28 September: Rs 600 crore with a Rs 500 crore green-shoe option, 10-year tenor, AA+ rated by ICRA and CARE, arranged by SBI Capital Markets.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO targets seven launches by March 2027
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — ISRO Chairman V Narayanan said on 30 September the agency targets seven rocket launches by March 2027, including Gaganyaan's first uncrewed flight, using PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 rockets.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Net FDI hits five-year high
capsules.body: 30 Sep 2026 — India's net FDI hit a five-year high of USD 13.4 billion in April-July 2026, up 38% year-on-year; gross inflows rose 12.6% to USD 43.9 billion.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: CM's aerial survey of flood-hit West Champaran and Saran
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary conducted an aerial survey of flood-affected areas in West Champaran (Bagaha, Bathna in Bairia, Machhargawan in Yogapatti, Shivrajpur and Bankatwa in Nautan) and Saran on 30 September, then visited the relief camp at PM Shri Govt Plus Two High School, Bathna, where he served food at the community kitchen and inspected the temporary Anganwadi and medical camps.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: New Gandak breaches in Gopalganj and Saran; Ganga above danger mark
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The Water Resources Department reported two fresh Gandak breaches on 30 September: a six-metre stretch of the Bandhauli-Sheetalpur-Faizullahpur zamindari bund at Sheetalpur (Gopalganj's Baikunthpur block) around 6 am, and an eight-metre subsidence of the right Saran embankment at Haijalpur (Maker block) with a damaged flood-control gate; the Ganga was above the danger mark in Patna, with NDRF and SDRF deployed at major ghats.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Barrage discharge data, 30 September
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — At Valmikinagar Gandak Barrage, discharge fell from 1,39,400 cusecs at 4 am to 1,31,500 cusecs at 7 am on 30 September; the Kosi Barrage at Birpur held steady at 1,04,100 cusecs, while the Indrapuri Sone Barrage fell sharply from 1,59,062 to 1,19,960 cusecs in the same window.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: INDIA bloc: district marches and paper-ballot demand
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The INDIA bloc announced nationwide district marches and five major rallies over alleged election malpractices, demanding a return to paper ballots; the BJP dismissed the meeting's outcomes as lacking political vision.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games archery clean sweep; India eighth with 60 medals
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — India completed a clean sweep of all three compound archery team golds at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on 30 September: the women's team (Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi, Prithika Pradeep) beat China 238-234, equalling the world record set by Korea at Incheon 2014; the mixed team (Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav) beat South Korea 158-157 in a shoot-off; and the men's team (Kushal Dalal, Ganesh Mani Ratnam) also won gold. India's tally stands at 60 medals (10 gold, 21 silver, 29 bronze), eighth overall.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cabinet approves Rs 1.86 lakh crore PM-DHARA
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet approved the PM-DHARA scheme to build intra-state power transmission networks with battery storage, aimed at transferring 135 GW of clean renewable energy across the country.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Wheat MSP raised to Rs 2,610/quintal
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The Centre raised the Minimum Support Price for wheat by Rs 25 to Rs 2,610 per quintal for the 2027-28 marketing year; pulses and oilseeds received hikes of up to Rs 675 per quintal.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Special Campaign 6.0; new birth/death registration rules
capsules.body: 1 Oct 2026 — The government begins Special Campaign 6.0 (2–31 October) for cleanliness and reducing pendency across ministries, and stricter rules for delayed birth and death registration took effect from 1 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: 32,388 teacher posts; apply till 26 October 2026
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) will fill 32,388 school teacher posts in Bihar; applications are open 25 September–26 October 2026 (fee payment by 25 October) with a uniform fee of Rs 100. Level-wise: Primary (1–5) 3,847; Middle (6–8) 8,563; Secondary (9–10) 3,877; Higher Secondary (11–12) 16,101.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: BPSC Project Manager preliminary exam (4 Oct) postponed
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — BPSC has postponed the Project Manager (Industries Department) preliminary examination (Advt 109/2025) that was scheduled for 4 October 2026, citing administrative reasons; a new date will be announced later.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Special gram sabhas on 2 Oct; 'Child Marriage-Free Village' push
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — Gram panchayats across Bihar joined the nationwide special gram sabhas on 2 October 2026 launching the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 ('Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'); panchayats were also directed to pass 'Child Marriage-Free Village' resolutions under the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.

capsules.subject: Employment
capsules.title: RRB NTPC CEN 06/2026: apply 8 Oct–6 Nov
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — The indicative notice for RRB NTPC Graduate recruitment (CEN 06/2026, 3,477 tentative posts) schedules online applications 8 October–6 November 2026 at rrbapply.gov.in (tentative); fee Rs 500 (UR/OBC/EWS) / Rs 250 (others), with refund on appearing in CBT-1; age 18–33 as on 01.01.2027.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI MPC 5–7 Oct: first hike since Feb 2023 likely
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — 35 of 61 economists polled by Reuters expect the RBI to raise the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% at the 5–7 October MPC meeting — the first hike since February 2023 — as August CPI (4.82%) stayed above the 4% target for a third straight month.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India defends Gaprindashvili Trophy at Chess Olympiad
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — India defended the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand — third straight edition after Chennai 2022 and Budapest 2024 — taking Open silver (gold: Uzbekistan) and women's bronze (gold: China); Savitha Shri B won individual gold on board 5.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Reform Utsav launched 2 Oct; Special Campaign 6.0 begins
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — PM Modi inaugurates 'Reform Utsav' on 2 October 2026, a first-of-its-kind campaign celebrating 12 years of transformative governance; alongside, Special Campaign 6.0 (2–31 October) drives Swachhata, pendency reduction and e-waste disposal in government offices.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST Council (8 Oct): arrest powers out, prosecution bar at Rs 5 crore
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The 57th GST Council (chaired by FM Nirmala Sitharaman, 8 October 2026) recommended removing GST officers' power to arrest taxpayers, raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, scrapping the minimum punishment for GST offences and cutting the general penalty from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000, with faster automated refunds.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: Uttarakhand becomes India's sixth fully literate state
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Uttarakhand was declared India's sixth fully literate state (after Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim) under NEP 2020 and the ULLAS–Nav Bharat Saaksharta Programme; CM Pushkar Singh Dhami felicitated NIOS-examined neo-literates at Dehradun on 6 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Health
capsules.title: JOSH teams launched for TB elimination (8 Oct)
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Health Minister J.P. Nadda launched JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) teams under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan at Bharat Mandapam on 8 October 2026: five NCC cadets plus five MY Bharat volunteers per team under a Class-I officer, first in 55 districts across 11 states; 'Khushi Avatar' AI chatbot also launched for TB awareness.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Smriti Mandhana named India women's cricket captain
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Smriti Mandhana has been appointed the new captain of the Indian women's cricket team, succeeding Harmanpreet Kaur.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Delhi doubles ASHA incentives to Rs 6,000
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Delhi government doubled monthly incentives for 6,690 ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) workers from Rs 3,000 to Rs 6,000, recognising their grassroots role in delivering healthcare and government schemes.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Djokovic wins China Open; Alcaraz takes Japan Open
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Novak Djokovic won the China Open 2026 men's singles title in Beijing; Carlos Alcaraz of Spain won the Japan Open 2026 for the second consecutive year, beating Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic 7-6(4), 6-4 in the Tokyo final.

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: 33,320 teacher posts; apply by 26 October 2026
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission has raised BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) vacancies from 32,388 to 33,320 school-teacher posts across classes 1–12 (announced 7 October 2026). Online applications are open 25 September – 26 October 2026 at bpsc.bih.nic.in. Qualification: graduation/post-graduation in the subject plus B.Ed / STET / CTET / D.El.Ed. Age (as on 1 Jan 2026): 18–37 (UR male), 40 (UR female, BC, EBC), 42 (SC/ST). Fee: ₹750 (General/OBC/EWS), ₹200 (Bihar SC/ST, domicile women, PwD). Selection: written examination followed by document verification. Pay scale: Level 6–9 (₹25,000–₹32,000/month).

capsules.subject: Bihar
capsules.title: Bihar STET 2026: 2nd dummy admit card out; corrections closed 7 October
capsules.body: The Bihar School Examination Board released the 2nd dummy admit card for the Bihar STET 2026 (Secondary Teacher Eligibility Test, Advt P.R.183/2026) on 1 October 2026, with a correction window during 1–7 October 2026 at stetregistration.cbrt.co.in. The computer-based test covers classes 9–12. Fee: ₹960 for one paper and ₹1,440 for both papers (UR/EWS/BC/EBC); ₹760/₹1,140 for SC/ST/PwD. Qualifying the STET is mandatory for BPSC TRE 4.0 applicants without CTET.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Tarang Shakti 2026 concludes at Jodhpur with historic F-35 debut (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The IAF’s multilateral Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 concluded on 13 October 2026 at Jodhpur Airbase — its second edition with eight nations. About 150 fighter aircraft flew 600+ sorties; the US F-35 Lightning II flew in Indian airspace for the first time. Also seen: US KC-135 tanker, UAE F-16s, French Rafales and A330 MRTT, C-130Js of Bangladesh and Australia, and Germany’s A400M. Chief Air Chief Marshal Amarpreet Singh’s final fighter-pilot sortie was in a Tejas before his 31 October retirement; Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit becomes Air Chief on 1 November.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: Odisha: free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Odisha Cabinet on 13 October 2026 approved free textbooks for ~28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10 in government and aided secondary schools (other than those already covered under SC/ST provisions). Outlay: Rs 284.07 crore over five years (2025-26 to 2029-30), aiming at equitable access, lower dropout and better elementary-to-secondary transition.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Six-state governor reshuffle (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu's 12 October 2026 reshuffle: Braj Mohan Ram to Odisha, Dr Sudha Yadav to Karnataka, Dr Dhal Singh Bisen to Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim; Om Prakash Mathur transferred from Sikkim to Kerala; Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completes five years
capsules.body: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, launched on 13 October 2021, completed five years on 13 October 2026, marking progress in integrated, GIS-based infrastructure planning across central ministries and states.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: DARPG’s September 2026 CPGRAMS report: record grievance disposal
capsules.body: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances published its 53rd monthly CPGRAMS report: a record 2,38,579 public grievances were redressed in September 2026 (disposal rate exceeding 104%), bringing pendency down to 85,687 cases; 454 Secretary-level reviews were registered.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: Lakshadweep: India’s first 100% literate UT under ULLAS
capsules.body: Lakshadweep has become India’s first 100% literate Union Territory under ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society), the national adult-literacy programme under the Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram.

capsules.subject: Agriculture
capsules.title: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana completes its first year
capsules.body: The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY), the agriculture-focused convergence scheme, completed its first year on 11 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC 72nd CCE Prelims postponed again (notice 12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission postponed the 72nd Combined Competitive Examination (Prelims) 2026 again through a notice dated 12 October 2026 (announced via @BPSCOffice). The exam was to be held on 25 October 2026 (Sunday); it was earlier scheduled for 26 July 2026. No revised date has been announced. The drive covers 1,186 posts - the initial 1,230 was reduced after 44 Sugarcane Officer vacancies were removed.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: Vaishali boat tragedy (13 Oct 2026 night)
capsules.body: At least 13 children died after a boat capsized in the Ganga river under the Raghopur police station area of Vaishali district, Bihar, on the night of 13 October 2026. The boat was ferrying villagers to a neighbouring village to attend a feast; seven people were rescued.

capsules.subject: Bihar Special
capsules.title: BPSC Exam Calendar 2026
capsules.body: BPSC has released its Exam Calendar 2026 with tentative schedules for major recruitments - covering one-phase, two-phase and three-phase exams, prelims, mains, interviews and expected result timelines. Candidates should treat the dates as tentative since they may change for administrative or legal reasons (Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: RRB NTPC UG (CEN 07/2026): 1,688 posts — apply 15 Oct to 13 Nov 2026
capsules.body: The Railway Recruitment Board has opened applications for 1,688 undergraduate-level posts under CEN No. 07/2026: Commercial-cum-Ticket Clerk (700), Accounts Clerk-cum-Typist (200), Junior Clerk-cum-Typist (600) and Trains Clerk (188). Candidates who passed Class 12 can apply online from 15 October to 13 November 2026; the age limit is 18–30 years as on 1 January 2027, with a correction window from 16 to 25 November 2026.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: UPSSSC PET admit card and RRB Technician answer key released (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The UPSSSC released the admit card on 15 October 2026 for the Uttar Pradesh Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET), with exams on 25 and 30 October and 1 November 2026, downloadable from upsssc.gov.in. On the same day, the RRB released the Technician Grade 3 (CEN 02/2026) answer key and response sheet at rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: Parliamentary panel seeks NTA overhaul: CBT, age caps, two-stage NEET (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The parliamentary standing committee on education (382nd report, chaired by Mukul Wasnik), presented in October 2026, recommended sweeping NTA reforms after NEET-UG 2026 had to be cancelled and held afresh: shift to computer-based testing, explore age and attempt caps, a two-stage medical entrance format, and 1,000 secure government-owned test centres by 2030. Separately, NEET 2026 stray-vacancy counselling started on 13 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: भारत–वेस्टइंडीज टी20 निर्णायक मुकाबला 17 अक्टूबर को बेंगलुरु में (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: सीरीज़ 2–2 से बराबर होने के बाद भारत–वेस्टइंडीज पांचवां और निर्णायक टी20 मुकाबला 17 अक्टूबर को बेंगलुरु के एम. चिन्नास्वामी स्टेडियम में खेला जाएगा। चौथे टी20 में वेस्टइंडीज ने 24 रन से जीत दर्ज की थी (शाई होप 102*, कीमो पॉल 5/41); भारत ने वनडे सीरीज़ 2–1 से जीती थी। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: एशियाई खेल 2026: भारत चौथे स्थान पर, 85 पदक; पैरा खेल 18–24 अक्टूबर से (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: एशियाई खेल 2026 में भारत 85 पदकों (21 स्वर्ण, 27 रजत, 37 कांस्य) के साथ चौथे स्थान पर रहा। NSDF, SAI और IOCL ने मुक्केबाज़ी के लिए ₹40 करोड़ की दो वर्षीय पहल शुरू की। एशियाई पैरा खेल 18–24 अक्टूबर को आइची-नागोया (जापान) में होंगे। (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Bihar GK
capsules.title: Anant Singh row rocks JD(U) before MLC polls (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Mokama JD(U) MLA Anant Singh claimed on 16 October 2026 that he had 'got nine people murdered' for former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar in the latter's early political days, amid his opposition to the JD(U)'s Patna Graduates MLC candidate Neeraj Kumar. He is backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh for the 23 October 2026 election. JD(U) national spokesperson Rajiv Ranjan Prasad said the remark did not deserve to be taken seriously.

capsules.subject: Bihar GK
capsules.title: BPSC TRE-4: 32,388 teacher posts; deadline 21 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission opened applications for the Teacher Recruitment Examination TRE-4 (2026) to fill 32,388 school teacher vacancies: 3,847 for Classes 1-5, 8,563 for Classes 6-8, 3,877 for Classes 9-10 and 16,101 for Classes 11-12. Candidates with CTET or STET certificates can apply on bpsc.bih.nic.in; the last date is 21 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Bihar GK
capsules.title: Bihar Legislative Council polls: Patna Graduates seat (23 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Bihar Legislative Council election for the Patna Graduates' constituency is scheduled for 23 October 2026. JD(U) has fielded Neeraj Kumar, while JD(U) MLA Anant Singh is supporting Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh, and Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar is campaigning for the NDA candidates.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Makhana Board and NIFTEM in Bihar, IIT Patna expansion, and support for the Western Koshi Canal.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh, was declared India's 58th tiger reserve on 9 March 2025.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in 'abeyance' on 23 April 2025 after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Odisha was notified as a national park on 24 April 2025, India's 107th; it is the only wild home of melanistic tigers.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar hosted the 7th Khelo India Youth Games (May 4-15, 2025); Maharashtra topped the table, hosts Bihar finished 15th.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Under Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojana, all above 60 get Rs 1,100 monthly by DBT on the 10th, from June 2025.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The 17th BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro (6-7 July 2025) adopted the Rio de Janeiro Declaration and condemned the Pahalgam terror attack.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India and the UK signed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) on 24 July 2025, giving duty-free access to 99% of Indian exports to the UK.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025, becoming India's 88th Grandmaster and fourth woman GM.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO-NASA's NISAR satellite launched on July 30, 2025 aboard GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota, the world's first dual-frequency (L+S band) SAR.

oneliners.subject: Schemes/Economy
oneliners.text: The PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, launched 1 August 2025, crossed 72 lakh first-time employees in its first year.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: 1991-batch IAS officer Pratyaya Amrit became Bihar Chief Secretary on September 1, 2025.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Teachers' Day is observed in India on 5 September, the birth anniversary of Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected India's 15th Vice President on 9 Sep 2025, defeating Justice B. Sudershan Reddy 452-300 with 98.2% turnout.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Hindi Diwas is celebrated on 14 September, marking the adoption of Hindi as an official language of the Union in 1949.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: In the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2025, India rose to 38th; Switzerland topped for the 15th consecutive year and China entered the top 10.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement on 17 September 2025, treating aggression against one as aggression against both.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Assamese music icon Zubeen Garg died in Singapore on 19 September 2025 aged 52 and was given a state funeral on 23 September.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The 56th GST Council scrapped the 12% and 28% slabs, moving to 5% and 18% plus a 40% demerit rate on sin/luxury goods ('GST 2.0').

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The ECI delisted 474 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties on 22 September 2025 for not contesting any election in six years.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: PM Modi released the first Rs 7,500 crore instalment of the Bihar Mukhya Mantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The IAF retired its last MiG-21s on 26 Sep 2025, decommissioning No. 23 and No. 3 squadrons and ending the type's 62-year Indian service.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana was launched by PM Narendra Modi on September 26, 2025, giving Rs 10,000 DBT to over 1.5 crore women in phase one and up to Rs 2 lakh in phase two.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: World Tourism Day is observed on 27 September every year.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India won Asia Cup 2025 in Dubai, beating Pakistan by five wickets for a record-extending ninth title, unbeaten in all seven matches.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite NISAR sent its first Earth images on 30 Sep 2025 ahead of full operations.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: The ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025 began on 30 Sep 2025, co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI's MPC held the repo rate at 5.5% (October 2025), raising the FY26 GDP forecast to 6.8% and cutting the CPI projection to 2.6%.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Bihar added three Ramsar sites in 2025: Gogabeel Lake, Gokul Jalashay and Udaipur Jheel.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Gandhi Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, is observed on 2 October.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Bihar Assembly elections (243 seats) will be held in two phases on 6 and 11 Nov 2025 (121 and 122 seats), with counting on 14 Nov.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Patna Metro's 3.45-km first phase (ISBT-Zero Mile-Bhoothnath) opened on October 6, 2025, extended to Malahipakri on July 2, 2026.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: Nobel Peace Prize 2025 went to Venezuela's Maria Corina Machado for her work for democratic rights.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Dhanteras fell on 18 October in 2025, marking the start of the Diwali festivities.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Diwali / Lakshmi Puja fell on 20 October in 2025.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Bhai Dooj was observed on 23 October 2025.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: United Nations Day is observed every year on 24 October.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Cochin Shipyard delivered 'Mahe', the first indigenous Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft of her class.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The United States sanctioned Colombian President Gustavo Petro, escalating the counternarcotics standoff.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Severe Cyclone Montha made landfall near Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, on 28 Oct 2025 with 90-100 kmph winds, damaging crops over 38,000 hectares.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Severe Cyclonic Storm Montha crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kakinada on 28 October 2025 with winds of 90-100 kmph.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: Odisha's annual Gahirmatha fishing ban (1 November–31 May) protects nesting Olive Ridley turtles.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: India's first digital museum on tribal freedom fighters is coming up in Chhattisgarh.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2025 found global emissions rose 2.3% in 2024 to 57.7 GtCO2e, with India and China recording the largest absolute increases.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The Navy's third survey vessel of her class, 'Ikshak', was commissioned at Kochi on 6 Nov 2025.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Playback singer and actress Sulakshana Pandit died in Mumbai on 6 November 2025 aged 71; she won the 1976 Filmfare award for 'Tu Hi Sagar Tu Hi Kinara' and was the sister of Jatin-Lalit and niece of Pandit Jasraj.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Uttarakhand observed its Foundation Day on 9 November 2025; the state was formed in 2000.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The 10 November 2025 Red Fort blast case was registered under the UAPA and the Explosives Act.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: COP30 in Belem, Brazil (10-21 November 2025) adopted the Belem Package of 29 decisions, targeting USD 1.3 trillion per year in climate finance by 2035.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Veteran actress Kamini Kaushal died in Mumbai on 13 November 2025 aged 98; her film Neecha Nagar (1946) remains the only Indian film to win the Cannes Palme d'Or.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Jharkhand observed its 25th Foundation Day on 15 November 2025; the state was carved out of Bihar in 2000.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: COP31 will be held at Antalya, Turkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026, with Turkiye as president and Australia leading negotiations.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Nitish Kumar took oath for a record tenth term as Bihar CM on November 20, 2025 at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, after the NDA won 202 of 243 seats.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: CAQM revised the GRAP schedule on 21 November 2025, pulling each stage's pollution curbs one stage earlier for Delhi-NCR.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Dharmendra, Padma Bhushan recipient and star of Sholay with 300+ films across six decades and a former Lok Sabha MP, died in Mumbai on 24 November at age 89.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Uzbekistan's 19-year-old Javokhir Sindarov won the FIDE Chess World Cup in Goa, becoming the youngest-ever champion, as the trophy was renamed the Viswanathan Anand Cup.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: The Golden Peacock for Best Film at the 56th IFFI (Goa) went to the Vietnamese film Skin of Youth by Ash Mayfair.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Chhattisgarh, Sikkim and Jharkhand received their first-ever Ramsar designations in 2025; Tamil Nadu leads India with 20 Ramsar sites.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The US assumed the G20 presidency on 1 December 2025; the Leaders' Summit will be held at Trump National Doral, Miami, on 14-15 December 2026.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The VB–G Ram G Bill (December 2025) replaced MGNREGA, guaranteeing 125 days of rural wage employment.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The SHANTI Bill (December 2025) replaced the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and opened civil nuclear energy to regulated Indian private participation.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: ICGS 'Samudra Pratap', India's first indigenous pollution-control vessel built by Goa Shipyard, was dedicated to the nation on 5 Jan 2026.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: CSIR-NPL's National Environmental Standard Laboratory, Asia's first facility to test and certify air-pollution monitors, was inaugurated on 5 Jan 2026.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: 55 scholarly works in classical languages (Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Odia, Tamil) were released on 6 Jan 2026 along with a 45-episode sign-language Tirukkural series.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The US withdrew from 66 international bodies on 7 Jan 2026, including the India-led ISA, and formally exited the WHO after 78 years.
