oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: India became the world's first country to commercially produce bio-bitumen: CSIR's paddy-straw pyrolysis technology, with 15% blending saving ~Rs 4,500 crore in forex.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India and the UAE agreed to double bilateral trade to $200 billion by 2032 alongside a new Strategic Defence Partnership (January 2026).

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited India on 12–13 January 2026; the two sides signed 19 strategic agreements.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO's 64th PSLV flight (PSLV-C62/EOS-N1) suffered a third-stage anomaly on 12 January 2026.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The UN High Seas Treaty, ratified by 60+ countries, entered into force on 17 January 2026.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: India's first sleeper Vande Bharat (Howrah–Kamakhya) was flagged off from Malda Town on 17 January 2026.

oneliners.subject: International

oneliners.text: World Maritime Day falls on the last Thursday of September; the 2026 theme was 'From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence'.

oneliners.text: The Defence Ministry signed an Rs 810.79 crore deal with BDL for 160 SAT-SAAW precision glide bombs.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: DRDO's indigenous 30kW truck-mounted laser weapon, part of Project Sudarshan Chakra, is moving toward production.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas is being held across Rajasthan and Uttarakhand.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Tata's 20,000 sq-m defence plant at Berrechid, Morocco, will build 150 WhAP 8x8 vehicles - India's biggest armoured-vehicle export order.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: SEBI proposed a mutual-fund-only PMS with a Rs 25 lakh minimum investment and Rs 2 crore net worth.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The United Forum of Bank Unions called a three-day nationwide bank strike for 28-30 September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The Finance Ministry clarified that P2P UPI transfers and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 remain free of charge.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The EPF wage ceiling was raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, effective 17 September 2026 - the first revision in about 12 years.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: EAM Jaishankar co-chaired the first-ever P4M Summit on multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity in New York.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Roshibina Devi became the first Indian to win medals at three successive Asian Games: bronze in 2018, silver at Hangzhou 2022 and silver in 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won bronze in men's double sculls at the Asian Games 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Mirabai Chanu's 49kg weightlifting silver ended India's 28-year wait since Karnam Malleswari's 1998 Bangkok silver.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Jay Meena won India's first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis, a bronze in men's singles.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka to win the 2026 US Open women's singles title - her third Grand Slam.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Ayushman Bharat, the world's largest healthcare scheme, covers 60+ crore beneficiaries with Rs 5 lakh annual health cover.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: At the 20th Rozgar Mela, the Prime Minister distributed 51,000+ appointment letters across 45 locations.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Exercise Veer Guardian 2026 marked the first-ever visit of Japanese fighter aircraft to India.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Fitch raised India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.9% and S&P to 7%.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: Luke Lindberg was appointed Executive Director of the World Food Programme for a five-year term.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India became the first South Asian country to host the World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF 2026, Gandhinagar).

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: The ISRO-ESA cooperative agreement was extended to 8 January 2032.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO's Advanced Radar Research Facility (IARRF) will come up at Chandrapur, Assam.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: The 9th Molecular Virology Meeting 2026 was held at BRIC-NII, New Delhi.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: The Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform crossed 3 crore registered youth.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Bharat Taxi, a zero-commission cooperative ride-hailing service, was launched in five UP cities.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: UP's Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana offers farm loans at 6% interest, down from 11%, to 5 lakh small and marginal farmers.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: India's installed solar capacity has risen to nearly 165 GW.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Rajat Sharma was re-elected NBDA President for 2026-27.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The BJP named in-charges for all 36 states and UTs: Smriti Irani got Haryana and Chhattisgarh, Ram Madhav got Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The ECI said its SIR checks expanded from 4 categories in West Bengal to 11 in Phase 3 states including Karnataka, Haryana, Delhi and Telangana.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The Centre cut basic customs duty on crude sunflower oil to nil and on crude palm and soyabean oil to 5% from 24 September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said bank credit grew about 18% year-on-year till June 2026 across agriculture, industry, housing and MSMEs.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India's installed solar capacity reached nearly 165 GW with PM Surya Ghar empowering over 51 lakh families.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The Asian Development Bank raised India's GDP growth forecast to 7% in September 2026 on stronger-than-expected Q1 performance.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: INS Trishul reached Toulon, France for the 24th edition of the bilateral naval exercise Varuna after a port call at Alexandria, Egypt.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: The Technology Development Board signed an Rs 63.84 crore agreement with Galax-E for next-generation multi-sensor satellite technology.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India reaffirmed at UNGA 81 its goal to eliminate Hepatitis B and C as public-health threats by 2030.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY, the world's largest health assurance scheme, turned eight in September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: The MY Bharat platform crossed 3 crore registered youth since its 2023 launch.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: KAVACH 4.0 was commissioned for the first time on South Central Railway, covering 108 km between Malkajgiri and Kamareddi.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: Premier Energies commissioned India's largest solar cell facility, a 7 GW plant at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: INS Trishul reached Toulon, France, for the 24th edition of Exercise VARUNA, the bilateral naval drill that began in 2001.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: CDS General N.S. Raja Subramani stressed the integration of technology, data and industry for defence modernisation.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: SEBI's 215th board meeting (24 Sep 2026) replaced the 2020 PMS rules: PMS can now invest in IPOs, primary-market debt and overseas securities, and a new mutual-fund-only PMS starts with ~Rs 25 lakh minimum versus Rs 50 lakh.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The United Forum of Bank Unions called a 3-day nationwide bank strike from 28-30 Sep 2026, demanding a 5-day banking week, pension updation, uniform DA formula and an NPS-to-OPS switch option.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: EAM S. Jaishankar chaired the 2nd FIPIC Foreign Ministers' Meeting (launched 2014 in Fiji) on 24 Sep in New York on the sidelines of UNGA 81, reviewing the 2023 12-Point Action Plan.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: FSSAI's draft 2026 amendment proposes banning non-milk 'analogue paneer' from using the word 'paneer', with public objections invited within 60 days of gazette publication.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: The Power Ministry has sent the draft National Electricity Policy 2026 to the Cabinet for approval.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Railways will build a 2nd rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra at Saraighat (Assam) under the Northeast Frontier Railway, plus doubling the Agthori-Kamakhya track.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: Domestic manufacturing now meets 99.2% of India's mobile-phone demand, a milestone for electronics self-reliance.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: NEET-PG 2026 results (2,63,544 candidates) declared 24 Sep; cut-offs are 262 (General/EWS), 244 (General-PwBD) and 226 (SC/ST/OBC).

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India won 5 medals on Day 6 of Asian Games 2026, taking the tally to 17 (1 gold, 6 silver, 10 bronze) and slipping to 15th, while China crossed 100 medals.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India's hockey team beat South Korea 8-2, their biggest-ever Asian Games win over the Koreans, while both kabaddi teams assured medals.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The India-New Zealand FTA enters into force on 20 Oct 2026, giving 100% of India's exports to NZ duty-free access and targeting doubled trade of Rs 35,000 crore in five years.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Fitch raised India's FY27 GDP growth forecast by 50 bps to 6.9% on stronger-than-expected expansion and resilient investment.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: MoD signed a Rs 810.79 crore Buy (Indian-IDDM) contract with BDL for 160 SAT-SAAW systems, the DRDO glide bomb with 60% indigenous content, deliverable in 2027-29.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The 18th India-Mongolia exercise Nomadic Elephant began at Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, with 45 personnel per side focusing on counter-insurgency under a UN mandate.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The 3rd National Conference of ANTF heads (NCB, 36 states/UTs) will implement the Vision Document on Narcotics Control targeting a drug-free India by 31 Dec 2029.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: India co-launched OneSCD, a global sickle-cell partnership with Nigeria, WHO, UNICEF and Africa CDC, and showcased its 2023 National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (72.9 million+ screened).

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: AB PM-JAY, launched 23 Sep 2018 at Ranchi, completed 8 years with 60+ crore beneficiaries, giving Rs 5 lakh annual family cover under 60:40 Centre-state funding.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance was renamed ICICI Life Insurance on 22 Sep 2026 as Prudential plc moves from promoter to passive investor.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: BIS certification becomes mandatory for smartphone screen protectors from 1 Apr 2027 under IS 19348:2025, the 66th category under the Compulsory Registration Order.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Pune will host the 2032 UCI Road World Championships, the first time cycling's road worlds come to India, beating Groningen/Drenthe (Netherlands).

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Jay Meena (Dewas, MP) won bronze in men's singles soft tennis, India's first-ever Asian Games medal in the sport.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Delhi's DURGA scheme provides 1,300 pink e-autos (1,170 for women, 130 for transgender persons) for self-employment of women aged 20-40 with income up to Rs 5 lakh.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: World Pharmacists Day is observed on 25 September; the 2026 theme 'Empowering pharmacists for healthier futures' was set by the International Pharmaceutical Federation.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Antyodaya Diwas is observed on 25 September, the birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, honouring his vision of uplifting the last person in the queue.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Premier Energies commissioned India's largest solar cell manufacturing facility in September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The Defence Ministry signed an Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics for anti-airfield weapons on 25 September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: TRAI launched its Digital Connectivity Rating Platform on 25 September 2026.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: India and France reaffirmed cooperation in the electricity sector on 25 September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won India's second Asian Games gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team final with an Asian record of 484.6 points.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: APEDA facilitated the export of GI-tagged Gulbarga Toor Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Mirabai Chanu's 49kg silver at Aichi ended India's 28-year wait for an Asian Games weightlifting medal.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: Biometric Aadhaar authentication becomes mandatory for subsidised domestic LPG refills from 1 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected India's 15th Vice President on 9 September 2025, defeating Justice B. Sudershan Reddy 452-300.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The 56th GST Council scrapped the 12% and 28% slabs, creating 5% (merit), 18% (standard) and 40% (demerit) rates effective 22 September 2025.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Election Commission delisted 474 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties on 22 September 2025 for not contesting any election in six years.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: PM Modi transferred the first instalment of Rs 7,500 crore under the Bihar Mukhya Mantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana on 25 September.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The IAF retired its last MiG-21s on 26 September 2025, ending 62 years of service.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India won the Asia Cup 2025 on 28 September, beating Pakistan by five wickets for a record-extending ninth title.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: The NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite sent its first Earth images on 30 September 2025.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The RBI held the repo rate at 5.5% on 1 October 2025, raising the FY26 GDP forecast to 6.8% and cutting CPI to 2.6%.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Fresh protests in Ladakh in September demanded Sixth Schedule safeguards and statehood.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Severe Cyclone Montha made landfall near Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, on 28 October 2025.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: 19-year-old Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan became the youngest-ever FIDE Chess World Cup champion in Goa; the trophy was renamed the Viswanathan Anand Cup.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Parliament passed the VB-G Ram G Bill on 18 December 2025, replacing MGNREGA with 125 days of guaranteed rural wage employment.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The SHANTI Bill passed on 18 December 2025 replaces the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, opening civil nuclear energy to private players.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: ICGS 'Samudra Pratap', built by Goa Shipyard, was dedicated to the nation on 5 January 2026 as India's first indigenous pollution-control vessel.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: On 7 January 2026 the US withdrew from 66 international bodies including the India-led International Solar Alliance, and exited the WHO after 78 years.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: India became the world's first country to commercially produce bio-bitumen from paddy straw, announced 7 January 2026.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO's 64th PSLV flight (PSLV-C62) suffered a third-stage anomaly on 12 January 2026 while carrying DRDO's Anvesha satellite.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The UN High Seas Treaty entered into force on 17 January 2026 after ratification by 60+ countries.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: India's first sleeper Vande Bharat Express was flagged off on 17 January 2026 on the Howrah-Kamakhya route.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: The Padma Awards 2026 comprised 131 honours - 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day on 26 January 2026 with EU leaders Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa as chief guests.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: India and the EU concluded their Free Trade Agreement - hailed as the 'Mother of All Deals' - at the 16th India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Nirmala Sitharaman presented her ninth consecutive Union Budget on 1 February 2026, targeting a 4.3% fiscal deficit and Rs 12.2 lakh crore capex.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The 16th Finance Commission retained states' vertical devolution at 41% of central taxes for 2026-31.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: Tarique Rahman became Bangladesh's 11th Prime Minister on 17 February 2026 after the BNP swept 212 of 299 seats.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: The IAF's Vayushakti-26 firepower demonstration was held at Pokhran on 27 February 2026.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: INS Taragiri, a 6,670-tonne Project 17A stealth frigate built by Mazagon Dock, was commissioned on 3 April 2026.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in as West Bengal Chief Minister on 9 May 2026, ending 15 years of Trinamool rule.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: BIS notified IS 19850:2026, India's first fuel standard beyond E20, covering E22, E25, E27 and E30 blends.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: V. D. Satheesan was sworn in as Kerala Chief Minister on 18 May 2026 as the UDF won 102 of 140 seats.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Lt Gen N. S. Raja Subramani took over as India's third Chief of Defence Staff on 31 May 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Royal Challengers Bengaluru won the IPL 2026 on 31 May, beating Gujarat Titans by five wickets under Rajat Patidar's captaincy.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: R Praggnanandhaa became the first Indian to win Norway Chess on 5 June 2026.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: On 10 June 2026 Narendra Modi completed 4,399 days in office, becoming India's longest-serving continuously elected PM.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: PM Modi toured Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand from 7-11 July 2026 - the first Indian PM visit to New Zealand in 40 years.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: Indonesia's President conferred the Bintang Adipurna, Indonesia's highest civilian honour, on PM Modi on 7 July 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The India-UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026, with the UK cutting tariffs on 98.8% of its tariff lines.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: On the 79th Independence Day (15 August 2026), PM Modi delivered a record 103-minute 13th consecutive Red Fort address.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: HAL handed over the Dhruv NG - India's first indigenous civil helicopter - in September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Asia's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, with Rs 5,500 crore investment and 18,000+ jobs.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI bond sales cut the banking liquidity surplus to Rs 4.92 trillion on 21 September, down 55% from the record Rs 11.16 trillion.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: At Tarang Shakti 2026 in Jodhpur, US F-35s will fly alongside the IAF for the first time.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Tata Advanced Systems' Berrechid (Morocco) facility will build 150 WhAP 8x8 armoured vehicles - the largest contract ever for Indian-made armoured vehicles.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: PM Modi handed out 51,000+ appointment letters at the 20th Rozgar Mela on 19 September.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The India-New Zealand FTA enters into force on 20 October 2026, giving 100% of India's exports to NZ duty-free access.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Samrat Choudhary offered his muretha (traditional turban) at Ram Janmabhoomi, Ayodhya, in July 2024 after Nitish Kumar rejoined the NDA.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: Chandrayaan-5, earlier called LUPEX, is a joint ISRO-JAXA mission in which an Indian lander will deploy a Japanese 350-kg rover at the lunar south pole.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The Global Firepower Index 2025 ranked India 4th in conventional military strength after the US, Russia and China, with defence spending third at about USD 76.6 billion.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The 2025-26 Union Budget announced a brownfield airport at Bihta, expansion of Patna airport, and support for the Western Koshi Canal benefiting over 50,000 hectares in Mithilanchal.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The Brand Finance Global Soft Power Index 2025 ranked India 30th.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: The Jnanpith Award, instituted in 1961, carries Rs 11 lakh, a bronze Saraswati statue and a citation.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The first WAVES summit was held from 1 to 4 May 2025 at the Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai, with its WAVES Bazaar recording deals worth over Rs 1,300 crore.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Maharashtra topped the 2025 Khelo India Youth Games medal table while host Bihar finished 15th.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The World Happiness Report 2025 ranked India 118th out of 147 countries, with Finland first.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Divya Deshmukh became India's 88th Grandmaster after winning the FIDE Women's World Cup on 28 July 2025 in Batumi, Georgia.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: NISAR flew on the 18th GSLV mission and the 12th flight with the indigenous cryogenic upper stage.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: In the Global Innovation Index 2025, India rose to 38th and China entered the top 10 for the first time at 10th place.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Bihar secured three new Ramsar designations in 2025: Gogabeel Lake in Katihar (October), and Gokul Jalashay and Udaipur Jheel (September).

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The first phase of the Patna Metro opened on 6 October 2025: a 3.45-km corridor linking Patliputra Bus Terminal, Zero Mile and Bhoothnath.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: The 2025 Chemistry Nobel went to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs).

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: The UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2025 put global adaptation finance at only about USD 26 billion a year against a need of USD 310-365 billion annually by the mid-2030s.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: COP30 in Belem adopted the Belem Package calling for at least USD 1.3 trillion per year in climate finance by 2035.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Nitish Kumar took oath for a record tenth term as Bihar CM on 20 November 2025 at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, with the oath administered by Governor Arif Mohammed Khan.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Cyclonic Storm Senyar formed over the Strait of Malacca (25-27 November 2025) and Ditwah over the southwest Bay of Bengal off Sri Lanka, closing out the costliest North Indian Ocean season on record.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The US assumed the G20 presidency on 1 December 2025 and will host the 2026 Leaders' Summit on 14-15 December at Trump National Doral, Miami.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The High Seas Treaty (BBNJ), adopted in June 2023 under UNCLOS 1982, entered into force on 17 January 2026 after crossing 60 ratifications.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: Cricketers Rohit Sharma and Harmanpreet Kaur were among the Padma Shri recipients for 2026.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement was concluded on 27 January 2026 at the 16th India-EU Summit in New Delhi, cutting up to 4 billion euros in annual tariffs.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Carlos Alcaraz became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam at 22 years 272 days after beating Novak Djokovic in the 2026 Australian Open final.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's per capita GSDP reached Rs 76,490 at current prices in 2024-25, up from Rs 66,828 the previous year.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's outstanding debt in 2024-25 stood at Rs 3,74,134 crore (37.7% of GSDP), with the fiscal deficit at 4.2% of GSDP.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's literacy rate stood at 61.8%, with life expectancy of 68.9 years for males and 69.7 for females (2019-23).

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's credit-deposit ratio was 56.3%, with bank deposits of Rs 5.27 lakh crore and advances of Rs 2.97 lakh crore.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar Budget 2026-27 projects GSDP of Rs 13,09,155 crore with a fiscal deficit of 2.99% of GSDP, within the 3% FRBM limit.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's outstanding public debt is projected at Rs 3,88,554 crore (29.68% of GSDP) by end-2026-27.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Bihar Budget 2026-27 backs the fourth agricultural roadmap alongside support for dairy, fisheries, animal husbandry and the makhana industry.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Bihar Governor set a target of creating one crore jobs and employment opportunities in the state by 2030.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Eligible women will receive Rs 2 lakh under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, the Finance Minister reiterated in the 2026-27 Budget speech.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India hit 106 sixes in the 2026 T20 World Cup, the first team to cross 100 sixes in one edition.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: At the 98th Oscars, Sinners earned a record 16 nominations and won four; Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman of colour to win cinematography.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: The Modified UDAN scheme, approved 25 March 2026 with a Rs 28,840 crore outlay, proposes developing 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Samrat Choudhary, born in 1968, began in politics with the RJD before joining the BJP in 2018.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: Surha Tal in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh — a natural oxbow lake on the Ganga's floodplain — was designated India's 100th Ramsar site in June 2026.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Under the Mukhyamantri Balika (Intermediate) Protsahan Yojana 2026, unmarried girls passing Class 12 through BSEB receive a one-time Rs 25,000 via the Medhasoft portal.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Beth Mooney became the first to win the Women's T20 World Cup Player of the Tournament award twice (2020 and 2026).

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Jannik Sinner retained the Wimbledon title on 12 July 2026, beating Alexander Zverev — his fifth Grand Slam title and 100th win at the majors.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme approved 31 July 2026, carries a Phase-I outlay of Rs 84,084 crore up to FY 2030-31 with drilling of 60 deepwater exploration wells.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Ahmedabad will host the centenary Commonwealth Games in 2030, announced at the Glasgow 2026 closing ceremony.

oneliners.subject: Geography
oneliners.text: The Ken-Betwa Link Project — the only one of 30 identified interlinking-of-rivers projects under implementation — had its foundation stone laid by PM Modi at Khajuraho on 25 December 2024.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 mandates investigation within two months and trial within three months, and was the only Bill debated in both Houses in the Monsoon Session 2026.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 replaces the colonial-era Bankers' Books Evidence Act of 1891 and formally recognises electronic and digital banking records as admissible evidence.

oneliners.subject: Awards
oneliners.text: No cricketer featured among the 17 Arjuna Award recipients announced on 18 August 2026.

oneliners.subject: Schemes
oneliners.text: The Abhaya Brigade provided 4,700 bicycles and two-wheelers to women police personnel; Bihar has about 40,000 women police personnel, the highest among states.

oneliners.subject: Miscellaneous
oneliners.text: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at slightly over $700 billion in early September 2026.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: Scientists described Gangaichthys indonepalicus, a new genus and species of miniature blind earthworm eel, from alluvial aquifers of the Indo-Gangetic plain in Bihar — the first stygobitic fish recorded from the Gangetic basin.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: The Tianjin Declaration at the 25th SCO Summit (2025) condemned terrorism in all forms and opposed unilateral tariffs and protectionism.

oneliners.subject: Defence

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The four labour codes are on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations (2020), Social Security (2020), and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (2020).

oneliners.text: The India–New Zealand FTA offers post-study work visas, 5,000 professional visas and a $20-billion investment commitment.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: On Jan 13, 2026, the Bihar cabinet approved 41 proposals and sanctioned Rs 33.29 crore for a 220 KV DC line to the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster at Gaya.

oneliners.text: On Jan 14, 2026, the ACC appointed Rakesh Aggarwal (NIA DG), Praveen Kumar (BSF DG) and Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor (ITBP DG) to lead three security agencies.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: National Startup Day (Jan 16, 2026) marked 10 years of Startup India (launched Jan 16, 2016); India has 2,00,000+ DPIIT-recognised startups, 53% from Tier 2/3 cities.

oneliners.text: Bihar doubled SC/ST pre-matric scholarships, first revision since 2011: Rs 1,200 / Rs 2,400 / Rs 3,600 for Classes 1-4 / 5-6 / 7-10, Rs 6,000 for hostelers; ~27 lakh students benefit.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Budget 2026-27 announced Biopharma SHAKTI (Rs 10,000 crore over 5 years), Semiconductor Mission 2.0, and Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Budget 2026-27 raised the Centre's capex to Rs 12.2 lakh crore (from Rs 11.21 lakh crore) and announced seven high-speed rail corridors, including Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The Income Tax Act, 2025 comes into force on April 1, 2026; share buybacks will be taxed as capital gains for all shareholders.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: March 2026 gubernatorial reshuffle: Jishnu Dev Varma became Maharashtra Governor, Taranjit Singh Sandhu became Delhi LG, and Vinai Kumar Saxena became Ladakh LG.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India topped the World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026 (New Delhi) with a record tally of 208 medals.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar Diwas 2026 marked the state's 114th foundation day (theme 'Unnat Bihar, Ujjwal Bihar'); Bihar was carved out of the Bengal Presidency on March 22, 1912.

oneliners.subject: International
oneliners.text: Balendra Shah (35), leader of the Rastriya Swatantra Party and a former rapper, became Nepal's youngest Prime Minister.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: CM Nitish Kumar unveiled 1,373 projects worth Rs 1,056 crore for Patna and distributed Rs 519.26 crore in bank loans to 2,06,989 Jeevika SHG women.

oneliners.text: NASA's Artemis II (launched April 1, 2026) is the first crewed lunar mission since 1972: four astronauts, a ~10-day, 1.12-million-km lunar flyby without landing.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: GST collections hit a record Rs 2.42 lakh crore in April 2026, at the start of FY 2026-27.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: INS Aridaman, commissioned on April 3, 2026, is India's third SSBN — the sea leg of India's nuclear triad.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO's second Integrated Air Drop Test (IADT-02) on April 10, 2026, validated parachute-based deceleration for the Gaganyaan crew module.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Nitish Kumar resigned as Bihar CM on April 14, 2026, ending a 20-year tenure as the state's longest-serving CM, after being elected to the Rajya Sabha.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: In Bihar's first BJP-led government, CM Samrat Choudhary retained 29 departments (incl. Home); Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Chaudhary received 10.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Samrat's first cabinet (April 22) approved 11 greenfield townships and froze land deals in Patna, Sonepur, Gayaji, Darbhanga, Saharsa, Purnea and Munger till March 31, 2027.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: 'Police Didi' initiative: 1,500 scooters (Rs 18.75 crore) for women police; Rs 305 crore grant to IIT Patna; ~50 acres at Punpun for an NFSU off-campus centre and CFSL.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India signed a Free Trade Agreement with New Zealand on April 27, 2026, weeks after concluding the India-EU free trade agreement.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI (April 2026) held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance, projecting FY27 GDP growth of 6.9% and inflation of 4.6%.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was negatived in the Lok Sabha; constitutional amendments require a special majority under Article 368.

oneliners.text: PMGSY-III was extended till March 2028 with an outlay of Rs 83,977 crore.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: India submitted updated NDCs for 2031-35 under the Paris Agreement, covering emission-intensity reduction, non-fossil power capacity and carbon sinks.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India set a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 under the Viksit Bharat vision.

oneliners.text: On Jan 1, 2026, Bihar promoted 43 IPS officers; Kundan Krishnan (1994 batch) was elevated to DGP rank.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor took charge as Vice Chief of the Air Staff on Jan 1, 2026, succeeding Narmdeshwar Tiwari.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech

oneliners.text: 'Pragati' and 'Vikas' are the mascots of Census 2027, India's first digital census.

oneliners.text: Census 2027 is India's first fully digital census; its population enumeration, including caste data, is set for February 2027.

oneliners.text: The Bihar Assembly passed 20 bills in its five-day Monsoon Session (20-24 July 2026).

oneliners.text: Parliament passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, creating a National Tribunals Commission for central tribunals.

oneliners.text: Parliament passed the MMDR Amendment Bill to ease mining auction rules and expand the critical minerals list.

oneliners.text: The RBI kept the repo at 5.25% in August 2026 but raised the FY27 GDP forecast to 6.7%.

oneliners.text: The National Sports Governance Bill, India's first comprehensive sports law, mandates 12-year tenure caps and 30% women's representation in federations.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: The 30th BWF World Badminton Championships began in New Delhi — India's first hosting since Hyderabad 2009.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar extended the Kushal Yuva Programme to 2030-31 (Rs 430.08 crore for 2026-27) for youth aged 15-28.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Kumhrar, near Patna, yielded the excavated pillared hall of Mauryan Pataliputra; D. B. Spooner's digs of 1912-13 uncovered its famous stone columns.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Agam Kuan in Patna is a legendary bottomless well linked in folklore to Emperor Ashoka, and is said never to run dry.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara were excavated mainly by the Archaeological Survey of India and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Nalanda's nine-storeyed library, Ratnodadhi, was destroyed during the Turko-Afghan invasions of the late 12th century, ending its manuscript collection.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Vikramashila Mahavihara was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala in the 8th century; its ruins lie at Antichak in Bhagalpur district.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The ancient university of Odantapuri near Bihar Sharif was founded by the Pala king Gopala I in the 8th century.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Sher Shah Suri's mausoleum stands in the middle of a lake at Sasaram in Rohtas district, a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Patna Museum, founded in 1917, houses the Didarganj Yakshi, a 3rd-century BCE polished sandstone masterpiece of Mauryan art.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Barabar and Nagarjuni hill caves in Jehanabad district are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, excavated under Ashoka for the Ajivika sect.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Lomas Rishi cave in the Barabar hills carries the earliest known rock-cut imitation of a wooden chaitya arch in India.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Lion Capital crowning the Ashokan pillar at Lauriya Nandangarh in West Champaran is among the best-preserved Ashokan capitals.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Rampurva bull capital of Ashoka, found in West Champaran, is now displayed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Kesaria stupa in East Champaran is counted among the largest Buddhist stupas in the world.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya was first built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The first Buddhist Council met at Rajagriha (Rajgir) soon after the Buddha's Mahaparinirvana, presided over by Mahakashyapa, with Upali reciting the Vinaya and Ananda the Sutta.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The third Buddhist Council was convened by Ashoka at Pataliputra under the presidency of Moggaliputta Tissa.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali about a century after the Buddha, under the patronage of King Kalashoka.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Vaishali was the capital of the Vajjian/Lichchhavi confederacy, regarded as one of the world's earliest republics.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Amrapali, the celebrated courtesan of Vaishali, donated her mango grove to the Buddha and his sangha.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Chirand in Saran district is Bihar's best-known Neolithic-Chalcolithic site, on the bank of the Ganga.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Chanakya, also called Kautilya or Vishnugupta and author of the Arthashastra, guided Chandragupta Maurya from Pataliputra.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Megasthenes, ambassador of Seleucus Nicator, lived at Chandragupta Maurya's court in Pataliputra and wrote the Indika.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Fa-Hien visited Pataliputra in the early 5th century CE during the reign of Chandragupta II and recorded its charitable hospitals.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda in the 7th century CE during Harshavardhana's reign and left a detailed account of the university.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Ajatashatru founded Pataligrama (later Pataliputra) as a fortified post against the Lichchhavis; his son Udayin later made it the Magadhan capital.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Mahapadma Nanda, founder of the Nanda dynasty, is described in the Puranas as the first non-Kshatriya (ekarat) king of Magadha.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Ashoka appointed Dhamma-mahamattas, officers of righteousness, in the 13th year of his reign to propagate dhamma.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 13th Major Rock Edict of Ashoka records his remorse after the Kalinga war fought in the 8th year of his reign.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur led the 1857 uprising in Bihar at nearly eighty years of age and defeated British forces at Arrah in July 1857.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Peer Ali, a Patna bookseller, led the July 1857 revolt in Patna and was hanged by the British.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India, opposed the tinkathia system forcing peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Raj Kumar Shukla, an indigo ryot of Champaran, persuaded Gandhi to visit Bihar and launch the Champaran inquiry.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929 to organise peasants against zamindari oppression.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, was born at Ziradei in Siwan district on 3 December 1884.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Jayaprakash Narayan was born at Sitab Diara in Saran district on 11 October 1902.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Sachchidananda Sinha, a leader from Bihar, served as the interim president of the Constituent Assembly when it first met on 9 December 1946.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Patna University, established in 1917, was the first university of Bihar and the seventh oldest in the Indian subcontinent.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar was carved out as a separate province on 1 April 1936, separating from Orissa; the combined Bihar-Orissa province had been formed in 1912.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The first Congress session held in Bihar met at Bankipore (Patna) in 1912 under the presidentship of R. N. Mudholkar.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Shri Krishna Sinha became the first Chief Minister of Bihar in 1946, with Anugrah Narayan Sinha as Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Nitish Kumar's first stint as Bihar Chief Minister, in March 2000, lasted only seven days for want of a majority.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Jayaprakash Narayan gave the call for Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution) from Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on 5 June 1974.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, was born in Patna in 1666; Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib at Patna Sahib marks his birthplace.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Sonepur Harihar Kshetra Mela, held at the Ganga-Gandak confluence, is famed as Asia's largest cattle fair.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Chhath Puja is dedicated to Surya, the Sun god, and Chhathi Maiya, and is observed with the greatest fervour in Bihar, eastern UP, Jharkhand and Nepal.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Pitrapaksha Mela at Gaya draws lakhs of pilgrims to perform pind-daan at the Vishnupad temple on the banks of the Falgu river.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Malmas Mela of Rajgir is held once every three years and is a major fair of the Magadh region.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Sama-Chakeva is a winter folk festival of the Mithila region celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bhikhari Thakur, called the Shakespeare of Bhojpuri, wrote the celebrated play Bidesiya on the theme of migrant labour.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Vidyapati, the 14th-15th century Maithil poet, is honoured as the Adi Kavi of Maithili literature.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Madhubani painting, the celebrated folk art of the Mithila region, was carried to national fame by artists like Sita Devi.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bhojpuri, Maithili, Magahi and Angika are the major regional languages of Bihar; Maithili entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment of 2003.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Ganga traverses roughly 445 km through Bihar, entering at Chausa (Buxar) and leaving near Kursela (Katihar). [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Sone joins the Ganga near Maner in Patna district, the Gandak near Hajipur-Sonepur, and the Kosi near Kursela in Katihar.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Ghaghra (Sarayu) meets the Ganga near Revelganj in Chhapra (Saran district).

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Kosi is called the Sorrow of Bihar because its frequent course-shifts cause devastating floods in north Bihar.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Burhi Gandak, Bagmati and Mahananda are other major north-Bihar tributaries of the Ganga.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar covers 94,163 sq km, making it the 12th largest state of India by area. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: As per the 2011 Census, Bihar's population was about 10.41 crore, the third highest among Indian states after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar recorded the highest decadal population growth (25.42%) among major states during 2001-2011.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: At 1,106 persons per sq km (2011), Bihar has the highest population density among the major states of India.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's sex ratio in 2011 was 918 females per 1,000 males, below the national average of 943.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's literacy rate in 2011 was 61.8% (male 71.2%, female 51.5%), the lowest among Indian states at that Census.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's state tree is the peepal, state flower the kachnar, state animal the gaur, and state bird the house sparrow.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Kanwar Lake in Begusarai, an oxbow lake of the Gandak, is Bihar's only Ramsar site and is counted among Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lakes.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries in Jamui district were added to the Ramsar list in 2024, taking Bihar's Ramsar count to three. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Valmiki National Park in West Champaran is Bihar's only national park and forms the core of the Valmiki Tiger Reserve.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary at Bhagalpur is India's only protected area dedicated to the Gangetic river dolphin.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: India's first National Dolphin Research Centre was inaugurated at Patna in 2024.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Rajgir Zoo Safari, opened in 2022, is Bihar's first zoo safari and among the largest such facilities in India.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The new Nalanda University campus at Rajgir was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 19 June 2024.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Mahatma Gandhi Setu across the Ganga between Patna and Hajipur, at 5.75 km, was India's longest river bridge when commissioned in 1982.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Digha-Sonepur rail-cum-road bridge (JP Setu) over the Ganga is about 4.56 km long and among India's longest rail-cum-road bridges.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Vikramshila Setu at Bhagalpur, about 4.7 km long, is a major Ganga bridge linking north and south Bihar.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Mithila Makhana received the GI tag in 2022; Bihar produces the overwhelming bulk of India's makhana.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Shahi litchi of Muzaffarpur received the GI tag in 2018.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Makhana Board in Bihar, expansion of IIT Patna, and support for the Western Koshi Canal project. [verify: legacy covers the same budget facts - angle differs]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's state budget for 2025-26 was about Rs 3.17 lakh crore, presented by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Samrat Choudhary. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Bihar Student Credit Card scheme offers education loans up to Rs 4 lakh to students pursuing higher education.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Under the Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana, the Bihar government provides staged cash incentives to girls from birth through graduation.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Mukhyamantri Nishchay Swayam Sahayata Bhatta Yojana gives Rs 1,000 per month to unemployed youth aged 20-25 in Bihar.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Har Ghar Nal Ka Jal, a flagship of the Saat Nischay programme, aims to provide piped drinking water to every Bihar household.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Kushal Yuva Karyakram under Saat Nischay imparts employable skills to Bihar's youth.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar was the first state to reserve 50% of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions, implemented in 2006.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Patna Metro's Phase-1 comprises two corridors - north-south and east-west - being executed through a special purpose vehicle.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The new terminal building of Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna, was inaugurated in 2025. [verify]

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: AIIMS Darbhanga was approved by the Union Cabinet with an outlay of about Rs 1,264 crore. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary has been proposed as Bihar's second tiger reserve after Valmiki. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: NTPC's Barh Super Thermal Power Project in Patna district is among the largest coal-based power projects in eastern India.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Nabinagar Super Thermal Power Project in Aurangabad is a joint venture of NTPC and the Indian Railways.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar hosted the 7th Khelo India Youth Games in May 2025, the first time the state staged the national multi-sport event.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Sher Shah Suri built the Grand Trunk Road's precursor, the Sadak-i-Azam, and introduced the silver rupiya of about 178 grains.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Sher Shah defeated Humayun at the Battle of Chausa (1539) and again at Kannauj/Bilgram (1540), forcing the Mughal into exile.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The 1934 Bihar-Nepal earthquake of 15 January 1934 (magnitude about 8.0) devastated north Bihar, with Muzaffarpur and Darbhanga among the worst hit.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000, reducing Bihar from 54 to 38 districts at the time.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The 2022 caste-based survey of Bihar reported Extremely Backward Classes as the largest group at about 36%, followed by OBCs at about 27%. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, the state's economy grew faster than the national average in 2023-24, with GSDP growth of about 14.5% at current prices. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Terai belt in north Bihar and the Kaimur-Rajgir hill ranges in the south give the state its three natural divisions: northern plains, Terai, and southern plateau fringe.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Falgu river at Gaya flows mostly underground and surfaces only during the monsoon, yet is central to the Pitrapaksha rituals.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar's first floating solar power plant was commissioned on the water bodies of the state as part of its renewable push. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Patna-Gaya-Dobhi section of the Buddhist circuit road links Bodh Gaya, Rajgir and Nalanda for pilgrim tourism.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Sugarcane, paddy, wheat, maize and pulses are Bihar's principal crops; the state is among India's top producers of litchi, makhana and maize.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 243G read with the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) devolves powers to Panchayats; Article 243W with the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) does so for municipalities.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to urban local bodies, adding Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 40, a Directive Principle, directs the state to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the size of the Council of Ministers at 15% of the legislature's strength and barred defectors from ministerial office till re-election.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Tenth Schedule on anti-defection was added by the 52nd Amendment (1985); a split no longer protects defectors after the 91st Amendment.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity into the Preamble and added the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A).

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from Fundamental Rights; it survives as a legal right under Article 300A.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced the Goods and Services Tax, adding Articles 246A, 269A and 279A.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 103rd Amendment (2019) provided 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in education and public employment.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 104th Amendment (2020) extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures till 2030 but ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 105th Amendment (2021) restored the power of states to identify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 97th Amendment (2011) gave constitutional status to cooperative societies, adding Part IXB and inserting the word 'cooperatives' in Article 19(1)(c).

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The S. R. Bommai judgment (1994) made the floor of the House the sole test of a government's majority, curbing the misuse of Article 356.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: NOTA (None of the Above) was introduced on ballot units following the 2013 Supreme Court judgment in PUCL vs Union of India.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: VVPAT slips were used in every Lok Sabha constituency for the first time in the 2019 general election.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the conduct of elections; Section 29A deals with registration of political parties.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Delimitation of constituencies was frozen till 2001 by the 42nd Amendment and the freeze was extended to 2026 by the 84th Amendment (2001).

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Bihar Legislative Assembly has 243 seats, Bihar sends 40 members to the Lok Sabha and 16 to the Rajya Sabha.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bihar is one of the six states with a bicameral legislature; its Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) has 75 members.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Mukhiya heads the Gram Panchayat, the lowest tier of Bihar's three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The District Planning Committee, mandated by Article 243ZD, consolidates rural and urban plans at the district level.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Gyanesh Kumar took charge as the 26th Chief Election Commissioner of India in February 2025.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The government announced in April 2025 that the forthcoming Census (2027) will enumerate castes alongside the population count.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 8th Central Pay Commission's constitution was announced in January 2025 to revise salaries of central government employees. [verify]

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The three new criminal laws - Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam - replaced the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act from 1 July 2024.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, restructuring the management of waqf properties, received Presidential assent in April 2025. [verify]

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The One Nation One Election proposal rests on the Kovind committee report submitted in March 2024; implementing bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 312 empowers Parliament to create new All-India Services; the IAS, IPS and IFoS are the three existing ones.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council; it was set up on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation in 1990.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Punchhi Commission (2007-2010) reviewed Centre-State relations and recommended, among others, fixed five-year terms for Governors.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 200 requires a Governor to act on a state bill - assent, withhold, reserve for the President, or return it once for reconsideration.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's prior recommendation (Article 109); the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes within 14 days.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: A Constitutional Amendment Bill needs a special majority - more than half the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting - under Article 368.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The basic structure doctrine, propounded in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), bars Parliament from destroying the Constitution's essential features.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: In Golaknath (1967) the Supreme Court held Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) overruled it, permitting amendment short of destroying the basic structure.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The collegium system for appointing higher-judiciary judges flows from the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges cases; the NJAC Act was struck down in 2015.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 124A, inserted by the 99th Amendment for the NJAC, became inoperative after the Supreme Court's 2015 verdict.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Bihar Public Service Commission was constituted on 1 April 1949 under the Government of India Act, 1935. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: BPSC conducts the Combined Competitive Examination for the state civil services; the 70th CCE prelims were held in December 2024 with a re-exam at one Patna centre in January 2025.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Arif Mohammed Khan was sworn in as the Governor of Bihar in January 2025. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Chairman of the Bihar Legislative Council is elected by the Council's members from among themselves under Article 182.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: A no-confidence motion against the Bihar Council of Ministers needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted in the 243-member Assembly. [verify]

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: President's Rule has been imposed in Bihar eight times, the last spell running from March to November 2005.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The National Commission for Backward Classes became a constitutional body through the 102nd Amendment (2018), with Article 338B.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 97th Amendment (2011) gave constitutional status to cooperative societies, adding Part IXB.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Centre's GST compensation to states for revenue loss ended in June 2022, five years after the tax was rolled out in July 2017.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Article 280 requires the Finance Commission to be constituted every five years; the 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The State Election Commission, constituted under Articles 243K and 243ZA, conducts all panchayat and municipal elections in Bihar.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Senuwar in Rohtas district is an important Neolithic site of the Vindhyan-Kaimur region with evidence of early rice cultivation.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Chechar in Vaishali district is a noted Neolithic-Chalcolithic site of the middle Ganga plain.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Allahabad pillar inscription (prashasti) of Samudragupta was composed by his court poet Harisena.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Skandagupta repelled the Huna invasion, an achievement recorded on the Bhitari stone pillar inscription.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Nalanda Mahavihara was founded in the 5th century CE during the reign of Kumaragupta I.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Chandragupta II assumed the title Vikramaditya after his victories over the Shakas of western India.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Mehrauli iron pillar inscription celebrates a king named Chandra, identified by most scholars with Chandragupta II.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Gopala, founder of the Pala dynasty around 750 CE, is recorded in the Khalimpur copper plate as having been elected by the people.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Devapala, the most powerful Pala king, extended the empire to Assam and Orissa according to the Badal pillar inscription.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur (now Bangladesh), built by Dharmapala, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: Bakhtiyar Khilji sacked the monasteries of Nalanda and Odantapuri around 1200 CE during the early Turko-Afghan incursions.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Battle of Chandawar (1194) in which Muhammad Ghori defeated Jayachandra of Kannauj opened the Ganga plain to Turko-Afghan rule.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the first Sultan of Delhi, died in 1210 from a polo accident at Lahore.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Balban's policy of blood and iron crushed the Turkish nobles (the Chahalgani) and asserted the Sultan's divine right.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Alauddin Khilji's market control system fixed prices of grain, cloth and other essentials, enforced through the Diwan-i-Riyasat.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and later reversed the decision.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded the cities of Fatehabad, Hissar and Jaunpur and dug extensive irrigation canals.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Battle of Talikota (1565) ended the imperial phase of the Vijayanagara Empire; the capital Hampi was sacked.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Krishnadeva Raya of Vijayanagara authored the Telugu work Amuktamalyada and patronised the Ashtadiggajas.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Hampi, the Vijayanagara capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Akbar's revenue minister Todar Mal introduced the zabti system and the dahsala (ten-year average) assessment.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri hosted Akbar's religious debates; the Din-i-Ilahi was proclaimed in 1582.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674; his council of eight ministers was called the Ashtapradhan.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Shivaji and the Mughals, represented by Jai Singh I.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas ended Maratha ambitions in the north for a generation.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Battle of Buxar (1764) gave the East India Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa through the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773); the Regulating Act of 1773 created the post.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 was introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa by Lord Cornwallis, making zamindars proprietors of land.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Ryotwari system was pioneered by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in the Madras Presidency.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Mahalwari system was introduced in the North-Western Provinces under Holt Mackenzie and later Lord William Bentinck.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse annexed Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and Awadh among other states.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Santhal rebellion of 1855-56 was led by the brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu against zamindars and moneylenders.

oneliners.subject: Bihar Special
oneliners.text: The Wahabi movement in India was inspired by Syed Ahmed Barelvi of Raebareli; Patna was one of its important centres.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Deccan Riots of 1875 targeted moneylenders in Maharashtra and led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act of 1879.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 erupted over allowing Indian judges to try European offenders.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 at Bombay; W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon was annulled in 1911, when the capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 marked the reunion of the Moderates and Extremists and a Congress-League accord on separate electorates.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Home Rule movements were launched by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (April 1916) and Annie Besant (September 1916).

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 during a protest against the Rowlatt Act; General Dyer ordered the firing.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali brothers, Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali, in defence of the Ottoman Caliphate.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in August 1920 and withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident of 5 February 1922.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Swaraj Party was founded in January 1923 by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru to enter the councils and wreck them from within.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted as an all-white body; Lala Lajpat Rai died of injuries from a lathi charge during the protests.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Nehru Report of 1928, drafted under Motilal Nehru's chairmanship, demanded dominion status for India.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution; 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati to Dandi, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931, leading to Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 between Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar reserved seats for the Depressed Classes within the general electorate.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Government of India Act, 1935, provided provincial autonomy and a federal structure; the Congress formed ministries in 1937 and resigned in 1939.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The August Offer (1940) first recognised the right of Indians to frame their own constitution after the war.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Cripps Mission of March 1942 offered dominion status but was rejected; Gandhi called it a post-dated cheque.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942 with Gandhi's Do or Die call; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The INA trials at the Red Fort in 1945-46 sparked nationwide protests in defence of Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal and Gurbaksh Dhillon.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Royal Indian Navy mutiny of February 1946 began aboard HMIS Talwar in Bombay and spread to other ports.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed a three-tier federation; both the Congress and the League initially accepted it.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 laid down the partition of India; the Indian Independence Act received royal assent in July 1947.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: The 38th National Games of 2025 were hosted by Uttarakhand from 28 January to 14 February with the mascot Mauli (monal pheasant).

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, defeating New Zealand in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: D. Gukesh became the World Chess Champion in December 2024 by defeating Ding Liren, the youngest undisputed champion in history.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
oneliners.text: India finished 71st at the Paris 2024 Olympics with six medals, including Manu Bhaker's two bronze medals in shooting.

oneliners.subject: General Knowledge
